This smallness condition amounts to a sufficiently large population size N (equivalently, small fluctuation strength 1/N): the existence theory thus operates in the perturbative regime around the deterministic mean-field limit, and for fixed coefficients it is always satisfiable once N is large enough.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: arXiv admin note: text overlap with arXiv:2202.12602 (same author) Derivation section split off, becomes companion paper

Analysis of PDEs.title: Gaussian fluctuations of the moderately interacting Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto particle system around the mollified mean-field limit
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study, at the logarithmic mollification scale $η^{-2(d+1+α)}\leδ\log N$ of Chen, Daus, Holzinger and J{ü}ngel, the fluctuation field $V^N=\sqrt N(μ^N-u_η)$ of the moderately interacting multi-species particle system whose mean-field limit is the Shigesada- Kawasaki-Teramoto (SKT) cross-diffusion system. The field is centred at the solution $u_η$ of the mollified equation, which depends on $N$ through $η$. On a scale of weighted Bessel-potential spaces of negative order we prove that the laws of $(V^N,M^N)$ are tight, where $M^N$ is the martingale part. Every limit point of $M^N$ is a continuous Gaussian martingale with an explicit deterministic bracket. Every limit point of $V^N$ is a weak solution, and the mild solution, of a linear Ornstein-Uhlenbeck SPDE whose drift is the linearisation of the SKT operator at the limit $u$. The initial field and the martingale are independent, and weak solutions are unique given both, so the whole sequence converges in law, jointly with the martingale part, and the limit is unique in law among solutions of the martingale problem. The noise is $d M_i=div(\sqrt{2u_iΘ_i}dW_i)$, with $Θ_i=σ_i+\sum_jf(a_{ij}u_j)$ and $W$ a cylindrical Wiener process on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^{nd})$. The hypotheses are those of Chen, Daus, Holzinger and J{ü}ngel, including the smallness and the nonnegativity on $\mathbb{R}$ of the nonlinearity $f$. We add radial kernels $B_{ij}$, the independence of the initial data and the Brownian motions across particles and species, a smaller $δ$, a regularity budget on $u_0$, a strengthened smallness condition on $f$ that makes the backward system diagonally dominant in weighted spaces, and an integer Sobolev index $s$.

Functional Analysis.title: Gelfand numbers of Schatten class embeddings in the quasi-Banach range
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove Conjecture 1.4 of Prochno and Strzelecki [J. Approx. Theory 277 (2022), 105736] on Gelfand numbers of embeddings between finite-dimensional Schatten classes. For $0<p\le1$ and indices bounded away from the ambient dimension by a fixed proportion, we obtain the conjectured lower bound, uniformly in the target exponent $2\le q\le\infty$. Together with the known upper estimate obtained by Hinrichs, Prochno and Vybíral [Math. Ann., 380(3-4):1563-1593, 2021], this gives the exact asymptotic order in the previously unresolved range. As a consequence, we obtain a complete all-index description by combining our result with the estimates of Hinrichs, Prochno and Vybíral and of Prochno and Strzelecki. The proof is deterministic and is based on Hilbert--Schmidt projections on rectangular matrix spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: A half-line of Schur idempotent norms
Functional Analysis.summary: Using a family of bipartite graphs constructed by hanging identical rooted trees at every vertex of a highly symmetric graph, we show that every sufficiently large real number is the norm of an idempotent Schur multiplier on the bounded operators on $\ell^2$. This answers a question previously raised by the author.

Functional Analysis.title: GNS-like representations of a quasi *-algebra in Krein spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper unbounded representations of quasi *-algebras on an indefinite inner product space are introduced and studied. After introducing the partial *-algebra of unbounded closable operators sharing a common dense domain in a Krein space, the appropriate notion of *-representation in this setting is developed, and a GNS-type construction for quasi *-algebras based on $α$-positive sesquilinear forms is established. Furthermore, the notion of abstract conditional expectation is generalized to quasi *-algebras and how \emph{admissible} abstract conditional expectations $P$ give rise to representable $P$-forms is shown. The relation between $α$-positive forms and $P$-forms is also clarified. Several examples are provided.

Functional Analysis.title: Maximally transitive semigroups of $n\times n$ matrices (revised and extended version)
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. We prove that for every $n\ge 1$ there is a pair of $n\times n$ matrices with entries in $\mathbb{K}$ that generates a dense subsemigroup of the space $M_n(\mathbb{K})$ of all $n\times n$ matrices. Since the powers of a single matrix are never dense, two generators is optimal. Equivalently, there is a $2$-generator semigroup of linear maps whose action on $(\mathbb{K}^n)^n$ is topologically transitive, whereas no semigroup of linear maps acts topologically transitively on $(\mathbb{K}^n)^{n+1}$. In fact, for such a semigroup every orbit closure in $(\mathbb{K}^n)^k$, for every $k\ge1$, is as large as linear algebra allows. Along the way we give a short self-contained proof of the density of explicit $2$-generator subsemigroups of $GL_2^+(\mathbb{R})$ and of $M_2(\mathbb{R})$, based on a simple criterion for closed subsemigroups of $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$.
Functional Analysis.comment: This is a revised and extended version of a published article

Functional Analysis.title: Fourier level inequalities on the discrete cube via complex hypercontractivity and Riesz transforms
Functional Analysis.summary:
Eldan's level-$1{:}3$ inequality is a central tool in his second-order correlation inequalities for increasing Boolean functions. His proof is going to Gaussian space and uses an entropy estimate for second Hermite tensors. We give a direct proof on the discrete hypercube. For increasing real-valued functions $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, we prove $$ W_3[f,g]\ge -2W_1[f,g]\log\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(f)\mathrm{Var}(g)}}{W_1[f,g]}\right). $$ The proof combines complex hypercontractivity with the discrete Riesz transforms. We also give a short proof of a level-$1:d$ inequality obtained by Keller and Kindler.
  As an application, we recover Eldan's correlation inequality with a slight improvement. If $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ are increasing and $g$ is antipodal, then $$ \mathrm{Cov}(f,g)\ge \frac1{24}\,\frac{\sum_i\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]\mathrm{Inf}_i[g]}{\sqrt{\log\!\left(4e\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(f)\mathrm{Var}(g)}/(\sum_i\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]\mathrm{Inf}_i[g])\right)}}, $$ where the square-root logarithm cannot be improved as shown in the OR--majority example.

Functional Analysis.title: Generalized gyrovector spaces revisited
Functional Analysis.summary: We revise a proof of a Mazur-Ulam theorem for generalized gyrovector spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: A centroaffine perspective on improved Brascamp--Lieb and dimensional Brunn--Minkowski inequalities
Functional Analysis.summary: We study dimensional concavity properties of even log-concave measures within the framework of weighted centroaffine differential geometry. We express the relevant local concavity inequalities in terms of a weighted Hilbert--Brunn--Minkowski operator and establish an anisotropic Poincaré inequality for odd functions and a strengthened Brascamp--Lieb inequality for even functions. As applications, we obtain quantitative dimensional concavity estimates for a class of geometric measures and measures with pinched Hessian, extending results of Cordero-Erausquin and Rotem for rotationally invariant measures and Eskenazis and Moschidis for the Gaussian measure.

Functional Analysis.title: Non-standard behaviour of semibounded forms and their representations
Functional Analysis.summary: A number of results is presented concerning the extreme behaviour of products of linear operators or relations from one Hilbert space ${\mathfrak H}$ to another Hilbert space ${\mathfrak K}$. It is shown that there exists a relation $T$ from ${\mathfrak H}$ to ${\mathfrak K}$ such that the closure of the nonnegative relation $T^*T$ in ${\mathfrak H}$ is not equal to the nonnegative selfadjoint relation $T^*T^{**}$; moreover, this may happen for a singular but also for a regular (i.e., closable) relation $T$. In fact, as an extreme situation the paper contains a construction of a densely defined closable operator $T$, such that ${\rm dom\,}T^*T=\{0\}$, while $T^*T^{**}$ is a densely defined selfadjoint operator. Likewise it is shown that there exist a linear relation $T$ from ${\mathfrak H}$ to ${\mathfrak K}$ and a nonnegative everywhere defined contraction $R$ in ${\mathfrak K}$ for which the product $RT$ is singular and the product $R^{1/2} T$ is regular. Such results illustrate situations that can arise in the Lebesgue type decomposition of linear relations and the Lebesgue type decomposition of semibounded forms.

Functional Analysis.title: The Ulam--Kaplansky problem in operator algebras
Functional Analysis.summary: The Ulam--Kaplansky problem up to similarity in operator algebras asks whether $A\oplus A\sim B\oplus B$ implies $A\sim B$. We construct block-diagonal compact operators for which this implication fails. For von Neumann algebras with separable predual, we prove that this cancellation property is equivalent to subhomogeneity. Moreover, we obtain a cancellation law for finite ampliations in unital Banach algebras when the commutant of one element is finite dimensional modulo its Jacobson radical.

Functional Analysis.title: On the existence of optimizers for nonlinear time-frequency concentration problems: the Born-Jordan distribution
Functional Analysis.summary: We study the $L^p$ concentration problem for the Born-Jordan distribution in dimension $d>1$, thus extending the one-dimensional analysis in [Stra-Svela-Trapasso, J. Math. Pures Appl. (2026)]. We show that the existence of concentration optimizers depends on the exponent $p$ with a critical threshold at $p_*(d)= \frac{2d}{d-2}$ for $d\geq2$ (with the understanding that $p_*(2)=\infty$). In particular, for subcritical exponents $1\leq p<p_*(d)$ we prove that the supremum is finite and is attained, whereas for supercritical exponents $p>p_*(d)$ we show that the functional is unbounded. We also provide the complete solution in the (significantly more) challenging critical regime in dimension $d=2$. For the critical case in dimension $d=2$ and the supercritical case in dimension $d>2$ we also show that $L^2$ functions whose Born-Jordan distribution does not belong to $L^p$ are generic in the Baire sense. For the critical exponent in dimension $d>2$, for which Wang has recently shown that the supremum is finite, we prove that the functional is not sequentially weakly upper semicontinuous, showing that the still open question of attainment is nontrivial.
Functional Analysis.comment: 29 pages. Analysis of the critical case in high dimension has been added

Functional Analysis.title: An interpretation of the BMO boundedness of Hörmander--Mikhlin multipliers
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove a pointwise domination of Poisson variances for Hörmander--Mikhlin multipliers on the real line. The estimate holds in operator order for operator-valued functions and gives a direct Fourier-side proof of BMO boundedness. The same argument gives an algebraic proof of the one-dimensional Schur multiplier estimate of Conde-Alonso, González-Pérez, Parcet and Tablate ( Annals of Mathematics, 2023), formulated here using Poisson BMO. The endpoint estimates are proved for $L^2$ functions and Hilbert--Schmidt operators; interpolation gives the corresponding $L^p$ and Schatten estimates.

Functional Analysis.title: Failure of Pólya-Szegő inequality for weighted nonlocal seminorm and on nonlocal C-K-N inequality
Functional Analysis.summary:
We create counterexamples to show that Pólya-Szegő type of inequality fails for the weighted nonlocal seminorm \begin{equation*}
  [u]_{W^{s,p, α}(\mathbb{R}^d)} := \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \frac{|x|^{α_{1} p} |y|^{α_{2} p} |u(x)-u(y)|^{p}}{|x-y|^{d+sp}} \, dx \, dy \right)^{\frac{1}{p}} \ , \end{equation*} in all three regimes $α_1 +α_2 < 0, \, α_1 +α_2 = 0$, and $α_1 +α_2 >0$. These counterexamples are such that it completely settles the first two cases for all parameters. We also provide necessary and sufficient conditions on the parameters for $ [u]_{W^{s,p, α}(\mathbb{R}^d)} < \infty$, thus extending an earlier known result of [Serena Dipierro and Enrico Valdinoci, A density property for fractional weighted Sobolev spaces]. We also provide another proof of the fractional C-K-N type inequality, for most of the parameters (Hardy and Sobolev are included), using a familiar technique which is involved in the proof of fractional Sobolev inequality of [Eleonora Di Nezza, Giampiero Palatucci, and Enrico Valdinoci, Hitchhiker's guide to the fractional Sobolev spaces, Bulletin des sciences mathematiques] together with a symmetrization technique.

Functional Analysis.title: Langevin Monte-Carlo Provably Learns Depth Two Neural Nets at Any Size and Data
Functional Analysis.summary: In this note we prove that the Langevin Monte Carlo (LMC) algorithm can minimize the population risk of appropriately regularized depth-2 nets with no restrictions on the size of the net and for any choice of training data --- and we give non-asymptotic convergence rates for it. We achieve this via showing that in q-Renyi divergence, the iterates of LMC converge to the Gibbs distribution of certain Frobenius norm regularized losses for these nets --- in both classification and regression settings. The key technicality of the work is two-fold (a) to keep the amount of regularization needed be independent of the size of the net and (b) to obtain convergence rates that scale with just the Poincare constant of the corresponding Gibbs measure. This work synthesizes several recent observations about isoperimetry conditions under which LMC converges and that two-layer neural loss functions can always be regularized by a constant amount such that they satisfy the Villani conditions, and thus their Gibbs measures satisfy a Poincare inequality.

Functional Analysis.title: The kinetic Kato square root problem
Functional Analysis.summary: We solve the kinetic Kato square root problem for the whole-space Kolmogorov operator $$H_A=\partial_t-X\cdot\nabla_Y-\operatorname{div}_X(A\nabla_X)$$ on \(\mathrm L^2\) with Lebesgue measure, where \(A\) is a bounded measurable complex uniformly accretive matrix depending on all variables. We define its realization through a sesquilinear form and identify the square-root domains of the resulting maximal accretive operator and its adjoint with the intrinsic Sobolev space defined by one velocity derivative and half a derivative along the transport flow. The homogeneous norm equivalences depend only on the dimension and the coefficient bounds. The energy also controls a position derivative of order one third. The proof uses second-order resolvents and localized affine testing. A regularized transport symmetrizer gives hidden coercivity, while comparison with a positive Rockland operator supplies intrinsic smoothing. Commutator and dyadic approximation estimates remove the smoothing before a Carleson argument is applied. We also obtain uniform shifted square-root estimates and bounded velocity, transport and position Riesz transforms.
Functional Analysis.comment: Revised exposition and expanded declaration of AI assistance

Functional Analysis.title: Characterization of Fréchet Spaces and Application to Hausdorff MNC
Functional Analysis.summary: We study the Hausdorff measure of noncompactness associated with compatible metrics on Fréchet spaces, with the aim of extending its Banach-space properties. After recalling the characterization by complete translation-invariant metrics with convex balls, we calculate the scalar Hausdorff measure for a standard weighted fractional metric. For bounded nonprecompact sets its value is the unique root of an equation involving a finite seminorm gauge determined by the covering radius. This yields an actual Hausdorff-condensing criterion for compact perturbations of maps having separate contraction constants at the seminorm levels. On countable products of Banach spaces we obtain an exact coordinate formula and a sharp scalar contraction bound on bounded domains, without requiring a uniform gap between the coordinate constants and one for strict condensation. For closed subspaces, an exact finite-projection formula retains the compatibility constraints on covering centers. Explicit examples show why separately computed seminorm measures cannot generally be substituted into the metric formula. Applications to spaces of real sequence-valued continuous functions give an explicit oscillation formula and exhibit the compatibility obstruction on an unbounded interval. Classical fixed-point consequences are recorded briefly.

Functional Analysis.title: Semigroups of matrices with dense orbits (revised version)
Functional Analysis.summary: For $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and every $n\ge 1$ we construct two $n\times n$ matrices $A$ and $B$ such that the orbit of every vector $p\in\mathbb{K}^n$ with $p_1\ne 0$ under the semigroup generated by $A$ and $B$ is dense in $\mathbb{K}^n$; the remaining vectors lie in an invariant hyperplane, so the set of vectors with dense orbit is exactly the complement of a hyperplane. Thus two generators always suffice for a hypercyclic semigroup of matrices, in contrast with the commutative case, where $n+1$ generators are needed on $\mathbb{C}^n$. We give a transparent reformulation of the hypotheses, a criterion for the density of $\{a^mb^n\}$ that makes them checkable, and explicit examples with complete proofs. As applications we obtain affine pairs on $\mathbb{K}^n$ all of whose orbits are dense, and, for every $n$, a pair of real matrices with an orbit that is somewhere dense but not dense in $\mathbb{R}^n$.
Functional Analysis.comment: This is a revised version of a published article

Functional Analysis.title: Recovering the Length of a Path from its Signature
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove the length conjecture of J. Chang, T. Lyons and H. Ni for paths of bounded variation for arbitrary real Banach spaces and any reasonable tensor (algebra) norms. More precisely, we establish the missing lower bound and in this way show that the length of a tree-reduced path is recovered from the asymptotic behaviour of its normalised signature. The main technical argument uses the norm duality and shuffle algebra to express natural powers of polygonal length approximations as combinations of linear functionals acting on restricted signatures, which are then glued by suitable integrations into a linear functional of controlled growth acting on the full signature. In particular, the full proof combines tools of classical analysis and functional analysis, such as localisation by continuous cutoff functions, Stone-Weierstrass approximation of continuous functions by signature polynomials, the Hahn-Banach theorem and a support detection lemma for compactly supported real signed Borel measures.

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp Finiteness Principles for the boundary values of $C^2$-functions
Functional Analysis.summary:
Let $Ω$ be an arbitrary domain in ${\bf R}^n$, and let $C^2(Ω)$ be the space of all functions whose partial derivatives of all orders up to two are continuous and bounded on $Ω$. We prove the following Finiteness Principle for the boundary values of $C^2(Ω)$-functions: A function $f$ defined on the boundary of $Ω$ is the trace of a function $F\in C^2(Ω)$ provided there exists $λ>0$ such that, for every set $E$ of at most $N=3\cdot 2^{n-1}$ boundary points, there exists a function $F_E\in C^2(Ω)$ with $\|F_E\|_{C^2(Ω)}\leλ$ whose trace coincides with $f$ on $E$. Moreover, $F$ can be chosen with $\|F\|_{C^2(Ω)}\leγλ$ where $γ$ depends only on $n$.
  We also refine this principle by showing that it suffices to consider $N$-point sets $E$ with specific geometric ``visibility'' properties relative to $Ω$.
Functional Analysis.comment: 51 pages, 2 figures. This is the journal version of the paper

Functional Analysis.title: The Approximation Property without the Bounded Approximation Property in a Separable Banach Space and Its Dual
Functional Analysis.summary:
We investigate whether a dual Banach space with the approximation property (AP) must necessarily have the bounded approximation property (BAP). Using a quantitative renorming theorem for the space of absolutely summable sequences, we establish a direct-sum construction yielding a negative answer.
  More precisely, we construct a separable Banach space (X) such that both (X) and its dual (X^*) have the approximation property, while neither space has the bounded approximation property. The construction uses a sequence of equivalent renormings of (\ell_1) with increasingly restrictive finite-dimensional approximation bounds. By assembling these spaces through a (c_0)-direct sum, we obtain a dual space whose approximation property is preserved, but whose approximation constants cannot be uniformly bounded.
  We establish the required transfer principles, including the preservation of approximation bounds under complemented coordinate projections and the descent of the bounded approximation property from a dual space to its predual. We also provide an explicit complex-scalar version of the construction.
  The argument separates the external quantitative renorming input from the direct-sum construction and its functional-analytic consequences. In particular, the resulting example demonstrates that the approximation property of a dual space does not imply its bounded approximation property, even when the predual is separable and both spaces possess the approximation property.

Functional Analysis.title: Pointwise convergence of noncommutative discrete spherical ergodic averages
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we establish spherical maximal inequalities associated with commuting trace-preserving automorphisms on von Neumann algebras, extending Magyar-Stein-Wainger's discrete spherical maximal inequalities to the noncommutative setting. On a noncommutative probability space, we further prove that, under a strong ergodicity assumption, the corresponding discrete spherical averages converge bilaterally almost uniformly to $τ(x)1$ for every $x\in L_p(\mathcal M)$, $\frac{d}{d-2}<p\leq\infty$, when $d\geq5$.

Functional Analysis.title: Geometric Functional Inequalities for Markov Processes: An Invitation via the Langevin Diffusion
Functional Analysis.summary: Functional inequalities provide a language for reasoning about the long-time properties of ergodic Markov processes in terms of their macroscopic geometry. This article offers an informal introduction to functional inequalities for readers who are more familiar with probabilistic tools based around couplings, Lyapunov techniques, and similar. The main ideas are developed through the overdamped Langevin diffusion, where various functionals related to this convergence admit particularly transparent expressions, and for which the key associated inequalities -- namely, the Poincaré and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities -- are especially well-studied. We explain the qualitative content of these inequalities, what they imply about convergence to equilibrium, how they transform and compose under natural operations, and how they interface with classical probabilistic approaches. Related inequalities are discussed more briefly, and an annotated guide is provided for readers wishing to enter the wider literature.
Functional Analysis.comment: 21 pages of writing, 4 pages of references, 6 figures

Functional Analysis.title: Singular values of iterated Aluthge transforms of compact operators
Functional Analysis.summary: Yamazaki proved that the norms of the iterated Aluthge transforms of an operator converge to its spectral radius, and Ando showed that for matrices the singular values of the iterates converge to the moduli of the eigenvalues. We prove that the latter holds for every compact operator on a Hilbert space and every generalized Aluthge transform $Δ_t$ with $0<t<1$: for every $j$, the $j$-th singular value of the $n$-th iterate converges to $|λ_j(T)|$, and the products of the $k$ largest singular values, as well as the Ky Fan norms, decrease monotonically to their limits. This is the Aluthge counterpart of the Yamamoto--Davis theorem. We also determine the limit in the Schatten $p$-norm whenever $T$ belongs to a strictly smaller Schatten class.

Functional Analysis.title: Algebras, Kernels and Correspondences
Functional Analysis.summary: This is a nearly complete draft of our paper in which we attempt to do three things. First, we show that when formulated in the context of reproducing kernel correspondences over Rieffel's category, Normod-$M$, the Kolmogorov decomposition/representation theorem of Ball, Marx, and Vinnikov is functorial in $M$. Second, we investigate relations between our work and the work of Clouâtre and Hartz concerning multipliers of reproducing kernels. This investigation leads to interesting questions about the geometry of the matricial unit disc associated with a correspondence over $M$. And third, we describe how some of the recent work of Salomon, Shalit and Shamovich may be formulated in our setting. This leads to the notion of subvarieties, their quotients, and their relation with the structure of reproducing correspondences.

Functional Analysis.title: On Continuous Wavelet Transform of Complex Radon Measures on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$
Functional Analysis.summary: This paper investigates a necessary and sufficient condition for a measurable function on $\mathbb{R}^{\times} \times \mathbb{R}^{d}$ to be the continuous wavelet transform of a complex Radon measure on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ under suitable regularity conditions on the wavelets. We investigate various integrability properties of the wavelet transform of complex Radon measures. We define a new norm on the collection of such functions and show that it is isometrically isomorphic to the Banach algebra of complex Radon measures under convolution. We show a wavelet inversion formula for measures, in a restricted sense. Under additional hypothesis, we provide a reconstruction formula for the measure of closed rectangles in $\mathbb{R}^d$ using wavelet transforms. We have included supporting examples to substantiate these assumptions.

Functional Analysis.title: The dimension-free threshold for maximal sections of $\ell_p$
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove the existence of a sharp threshold $p_0 \approx 26.265\ldots$, such that for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p\geq p_0$, the volume maximizing section of the unit ball of $\ell_p^n$ is the section with Ball's hyperplane $(\frac{e_1+e_2}{\sqrt{2}})^\perp$, whereas for $p\in(2,p_0)$ the asymptotic maximizer as the ambient dimension $n\to\infty$ is the hyperplane orthogonal to the diagonal vector $\frac{e_1+\cdots+e_n}{\sqrt{n}}$.

Functional Analysis.title: Holomorphic calculus on $L^p(\ell^q)$ I: optimal angles
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $L$ generate a symmetric contraction semigroup. We prove a holomorphic Hörmander calculus on $L^p(X;\ell^q)$ at the optimal angle $\max\{\arcsin|1-2/p|,\arcsin|1-2/q|\}$, with boundary Sobolev order $s>3$.

Functional Analysis.title: Löwner equations and de Branges--Rovnyak spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We study one-parameter families of de Branges--Rovnyak spaces associated with Löwner equations. The purpose of this paper is to give a new approach to a problem discussed by Sarason, Fricain--Hartmann--Ross, Fricain--Mashreghi, and Łanucha--Nowak. Our approach is based on a little-known technique, ``\textit{Löwner expansions}'', developed by the de Branges school. We recast ``\textit{Löwner expansions}'' in the theory of direct integrals and integral operators. Further, our framework also provides a natural setting for applying the theory of the chordal Löwner equation to the theory of de Branges--Rovnyak spaces. As an application, we prove Fourier-type expansion theorems induced by the Löwner equations.

Functional Analysis.title: Non-symmetric integral geometry: alternative reconstruction procedure with dual Radon transform
Functional Analysis.summary: In the note, we use the principles of non-symmetric integral geometry (non-integral geometry), related to the non-symmetric restricted integration measure, to extend the well-known relations traced from the Fourier slice theorem and the dual Radon transform. The proposed generalization is a very useful for the alternative restoration of the outset function. The latter impacts entirely on the image reconstruction process. The derived relations confirm the complexity of the inversion operator thanks for the symmetry breaking of integration measure.

Functional Analysis.title: Compressions of Linear Relations in Krein Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: Given an orthogonal decomposition \(\widetilde{\mathfrak{H}} = \mathfrak{H}[\dotplus]\widehat{\mathfrak{H}}\) of a Krein space, we study compressions \({\mathrm{C}_{\mathfrak H}}(R)\) of linear relations \(R\) in \(\widetilde{\mathfrak{H}}\) to \(\mathfrak{H}\). We formulate a sufficient condition that ensures that compression commutes with taking adjoints, that is, the adjoint identity \({\mathrm{C}_{\mathfrak H}}(R^{\widetilde{*}}) = {\mathrm{C}_{\mathfrak H}}(R)^{*}\) holds. We derive preservation and reflection results for the compression of maximal dissipative, maximal symmetric, and self-adjoint linear relations. For nonnegative linear relations, the adjoint identity also implies that compression commutes with taking the Friedrichs extension. For \(\mathfrak{H}\ne\{0\}\), we characterize finite dimensionality of the exit space \(\widehat{\mathfrak{H}}\) by universal compression properties. Finally, we give a criterion for the adjoint identity to hold in terms of bounded linear functionals on \(R\).

Functional Analysis.title: Optimal Sobolev embeddings for generalized Lorentz-Zygmund spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: This work deals with embeddings, of any integer order, for generalized Lorentz-Zygmund-Sobolev spaces on Euclidean domains satisfying minimal regularity assumptions. Explicit rearrangement-invariant, Hölder, Morrey and Campanato optimal target spaces are exhibited.

Functional Analysis.title: Extensions of operators between ordered vector spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove analogues of several classical theorems about operators between vector lattices in the context of directed Archimedean ordered vector spaces. In particular, we show that every order continuous operator between pervasive Archimedean ordered vector spaces can be extended to an order continuous operator between their Dedekind completions. Additionally, we introduce the universal completion of a directed Archimedean ordered vector space, and show that every supremum-preserving operator between directed Archimedean ordered vector spaces can be extended to an order continuous homomorphism between their universal completions. We also establish some universal properties for the relative uniform completion.

Functional Analysis.title: Operator space theory from the maximal viewpoint
Functional Analysis.summary: We initiate a theory of ``operator spaces" (in other words subspaces of $C^*$-algebras) with an emphasis on the maximal tensor product. The natural morphisms become the maximally bounded maps instead of the completely bounded ones. With this new looking glass we first examine various issues : lifting and extension properties, local reflexivity, inner derivations, similarity problems.This first part is semi-expository while the second one focuses on the class of von Neumann algebras $M$ such that any completely bounded unital homomorphism on a $C^*$-algebra with values in $M$ is maximally bounded (or equivalently is similar to a $*$-homomorphism via a similarity belonging to $M$). We show that this holds if and only if $M$ is the direct sum of a finite von Neumann algebra and an injective one. This also characterizes the $M$'s such that all completely bounded derivations into $M$ are inner. Our main tool for this is a new characterization of injective von Neumann algebras.

Functional Analysis.title: Fractional Fefferman--Stein inequalities on infinite rooted $k$-ary trees
Functional Analysis.summary:
We study weighted endpoint estimates for the centered fractional maximal operator on the infinite rooted $k$-ary tree, $T$. Our first result is a Fefferman--Stein type estimate \[ w\bigl(\{M_αf>λ\}\bigr) \lesssim_{α,s} \frac1λ\sum_{x\in T}|f(x)|M_{α,s}w(x), \qquad s>1, \] with a constant independent of the branching parameter $k$. Although the proof is inspired by the non-fractional argument of Ombrosi, Rivera-Ríos and Safe in \cite{ORRS}, the fractional normalization introduces a genuinely new scale interaction. At radius $r$, one must renormalize the function by $k^{rα}$ while keeping the dyadic cutoff at $k^r$; this leads to a new summation mechanism involving simultaneously $k^{rα}$ and $k^{r(1-α)}$.
  We then study sharpness and the geometry of admissible weights. We construct counterexamples showing that the estimate cannot in general be reduced to $s=1$ for any $0<α<1$. In the subcritical range $0<α<1/2$, we characterize power-type radial weights satisfying the natural fractional $A_1$ condition and prove that the failure persists after any fixed finite number of iterations of $M_α$. We also prove that $M_αw\lesssim w$ is necessary for the corresponding weighted weak type estimate but is not sufficient in the subcritical range. Finally, we identify a phase transition: for $1/2\leα<1$ no nonzero global weight can satisfy $M_αw\lesssim w$.

Functional Analysis.title: Fejer-Riesz factorization for free products
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish an operator-valued Fejer-Riesz factorization theorem for the algebraic free product A of C[F], the group algebra on the free group F on finitely many generators, with finitely many finite dimensional C-star algebras. With respect to a natural reduced-word length, called extent, we show that every linear combination F of elements of A with coefficients from the algebra of operators on a Hilbert space of extent at most 2d that is positive under all finite-dimensional unital *-representations of A admits a factorization F=B^*B with B of extent at most d. This sharp half-extent bound holds without strict positivity. The proof combines a new finite-dimensional realization theorem for positive truncated kernels with operator-system methods. We also establish factorization results for tensor products with group algebras of arbitrary discrete groups under strict positivity in the maximal C-star-tensor product; for amenable groups, strict positivity in the minimal tensor product suffices.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global Two-Sided Estimates for Time-Fractional Diffusion Kernels on Hyperbolic Space
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study time-fractional diffusion on real hyperbolic space $\mathbb H^n$, $n\ge2$, with Caputo order $0<α<1$. We establish global two-sided pointwise estimates for the homogeneous fundamental kernel $Z_{\mathbb H}(t,r)$ and the inhomogeneous (Duhamel) kernel $Y_{\mathbb H}(t,r)$, uniformly over all $t>0$ and positive geodesic distances $r$. By combining inverse-stable subordination with global bounds for the hyperbolic heat kernel, we distinguish a short-time local regime, a large-time interior region, and an exterior region governed by a saddle-point problem with parameter $r/t$. Both kernels have the same exterior exponential rate, while their amplitudes are related by an explicit saddle-point factor. The estimates are uniformly comparable on the interfaces between regimes, recover the Euclidean time-fractional singularities at small scales, and identify the influence of hyperbolic geometry on large-scale decay. The kernel $Z_{\mathbb H}$ also describes the one-time marginal density of hyperbolic Brownian motion under an independent inverse stable clock. This representation yields a radial limit law, moment and quantile asymptotics, and a change in the mean square displacement from order $t^α$ at small times to order $t^{2α}$ at large times.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Unconditional Uniqueness of KdV and mKdV Green Solutions at Low Regularity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove unconditional uniqueness for the Korteweg--de Vries (KdV) equation in $C_tH^{-1}_x(\mathbb R)$ and the real defocusing modified KdV equation in $C_tL^2_x(\mathbb R)$ within the class of Green solutions, an intrinsically well defined solution notion that encodes the evolution at these low regularities through the diagonal Green functions of the associated Lax operators. A key contribution is automatic local smoothing: the Green identities imply $q\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for KdV and $u_x,u^2\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for mKdV in spacetime, with estimates uniform over spatial translates. The uniqueness results therefore identify every Green solution in these classes with the continuous extension of the corresponding Schwartz flow.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Large-Time Behavior and Asymptotic Profiles for Time-Fractional Nonlinear Diffusion Equations via Entropy Methods
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the large-time behavior of nonnegative solutions to the time-fractional nonlinear diffusion equation $\partial_t^α(u-u_0) = Δu^m$, $0<α<1$, $m>0$, in a bounded domain with the homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. We prove that the rescaled solution $t^{\fracα{m}}u$ converges as $t\to\infty$ to an asymptotic profile $S$ characterized by $-ΔS^m = u_0/Γ(1-α)$. Moreover, we show that $t^αu^m$ converges to $S^m$, which admits an explicit representation in terms of the Green function and the initial datum. In contrast to the classical case $α=1$, the asymptotic profile depends explicitly on the initial datum.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Mixing times for the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We review quantitative results on the convergence to equilibrium of the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation, $p>1$, on a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with additive, possibly degenerate Wiener noise. From these results we derive upper bounds on $\varepsilon$-mixing times in different distances, depending on the initial data. We show that the Wasserstein distance to equilibrium is non-increasing in time and that, for $p>\frac{2d}{d+2}$, the invariant measure has moments of all orders. For $1<p<2$ with $p>\frac{2d}{d+2}$ and possibly degenerate noise, the $\varepsilon$-mixing times in every Wasserstein distance $\mathcal{W}_r$, $r\ge1$, are $O(\varepsilon^{-δ})$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow 0$ for every $δ>0$. Two tables collect the convergence rates and the mixing-time bounds.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Mass-lumped finite elements with maximum-bound preservation and original-energy dissipation for the degenerate-mobility Allen-Cahn equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this work, we propose a mass-lumped finite element method for the Allen-Cahn equation that incorporates nonlinear mobility which may degenerate. The spatial approximation uses continuous, piecewise linear, mass-lumped finite elements, while convex splitting is employed for the double-well potential in time. Under the standard non-obtuse mesh condition, it is shown that the resulting fully discrete method preserves the maximum-bound principle unconditionally: if the initial approximation takes values in $[-1, 1]$, then so does the numerical solution at every time level. Additionally, the method dissipates the original discrete Ginzburg-Landau energy without any time-step restriction, even when the mobility vanishes at pure phases. This analysis relies on the monotonicity of the lumped finite element operator and the convexity of the split potential. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical properties and demonstrate the robustness of the method in phase-separation dynamics involving degenerate mobility.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Radial reductions of variable exponent Laplacian equations on warped products with compact symmetry
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study nonlinear elliptic equations of variable exponent type, \[ -Δ_{q(x)}u+|u|^{q(x)-2}u=f(x,u), \] on non-compact Riemannian manifolds with symmetry. We consider complete warped products \[ M=\mathcal R\times_φY,\qquad g_φ=dr^2\oplusφ(r)^2g_Y, \] where $\mathcal R$ is a non-compact interval, possibly with boundary, and $Y$ is a compact homogeneous manifold. We establish sufficient conditions on the warping function ensuring a Ricci lower bound, a uniform non-collapsing volume condition, and the orbit-growth hypothesis of the abstract existence theorem proved in \cite{JFA}. We also obtain comparison bounds for the admissible warping functions.
  We analyze the corresponding radial equations for the admissible exponential and linear models $φ(r)=e^{ar}$ and $φ(r)=ar$, with $r\geq r_0>0$. For a constant diffusion exponent $q=k$, we consider explicit decaying profiles $u=φ^{-σ}$, which belong to $L_1^k(M)$ provided $σk>\dim Y$ in the exponential case and $σk>\dim Y+1$ in the linear case. Under additional explicit parameter restrictions, these profiles solve a resonant equation with a positive bounded coefficient, a construction distinct from the superlinear regime of the abstract existence theorem. Finally, we establish logarithmic reductions for constant and variable radial exponents, and justify the passage from radial identities to weak formulations against arbitrary compactly supported interior test functions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the Principal Eigenvalue of the $(p,A)$-Laplacian with Sign-Changing Morrey Potentials: Complete Continuity, Optimization, and Differentiability
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We establish a unified framework to study the continuity and complete continuity of the principal eigenvalue functional $λ_1(V,m)$ associated with the following $(p,A)$-Laplacian operator involving both sign-changing potential $V$, and positive weight $m$ in a Morrey space: \begin{align*}
  -Δ_{p,A}(u) + V|u|^{p-2}u &= λm|u|^{p-2}u \quad \text{in}\,\, Ω,
  u &= 0 \quad\quad\quad \quad\quad \text{on}\,\, \partialΩ,
  \end{align*} where $1<p<N$, $λ\in\mathbb{R}$ is a parameter, and $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^N (N \geq 2)$ is a bounded domain with boundary $\partial Ω$. As a consequence, we investigate the existence and uniqueness of optimal principal eigenvalues $λ_1(V,m)$ over a weakly compact subset of the Morrey space. Finally, we derive a formula for the derivative of $λ_1(V,m)$ with respect to regular perturbations of potential $V$, and positive weight $m$ within a closed subspace of Morrey space.
  Our results develop analytic tools to overcome the lack of separability and reflexivity in Morrey spaces to investigate this eigenvalue problem. In particular, the study is new even for the linear case $p=2$. We also emphasize that the tools established are applicable for a wide class of PDEs with coefficients in Morrey spaces.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The variational formulation of the follow-the-leader model
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We provide a variational formulation of a finite-dimensional Follow-the-Leader system through a minimizing-movement scheme based on a discrete transport distance with nonlinear mobility. Despite the degeneracy of the kinetic action at maximal density, we prove finiteness of the distance, $C^1$ regularity of geodesics, and suitable Euler--Lagrange relations. For a decreasing external potential, we show that the JKO scheme yields an approximate implicit Euler discretization of the Follow-the-Leader dynamics. Consequently, as $τ\to0^+$, the piecewise affine interpolations converge, up to a subsequence, to a $C^1$ solution of the continuous Follow-the-Leader system. This complements the many-particle convergence theory for the discrete nonlinear-mobility transport distance by establishing the continuous-time limit at fixed number of particles.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Finding geometric criteria for negative eigenvalues of the Neumann--Poincaré operator
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Motivated by a question of Grigori Rozenblum, we study how the geometry of the boundary of a convex domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ affects whether the Neumann--Poincaré operator on $\partialΩ$ has negative eigenvalues. First, we show that a flat face on the boundary of a bounded, convex Lipschitz domain produces an infinite-dimensional negative spectral subspace. For convex domains with $C^{1,α}$ boundary, we bound the number of negative eigenvalues from below by the Dirichlet eigenvalue counting function of a projected patch over which the chords are sufficiently short. A Rellich identity gives a sufficient condition on a defining function to exclude negative eigenvalues. We also report numerical computations, which led us to the theoretical results.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Seifert type magnetohydrostatic equilibria in rotationally symmetric toroidal domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct magnetohydrostatic equilibria in rotationally symmetric toroidal domains whose magnetic lines define an $(m,n)$ Seifert fibration for arbitrary coprime integers $m,n$.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 12 pages. The existence result was upgraded to smooth solutions

Analysis of PDEs.title: A generalisation of the Gagliardo--Nirenberg Inequality with applications to mass-critical and mass-subcritical elliptic equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Via a new inequality à la Gagliardo--Nirenberg, we prove the existence and nonexistence of solutions to \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} (-Δ)^s u + \fracμ{|y|^{2s}} u + λu = f(u), \quad \mathbb{R}^N \ni x = (y,z) \in \mathbb{R}^K \times \mathbb{R}^{N-K}, \\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} u^2 \, \mathrm{d}x = ρ\end{cases} \end{equation*} in the mass-critical and mass-subcritical regimes, where $s>0$, $N \ge K \ge 2$, $μ\in \mathbb{R}$ belongs to a specific range, $ρ>0$ is given a priori, and $λ\in \mathbb{R}$ is unknown. Additionally, we obtain similar results for the problem above with $μ=0$ and $N \ge 1$ as well as a related curl-curl equation. Finally, we provide a thorough insight into the threshold for $ρ$ that divides the scenarios of negative and zero least energy.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 31 pages, to appear in Ann. Mat. Pura Appl.; comments are welcome

Analysis of PDEs.title: Free energy Wasserstein gradient flow and their particle counterparts: toy model, (degenerate) PL inequalities and exit times
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
In finite dimension, the long-time and metastable behavior of a gradient flow perturbated by a small Brownian noise is well understood. A similar situation arises when a Wasserstein gradient flow over a space of probability measure is approximated by a system of mean-field interacting particles, but classical results do not apply in these infinite-dimensional settings. We are concerned with the situation where the objective function of the optimization problem contains an entropic penalization, so that the particle system is a Langevin diffusion process.
  The work has two parts: the first and main one is devoted to the general study of a very simple class of models, for which the infinite-dimensional behavior is fully characterized by an autonomous diffusion process at fixed finite dimension. On the one hand, we prove the equivalence between fast convergence for the mean-field gradient flow and for the particle system in terms of functional inequalities (log-Sobolev, Polyak-Łojasiewicz, Talagrand and variants thereof) including the degenerate polynomial case occurring at phase transitions, and on the other hand we characterise the metastable behavior in terms of transition time between local minimiser -- establishing an Eyring-Kramers formula -- and of exit time from unstable critical points.
  In a second part, motivated by and building on the systematic study of the toy models, we consider the continuous Curie-Weiss model in a symmetric double-well potential, exactly at the critical temperature. We show that, although the $N$-particle Gibbs measure does not satisfy a uniform-in-$N$ standard log-Sobolev inequality (the optimal constant growing like $\sqrt{N}$), it does satisfy a more general Łojasiewicz inequality uniformly in $N$, inducing uniform polynomial long-time convergence rates, propagation of chaos at stationarity and uniformly in time, and creation of chaos.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Generalized and Classical Harnack Inequalities for semilinear equations on Carnot Groups
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove generalized and classical Harnack inequalities for non-negative smooth solutions of divergence-form semilinear subelliptic equations on Carnot groups. The proof combines smooth horizontal Gauss--Green and coarea formulas, energy estimates for level sets, a Vitali covering argument, and a horizontal Keller--Osserman barrier. The companion paper, Reference [10], develops the geometric foundations and extends the estimates to weak solutions with nonsmooth data.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 74 pages. The companion paper [10] can be found at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24013096

Analysis of PDEs.title: Regularity of planar Griffith minimizers with connected cracks through a monotonicity formula
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove a new monotonicity formula for the two-dimensional Neumann elasticity equation with connected boundary. From this we deduce a regularity result for two-dimensional minimizers of the Griffith energy with connected crack set: the crack may be partitioned into regular points, triple junctions, and cracktips. We give a classification of the global minimizers of the Griffith energy with connected crack set. Finally, we discuss some consequences of the monotonicity formula on the evolution of the stress intensity factors along a crack, which may present independent interest.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The BCC lattice is the optimal 3D lattice quantizer for all $p\geq1$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For every finite $p\ge1$, the body-centered cubic lattice uniquely minimizes the $p$th moment of the Voronoi cell among three-dimensional lattices of covolume one, up to orthogonal transformations. This proves the Graf--Luschgy conjecture for three-dimensional lattice quantizers (\cite{GL}).

Analysis of PDEs.title: Angular Besov Refinement of the Spherical Stein--Tomas Theorem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The spherical Stein--Tomas inequality maps $L^2(\mathbb S^2)$ into $L^4(\mathbb R^3)$. We study its refinement in which the angular input is measured by the strictly weaker Besov norm $B^0_{2,4}(\mathbb S^2)$. The central separated-band inequality bounds the squared $L^2$ norm of the product of extensions from degrees $L\ll K$ by $C(L/K)$ times the squared input norms. An exact spherical-Hankel expansion controls the far field, while angular-momentum leakage and transversality handle the Fresnel region. We construct scale-separated, normalized angular bands for which the extension norm is equivalent to the $\ell^4$ norm of the coefficients. This proves that the fourth-power summation is optimal and quantitatively distinguishes the result from the classical $\ell^2$ summation. As an application, small angular Besov data generate small $L^4$ solutions to the cubic nonlinear Helmholtz equation in $\mathbb R^3$, with a smallness condition that remains sharp on multiscale data even when their $L^2$ norm is arbitrarily large or infinite. The associated on-shell nonlinear scattering amplitude has improved angular $B^0_{2,4/3}$ regularity, and its leading cubic term is quantitatively decoupled across widely separated angular bands.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharper energy scaling bounds of the singularly perturbed Tartar square
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this article, we discuss the scaling behaviour of the singularly perturbed Tartar square, revisiting the results by [Rüland-Tribuzio '22]. Therein, it was proven that both lower and upper bounds satisfy a behaviour of the same type, up to a small mismatch of logarithmic powers. We show by an improvement of the ansatz free lower bound that the logarithmic powers indeed match and that the bounds are of order $\exp( - C \log(\varepsilon^{-1})^{1/2} )$ for suitable constants $C = C_{\rm low}$ and $C = C_{\rm upp}$, where $\varepsilon$ denotes the singular perturbation parameter. More specifically, the bootstrap argument in the Fourier space is refined by resorting to Fourier multipliers enjoying $L^\infty$-bounds which are constructed via de la Vallée Poussin kernels. Regarding upper bounds, we perform iterated branching constructions sharpening the upper bound of [Winter '97] which resorted to an iteration of laminates as a competitor. Eventually, the mismatch of upper and lower bound is quantified, and for quadratic energies we obtain the bounds $C_{\rm low} \leq 7.0339$ and $C_{\rm upp} \geq 2 \log(2) - ν$ for any $ν>0$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonlinear stability of planar contact waves for the 3-D compressible Navier--Stokes equations in the whole space
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove the global nonlinear stability of small planar contact waves for the three-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations in $\R^3$ under general $H^4(\R^3)$ perturbations, without any $L^1$ integrability or zero-mass assumptions. Unlike the one-dimensional problem or the periodic channel, the problem in $\R^3$ admits neither a Poincaré inequality in the transverse directions nor a square-integrable anti-derivative. Our proof relies on three main ingredients: a perturbation around the one-dimensional Navier--Stokes solution starting from the smooth contact profile, a formulation of the low-order perturbation system in the velocity, pressure, and entropy variables with separate estimates for the velocity--pressure pair and the entropy, and the construction of characteristic and space-time Gaussian weight functions. Combining these weighted estimates with higher-order derivative bounds and homogeneous Gagliardo--Nirenberg interpolation yields global stability and algebraic $L^\infty$ decay rates in $\R^3$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Well-posedness of weak solutions for the time-dependent thermal-fluid-solid multiphysical coupled model
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper constructs a time-dependent thermal-fluid-solid multiphysical coupled model describing the interaction between a free fluid and a thermo-poroelastic medium and provides a rigorous mathematical analysis. The model consists of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations and the heat equation in the free-fluid region, together with the thermo-poroelasticity equations in the porous medium. The two regions are coupled on a fixed interface through conditions for normal velocity, tangential velocity, stress balance, temperature continuity, and heat flux continuity. Under a small-data assumption, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a weak solution for this fully dynamic nonlinear coupled system. The proof employs the Galerkin method to construct semi-discrete approximations, establishes uniform a priori estimates that enable the extension of local solutions to global ones, and invokes compactness arguments to pass to the limit, yielding a solution to the original coupled system.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Smooth Piecewise Cutting for Neural Operator to Handle Discontinuities and Sharp Transitions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Neural operators have achieved strong performance in learning solution operators of partial differential equations (PDEs), but their inherently continuous representations struggle to capture discontinuities and sharp transitions. Existing approaches typically approximate such features within continuous function spaces, often requiring increased model capacity and high-resolution data. In this work, we propose Cut-DeepONet, a two-stage training framework that explicitly models discontinuities while reducing learning complexity. Our approach reformulates the problem via a lifting strategy, partitioning the domain into smooth subregions while representing discontinuities as boundaries in a higher-dimensional space. This separation aligns the operator learning task with the inductive bias of neural networks and avoids directly approximating discontinuities. An additional network predicts input-dependent discontinuity locations for unseen inputs, which are then used to guide the neural operator in generating smooth components within each region. Experiments on benchmark PDEs show that Cut-DeepONet outperforms state-of-the-art methods, even when trained on low-resolution datasets. The method excels on problems with discontinuities and sharp transitions, while using fewer trainable parameters. Our results highlight the benefits of changing the representation of operator learning rather than increasing model complexity.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Duality for the Adversarial Total Variation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Adversarial training of binary classifiers can be reformulated as regularized risk minimization involving a nonlocal total variation. Building on this perspective, we establish a characterization of the subdifferential of this total variation using duality techniques. To achieve this, we derive a dual representation of the nonlocal total variation and a related integration-by-parts formula, involving a nonlocal gradient and divergence. We provide such duality statements both in the space of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on proper metric spaces and for the space of essentially bounded functions on separable metric spaces. Furthermore, under some additional conditions we provide characterizations of the subdifferential in these settings.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Isolated yet highly unstable 2D Euler equilibria
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct steady solutions of the two-dimensional Euler equations on smooth annular domains that are isolated, modulo scaling, in the $L^\infty$ vorticity topology. They are highly unstable: any Yudovich trajectory remaining sufficiently close to such an equilibrium on an open time interval is a stationary multiple of it and, moreover, at fixed energy, enstrophy and circulations, distinct nearby trajectories cannot return even weakly to the equilibrium. Further, on any non-circular annulus, we show that this kind of isolated, highly unstable equilibria occurs arbitrarily close in the Yudovich norm to smooth equilibria which are themselves non-isolated.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp isoperimetry in groups of polynomial growth
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study weighted edge boundary and outer vertex boundary on Cayley graphs of polynomial growth of degree $Q>1$. For every finite symmetric generating set, we prove that each exact isoperimetric profile satisfies $I(n)=c n^{(Q-1)/Q}+O(n^{(Q-1)/Q-β})$, where $β=1/(8Q^2)$. We identify the leading constant with the isoperimetric constant of a horizontal perimeter on the limiting Carnot group, after accounting for the counting density. Its integrand is a norm with polyhedral unit ball, determined by a convex minimization with one real variable for each coset of a torsion-free nilpotent subgroup. For every asymptotically minimizing sequence, we translate its vertex sets so that the characteristic functions of the associated rescaled regions are precompact in $L^1$. The limiting regions minimize continuum perimeter at fixed volume. The exact-cardinality estimate requires no regularity assumption on these regions. For virtually abelian groups, we prove a quantitative stability estimate using a discrete approximation to the Euclidean Wulff body. The relative symmetric difference from a translate is bounded by the square root of the sum of the relative boundary deficit and a cardinality error. We also characterize when bounded additive changes of Cayley metric preserve the leading vertex constant. Failure occurs already in rank two; we construct pairs with the same measured asymptotic cone whose leading constants have an unbounded ratio as the rank grows.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 28 pages, split off from arXiv:2509.22260v1. Comments most welcome!

Analysis of PDEs.title: Asymptotic behavior of solutions to the critical $p$-Laplace equation near isolated singularities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the asymptotic behavior of weak solutions to the following critical $p$-Laplace equation \[ -Δ_p u=u^{p^*-1}, \quad u\ge0 \quad\hbox{in }B_1\setminus\{0\}, \] where $Δ_pu=\diver(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u)$ is the classical $p$-Laplacian with $1<p<n$, $p^*=\frac{np}{n-p}$ is the Sobolev critical exponent and $B_1\setminus\{0\}\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is the punctured unit ball. We develop a nonlinear potential-theoretic method to establish sharp upper bounds for solutions, without using the method of moving planes or moving spheres. Furthermore, we use Steiner symmetrization to study the radial symmetry of global singular solutions, and thereby classify all Fowler singular solutions. Finally, we prove that every local singular solution is asymptotic to a global Fowler singular solution.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Trace and Regularized Index of Callias Operators on Hyperbolic Space
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $d \geq 3$ be odd. On hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^d$, we consider Callias-type operators, i.e. Dirac-Schrödinger operators of the form $D = ic \nabla + A$, where $c \nabla$ is the Dirac operator and $A$ a function with values in the self-adjoint operators, and provide an explicit formula for the iterated trace $\text{tr}_{L^2(\mathbb{H}^d,H)} \text{tr}_{S}( e^{-tD^*D} - e^{-tDD^*})$, $t>0$, that appears in the formulation of the Witten index. Thereby, the operator $D$ is not assumed to be Fredholm.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp Convergence to the Half-Space for Mullins-Sekerka in the Plane
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We revisit the HED Method for the Mullins-Sekerka evolution in the plane. We identify a natural notion of distance, intrinsic to the interface itself. Using this distance, the energy, and the dissipation, we develop natural assumptions on the flow and, assuming existence of a solution satisfying these conditions, obtain not just the algebraic rate (already previously derived by Chugreeva, Otto, and M.G. Westdickenberg) but also the sharp leading order constant for the convergence to the flat limiting interface. To carry this out, we introduce a lemma that obtains optimal algebraic decay behavior (rate and prefactor) from given variational information.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Added Lemma 1.4, which yields the sharp leading order constant in the decay estimate

Analysis of PDEs.title: Kolmogorov Obstacle Problems: Euclidean Free Boundary Regularity under a Cone Condition
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study obstacle problems for Kolmogorov-type operators that diffuse in one variable and transport in another. Such problems describe American options on running averages. Under a cone estimate, a strong monotonicity condition on the solution in the diffusive direction, we show that the free boundary is a graph in the diffusive direction with Hölder continuous first derivatives in the Euclidean sense, and that every free boundary point is regular. The key observation is that a Euclidean Lipschitz free boundary is flat at the intrinsic scale. For the American fixed-strike Asian option we verify the cone estimate, so that its exercise boundary has the same regularity.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Self-similar solutions for the gSQG patch equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The inviscid generalized surface quasi-geostrophic (gSQG) equations are a family of active scalar equations parametrized by a scalar $α$ that includes the two-dimensional Euler equations ($α= 0)$ and the SQG equation $(α= 1)$. We prove that, for every $α\in (\frac{7}{4}, 2)$ and every $T > 0$, there exists a self-similar patch solution whose boundary is a smooth, unbounded graph for $0 \leq t < T$ and develops a corner singularity at time $T$. The proof has been formally verified in Lean 4.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 81 pages, added a Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem

Analysis of PDEs.title: Regularity for fully nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with strong absorption
Feynman-Kac Representation and the Asymptotic Speed of the Fisher-KPP Equation with Finite-Activity Jump Noise
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the asymptotic propagation speed of travelling wave solutions to the stochastic Fisher--KPP equation with multiplicative finite-activity pure jump Lévy noise, i.e.\ a compensated Poisson random measure of finite intensity, so that the solution evolves deterministically between successive jumps and jumps multiplicatively at the event times.
  Our main contribution is a stochastic Feynman--Kac representation for the solution, which expresses the random field as the product of the exponential martingale of the jump noise and an expectation over the paths of an independent Brownian motion. The representation converts the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation into an expectation problem, allowing a direct analysis of the front position.
  Building on this representation, we derive sharp upper and lower bounds for the propagation of the front: for every speed $c>2\sqrt{1+a}$ the solution decays exponentially along the ray $x=ct$, while for every speed $c<2\sqrt{1+a}$ it does not. The two together identify the asymptotic speed in the critical-speed sense: the threshold between exponentially decaying and non-decaying fronts equals $2\sqrt{1+a}$ almost surely, an identity proved without any a priori existence of the limit $R_δ(t)/t$. The complementary bounds $2\sqrt{\underlineγ}\le c\le2\sqrt{\overlineγ}$ also hold, with $\overlineγ,\underlineγ$ explicit in $ε$ and $μ$.
  Under the finite-activity assumption, a stopping-time iteration yields pathwise $L^\infty$ bounds and finite-speed propagation of the level sets of the front, which underlie the existence of a travelling wave profile. The framework extends naturally to multi-species cooperative systems, and numerical simulations illustrate the informativeness of the speed bounds.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Fundamental solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplacian in cone-like domains, with applications to Liouville-type theorems and global Hölder regularity
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
Let $ C_ω$ be the cone generated by a proper $C^2$ domain $ω\subset\mathbb S^{N-1}$. We study positive homogeneous solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplace equation in $C_ω$ with zero exterior values. For $p\ne2$, the operator is nonlinear and not uniformly elliptic. For every $p>1$, we identify two extremal homogeneities $β^+>0>β^-$, prove that every fundamental solution, if one exists, has one of these exponents, and construct homogeneous eigenfunctions whose eigenvalues have signs determined by the position of the homogeneity relative to $β^\pm$.
  As an application, we obtain the Lane-Emden threshold $q^*=p-1+sp/β^+$ for every $p>1$: nontrivial nonnegative supersolutions of $(-Δ_p)^s u\ge u^q$ in $C_ω$ do not exist for $0<q<q^*$, whereas homogeneous supersolutions exist for $q>q^*$. We also establish Hopf-type lower bounds at conical boundary points with the optimal exponent. When $p-1>sp$ , we construct both fundamental solutions, one singular at the vertex and the other vanishing there. For $p=2$, these solutions are known; our method recovers them for every $s\in(0,1)$.
  The homogeneous eigenfunctions also serve as barriers, yielding boundary decay and global Hölder regularity for $(-Δ_p)^s u=f$ in bounded Lipschitz domains, with zero exterior values and $f$ continuous up to the boundary. The admissible Hölder exponents are determined by the exterior cones. All results hold for every $N\ge2$; in particular, $N>sp$ is not needed.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Corrected minor typographical and grammatical errors, and improved the organisation and clarity of the exposition. The main results and mathematical arguments remain unchanged

Analysis of PDEs.title: Single-scale regularity from Dirichlet energy for the five-dimensional stationary Navier--Stokes equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish an interior $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion for suitable weak solutions of the unforced stationary Navier--Stokes equations in an open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^5$. There exists a universal constant $\varepsilon_\ast>0$ such that $x_0$ is regular if, for some ball $B_R(x_0)\subsetΩ$ with $R>0$, \[ \frac1R\int_{B_R(x_0)}|\nabla u|^2\,dx \leq \varepsilon_\ast^2. \] The main difficulty is that the Dirichlet energy controls the velocity oscillation while its mean may be arbitrarily large. Subtracting the mean introduces a large constant drift into the perturbation equation. Moreover, smallness in $H^1$ alone is insufficient to close a direct nonlinear elliptic estimate in five dimensions. We overcome these difficulties through uniform Oseen estimates and a relative-energy comparison yielding quadratic improvement of the perturbation. As a consequence, the singular set has zero one-dimensional upper Minkowski content on every compact subset of $Ω$, and hence local upper Minkowski dimension at most one.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundary-layer separation beyond the square-root law
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We construct solutions to the two-dimensional stationary Prandtl system under a constant adverse pressure gradient exhibiting a family of distinct separation laws. More precisely, for every integer $\ell\ge1$, we construct smooth initial data for which separation occurs at a finite location $x=x^\ast$, with
  \[
  \partial_y u(x,0)
  =\mathbf C_\ell(x^\ast-x)^{\ell/2}\bigl(1+o(1)\bigr),
  \qquad x\uparrow x^\ast,
  \]
  where $\mathbf C_\ell>0$ depends on the initial data. We determine the local asymptotic structure of the solution near separation through matched inner and outer expansions based on linearization around the ground state in von Mises variables. This description addresses Open Problem~5 proposed by Oleinik and Samokhin~\cite{OleinikSamok-book-99}. We prove the nonlinear stability of the square-root separation law ($\ell=1$) under small admissible perturbations of the initial data in a suitable topology.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundary singularities for the Lane-Emden equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For every $n\ge3$ and $(n+1)/(n-1)<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, we construct positive solutions of $Δu+u^p=0$ in the half-space with zero Dirichlet data away from the origin, the homogeneous singular profile there, and Poisson-kernel decay at infinity, resolving a question of del Pino--Musso--Pacard. Under a weighted non-degeneracy condition, these half-space solutions serve as building blocks for positive very weak solutions in smooth bounded domains, singular along prescribed compact smooth boundary submanifolds of normal dimension $n$. We verify non-degeneracy in the initial stable interval and at and just beyond its threshold when this lies below $(n+2)/(n-2)$. For isolated boundary singularities, the construction applies throughout the strict subcritical interval outside a locally finite exceptional set.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundary integral methods and shape reconstruction for periodic fluid--solid interfaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper studies direct scattering by periodic fluid--solid interfaces and interface reconstruction from multifrequency near-field data. Using Helmholtz decomposition and quasi-periodic single-layer potentials, we formulate a coupled boundary integral system with the standard stress traction, establish its equivalence to the original fluid--solid transmission problem under suitable assumptions, and construct a corresponding Nyström discretization. For near-field observations at finitely many measurement points, we establish local Fréchet differentiability of the observation map with a quadratic remainder estimate. In the smooth setting, the derivative transmission problem and its boundary integral formulation are used to compute the observation Jacobian required for interface reconstruction. The interface is reconstructed by regularized Gauss--Newton iteration in a Fourier space that is progressively enriched as the frequency increases. Numerical experiments assess direct-solver accuracy and reconstruction performance for different interfaces, material configurations, and noise levels.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Dynamics of subcritical threshold solutions for the three-dimensional energy-critical NLS
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We extend the radial threshold classification of Duyckaerts and Merle on the lower kinetic branch to nonradial solutions of the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation in \(\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)\). At the ground state energy and with initial gradient norm strictly below that of the ground state, every solution is global and either scatters in both time directions or is a symmetry transform of the special solution \(W^-\), possibly after conjugate time reversal. The proof combines Su and Zhao's below-threshold scattering theorem with a coercivity estimate for the interaction form at threshold under a kinetic gap and a local analysis near the ground state orbit.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Positive self-similar solutions of a parabolic equation with spatially weighted absorption in a half-space
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study positive solutions of $u_t-Δu+x_1^{2α}|u|^{q-1}u=0$ in the half-space $\{x_1>0\}$, with $α>-1$ and $q>1$, vanishing on $\{x_1=0\}$ and at $t=0$ away from the origin. Let $q_c=(N+3+2α)/(N+1)$. For $1<q<q_c$ we prove that there is exactly one positive self-similar solution continuous away from the origin, and that its profile satisfies Gaussian bounds that are sharp up to multiplicative constants. For $q\ge q_c$ there is none. We also show that, after removing the Gaussian factor, the profile has an angular limit shape $Φ$ in every mode, give an integral formula for its Kummer coefficients, prove that $Φ$ is real-analytic and is the uniform limit of the rescaled profiles, that $Φ/(η_1/|η|)$ is monotone along meridians, and that $Φ$ is proportional to $η_1/|η|$ if and only if $2α+q=1$. Every self-similar solution of finite energy, or continuous away from the origin, is dominated in absolute value by the positive one, and for $(N+4+2α)/(N+2)\le q<q_c$ the only nontrivial ones are $\pm u_s$. For $α=0$ existence, uniqueness and the upper bound are due to Marcus and Véron; the lower bound with the sharp exponent and the description of $Φ$ are new also in that case. The existence and uniqueness proofs use a Brezis--Oswald type comparison principle and explicit barriers, given by explicit formulas; the analysis of $Φ$ uses Kummer functions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the optimal mass threshold for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel system coupled to the Navier-Stokes equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We investigate the mass threshold for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel system coupled with the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. In the absence of fluid interaction, the classical Keller-Segel system admits a well-known $4π$-critical-mass dichotomy: for every suitably regular initial datum of total mass \(m<4π\), the associated no-flux initial-boundary value problem admits a global bounded classical solution, whereas for \(m>4π\), there exist smooth initial configurations of mass $m$ such that the associated solution blows up in finite or infinite time. For the fluid-coupled system, Winkler first established global generalized solvability under the condition \(m<2π\) and proposed an open question whether the fluid action may lower the critical blow-up mass to some value lying between $2π$ and $4π$.
  In the present work, we resolve this open problem and show that the presence of the fluid does not alter the critical mass threshold, and the entire classical subcritical regime remains intact: every admissible initial datum with total mass \(m<4π\) generates a unique global classical solution that is uniformly bounded with respect to time.
  Our proof relies on the construction of a new quasi-energy inequality. The key underlying observation is that combining relative isoperimetric estimates with rearrangement techniques yields a Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality on bounded planar domains with an explicit leading constant.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Maximizing Reaction via Spatial Localization: The Reaction-Flux Landscape and Maximizing Sequences
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We continue our study of a PDE-constrained variational model for maximizing the total reaction flux by optimizing the spatial distribution of catalytic materials, such as enzymes. The total amount of enzyme is fixed, and the substrate concentration is governed by a reaction-diffusion equation with prescribed boundary values. We consider both linear and nonlinear Michaelis-Menten reaction kinetics. In previous work, we constructed a maximizing sequence, computed the first and second variations of the reaction functional, and established the nonexistence of local maximizers. Here, we conduct a more comprehensive analysis. We prove that the functional is strictly concave for linear kinetics but need not be concave or convex for nonlinear kinetics. We also show that no critical points exist. We then characterize maximizing sequences and identify all their possible limiting measures. Our analysis reveals the mechanism of reaction maximization through spatial localization: maximizing sequences concentrate enzymes near the portion of the boundary where the substrate concentration is largest. Moreover, the landscape of the functional defining the total reaction differs between the linear and nonlinear cases, a point less emphasized in applications. Consistent with existing biophysical studies, these findings motivate the development and analysis of regularized models.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the regularity of entropy solutions to stochastic degenerate parabolic equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the regularity of entropy solutions for quasilinear parabolic equations with anisotropic degeneracy and stochastic forcing. Building on previous works, we establish space-time regularity under a non-degeneracy condition that does not require an assumption on the derivative of the symbol of the corresponding kinetic equation, a restriction imposed in earlier studies. This allows us to obtain regularity results for certain equations not accounted for by prior theory, albeit with reduced regularity exponents. Our approach uses a kinetic formulation with two transport equations, one of second order and one of first order, leveraging a form of "parabolic regularity" inherent in these equations that was not utilized in previous studies.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Complete uniqueness for two-dimensional asymmetric incompressible jet flows
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Alt, Caffarelli and Friedman established the existence of two-dimensional asymmetric incompressible jet flows in [Asymmetric jet flows. Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 35, 29--68, 1982]. In their formulation, the constant fluid speed $λ$ on the free boundaries and the downstream asymptotic angle $θ$ are selected as part of the solution. In this paper, we prove that the asymmetric jet is unique for a prescribed nozzle and mass flux.
