We first establish the strict vertical monotonicity of the stream function $u$ and introduce the partial hodograph coordinates $ξ=x$ and $η=u(x,y)$, which map every fluid domain onto the same fixed strip. Under this framework, each jet is characterized by a height function $y=h(ξ,η)$, which determines the vertical position along the streamline $u=η$ at horizontal coordinate $ξ$. By analyzing the difference between the height functions of two candidate jets on this strip, we derive an elliptic equation with Dirichlet conditions on the fixed walls and conormal conditions on the free boundaries. Combining these mixed boundary conditions with the asymptotic behaviors, we first establish the uniqueness of the free-boundary fluid speed $λ$. For the resulting common speed, a local perturbation of the height function near a nozzle endpoint, together with the maximum principle, proves that the two height functions must coincide. Inverting the partial hodograph transformation then establishes the uniqueness of the physical jet.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Delaunay classification of positive singular solutions to the critical Lane--Emden system
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We classify positive classical solutions of the Lane--Emden system \begin{align*} \begin{cases}
  -Δu=v^p & ~~\text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\},\\
  -Δv=u^q &~~ \text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}, \end{cases}
  \end{align*} with a nonremovable singularity at $0$ (i.e., $\lim_{x\to0}u(x)=\lim_{x\to0}v(x)=+\infty$), where $n\ge3$ and $p,q>0$ satisfy \[
  \frac1{p+1}+\frac1{q+1}=\frac{n-2}{n}. \] Without additional growth or integrability assumptions, we establish radial symmetry about the origin, strict radial decrease, and global two-sided power bounds for both components. Furthermore, every such solution can be written as \[
  u(x)=|x|^{-α}U(\log|x|),\qquad
  v(x)=|x|^{-β}V(\log|x|), \] where $α=\frac{n}{q+1}$, $β=\frac{n}{p+1}$, and $(U,V)$ is either the positive equilibrium $(A,B)=((\fracαβ)^{\fracα{2}}, (\fracαβ)^{\fracβ{2}})$ or a positive nonconstant periodic solution of the associated Emden--Fowler system. These periodic solutions form a Delaunay family: for every $\varepsilon\in(0,A)$, there is a unique profile pair, up to translation in $t=\log|x|$, with $\min_{\mathbb{R}}U=\varepsilon$. The Hamiltonian energy provides an alternative parameter, decreasing continuously and strictly from zero to the equilibrium energy as $\varepsilon$ increases from $0$ to $A$. The common least period of the two components tends to infinity as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ and to the period of the linearized oscillation at $(A,B)$ as $\varepsilon\uparrow A$. The classification includes the case of a sublinear exponent.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Bottom-boundary identification using asymptotic observers in dispersive shallow-water models
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper we consider the problem of identifying the bottom-boundary of an ocean basin, particularly in the coastal region where shallow-water theory applies. Our main contribution is the development of an easy-to-implement observer-based approach of identifying the bottom-boundary profile from measurements of the free-surface. Furthermore, we prove that the true profile can be obtained by minimising the long-time observation-error as computed from the observer equations associated with a class of linear dispersive shallow water-wave models. Numerical simulations indicate the same optimisation problem can recover the true profile for the nonlinear versions of the same dispersive water-wave models.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Critical orthonormal Strichartz estimates for Lebesgue spaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates at the critical coefficient exponent $q/2$ for fractional Schrödinger propagators. The proof for $d\geq3$ combines annular Schatten estimates with a frequency summation argument based on potential duality and Littlewood--Paley theory. In dimension two, a trace computation supplies the annular estimate needed for the global estimate. We also construct a counterexample to the global estimate with spatial $L^\infty$ and coefficients in $\ell^{q/2}$, even with a weak time norm.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Version 2 adds more background introductions in Section 1. Version 2 also fixes few notations in the final section. No changes for math contents

Analysis of PDEs.title: Critical Resonance and the Radial Branch in Maz'ya's Weighted Hessian--Gradient Inequality
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the sharp constant $C(p,γ)$ in Maz'ya's planar weighted inequality \[
  \int_{\mathbb{R}^2}|\nablaψ|^p|x|^{p(γ-1)}\, \mathrm{d} x
  \le C(p,γ)\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}|D^2ψ|_{\mathrm{F}}^p|x|^{pγ}\, \mathrm{d} x, \] where $|\cdot|_{\mathrm{F}}$ denotes the Frobenius norm. For every fixed $1\le p<\infty$, with $a=γ-1+2/p$, we prove \[
  C(p,γ)^{-1}=2^{p/2}|a|^p+O_p(|a|^{p+1})\qquad(a\to0). \] The leading term comes from the first angular harmonics after the Emden--Fowler transform. We also determine explicit exterior parameter rays on which the unrestricted constant equals the radial value $(1+a^2)^{-p/2}$. The proof uses an entropy identity and a homogeneous calibration. In the remaining transition region, we obtain symmetry-breaking intervals and a necessary and sufficient condition for nonnegativity of the periodic second variation at the radial state. An explicit example shows that global symmetry breaking can occur even when this second variation is nonnegative.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 25 pages; submitted to a journal on 16 September 2026

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp condition for Superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We determine the sharp condition for local superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation $(-Δ)^m u=u^{(n+2m)/(n-2m)}$, where $m\geq2$ is an integer and $n>2m$. For a solution in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at zero, local superharmonicity holds if and only if $\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)>0$. The threshold is sharp. In the biharmonic case $m=2$, for every $n\geq5$, we construct smooth positive solutions of $Δ^2u=u^{(n+4)/(n-4)}$ in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at $0$, satisfying $\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)=0$ and $\limsup_{x\to0}u(x)=+\infty$, while $-Δu$ converges to a finite negative limit along a fixed ray. The construction relies on an infinite array of concentrating bubbles arranged on concentric polygons, with a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction controlling their interactions against a vanishing background.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Logarithmic upper bounds and axial front selection for spatially periodic lattice Fisher--KPP equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Cauchy problem $u_t=Δ_{\Z^d}u+F(x,u)$ on $\Z^d$ ($d\geq2$) with a spatially periodic Fisher--KPP reaction $F$ and a nonzero, finitely supported initial datum $u_0:\Z^d\to[0,1]$. We establish a logarithmic upper bound on the front position that holds uniformly in the observation direction, with a logarithmic delay coefficient governed by the outward normal to the asymptotic spreading body. When the linearized growth rate $F_s(x,0)$ is independent of the longitudinal coordinate, we prove the matching axial Bramson correction and show that the solution converges uniformly on fixed-width half-tubes to a critical pulsating front up to a bounded, slowly varying phase shift. For critical pulsating profiles $Φ(s,x)$ satisfying $Φ(s,x)\leq C(1+s)\ee^{-λs}$ for $s\geq0$ and $x\in\Z^d$, where $λ>0$ is the critical spatial decay rate, we derive the precise leading-edge asymptotic expansion and prove uniqueness up to translation. As a consequence, in the axial regime we obtain sharp asymptotics for the arrival times $T_θ(x)=\inf\{t\geq0:u(t,x)\geqθ\}$ ($0<θ<1$), including the asymptotic time lag between distinct level sets at a remote site and the period-to-period passage time along the axis. For general periodic linearized growth rates, we introduce a nonlinear subsolution built from a positive quotient of linear Dirichlet evolutions on a retreating domain and formulate sufficient kernel estimates for a matching directional lower bound.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local conservation laws, symmetries and Hamiltonian structure of three-dimensional incompressible Euler flow
Analysis of PDEs.summary: All smooth local conservation laws, symmetries and adjoint symmetries of three-dimensional homogeneous incompressible Euler flow are classified in the primitive velocity--pressure variables. Explicit dependence on time and position and arbitrary finite orders of mixed time and spatial derivatives are allowed. Up to trivial currents, the conservation laws consist of incompressibility, linear and angular momentum, kinetic energy, helicity and generalised time-dependent momentum. Every local adjoint symmetry is represented by a multiplier of these currents. Every finite-order local symmetry is equivalent on solutions to a classical point symmetry, resolving a conjecture of Olver. An explicit local first-order Hamiltonian structure of the primitive system is also established in the geometric theory of partial differential equations. It maps the energy multiplier to time translation; its kernel on local adjoint symmetries is spanned by the helicity and incompressibility multipliers. The proof first excludes higher-order symmetries by comparing their responses to transverse and harmonic characteristic directions in compatible derivative data. The Hamiltonian map and its kernel then determine all local adjoint symmetries from the symmetry classification. Exact multiplier identities and the correspondence between multipliers and current classes complete the conservation-law classification.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Logarithmically Coupled p-Laplacian Systems: From Discrete Ground States to Rigidity and Critical Continuous Limits
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We introduce a new class of logarithmically coupled \(p\)-Laplacian systems on locally finite graphs and in the critical case \(p=N>4\). The coupling poses two challenges: the energy functional is ill-defined on the natural Sobolev space, and loss of the \(L^\infty\)-embedding prevents standard control of logarithmic terms. To resolve this non-separable logarithmic singularity, we develop an \textbf{exponent calibration technique} that converts logarithmic terms into strictly lower-order power estimates. The technique plays an essential role in two critical steps: the existence proof for the regularised problem and the uniform boundedness of regularised ground states that restores compactness. Thus, we prove solvability of the original ill-posed continuous critical equation. In the discrete setting, we identify five new intrinsic structures, including an exact constrained Hessian factorisation and a scalar rigidity index. We complete a discrete--continuous double loop, providing a unified variational framework for logarithmically coupled systems.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On nonlocal geometric rigidity estimates in bounded uniform domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove fractional geometric rigidity estimates and fractional Korn's first inequalities with general singular weights in bounded uniform domains in $\mathbb R^n.$ The classical choice of the energy well $SO(n)$ for the geometric rigidity estimate fails due to the lack of a notion of orientation for Lebesgue fields. The remedy is to choose $O(n)$ as the energy well. Due to the recently developed theory of local-to-nonlocal passage of rigidity estimates developed by the first author, both estimates reduce to the analogous local estimates on the cube, which we prove in several steps by compactness and linearization arguments.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Exponential Decays of Steklov Eigenfunctions for the Magnetic Laplacian
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Consider the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $Λ_β$ associated with the Schrödinger operator $(D+β\A)^2$ with a magnetic potential in a bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω$, where $β>1$ is the field strength parameter. Assume that the magnetic field $\B=\nabla \times \A$ is of finite type. We show that if $β>β_0$, the ground state for $Λ_β$ decays exponentially away from a neighborhood of the subset of $\partialΩ$, on which $\B$ vanishes to the maximal order.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 15 pages. Minor revision. Accepted for publication in Proc. Amer. Math. Soc

Analysis of PDEs.title: Resolvent Estimates for the Stokes Operator in a Three-Dimensional Lipschitz Domain
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
By refining the approach developed in \cite{AGH-2015, GS2026a}, we establish resolvent estimates in $L^p_σ(Ω)$ for the Stokes operator in a bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω$ in $\R^3$ for $(3/2)-\e< p\le \infty$, where $\e>0$ depends on $Ω$. As a consequence, the Stokes operator generates a uniformly bounded analytic semigroup in $L^p_σ(Ω)$. The range for $p$ is sharp. The results are particularly surprising, as it is long believed that the $L^p$ resolvent estimates in three-dimensional Lipschitz domains may fail for large $p$.
  In the appendices we prove an interpolation theorem between $L^2_σ(Ω)$ and $L^\infty_σ(Ω)$. We also show that for $1< p< \infty$ and a bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω$ in $\R^d, d\ge 2$, the resolvent estimate in $L^p(Ω; \C^d)$ can hold only if the Helmholtz projection is bounded on this space. This explains the counter-example constructed in \cite{Deuring-2001}. Finally, we prove that the resolvent estimate may fail in $L^p_σ(Ω)$ for $1< p< (3/2)$ and $d\ge 3$ as a consequence of failure of the Helmholtz decomposition of $L^p(Ω; \C^d)$.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 30 pages. Appendix C is added. It shows that the range $(3/2)-\e< p\le \infty$ is sharp for $d=3$ and the range $(4/3)-\e< p\le \infty$ is sharp for $d=2$. Comments are welcome

Analysis of PDEs.title: Convergence of iterated restricted mean values to harmonic functions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain and let $δ$ be a continuous positive function on $Ω$ with $B(x,δ(x))\subseteqΩ$ for every $x\inΩ$. Let $σ(f)(x)$ denote the average of $f$ over the ball $B(x,δ(x))$. Restricted mean value theorems give conditions under which a fixed point of $σ$ must be harmonic. We study the dynamical counterpart of this question: the behavior of the iterates $σ^k(f)$. We show that for \emph{every} bounded domain and every bounded measurable $f$ that is continuous at the points of $\partialΩ$, the iterates $σ^k(f)$ converge locally uniformly in $Ω$ to the Perron--Wiener--Brelot solution of the Dirichlet problem with boundary values $f|_{\partialΩ}$, and that the convergence is uniform on $\overlineΩ$ for all continuous $f$ if and only if $Ω$ is regular for the Dirichlet problem. This contains and extends earlier results for $C^{2,α}$ domains with $C^{2,α}$ data and for strictly convex domains with continuous data. We also give explicit rates of convergence: an algebraic rate $O(1/k)$ on domains with a uniform exterior ball condition and a geometric rate on convex domains, when $δ$ is comparable to the distance to the boundary.

Functional Analysis.title: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that the set $\mathcal{N}_N$ of ReLU networks with one hidden layer and at most $N\in\mathbb N$ neurons is weakly closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$, for a bounded connected open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$. Consequently, every coercive, weakly lower semicontinuous energy on this space attains its minimum over $\mathcal{N}_N$. This covers the Deep Ritz method with convex integrands, Sobolev training and Lipschitz learning. Moreover, as the weight decay parameter tends to zero, minimizers of the regularized problem converge, up to subsequences, to minimizers with minimal parameter norm. We also prove that the set of ReLU networks with two hidden layers of bounded widths is not closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$ or in $C(\overlineΩ)$. This disproves a conjecture of Petersen, Raslan and Voigtlaender.

Functional Analysis.title: Mixing times for the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation
Functional Analysis.summary: We review quantitative results on the convergence to equilibrium of the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation, $p>1$, on a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with additive, possibly degenerate Wiener noise. From these results we derive upper bounds on $\varepsilon$-mixing times in different distances, depending on the initial data. We show that the Wasserstein distance to equilibrium is non-increasing in time and that, for $p>\frac{2d}{d+2}$, the invariant measure has moments of all orders. For $1<p<2$ with $p>\frac{2d}{d+2}$ and possibly degenerate noise, the $\varepsilon$-mixing times in every Wasserstein distance $\mathcal{W}_r$, $r\ge1$, are $O(\varepsilon^{-δ})$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow 0$ for every $δ>0$. Two tables collect the convergence rates and the mixing-time bounds.

Functional Analysis.title: The Matrix Kawada--Itô Theorem and Harmonic Rigidity on Locally Compact Groups
Functional Analysis.summary:
A positive $M_n$-valued measure on a locally compact group need not have positive convolution products: matrix multiplication preserves neither self-adjointness nor positivity. We prove that this obstruction disappears completely at an idempotent. If $μ\in M(G,M_n)$ is positive and $μ*μ=μ$, then all its matrix values commute and there is a unique finite decomposition \[
  μ=\sum_{j=1}^r m_{K_j}\otimes E_j, \] where the $K_j$ are distinct compact subgroups and the $E_j$ are pairwise orthogonal nonzero projections. The result holds for arbitrary locally compact groups, without countability assumptions or a priori commutativity. The proof combines projection-valued dilations, rigidity of contractive idempotent Fourier coefficients, and faithfulness of the regular representation on finite measures over $G\times G$. For normalized positive matrix convolution semigroups, we further identify the Cesàro harmonic projection with convolution by such an idempotent, even if mass escapes to infinity. Its surviving matrix directions are exactly those uniformly confined to a compact subset of the group, yielding an explicit direct Haar-channel decomposition for all $1<p<\infty$ (orthogonal in $L^2$). A bounded Zeno product formula and independent density, atomic, and subgroup-support classifications illustrate the rigidity.

Functional Analysis.title: Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on weighted Bergman spaces are the fixed points of a normal unital completely positive map
Functional Analysis.summary: In this article, we consider weighted Bergman spaces over open unit disk corresponding to nonnegative integrable radial functions with positive mass arbitrarily close to the unit circle. Then we show that Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on the weighted Bergman space are the fixed points of a normal unital completely positive map. This result generalizes the classical characterization of Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space due to Brown and Halmos. Moreover, we prove that there is no compact Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on weighted Bergman space.
Functional Analysis.comment: This is a preliminary draft of the article, 18 pages, Comments are welcome

Functional Analysis.title: Coarse comparison of Bessel families
Functional Analysis.summary: A Bessel family is a collection of vectors of a Hilbert space whose coefficients are square summable; orthonormal bases and frames are examples. We compare two such families by asking when the size of the coefficients of one is controlled, up to constants, by that of the other after a change of variables taken from a fixed class $\mathcal O$ of operators. Each class (bounded, injective, bounded below, invertible, Fredholm, and others) gives an equivalence relation that ignores redundancy and treats frames and nonframes on the same footing. For every relation we determine the classes by explicit spectral data: the singular numbers of the analysis operator, its kernel, the closedness of its range, and the multiplicities of its spectrum at each dyadic scale. We also characterize the families equivalent to an orthonormal basis, compute an operator Banach--Mazur distance, and prove a Paley--Wiener stability result that needs no frame assumption. These relations are instances of the comparison categories of a companion article.
Functional Analysis.comment: AI-generated from an initial draft and supervision by the author. 30 pages

Functional Analysis.title: Alternating chains and lattice strict singularity
Functional Analysis.summary: We present an alternating-chain argument intended to show that every lattice strictly singular operator from a real Banach lattice to a real Banach space is disjointly strictly singular. A hypothetical counterexample yields two LSS operators on a reflexive sequence lattice whose difference is bounded below. Quotienting by the range of that difference gives a common map bounded below on a positive tail cone. Finite chains of positive disjoint vectors with alternating small differences lead to incompatible length estimates. We record the resulting operator and sequence consequences and extend the construction to common postcompositions with DSS errors. Independently of the proposed equality, we prove simultaneous nuclear restriction results for norm-sigma-compact DSS families and uniform nuclear tails on each compact piece. For norm-compact families we also obtain common Hilbert-space factors and uniformly small nuclear corrections having a common infinite-dimensional kernel. Examples identify limits of these selection statements. We present the main argument as a candidate proof over the real field.

Functional Analysis.title: A Regular First-Order Calculus for the Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao Geometry
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce a notion of intrinsic differentiability for functionals on the space of finite nonnegative measures equipped with the Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao (WFR) distance, also known as the Hellinger--Kantorovich (HK) distance. The resulting static first-order calculus accounts simultaneously for spatial transport and mass reweighting. We characterize regular barycentric logarithms through optimal semicouplings and measurable selections at the transport threshold, and prove their tangency at arbitrary finite source measures. The defining expansion extends to non-optimal semicouplings, with remainder of smaller order than the square root of their cost. This yields differentiation formulas for simultaneous transport and reweighting and uniqueness of the gradients. We also give a sufficient criterion in terms of regular flat derivatives. We characterize differentiability of one half the squared WFR distance by a common optimal Monge transport--growth representation with no target mass created from the cone vertex. Equivalently, the regular barycentric logarithm is unique and its norm equals the distance; the gradient is minus this logarithm. Finally, we formulate the corresponding calculus on probability measures. On $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, WFR differentiability implies intrinsic Wasserstein differentiability, with the transport component of the WFR gradient coinciding with the Wasserstein gradient. Whenever a flat derivative exists, one quarter of the reaction component agrees almost everywhere with its centered representative. As a byproduct we obtain a Wasserstein differentiability result for the squared $\mathrm{WFR}$ distance.

Functional Analysis.title: The maximal monotonicity of the subdifferential in locally convex spaces via upper envelopes
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish equivalent conditions for the convex subdifferential to be maximal monotone in general settings, expressed in terms of the associated upper envelopes.

Functional Analysis.title: Fourier Positivity and Sharp Poincaré Inequalities on Graphs
Functional Analysis.summary:
We prove sharp dimension-free $L^1$-Poincaré inequalities on Hamming cubes, a sharp quadratic $L^1$-Poincaré inequality on product Poisson spaces, and a sharp pseudo-Poincaré inequality on finite abelian Cayley graphs. These inequalities use a generalization of the Beckmann boundary introduced by Ivanisvili, Xie, and Zhang. In particular, we prove that the optimal dimension-free constant in the classical $L^1$-Poincaré inequality on the Hamming cube is $\sqrt{π/2}$, answering a question of Ivanisvili et al.
  Semigroup duality and explicit Malliavin weights reduce these estimates to integrals of first absolute moments of centered Bernoulli and Poisson sums. The key ingredient is a Fourier positivity principle, which shows that replacing the coefficients by their absolute values can only increase these integrals. For the underlying Bernoulli functional at subquadratic exponents, we also characterize the maximizers and determine their exact phase transitions.

Functional Analysis.title: Isometric Classification of Sobolev Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We show that the norm obtained by summing the $L^1$ norms of all weak derivatives through order $k$, including the function itself, determines both $n$ and $k$ on the real Sobolev space $W^{k,1}(\R^n)$. Every surjective linear isometry for this norm is given by a translation, a signed permutation of the coordinates and multiplication by a fixed sign $c\in\{-1,1\}$.

Functional Analysis.title: The small ball problem for the Brownian sheet: sharp bounds via entropy numbers in $L_\infty$
Functional Analysis.summary: We settle the uniform small deviation conjecture for the Brownian sheet in every dimension $d\ge2$, namely, that the logarithmic exponent is $2d-1$. Our proof proceeds through sharp entropy and Kolmogorov estimates for the associated anchored mixed Sobolev embedding in the uniform norm. Their connection to small deviations is known from the Kuelbs--Li theorem. To establish the entropy estimates, the key is a probabilistic small ball inequality for smooth tensor product atoms whose exceptional set has Gaussian measure exponentially small in the number of atoms. Its proof combines a count of dyadic rectangles with tools from probability, in particular Ehrhard's Gaussian Brunn--Minkowski inequality. This also yields sharp entropy and Kolmogorov number estimates for embeddings of periodic mixed Sobolev, Besov and Nikol'skii classes with smoothness $r>1/2$ in $L_\infty$. Finally, we extend our results to fractional and integrated Brownian sheets.

Functional Analysis.title: Ahlfors $1$-Regularity and Conformal Criteria for Carleson Measures
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that a bounded Jordan domain $Ω$ has Ahlfors $1$-regular boundary if and only if the following criterion holds for every positive Borel measure $μ$ on $Ω$: $μ$ is Carleson exactly when $\int_Ω|φ'(w)|\,dμ(w)<\infty$ for every conformal bijection $φ$ from $Ω$ onto a bounded domain with rectifiable boundary. The same characterization holds using only arclength measures on simple locally rectifiable curves, with the integral condition replaced by finite length of every such conformal image. These results extend Bishop's theorem on the unit disk. We also study analogous criteria for vanishing Carleson measures.

Functional Analysis.title: Duality for the Adversarial Total Variation
Functional Analysis.summary: Adversarial training of binary classifiers can be reformulated as regularized risk minimization involving a nonlocal total variation. Building on this perspective, we establish a characterization of the subdifferential of this total variation using duality techniques. To achieve this, we derive a dual representation of the nonlocal total variation and a related integration-by-parts formula, involving a nonlocal gradient and divergence. We provide such duality statements both in the space of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on proper metric spaces and for the space of essentially bounded functions on separable metric spaces. Furthermore, under some additional conditions we provide characterizations of the subdifferential in these settings.

Functional Analysis.title: Step-isometries on Banach spaces
Functional Analysis.summary:
Step-isometries are maps preserving the integer part of pairwise distances on metric spaces. They arise naturally in the study of infinite random geometric graphs, where graph isomorphisms between LARG-type random graphs reduce to step-isometries on the underlying vertex sets. Several fundamental open problems concerning the rigidity, extendability, and continuity of step-isometries were raised in recent literature, notably by Šemrl, and by Balogh, Walters, and Zsák. In the present paper we resolve a number of these long-standing open questions.
  We establish rigidity results for step-isometries defined on norm-dense subsets of both real and complex Banach spaces. For complex Banach spaces, we prove that every almost-surjective step-isometry on a norm-dense subset admits a unique extension to a surjective real-affine isometry of the whole space. In the real setting, we investigate three key properties $A$, $B$, $C$ formulated by Šemrl, which ask whether certain classes of step-isometries extend to surjective affine isometries. We verify these properties for uniformly non-square Banach spaces, for spaces with a dense set of Fréchet-smooth points, and for strictly convex Banach spaces with separable dual. In particular, we confirm Conjecture 2 due to Balogh, Walters, and Zsák without countability assumptions on the dense domain set. We further show that every bijective step-isometry defined on the entire Banach space is a homeomorphism, answering their Question 3 affirmatively. Specializing to $\ell_1^n$, we obtain that $\ell_1^n$ satisfies Property $A$ for all integers $n\ge 3$, settling an open problem posed by Šemrl.

Functional Analysis.title: Trace and Regularized Index of Callias Operators on Hyperbolic Space
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $d \geq 3$ be odd. On hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^d$, we consider Callias-type operators, i.e. Dirac-Schrödinger operators of the form $D = ic \nabla + A$, where $c \nabla$ is the Dirac operator and $A$ a function with values in the self-adjoint operators, and provide an explicit formula for the iterated trace $\text{tr}_{L^2(\mathbb{H}^d,H)} \text{tr}_{S}( e^{-tD^*D} - e^{-tDD^*})$, $t>0$, that appears in the formulation of the Witten index. Thereby, the operator $D$ is not assumed to be Fredholm.

Functional Analysis.title: Isomorphisms and representations of noncommutative function algebras
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $V$ be a noncommutative (NC) variety in a NC operator ball. We study the dual operator algebra $H^\infty(V)$ of bounded NC functions on $V$, and the operator algebra $A(V)$ obtained as the closure of NC polynomials in $H^\infty(V)$. We identify the space of weak-$*$ continuous finite-dimensional representations of $H^\infty(V)$ as the similarity envelope $\widetilde{V}$ of $V$, and equip $\widetilde{V}$ with a metric which turns $\widetilde{V}$ into a complete invariant for $H^\infty(V)$, in the sense that $H^\infty(V)$ is weak-$*$ continuously isomorphic to $H^\infty(W)$ if and only if $\widetilde{V}$ and $\widetilde{W}$ are NC biholomorphic via a bi-Lipschitz map. Similar results are obtained in the completely bounded category as well as for the algebras $A(V)$ when $V$ is assumed homogeneous. In the case of homogeneous varieties $V$ and $W$, we obtain a sharper classification result, by which $H^\infty(V)$ is (completely) boundedly isomorphic to $H^\infty(W)$ if and only if there is a linear map which gives a bi-Lipschitz bijection between $\widetilde{W}$ and $\widetilde{V}$. The reduction to the linear case in the generality we work in depends on showing that the existence of maps implies the existence of origin-fixing maps, which we show using a novel ``two-circle trick" of independent interest. In the important case where the varieties are the full NC operator balls we find a striking rigidity phenomenon: if $A(B_E)$ and $A(B_F)$ are completely boundedly isomorphic then $E$ and $F$ are completely isometric. We also present a variety of examples illustrating the results and their sharpness, showing how several results from the literature fail to generalize to the setting studied here.

Functional Analysis.title: A family of matrix flows converging to normal matrices
Functional Analysis.summary: The celebrated Antezana-Pujals-Stojanoff Theorem states that the iterated Aluthge transforms of an arbitrary matrix converge to a normal matrix. We introduce a family of matrix flows that share this convergence property by defining them through ordinary differential equations. The family includes a continuous analogue of the Aluthge transform, as well as a differential equation discussed by Haagerup in the context of II$_1$ factors. We also examine the same type of flows in the setting of Hilbert space operators equipped with unitarily invariant norms.
Functional Analysis.comment: v2:minor revision, typos corrected, to appear in Reviews in Mathematical Physics

Functional Analysis.title: Commuting Toeplitz and Little Hankel Operators on the Bidisk
Functional Analysis.summary: Necessary and sufficient conditions are obtained for two Toeplitz operators and for a Toeplitz operator and a little Hankel operator to commute on the pluriharmonic Hardy space of the bidisk.

Functional Analysis.title: Multilinear extrapolation on Banach function spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We solve an open problem on the multilinear Rubio de Francia extrapolation on Banach function spaces. The main result states that, under the assumption of the boundedness of the multisublinear Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, the multivariable boundedness on Banach function spaces can be extrapolated from some weighted Lebesgue space, including the cases where some exponents may be infinite. Based on this result, we also establish multilinear extrapolation of boundedness on rearrangement invariant Banach function spaces, and multilinear extrapolation of compactness on general Banach function spaces. Beyond that, we give characterizations of the boundedness of the multisublinear Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on both general Banach function spaces and certain specific function spaces. All results do not require any convexity or concavity conditions on Banach function spaces. The main ingredients in the proof are a multilinear version of the Rubio de Francia algorithm, a stopping-time argument, convex analysis, and a compactness criterion on Banach function spaces. As applications of extrapolation theorems, we obtain multilinear extrapolation for the boundedness and compactness of commutators on Banach function spaces. These results can be further applied to specific operators, which cover both the full range case including multilinear Calderón-Zygmund operators, multilinear pseudo-differential operators, and bilinear paraproducts, and the limited range case including the bilinear Hilbert transform, multilinear rough singular integrals, and bilinear oscillatory Fourier multipliers.
Functional Analysis.comment: The new version includes multilinear extrapolation on RIBFS and characterizations of the boundedness of the multisublinear Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on BFS

Functional Analysis.title: On a characterization of spaces satisfying open mapping and equivalent theorems
Functional Analysis.summary: We study open-mapping, continuous-inverse and closed-graph properties for maps whose domain and range belong to the same class of Hausdorff topological vector spaces. Quotient and graph stability imply equivalence of these properties. In the locally convex setting, we characterize barrelled infra-Pták spaces and barrelled Pták spaces as largest classes determined by the closed-graph property, Banach test spaces and appropriate nearly-open image conditions.

Functional Analysis.title: A Fermat--Torricelli convex-hull characterization of inner-product spaces via Birkhoff--James orthogonality
Functional Analysis.summary: The classical location problem posed by Weber [Über den Standort der Industrien,Tübingen: J. C. B. Mohr, 1909] has motivated various geometric characterizations of inner-product spaces. Benítez, Fernández and Soriano [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. \textbf{354} (2002), 5027--5038] characterized real inner-product spaces through the convex-hull property of Fermat--Torricelli medians.Pakhrou [J. Funct. Anal. \textbf{285} (2023), 110078] further established a characterization using $γ$-centers and equilateral triangles. Building on these results, we show that the Fermat--Torricelli convex-hull criterion remains valid when restricted to triples satisfying a one-sided Birkhoff--James orthogonality condition.The proof combines norming functionals, radial rescaling,Alexandrov differentiability, and the area formula.No completeness, smoothness, or strict convexity assumptions are required.

Functional Analysis.title: Entropy and frame measures for self-similar measures
Functional Analysis.summary:
For $0<ρ<1$ and a set of $N\ge2$ distinct real digits $\mathscr D=\{d_0,\ldots,d_{N-1}\}\subset\mathbb{R}$, let \[
  μ_{ρ,\mathscr D}=\frac1N\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}μ_{ρ,\mathscr D}\circ S_i^{-1},
  \qquad S_i(x)=ρ(x+d_i). \] Write $X=\sum_{j\ge1}ρ^j d_{ω_j}$, where the symbols $ω_j$ are independent and uniform on $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$. We prove that $μ_{ρ,\mathscr D}$ admits no frame measure if the conditional entropy $H(ω_1\mid X)>0$. In particular, this holds for all $ρ>1/N$, without any absolute-continuity assumption or arithmetic restriction on the digits or the contraction. At $ρ=1/N$, for commensurable digits, a frame measure exists if and only if $μ_{ρ,\mathscr D}$ is normalized Lebesgue measure on its attractor. For $\mathscr D=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ and $ρ<1/N$, we also prove nonexistence whenever $ρ^{-m}=a/b$ for some $m\in\N$, with $a/b$ in lowest terms, $b\mid N$ and $N/b\nmid a$, extending the integer-power obstruction. The extension compares mask quotients using finite families of target pole classes in place of one target class.

Functional Analysis.title: Recurrent and rigid multipliers on commutative Banach algebras. The Fourier algebra
Functional Analysis.summary: We study recurrence, rigidity and uniform rigidity of multipliers on semisimple commutative Banach algebras. For a power-bounded multiplier $T$ on a Tauberian, self-adjoint algebra $\mathfrak{A}$, we show that $T$ satisfies each of these properties if and only if the multiplication operator on $C_0(Δ(\mathfrak{A}))$ induced by the Gelfand transform of $T$ does. One consequence of our analysis is that, if $Δ(\mathfrak{A})$ is $σ$-compact, then recurrence implies rigidity for such multipliers. We examine in detail the multipliers of the Fourier algebra $A(G)$. In particular, we show that recurrence of a multiplier of $A(G)$ is equivalent to recurrence of the corresponding multiplier on $C_0(G)$ when the connected components of $G$ are open. For multipliers that are not power bounded, a flexible construction based on chains of compact subgroups of a locally compact abelian group $G$ produces multipliers of $A(G)$ that are rigid but not uniformly rigid, and multipliers that are recurrent but not rigid, such that in each case the corresponding multiplier on $C_0(G)$ is uniformly rigid. Via the Fourier-Stieltjes transform, these results describe the recurrence and rigidity properties of convolution operators on $L^1(G)$.

Functional Analysis.title: Holomorphic calculus on $L^p(\ell^q)$ with optimal angle
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $\mathcal{L}$ generate a symmetric contraction semigroup. We prove a holomorphic Hörmander calculus on $L^p(X;\ell^q)$ at the optimal angle $\max\{\arcsin|1-2/p|,\arcsin|1-2/q|\}$, with boundary Sobolev order $s>3$.

Functional Analysis.title: A Dirichlet form approach to the potential theory of $m$-subharmonic functions
Functional Analysis.summary:
On a bounded open subset of $\mathbb{C}^n$, we study the Dirichlet form induced by an admissible pair $(θ,μ)$, where $μ$ is a positive Radon measure and $$θ=dd^c u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dd^c u_{m-1}\wedge(dd^c \lvert z\rvert^2)^{n-m}$$ for locally bounded $m$-subharmonic functions $u_1,\dots,u_{m-1}$. We prove that locally bounded $m$-subharmonic functions belong locally to the domains of these Dirichlet forms and are quasi-continuous with respect to the induced capacities. We establish a monotonicity property for Dirichlet forms, which motivates the introduction of $μ$-quasi-monotone convergence of $m$-subharmonic functions. The natural embeddings into these domains are continuous with respect to this convergence. These results yield new proofs of the commutativity and continuity of complex Hessian operators.
  Using this framework, we characterize quasi-continuity with respect to the induced capacity for an arbitrary $m$-subharmonic function in terms of its pole set having zero measure $μ$, or equivalently, zero induced capacity. On bounded strictly $m$-pseudoconvex domains, we prove that the Bedford--Taylor capacity for $m$-subharmonic functions and the capacities induced by the corresponding Dirichlet forms have the same null sets. We further characterize $m$-polar sets in terms of Dirichlet forms and stochastic processes, extending the corresponding characterization of pluripolar sets due to Fukushima and Okada to the $m$-subharmonic setting.

Functional Analysis.title: Gelfand numbers of Schatten class embeddings in the quasi-Banach range
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove Conjecture 1.4 of Prochno and Strzelecki [J. Approx. Theory 277 (2022), 105736] on Gelfand numbers of embeddings between finite-dimensional Schatten classes. For $0<p\le1$ and indices bounded away from the ambient dimension by a fixed proportion, we obtain the conjectured lower bound, uniformly in the target exponent $2\le q\le\infty$. Together with the known upper estimate obtained by Hinrichs, Prochno and Vybíral [Math. Ann., 380(3-4):1563-1593, 2021], this gives the exact asymptotic order in the previously unresolved range. As a consequence, we obtain a complete all-index description by combining our result with the estimates of Hinrichs, Prochno and Vybíral and of Prochno and Strzelecki. The proof is deterministic and is based on Hilbert--Schmidt projections on rectangular matrix spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: Characterization of Attenuated V-Line Transform and Direct Reconstruction from Samples
Functional Analysis.summary: The V-line transform (V-LT), a generalized Radon transform (RT), is widely used in Compton scattering imaging (CSI). The central mathematical problem of CSI is to reconstruct a function from its V-LT. Unlike V-LT, the attenuated V-line transform (AV-LT) accounts for the medium-induced loss of intensity, and has been demonstrated to improve image quality. The present paper makes two main contributions. (1) We establish the fundamental characterizations for AV-LT including operator properties ($L^2$-boundedness, operator norm etc.), a necessary and sufficient condition for the preservation of compact support, and sharp estimation of Sobolev smoothness. These characterizations remain unexplored, and they reveal essential differences among AV-LT, RT and V-LT. (2) We develop a direct reconstruction method based on AV-LT samples that does not require solving any equation. Our sampling formula gives exact reconstruction for band-limited functions. We also provide approximate reconstruction for functions in $H^s(\mathbb{R}^2)$ with $s>2$.

Functional Analysis.title: Critical orthonormal Strichartz estimates for Lebesgue spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates at the critical coefficient exponent $q/2$ for fractional Schrödinger propagators. The proof for $d\geq3$ combines annular Schatten estimates with a frequency summation argument based on potential duality and Littlewood--Paley theory. In dimension two, a trace computation supplies the annular estimate needed for the global estimate. We also construct a counterexample to the global estimate with spatial $L^\infty$ and coefficients in $\ell^{q/2}$, even with a weak time norm.
Functional Analysis.comment: Version 2 adds more background introductions in Section 1. Version 2 also fixes few notations in the final section. No changes for math contents

Functional Analysis.title: Walsh Analysis in the Twenty-First Century: Convergence, Summability, Nonlinear Approximation, Universality, and Digital Applications
Functional Analysis.summary: Walsh analysis connects ordered Fourier convergence, summability, nonlinear approximation, and universal representation through a common character algebra. This survey examines developments from 2000-2026 against their classical foundations. Binary kernel geometry explains Hardy-space losses and summability thresholds; interval and packet methods control spectral selection; localized blocks produce correction and universal representations with distinct coefficient and exceptional-set requirements. Selected proofs and counterexamples compare these mechanisms and identify where an implication needs an additional hypothesis. The same distinctions organize digital integration, sparse measurements, Boolean spectra, and generalized Walsh bases. Quantitative thresholds, source conventions, and published theorem pointers are collected in comparative tables. The concluding problems separate source-listed questions, proposed refinements, and elementary obstructions. Supplementary derivations preserve normalization checks and finite covariance calculations while keeping the main exposition focused on the analytic mechanisms.

Functional Analysis.title: Finite-rank Toeplitz commutators on the harmonic Bergman space
Functional Analysis.summary: We completely characterize finite-rank commutators of Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on the harmonic Bergman space of the unit disk. Apart from affine dependence, finite rank occurs precisely when both symbols are analytic with rational primitives, or both are coanalytic and their complex conjugates have rational primitives. Our approach combines a block-matrix decomposition with Luecking's theorem, which rules out nonzero finite-rank Toeplitz operators with bounded symbols on the Bergman space. In particular, every such finite-rank commutator has square zero.

Functional Analysis.title: Power Mean, Karcher Mean, and Log-Euclidean Mean on Positive Constant Upper Triangular Matrices
Functional Analysis.summary: We study weighted power, Karcher, and log-Euclidean means on the Lie group CP_n of real upper triangular matrices with a constant positive diagonal. Building on the general triangular-group theory, we use the central decomposition CP_n \cong \mathbb R_+ -by-UP_n to separate the scalar power mean from a unipotent mean with reweighted coefficients. We prove that the power mean extends real-analytically through order zero, where it equals the Karcher mean. We establish exterior-power covariance for the Karcher and log-Euclidean means, and tensor-product identities for all three means, distinguishing product weights from paired inputs. Finite nilpotent functional calculus yields concise formulas on CP_2 and CP_3, where the Karcher and log-Euclidean means coincide. In dimension four, their difference is exactly a central cubic commutator, giving a necessary and sufficient equality criterion and an explicit counterexample. In every dimension, the same commutator is the leading term of their small-dispersion difference.

Functional Analysis.title: Disjointness preserving operators on Köthe-Banach spaces
Functional Analysis.summary:
A well-known result of Abramovich says that if $E$, $F$ are rearrangement invariant Banach spaces on a finite atomless measure space such that $E$ has an absolutely continuous norm and $E\not\subseteq F$, then there are no nonzero disjointness preserving bounded linear operators $T \colon E\to F$.
  We obtain an analogue of this result in the setting of general Köthe-Banach spaces. Specifically, we identify a sufficient condition on Köthe-Banach spaces $E$, $F$ on finite atomless measure spaces that implies that there are no nonzero disjointness preserving bounded linear operators $T \colon E\to F$. Consequently, by a representation theorem for regular operators due to O.~Maslyuchenko, Mykhaylyuk and the second named author, this condition implies that every regular linear operator $T \colon E\to F$ is narrow. As an application, we obtain that if $1\le \max\{p_1,p_2\}< \min\{ r_1, r_2\}\le \infty$, then every regular linear operator $T \colon L_{p_1}(L_{p_2}) \to L_{r_1}(L_{r_2})$
  is narrow. The latter may be seen as an analogue of the classical Pitt compactness theorem.

Functional Analysis.title: Optimal domains of Volterra-type operators on Bergman spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We consider bounded Volterra-type operators $T_g$ from the weighted Bergman space $A^q_β$ to $A^p_α$. The holomorphic optimal domain $[T_{g},A^p_α]$ is introduced and shown to be a quasi-Banach space. We show that the intersection of the optimal domains is equal to $A^q_β$ if $p\le q$, while if $p>q$, it is strictly larger than $A^q_β$. Moreover, $A^q_β \subsetneq[T_{g},A^p_α]$ is established for $p\neq q$. If $p=q$, by contrast, $A^p_β$ may coincide with $[T_{g},A^p_α]$. The multiplier algebras and strict inclusions with respect to varying parameters are established. For example, we determine exactly when $[T_{g},A^s_γ] \subset [T_{g},A^p_α]$ for some $g\in \operatorname{Hol}(\mathbb{D})$. We further study the set $V_g^p$ and characterize the coincidence of the holomorphic optimal domains.

Functional Analysis.title: A Stone-Weierstrass Theorem for Polish Spaces, Given by Logic
Functional Analysis.summary: The Stone-Weierstrass theorem obtains every continuous function on a compact space as a uniform limit of functions built from a separating family by finitely many operations, and Reggio proved the theorem equivalent to the Beth definability property of an infinitary equational logic. We extend both results beyond compactness: on every separable metric space, and in particular on every Polish space, every bounded uniformly continuous function is a uniform limit of functions built from countably many bounded separating functions by the connectives of infinitary real-valued logic, and an approximate Beth property of this logic is equivalent to the new theorem. The extension rests on a rule of syntax, which admits a countable supremum when its terms share an a priori bound and thereby makes the sentences define exactly the bounded Lipschitz functions, and on a model existence game that does the work of compactness in the proof of interpolation.

Functional Analysis.title: Empirical approximation of $L_p$ norms for $p\in (2, \infty)$
Functional Analysis.summary: For $p>2$ and an $N$-dimensional subspace $X\subset L_\infty(μ)$ satisfying \[ \|f\|_\infty\le (KN)^{1/p}\|f\|_{L_p(μ)} \quad\forall f\in X, \] we show that $m\ge C(p)KN \bigl(\varepsilon^{-p} +\varepsilon^{-2}\log_2(2N)\bigr)$ independent samples $ξ^1,\ldots,ξ^m$ with distribution $μ$ satisfy \[ (1-\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(μ)}^p \le\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|f(ξ^j)|^p \le(1+\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(μ)}^p \quad\forall f\in X \] with probability at least $1-\exp(-c(p)\frac{m\varepsilon^2}{KN})$. This gives the optimal sample-size order $N\log_2 N$ for independent random sampling with fixed $K$, $p$, and $\varepsilon$. This result follows from a more general empirical moment estimate over unit balls of $p$-convex norms.

Functional Analysis.title: A Novel Two-Parameter Penalty: Relaxation Degree Analysis and Sparse Signal Recovery
Functional Analysis.summary: In this article, we introduce a nonconvex two-parameter penalty function $P_{a,p}$, parameterized by $a\in(0,\infty)$ and $p\in(0,1]$, and the relaxation degree RD$_P$ for a separable nonconvex penalty function $P$. Based on $P_{a,p}$, we further propose the $P_{a,p}$ minimization framework for sparse signal recovery. This framework generalizes the TL1 minimization model established by S. Zhang and J. Xin (corresponding to the special case $p=1$) and provides a unified family of nonconvex penalty functions for sparse signal recovery. Using the sparse convex-combination technique, we establish both exact and stable sparse signal recovery under the restricted isometry property (RIP). To efficiently solve the resulting nonconvex optimization problem, we apply a modified iteratively re-weighted least squares method and the difference of convex functions algorithm (DCA) to develop the IRLSTLp algorithm for unconstrained $P_{a,p}$ minimization and prove some convergence results. Finally, numerical experiments compare recovery and runtime against single- and double-loop baselines, examine sensitivity to $(a,p)$, and assess the empirical correlation between RD$_{P_{a,p}}$ and recovery within the proposed family.

Functional Analysis.title: Characterizations of minimal Hermitian completions via moments and subdifferentials
Functional Analysis.summary: Given a Hermitian matrix $A_0$ and a real subspace $W$ of Hermitian matrices, we study the matrices $A_0+W_0$, $W_0\in W$, of minimal spectral norm, which we call $W$-minimal. The main motivation is the Hermitian matrix completion problem, where $W$ is spanned by the Hermitian matrix units corresponding to the unspecified entries. Our main tool is the moment of a subspace $S\subseteq\mathbb{C}^n$ relative to $W$, a compact convex subset of $\mathbb{R}^r$, $r=\dim(W)$, which we relate to the joint numerical range and to the $k$-dimensional field of a family of matrices. We compute the subdifferential of $\|A_0+W(x)\|$ in terms of the moments of the eigenspaces of the extreme eigenvalues of $A_0+W(x)$, and we obtain several equivalent characterizations of $W$-minimality: in terms of eigenvectors, of moments, of subdifferentials and of norm one functionals that annihilate $W$. When the identity belongs to $W$, every $W$-minimal matrix has balanced spectrum, and minimality is equivalent to the moments of the eigenspaces of the maximum and minimum eigenvalues having nonempty intersection; we show that this characterization fails if $I\notin W$. We illustrate the results with several examples, and we prove that the adjacency matrix of a connected graph is minimal for its completion problem if and only if the graph is complete bipartite.

Functional Analysis.title: A Time-Frequency Framework for GKP Codes
Functional Analysis.summary: We develop a time--frequency framework for lattice GKP codes in which ideal codewords are realized in the modulation space $M^\infty$ and identified, through a vector-valued Zak transform, with a finite logical fibre over the continuous syndrome torus. Multi-window Gabor analysis then represents the logical vector by a finite block of adjoint-lattice coefficients. We prove that the normalized block map is an isometry, obtain an explicit recovering projection, and derive stable logical reconstruction. We further construct normalizable GKP approximants as lattice-envelope Gabor multipliers and establish weak-$*$ convergence and asymptotically isometric encoding. Finally, we recover displacement syndromes from phase relations between translated coefficient blocks and quantify their stability under additive perturbations.

Functional Analysis.title: A metric characterization of free unitary quantum groups
Functional Analysis.summary: For a compact matrix quantum group $G$ with a fundamental unitary representation $u$ of dimension at least two, the reduced operator norm of the self-adjoint main character satisfies $\left \|χ_u+χ_u^*\right \|_{C_r(G)}\geq2\sqrt2$. Within the category of free quantum groups of Kac type, it is known that the minimum $2\sqrt2$ is attained only by free unitary quantum groups. We establish this characterization in full generality, including the non-Kac setting: this minimum is attained if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to a free unitary quantum group $U_Q^+$ as compact matrix quantum groups.

Functional Analysis.title: Multipoint Characterization of Higher-Order Sobolev Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: In the paper, we prove a rather general characterization of higher-order Sobolev spaces. We show that the $k\mathrm{th}$-order regularity, where $k \in \mathbb{N}$, is captured via inequalities involving $2^k$-tuples of points. In fact, in full generality, the obtained results characterize higher-order Sobolev spaces based on Banach function spaces. Moreover, we show an analogous characterization of higher-order Hölder spaces. Finally, we propose a way to use the obtained results to define higher-order Sobolev and Hölder spaces on metric measure spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: Compact Quasi-Metric Spaces Are Expand-Contract Plastic
Functional Analysis.summary: On a totally bounded metric space, every non-contractive self-map is an isometry. For quasi-metric spaces this fails. Here quasi-metrics are $T_1$: $d(x,y)=0$ implies $x=y$. Zavarzina gave a hereditarily precompact counterexample and asked whether rigidity holds at least for bijections. The author's toll spiral (arXiv:2610.13973) shows that it does not. We prove that compactness restores it: every compact quasi-metric space is expand-contract plastic, that is, each of its bijective non-contractive self-maps is an isometry. Countable compactness suffices, as does compactness of the conjugate topology. Bijectivity is needed, even on a compact, hereditarily precompact space. For arbitrary non-contractive self-maps, we prove rigidity when the space is hereditarily precompact and its conjugate topology is sequentially compact, in particular when it is also Yoneda complete; neither hypothesis can be dropped. Such maps are then surjective. In both theorems the $T_1$ axiom can be weakened to $R_0$, $d(x,y)=0$ implies $d(y,x)=0$, if hereditary precompactness is taken to mean that every sequence has a left K-Cauchy subsequence; surjectivity then holds up to points at distance 0 both ways. The weaker $T_0$ axiom is not enough: there is a $T_0$ space, compact in both topologies and satisfying all the other hypotheses of both theorems, with a bijective non-contractive non-isometry. Finally, for an asymmetric norm in finite dimension, the classical theorem makes the symmetric unit ball and sphere rigid for all non-contractive self-maps, and the forward ones if the norm is $T_1$. In infinite dimension, the symmetric ball and sphere need not be plastic, and for the forward ones we pose the quasi-metric form of the unit-ball question of Cascales, Kadets, Orihuela and Wingler. The two theorems and the counterexamples of Section 6 are machine-checked in Lean, except the steps listed at the end.
Functional Analysis.comment: 23 pages. Lean 4 verification files included as ancillary files and archived with the paper at Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23265517. Answers two questions of the toll-spiral paper, arXiv:2610.13973. v2: Section 7 on asymmetric unit balls added. v3: numbering unchanged; notes that the maps of the second theorem are surjective, and derives Proposition 7.1 from the classical theorem

Functional Analysis.title: Bijective Non-Contractive Maps of Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Spaces Need Not Be Isometries
Functional Analysis.summary: Zavarzina asked whether every bijective non-contractive self-map of a precompact quasi-metric space is an isometry. We show that it need not be, even when the space is hereditarily precompact. On the integers, take the distance of an irrational rotation and add a fixed toll $c>0$ to every step from a nonnegative integer down to a smaller one. The resulting space, the toll spiral, is a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space, and the shift $n\mapsto n+1$ is a bijective non-contractive map that is not an isometry. The construction works over any metric space $Y$: for every bijective isometry $σ$ of $Y$ and every point whose $σ$-orbit is aperiodic and totally bounded, adding the same toll along the orbit gives such a counterexample, for instance over the $p$-adic odometer. The conjugate of the toll spiral is not even precompact, so the hypothesis on the conjugate in Zavarzina's positive result cannot be dropped, even for bijections. The toll spiral is also not expand-contract plastic, since the inverse shift is a non-expansive bijection that is not an isometry. For an arbitrary bijective non-contractive map $F$, the distance from $F^kx$ to $F^ky$ has a limit as $k\to-\infty$; $F$ is an isometry for this limit, and the excess $D_0$ of the distance over it is the defect. On a hereditarily precompact space, we prove a monochromy theorem: if a pair $(a,b)$ has positive defect $η$, then there are natural numbers $t_1<t_2<\cdots$ such that either $D_0(a,F^{-Δ}a)>η/4$ for every difference $Δ=t_j-t_i$ with $i<j$, or $D_0(F^{-Δ}b,b)>η/4$ for every such $Δ$. Three boundary results delimit the remaining question; the open case, that of separated spaces compact in one of their topologies, has since been settled by the author (arXiv:2610.14301). The construction, in general and for the circle, is machine-checked in Lean 4 using Mathlib, with no unproved steps.
Functional Analysis.comment: 18 pages. Lean 4 verification files included as ancillary files and archived with the paper at Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.22801324. v2: numbering unchanged; a note at the end of Section 7 reports what the author has since answered, including Questions 7.1 and 7.6

Functional Analysis.title: Reduced Embry characterizations of quasinormal operators
Functional Analysis.summary:
We prove that, for any two integers $2\le m<n$, a bounded operator $A$ on a complex Hilbert space satisfying \[
  A^{*k}A^k=(A^*A)^k,
  \qquad k\in\{m,n\}, \] is quasinormal. More generally, we show that the inequalities \[
  A^{*m}A^m\ge(A^*A)^m
  \quad \text{and} \quad
  A^{*n}A^n\le(A^*A)^n \] already imply quasinormality. Together with the known single-exponent counterexamples, this completely resolves the reduced Embry problem for bounded operators: the identities $A^{*k}A^k=(A^*A)^k$, $k\in S\subseteq\{1,2,\ldots\}$, characterize quasinormality if and only if $S$ contains at least two distinct integers greater than one. We also resolve the flatness problem for operators of class $\mathcal A$: equality between two consecutive normalized moments $(A^{*n}A^n)^{1/n}$ and $(A^{*(n+1)}A^{n+1})^{1/(n+1)}$, with $n\ge2$, implies quasinormality. Both results rely on an interpolation estimate obtained either from Hansen's inequality or from the transformer inequality for weighted operator geometric means. The solution to the reduced Embry problem additionally uses an extremal argument for optimal power bounds.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Quantitative global regularity for Navier--Stokes equations with odd viscosity on the cubic three-torus
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equation on the cubic torus with a constant odd-viscosity operator given by the vertical derivative of the curl. Arbitrary real, mean-zero, divergence-free initial data and an independent steady force, both in the second-order Sobolev space, admit a unique global strong solution when the magnitude of one fixed odd-viscosity coefficient is at least a norm-uniform sufficient threshold. In the unforced case the solution is smooth at positive times. The qualitative argument adapts the resonant-averaging framework for rapidly rotating fluids to the different odd-viscous dispersion. Weighted lattice counts and signed corrected-energy estimates yield a sufficient bound for the odd-to-ordinary viscosity ratio that is polynomial in the normalized initial-data radius at each fixed normalized force radius, together with a separate bound in a specified force-dominated regime. No optimality is claimed for the polynomial exponents or prefactors; determining the sharp viscosity threshold for the original equation remains open. Direct kinetic and weighted enstrophy barriers also give regularity for every coefficient on explicit bounded data and force regions, including the closed unforced ball of homogeneous second-order Fourier Sobolev radius ninety-seven fortieths times the viscosity and seven closed forced rectangles. We specify how finite certificates enter the analytic argument and distinguish minimization of a sufficient formula from sharpness for the original equation. All three main theorems are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Delaunay Asymptotics for the Singular Escobar-Yamabe Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In dimensions $n\geq3$, we prove that near an isolated boundary singularity a positive solution of the Escobar--Yamabe equation for a smooth metric approaches a fixed periodic Delaunay solution or the cylindrical solution if its trace lies between positive multiples of $|\overline x|^{-(n-2)/2}$, where $\overline x$ is the tangential Fermi coordinate. The relative error decays at a positive power rate, with weighted estimates through two derivatives in Fermi coordinates. The necksize is unique, and the translation parameter is unique modulo the least positive period in the periodic case. The Hamiltonian smoothly parametrizes the periodic family modulo translation. We classify Jacobi fields of polynomial growth at both ends without assuming symmetry. Translation and energy differentiation generate these fields along periodic solutions, and two oscillatory fields generate them along the cylindrical solution. We also exhibit a first-order obstruction to improving these asymptotics by boundary-preserving conformal deformations of the flat models.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stability of patterns in variational systems with continuous symmetries: a computer-assisted approach
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In variational models of pattern formation, periodic solutions are never isolated: since the energy does not change under translations, every shifted copy of a pattern is again a solution. This is an obstacle for computer-assisted proofs, which need isolated solutions. Imposing discrete symmetries removes the obstacle, but restricts the patterns that can be studied and only gives stability against symmetric perturbations. We develop a computer-assisted method that deals with the translations directly. We fix the position of the pattern with phase conditions and add unfolding parameters. They act as Lagrange multipliers, and translation invariance of the energy ensures that they vanish at a solution, under a condition that is verified rigorously by the computer. We then derive the stability of the pattern from the computer-assisted proof. We obtain the number of unstable directions and show that the only neutral directions are the translations. We apply the method to the Swift-Hohenberg equation in two dimensions and prove the existence of stable and unstable patterns without imposed symmetry. Since the linear algebra does not depend on the number of translation directions, the approach extends to higher dimensions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Normalized ground states as sharp dynamical thresholds for the inhomogeneous NLS with an inverse-square potential
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the focusing inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrödinger equation with an inverse-square potential, in the mass-supercritical and energy-subcritical regime and in every dimension $N\ge3$. Two lines of research on this model have so far developed separately, namely the scattering theory below the ground state and the variational theory of solutions with prescribed mass. We connect them. We compute explicitly the minimax level $m_a(c)$ of the energy on the Pohozaev manifold of mass $c$, introduced by Hajaiej, Luo and Wang, in terms of the sharp constant of the associated Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality. We prove that the minimizers of $m_a(c)$ are exactly the optimizers of this inequality lying on the Pohozaev manifold, and that they are ground states of the stationary problem. This answers a question left open by these authors. We then show that $m_a(c)$ is a sharp dynamical threshold. Below it, the sign of the Pohozaev functional is preserved by the flow. If this sign is positive, the solution is global. If it is negative and the datum has finite variance, the solution blows up in finite time. For the three-dimensional cubic model, the global solutions also scatter, by the scattering criterion of Hajaiej, Luo and Wang read in its scale-invariant form. As consequences, we obtain the strong instability of all normalized ground states, with destabilizing data on the same mass sphere, the strict monotonicity of the threshold with respect to the coupling constant, and a positive lower bound for $m_a(c)$ which is uniform up to the critical Hardy coupling.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: The title has been revised, and the presentation has been further enhanced and improved

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp double logarithmic $L^\infty$ bounds for second-order Sobolev functions in dimension four
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
Although $W^{2,2}(\mathbb{R}^{4})$ does not embed into $L^\infty$, we prove that radial symmetry allows the $L^\infty$ norm to be controlled by the homogeneous Sobolev seminorm $\dot H^2$, at the cost of a logarithmic correction involving a stronger Hölder-type norm.
  Our main result is a sharp double-logarithmic inequality with optimal leading constant $1/(8π^2α)$. We also establish a single-logarithmic estimate and prove the sharpness of its threshold. The optimal lower bound is derived by analysing a biharmonic obstacle problem with Hölder-type obstacle. A tailored penalization argument yields existence, uniqueness, and regularity of the minimizer, while an explicit transcendental equation for the free-boundary radius determines the sharp constant through its asymptotic behavior.
  These results provide fourth-order, four-dimensional analogues of the two-dimensional first-order inequalities of Ibrahim--Majdoub--Masmoudi (\textit{Proc.\ Amer.\ Math.\ Soc.}, 2007), with potential applications to fourth-order semilinear evolution equations with exponential nonlinearities.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: The title has been revised, and the presentation has been further enhanced and improved

Analysis of PDEs.title: A New Approach to Inspect Weakly Coupled Logistic Systems and their Asymptotic Behavior
On regularity and stability results of global weak solutions to two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with density-dependent viscosity and vacuum
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
For the initial and initial-boundary value problems of the two-dimensional (2D) incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with density-dependent viscosity and vacuum, Lions' global weak solutions are shown to possess additional regularity, via establishing some key a priori decay-in-time rates for the approximate problem, under suitable
  smallness condition on the density-dependent viscosity.
  In addition, large-time decay rates of the pressure and gradient of velocity are obtained,
  which are even exponential in time for bounded domains or the periodic case. Note that these results hold without any smallness conditions on the initial data, even for initially vanishing density.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Cheng--Yau gradient estimate for Jacobi fields
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove a pointwise gradient estimate for positive Jacobi fields on minimal hypersurfaces of dimension two and three, inspired by the Cheng--Yau estimate for harmonic functions. The estimate also controls the second fundamental form, and so provides yet another proof of the stable Bernstein theorem in dimensions two and three.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniform Exponential Stability Analysis of Impulsive Linear Time-Invariant Systems on Banach and Hilbert Spaces: Non-Coercive and Coercive Stability Conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the uniform exponential stability analysis of infinite-dimensional impulsive systems defined on a Banach or Hilbert space, whose flow is governed by a fixed $C_0$-semigroup generator and whose jumps occur at a prescribed time sequence. While the flow and jump maps are themselves time-invariant, the time-triggered impulses render the propagator a genuinely time-varying evolution family, which is the source of the analysis difficulty addressed here. We combine ideas from hybrid systems theory and infinite-dimensional systems to produce operator-based stability conditions, which can be analytically or numerically checked via convex programming. Necessary and sufficient conditions for the uniform exponential stability of impulsive systems on Banach spaces are obtained in the context of a fixed impulse-times sequence but also of arbitrary, constant, minimum, and range dwell-times using both non-coercive and coercive Lyapunov functionals. Some of those results are then adapted to systems on a Hilbert space and quadratic Lyapunov functionals. As an application, linear switched systems are shown to be an exact special case: reformulated as impulsive systems with unit-norm selector jumps, they inherit non-coercive and clock-dependent dwell-time stability conditions on both Banach and Hilbert spaces. Theoretical and numerical examples are given for illustration, notably on the sampled-data control of time-delay systems.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Relative isoperimetry in the three-dimensional cube: classification and quantitative stability
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We compute the relative isoperimetric profile of the three-dimensional unit cube. Up to cube isometries and complementation, its minimizers are corner eighth-balls, edge quarter-cylinders and coordinate slabs, with both adjacent families minimizing at $4π/81$ and $1/π$. At each fixed volume the perimeter deficit bounds the squared $L^1$ distance to the minimizing family, with optimal exponent two. Near each transition the deficit controls the minimum, over the two adjacent families, of squared distance plus excess perimeter. The best constant for distance to the minimizing family decays linearly as the volume approaches a transition. We also obtain the conjectured profile for $(0,β)\times(0,1)^2$, $0<β\le1$, and resolve the three-dimensional case of Brezis's Open Problem~10.1.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Convergence Analysis of an Upwind Finite-Difference Scheme for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the convergence of an upwind finite-difference scheme for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations on a one-dimensional periodic domain, considering both the value function and the feedback control selected by the discrete pointwise minimization. For classical value functions whose time and spatial derivatives are Hölder continuous in their respective variables, we bound the error at the grid points by a constant times the sum of the time step and spatial mesh width each raised to their common Hölder exponent. This yields first-order convergence when these derivatives are Lipschitz continuous and the meshes are refined proportionally. Under additional spatial regularity of the problem data, we also prove convergence of both one-sided difference quotients of the discrete value function to the spatial derivative of the value function: the integral over space and time of the absolute error tends to zero for each difference quotient. We further establish convergence of the discrete controls to the continuous feedback control when the continuous pointwise minimizer is unique, regardless of how the discrete minimizers are selected. These theoretical results are supported by numerical experiments that illustrate the accuracy of the value-function approximation and the behavior of the computed feedback controls.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Asymptotic stability of the 2D Boussinesq equations around Couette flow in infinite channel
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we investigate the stability threshold of the two-dimensional Boussinesq system around the Couette flow in an infinite channel $\mathbb{R}\times[-1,1]$ under Navier-slip boundary condition. To address nonlinear echo chains induced by temperature-vorticity coupling, we construct a two-level frequency-dependent temporal decomposition, with the two levels matched to the infinite and finite superposition principles for the equation, respectively. By fully exploiting the enhanced dissipation effect at each decomposition level, we prove that if the initial perturbation $(ω^{in}, θ^{in})$ around the Couette flow satisfies $\|ω^{in}\|_{H^4_{x,y}\cap L^1_xH^4_y}\leq cν^{\frac{1}{3}}$, and $\|θ^{in}\|_{H^5_{x,y}\cap L^1_xH^5_y}\leq cν^{\frac{2}{3}+}$, the Boussinesq system admits a globally asymptotically stable solution. It should be emphasized that the method in this paper provides an effective approach for the hydrodynamic equations with coupling effects.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Large Gap between Galerkin Errors with and without Mesh-Uniform Regularity for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We compare two cubic Hermite Galerkin semidiscretizations of the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation. They use the same trial space. The first is the weighted scheme considered in our previous paper (arXiv:2610.39269), called the W-scheme. It has mesh-uniform regularity: the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit Crandall-Pazy regularity and Kato smoothing, with bounds uniform in the mesh size $h$. The second is the standard Galerkin method in $L^2$, called the S-scheme. It has no mesh-uniform regularity. For the W-scheme, the full error and the ordering error converge at an algebraic rate in $h$, uniformly on $[t_0,\infty)$ times small balls of $L^2$ for any fixed $t_0>0$. They are bounded by $Ch^p\varepsilon$ and $Ch^p\varepsilon^2$, respectively, where $\varepsilon$ is the size of the datum and $p>0$. We prove that neither bound holds for the S-scheme by using exact high-frequency spurious eigenpairs of the S-scheme. The existence of such eigenpairs for fine meshes with at least 512 elements has a proof checked by Lean 4. Computations compare the two schemes on unit-norm data built from these eigenfunctions, on 512, 1024 and 2048 elements. The full error of the S-scheme stays at $4.6\times10^{-2}$. That of the W-scheme is at most $2.2\times10^{-9}$. The ordering error of the S-scheme stays at $9.6\times10^{-6}$. That of the W-scheme falls from $2.3\times10^{-9}$ to $1.4\times10^{-10}$. Their ratio grows from $4.2\times10^3$ to $6.6\times10^4$.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 44 pages, 2 figures. Ancillary files: the Lean 4 development for Theorem 3.1, and the programs, outputs and logs of the computations

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Higher-Dimensional Nitsche Conjecture: Sharp Bounds and Rigidity
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
Let $n\ge3$ and let $h:\A(r,1)\to\A(R,1)\subset\mathbb R^n$ be an onto homeomorphism with harmonic coordinate functions. We prove the sharp Nitsche bound \[
  R\le R_{n,+}(r):=\frac{nr}{n-1+r^n}, \] and, when $h$ interchanges the two ends, the strictly stronger sharp bound \[
  R\le R_{n,-}(r):=\frac{nr^{n-1}}{1+(n-1)r^n}. \] In each case, equality holds only for the corresponding radial harmonic homeomorphism, up to an orthogonal transformation.
  Both bounds and their equality cases extend to bounded harmonic maps in every dimension $n\ge2$. This requires nonzero degree of $h/|h|$ on interior spheres, $|h|\ge R$, and the corresponding $L^2$ limits of the modulus at the two ends. In the plane, we also prove the nonzero-winding-number conjecture of Iwaniec--Kovalev--Onninen [\emph{J. Amer. Math. Soc.} \textbf{24} (2011), 345--373], without endpoint modulus conditions.
