  We prove a sharp $L^1$ contraction theorem for vector measures associated with spherical couplings. The first marginal is uniform, while the second is unrestricted. For bounded nonnegative nondecreasing zonal kernels, the optimal constant is the degree-one multiplier. If the kernel is also strictly increasing, equality holds exactly for couplings supported on orthogonal graphs. This theorem is the main tool in the proofs of the annular bounds and their rigidity.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Single-point determination of a potential and a nonlinearity in a semilinear biharmonic equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the inverse problem of determining the coefficient $q$ and the nonlinearity $F$ in the semilinear biharmonic equation $Δ^2 u+q(x)u=F(x,u)$ with Navier boundary data. The measurement consists of $\partial_νu(x_0)$ at a fixed boundary point $x_0$. We apply the mixed variation approach to linearize the nonlinear problem and construct semiclassical boundary-localized solutions for the linearized equation. Under suitable analyticity, nonresonance, and nondegeneracy assumptions on $q$ and $F$, we prove that this boundary point measurement uniquely determines both $q$ and $F$. We also establish boundary determination of all normal derivatives of $q$ and of the first nonzero Taylor coefficient of $F$ on a nonempty relatively open subset of the boundary. When the linear potential $q$ is known, we prove that either component of the Navier boundary input alone suffices to determine $F$, and that the polynomial nonlinearity can be uniquely determined without requiring any analyticity conditions. For suitable finite-dimensional classes of nonanalytic potentials, we also obtain, for fixed $F$, the stable determination of $q$ from finitely many boundary inputs and the associated point measurements. In addition, as an important supplement, we provide nontrivial examples verifying the main assumptions, as well as counterexamples concerning the recovery of the linear coefficient. Finally, we present numerical experiments that demonstrate the theoretical results.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A SHARP MASS THRESHOLD FOR BOUNDEDNESS IN A CRITICAL QUASILINEAR CHEMOTAXIS MODEL WITH INDIRECT SIGNAL PRODUCTION: THE RADIALLY SYMMETRIC CASE
Analysis of PDEs.summary: A critical quasilinear chemotaxis model with indirect signal production in space dimensions higher than two is studied under radial symmetry. Exploiting the variational structure of the system, the existence of a sharp mass threshold M\textsubscr{c} > 0 is established: all solutions with mass below M\textsubscr{c} are global and bounded, while those with mass above M\textsubscr{c} and sufficiently negative energy are global but blow up in infinite time. Moreover, the value of the critical mass M\textsubscr{c} is related to the best constant of a variant of a Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Scattering for the KP-II equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove scattering in $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ for real-valued solutions of the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili II (KP-II) equation with localized initial data. The localization is measured in scale-invariant Lorentz or mixed Lebesgue spaces. The admissible data include all real-valued Schwartz functions. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result establishing scattering for the KP-II equation for every real-valued Schwartz initial datum, without any smallness assumption and without the zero mean condition. We also show that some localization is necessary: there are smooth real-valued initial data of arbitrarily small $L^2$ norm, with a logarithmic moment, for which the solution does not scatter in $L^2$.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 94 pages. The scattering theorem is extended to more initial data. This version also constructs smooth initial data of arbitrarily small $L^2$ norm whose solutions fail to scatter in $L^2$ in both time directions

Analysis of PDEs.title: Exponential mixing for the randomized two-vortex model
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper investigates the mixing of passive scalars advected by a randomized two-vortex model on $\mathbb{T}^2$, in which the vortices interact through a regularized Biot--Savart kernel and are driven by independent Brownian motions. We establish quenched exponential mixing for the Lagrangian flow, characterized by the exponential correlation decay of mean-zero $H^s$ observables. The proof proceeds by establishing ergodicity of the associated two-point Markov process. We combine a uniform contraction estimate with controllability arguments to verify the Lyapunov drift and minorization conditions, allowing us to apply Harris-type theorem.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence of a non-zero steady-state solution to a population density equation subject to horizontal transfer
Analysis of PDEs.summary: From plasmid dynamics and efflux pump expression in bacteria to risk-taking behaviour in human groups, horizontal interactions can drive the transmission of deleterious traits that spread despite carrying no selective advantage, thereby burdening the population. How can such detrimental traits persist, and under what conditions can the population avoid extinction?  To address these questions, we model a population structured by a continuous trait representing individual burden within a non-linear, non-local integro-differential framework. From an analytical perspective, mutations are modeled via a jump operator rather than a diffusion term; consequently, the mutation operator lacks regularizing properties and is generally non-self-adjoint. Moreover, working in a weighted L 1 setting precludes the direct application of standard Krein-Rutman theory. To overcome these hurdles, we construct a custom fixed-point operator by first freezing the non-linearities to solve an auxiliary eigenvalue problem, and then tuning the resulting principal eigenvalue. Applying the Leray-Schauder fixed-point theorem to this operator rigorously yields the existence of a non-trivial steady state. Finally, numerical simulations illustrate the qualitative dynamics of the model and delineate the parameter regimes governing population persistence and extinction.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Non-connected minimal clusters of small volume in a compact Finsler manifold
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that isoperimetric clusters in general Finsler manifolds can be disconnected even when the volume constraint is small. This is in contrast with the Riemannian case and the ``fixed-norm'' case, where connectedness for arbitrarily small volume has recently been proved.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Microlocal properties of Cauchy evolution under metric variations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We develop the microlocal analysis of the Cauchy evolution for wave-type equations on the infinite-dimensional space of Lorentzian metrics. We regard the Cauchy evolution operator as a distributional function of the metric, and give this notion a precise meaning through restrictions to finite-dimensional families of metrics. We study the singularities of this metric dependence. For normally hyperbolic operators on vector bundles, we determine the resulting operator-valued wavefront sets. Their parameter covectors are given by integrals of metric variations along individual null geodesics. At ultrastatic ends, metric dependence also determines the time-translation generators and their positive- and negative-energy splitting. More generally, the parameter singularities distinguish the two characteristic sheets and can be used to reconstruct the ordinary Cauchy propagation relation, which describes propagation of singularities. Consequences include smoothing under parameter averaging and polar-cone bounds associated with averaged null-positive variations, linking the result to averaged null energy conditions. The analysis also covers the Cauchy evolution of the Dirac equation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Fujita exponents beyond integrable forcing
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We develop a unified framework for Fujita-type blow-up of solutions to the inhomogeneous semilinear heat equation $$\partial_tu-Δu=|u|^p+\mathbf{w}(x), \qquad (t,x)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^N, \qquad u(0, \cdot)=u_0.$$ The classical integrability assumptions on the forcing term are replaced by quantitative regular variation properties of its spatial mass $$F(R)=\int\limits_{|x|\le R}\mathbf{w}(x)\,dx.$$ Using techniques from regular variation theory together with the Mitidieri--Pohozaev test-function method, we establish sharp Fujita-type nonexistence results and identify the critical exponent in terms of the variation index of $F$. We prove that global solutions do not exist in the subcritical range and obtain critical-case blow-up under suitable slowly varying corrections.
  The regular variation framework further shows the optimality of the underlying mass condition, extends naturally to anisotropic settings through operator regular variation, and yields sufficient blow-up criteria for sign-changing forcings via the Gaussian-Laplace transform. The approach also applies to space-time dependent forcings, Riesz-potential type forcings, and equations involving the fractional Laplacian, providing a unified description of blow-up thresholds beyond the classical Fujita theory.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: The title has been revised, and the presentation has been further enhanced and improved

Analysis of PDEs.title: An almost sharp tomas-stein restriction theorem for a class of anisotropic operators
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $d\geq 2$. For each $j\in \{1,\dots,d\}$, let ${\ell}_{j}\geq 1$ and $m_{j}\geq 2$ be integers, and let $a_{j}$ be a nonzero real number. We prove that the oscillatory integral operator \begin{equation*} T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} e^{\dot{\imath} \left(a_{1}x^{{\ell}_{1}}_{1}y^{m_{1}}_{1}+\dots +a_{d}x^{{\ell}_{d}}_{d}y^{m_{d}}_{d} \right)}f(y)dy,\;\;\; x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation*} satisfies the restriction estimate \begin{equation*} \|T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{d})}, \end{equation*} for each $1\leq p\leq 2$, whenever $(\frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}-\frac{1}{m_{j}}+1)\frac{2}{p^{\prime}}\geq 1$, for every $j\in Γ$, and \begin{equation*} \mathcal{E}:=\min{\left\{\min_{1\leq j\leq d}{\frac{m_{j}}{{\ell}_{j}}},\,\min_{1\leq k\leq d}{\frac{d-1}{\sum_{j\neq k} \frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}+\frac{2}{m_{k}}}}\right\}}> \frac{2}{p^{\prime}}. \end{equation*} We also give counterexamples that show that the condition $\mathcal{E}\geq 2/p^{\prime}$ is necessary for this restriction inequality.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Branch Obstructions for Area-Minimizing Currents and Flat Critical Points of Weakly-Conformal Maps
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study two problems motivated by the local geometry of conformal $φ$-curves. First, let $T$ be a $k$-dimensional locally area-minimizing integral current in Euclidean space, with $k\geq3$, codimension at least two, no boundary, and a locally conformally flat induced metric on $\operatorname{reg} T$. We prove the following branch obstruction: at any rapid-decay branch point whose planar frequency differs from $2$, every nonzero cyclic component of every cylindrical normalized tangent function has repetition multiplicity at least two. Consequently, the nonintegral-frequency points of densities $2$ and $3$ in the rapid-decay branch set have Hausdorff dimension at most $k-3$. On the full branch set, they have zero $\mathcal H^{k-2}$ measure. These conclusions apply to Euclidean image currents of conformal $φ$-curves with locally conformally flat domains, provided the image currents satisfy the stated hypotheses.
  Second, for $C^j$ weakly-conformal maps between smooth Riemannian manifolds, with domain dimension $k\geq3$ and $j\geq2$, we prove that all derivatives of orders $1$ through $j$ vanish at every critical point. As a consequence, for smooth weakly-conformal maps with connected domain, we establish a curvature condition under which the map is constant or has no critical points. The flatness and continuation results apply in particular to conformal $φ$-curves with the corresponding regularity and curvature assumptions. Finally, we examine the Borůvka cone, which illustrates the role of regularity and the distinction between critical points and branch points.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A capillary logarithmic Gauss curvature flow and the capillary Minkowski problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a logarithmic Gauss curvature flow of strictly convex capillary hypersurfaces in the Euclidean half-space. For an acute contact angle and an arbitrary positive smooth prescribed function, we prove that a suitable initial dilation yields a global solution which converges smoothly after a horizontal translation with a uniquely determined constant velocity. As an application, we provide a logarithmic flow proof of the capillary Minkowski problem, previously established by Mei-Wang-Weng [Adv. Math. 469, 110230 (2025)].

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Hadamard Formula for Equilibrium Envelopes under Parallel Deformation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $(X,ω_0)$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $U\Subset X$ have $C^{3,1}$ uniformly strongly pseudoconvex boundary. Consider the signed parallel family $U_t=\{ρ<t\}$, where $ρ$ is a defining function agreeing near $\partial U$ with the signed distance, negative in $U$. Let $u_t$ be the equilibrium envelope with zero obstacle on $X\setminus U_t$, and write $Σ_t=\partial U_t$, with outward unit normal $ν_t$. We prove that the normalized Monge--Ampère energy $e(t)=E_{ω_0}(u_t)$ belongs to $C^{1,1/2}([-τ,τ])$ for some $τ>0$ and satisfies the Hadamard formula $$ e'(t)=\frac{1}{n+1}\int_{Σ_t}\left(-\partial_{ν_t}u_t\right)^2 dσ_{ρ,t}^{\mathrm{tot}}, |t|<τ. $$ Here $dσ_{ρ,t}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the interior outward Anzellotti trace of $$ \frac{1}{V} d^cρ\wedge \sum_{p=0}^{n-1}(p+1) ω_{u_t}^{p}\wedgeω_0^{n-1-p}, V=\int_Xω_0^n, ω_{u_t}=ω_0+dd^c u_t. $$ This measure is positive and uniformly comparable to the induced surface measure. The proof combines uniform $C^{1,1}$ estimates up to the boundary from the interior with $1/2$-Hölder stability of the normal derivatives under the normal-flow identifications. We identify the boundary part of the normalized Monge--Ampère measure with the negative outward trace of a divergence-measure flux current. The one-sided weak-* limits of the mixed Bedford--Taylor boundary measures yield the weighted total flux appearing in the variation formula.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 34 pages, 1 figure. Revised exposition and proofs, including clarifications of the boundary densities and uniform regularity estimates; corrected references. Comments are welcome!

Analysis of PDEs.title: Positive solutions of power equations in planar corner domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study positive solutions of $Δu=λu^k$ on bounded planar corner domains with zero boundary values away from the vertex. For negative-power absorption we identify the admissible interval of Martin masses and prove uniqueness at the minimum mass. Along the ordinary boundary, we identify the weak Hessian endpoint and its sharp tail when the set of zero inward derivative has positive length. For superlinear sources we prove attainment of the largest positive Martin mass in the subcritical range. At criticality we construct a family of singular solutions with zero Martin mass and distinguish its members by their second logarithmic coefficient and the endpoint integrability of their Hessian differences. Above criticality an angular eigenvalue governs the Morse index away from its zero threshold. We also give sharp physical-Hessian asymptotics for finite-mass remainders and joint corner and side estimates for negative-power sources.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Silverman-Meadows-type criterion for the null controllability of time-dependent coupled heat equations with non-diagonalizable diffusion matrices
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper is devoted to a uniform spectral Silverman-Meadows rank condition for the nullcontrollability of coupled systems of heat equations with time-dependent diffusion, coupling and control matrices. The proof relies on an adaptation of the Lebeau-Robbiano strategy combined with uniform finite-dimensional observability estimates associated with each Laplace eigenmode.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Persistence in weighted Sobolev spaces for the Calogero-Moser derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper is devoted to the study of invariant weighted Sobolev spaces for the Calogero--Moser derivative nonlinear Schrödinger (CMDNLS) equation on the real line. For \(s\geq 1\) and \(0\leq r\leq s\), we first prove that the \(H^s(\mathbb R)\) flow preserves the condition \((1+x^2)^{r/2}u\in L^2(\mathbb R)\). The proof uses truncated weighted energy estimates and weighted interpolation. We then establish the persistence of weighted regularity for spatial derivatives. For integers \(p\geq 3\) and \(1\leq m\leq p-2\), and for \(0\leq r\leq p-m \), the \(H^p(\mathbb R)\) flow preserves the conditions \((1+x^2)^{r/2}\partial_x^j u\in L^2(\mathbb R)\) for \(0\leq j\leq m\). This result combines weighted energy estimates, the unitary equivalence and the integrable structure of the CMDNLS equation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the Abels--Garcke--Grün Model for Incompressible Two-Phase Flows with Unmatched Densities: Phase Separation and Rayleigh--Taylor Instability
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Instability phenomena are ubiquitous in multi-fluid flows. For binary fluid mixtures, phase separation may occur under specific conditions, in which a homogeneous state becomes unstable and spontaneously segregates into different phases, leading to the formation of distinct patterns. Furthermore, when a heavier fluid is superposed over a lighter one in a gravitational field, the fluid interface can be sensitive to perturbations that trigger the Rayleigh--Taylor (RT) instability, i.e., the lighter fluid penetrates upward into the heavier fluid against gravity. We investigate such instability phenomena and the inhibiting conditions for incompressible, immiscible two-phase flows with unmatched densities, within the framework of a diffuse-interface model, which is called the Abels--Garcke--Grün (AGG) model. More precisely, we adopt energy methods to establish several stability/instability conditions for the perturbed system of the AGG model, which is obtained by slightly perturbing the equilibrium profile $(\mathbf{0},\overline{\varphi})$, where $\overline{\varphi}=\overline{\varphi}(x_3)$ depends solely on the vertical coordinate $x_3$. Notably, for a constant equilibrium profile $\overline{\varphi}=α\in(-1,1)$ satisfying $Ψ''(α)<0$, we establish a threshold for stability and instability of the phase-separation problem.Similar stability results are also established for the perturbed system with $\overline{\varphi}$ satisfying the RT instability condition in the presence of gravity. In particular, if the phase-separation condition fails and $\partial_{x_3}\overline{\varphi}$ is a constant, a larger value of $\partial_{x_3}\overline{\varphi}$, a greater interfacial thickness and a higher surface energy density contribute to inhibiting RT instability.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Asymptotic spreading of Fisher-KPP equations in shifting environments with time-periodic limits
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the rightward spreading speed of solutions for Fisher-KPP equations in shifting environments. The linear growth rate has time periodic limits at the two ends of the moving frame. Each limit has a positive average and may be negative during a period. When the growth rate lies between the two limits at each time, we show that the spreading speed depends only on their averages and the asymptotic shift speed. For intermediate shift speeds, the formulas give nonlocal pulling if the right end has the larger average and speed locking if the left end has the larger average. The interior growth profile may be nonmonotone in space and aperiodic in time. We prove the formulas by constructing upper and lower solutions for a stepwise profile and then comparing with shifted stepwise problems.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck Operator
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the subellipticity of the analytically deformed Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator and give two definitions of resonances, one based on analytic dilation and the other on analytic distortion in the $x$-variables. Due to the failure of global subellipticity of the distorted operator in dimensions $n \geq 2$, the second method can only be used in dimension one. We show that, whenever both methods are applicable, they give rise to the same set of resonances. We also prove that, when $|\na V(x)| = O(\w x^{-ρ})$ with $ρ>1$, positive resonances are embedded eigenvalues and/or scattering resonances whose resonant states belong to weighted $L^2$-spaces and satisfy an outgoing radiation condition.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Generation of semigroups for vector-valued pseudodifferential operators on the torus with space-dependent symbols
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider toroidal pseudodifferential operators with spatially dependent, operator-valued symbols of positive order and finite regularity. For an arbitrary complex Banach space $E$, we prove that the negative of the closure of a parabolic operator on $C^\infty(\mathbb T^n,E)$ generates an analytic semigroup on $W_p^k(\mathbb T^n,E)$, where $1\le p<\infty$ and $k\in\mathbb N_0$, provided the symbol has sufficiently many spatial derivatives and discrete differences. The proof combines uniform estimates for parameter-dependent kernels with right and left parametrices. It does not require the UMD property of $E$. Real interpolation gives corresponding resolvent estimates on $B_{pq}^s(\mathbb T^n,E)$ for $0<s<k$ and $1\le q\le\infty$. The induced semigroups are strongly continuous for $q<\infty$ and on the little Besov spaces when $q=\infty$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A method of moving planes for a mixed local-nonlocal parabolic equation with quenching
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper we develop a parabolic version of the method of moving planes on systems with a mixed local and nonlocal diffusion operator, that being $\mathcal{L} = -(-Δ)^s + Δ$, where $(-Δ)^s$ is the integral fractional laplacian. We then use this result to study the quenching phenomena occurring in said systems with a singular absorption term of the type $(1-u)^{-p}$. We prove that there exists a range of multiplicative parameters for which every solution presents quenching, and that for any initial datum $u_0$, there exists a small enough multiplicative parameter such as the solution is globally defined. We also prove that the quenching phenomena cannot happen arbitrarily close to the boundary, but they are contained in a compact subset of the domain.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp condition for Superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We determine the sharp condition for local superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation $(-Δ)^m u=u^{\frac{n+2m}{n-2m}}$, where $m\geq2$ is an integer and $n>2m$. For a solution in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at zero, local superharmonicity holds if and only if \(\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)>0\). The threshold is sharp. In the biharmonic case $m=2$, for every $n\geq5$, we construct smooth positive solutions of $Δ^2u=u^{\frac{n+4}{n-4}}$ in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at $0$, satisfying $\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)=0$ and $\limsup_{x\to0}u(x)=+\infty$, while $-Δu$ converges to a finite negative limit along a fixed ray. The construction relies on an infinite array of concentrating bubbles arranged on concentric polygons, with a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction controlling their interactions against a vanishing background.

Analysis of PDEs.title: An optimal local theory for reaction-diffusion equations driven by non-trace-class noise
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study local well-posedness for a class of stochastic reaction-diffusion equations driven by multiplicative, possibly colored, noise. The interaction between rough stochastic forcing and polynomial nonlinearities naturally leads to solutions with low spatial regularity, making the treatment of the nonlinear terms delicate. Our main contribution is a general local existence and uniqueness theory for SPDEs with rough noise and highly irregular initial data. The framework also yields new results in standard noise regimes, including trace-class noise and space-time white noise. We identify the critical initial-data spaces for a wide range of nonlinearities, and we establish instantaneous parabolic regularization, general blow-up criteria, and sufficient conditions for positivity preservation. We apply the abstract theory to several prototypical models, including the stochastic Allen-Cahn, Burgers, Fisher-KPP, and coupled Gray-Scott equations. Finally, in the one-dimensional space-time white-noise setting, we combine our local theory with existing global a priori results in a highly singular regime.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 50 pages; Corrected some mistakes and typographical errors identified with the assistance of LLM

Analysis of PDEs.title: Lie-Lions brackets of nonlocal vector fields
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study nonlocal vector fields on the space of probability measures with finite second moment. Using Lions derivatives, we define their Lie-Lions bracket, which adds to the spatial Lie bracket a correction due to the evolution of the law, and prove that its vanishing is equivalent to commutation of the global flows, under first-order regularity and linear growth assumptions. We then construct a Lie algebra of complete polynomial nonlocal fields. For this class, we establish commutator and second-order Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formulas with cubic remainders in the Wasserstein distance $W_2$, controlled by the second moment and uniform in the number of particles. The proofs rely on finite-particle realizations, which preserve the bracket and jointly determine the nonlocal field. We also obtain uniform estimates for smooth bounded kernels and a Leibniz rule for the action of polynomial fields on polynomial observables. Examples from collective dynamics show that the vanishing of the spatial bracket at a fixed law is neither necessary nor sufficient for commutation. They concern symmetries, aggregation-dependent rotation, synchronization, the transmission of a turn along a hierarchy, effective three-body interactions and occupancy-dependent circulation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Regularity of Lipschitz free boundaries for weak solutions of Alt-Caffarelli type problems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Motivated by the Serrin problem, we study weak solutions of the generalised Alt-Caffarelli problem $-Δu = f$ in $Ω$, $u = 0$ on $\partialΩ$, $\partial_νu = Q$ on $\partialΩ$. Our main result establishes that if $Ω$ is Lipschitz, then it is actually $C^{\infty}$ (provided that $f$ and $Q$ are smooth). This was known before only for viscosity solutions. As a corollary, we obtain an alternative solution of Serrin's problem in the case of Lipschitz domains. We also discuss the characterisation of the regularity of Lipschitz domains in terms of their Poisson kernel.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Version changes: we added the missing hypothesis Q > 0 in Theorem 1.4

Analysis of PDEs.title: Smooth asymptotically Self-similar blow up for the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We construct blow up solutions to the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$. More precisely, we construct the solutions $(ψ,n)$ defined for $t\in[0,T)$, blowing up at $t=T$ and taking the form
  \begin{align}
  ψ(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{T-t}P\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right)e^{i(T-t)^{-1/3}},
  n(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{3(T-t)^{4/3}}N\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right)
  \end{align}
  in the region $|x|\ll 1$. Here $(P,N)$ is the solution to a specified ODE system related to Zakharov system.
  The solutions we construct are smooth for $0\leq t<T$. Moreover, there exist $n_0,n_1\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^3\backslash\{0\})$ with bounded support such that for any $r>0$, $(ψ,n,\partial_t n)$ converge to $(0,n_0,n_1)$ in $C^{\infty}(|x|>r)$.
  We correct the profile $(P,N)$ and obtain a sequence of approximate solutions that coincide in the region $|x|\gtrsim 1$ with higher and higher accuracy. Then we apply perturbative analysis to construct solutions with arbitrarily high finite regularity. The fixed point argument in this procedure actually yields that these solutions are the same for $t$ sufficiently close to $T$, which combined with the persistence of high regularity gives the existence of smooth asymptotically self-similar blow up solutions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness of positive solutions of mixed Laplacian and fractional Laplacian in $\mathbb R$
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We establish the uniqueness and nondegeneracy for positive finite-energy solutions of the following one-dimensional mixed Schrödinger equation \begin{equation}
  -Q'' + (-Δ)^s Q + Q = |Q|^p Q \quad \text{in } \mathbb R, \end{equation} where $0<s<1$ and $p>0$.
  For every $0<s<1, p>0$, we obtain the corresponding results for positive solutions whose linearized operators have Morse index equal to one. We extend the nodal analysis developed by Frank-Lenzmann-Silvestre to the mixed operator establishing the monotonicity of the quotient of a hypothetical nontrivial even kernel element by $-Q'$. We then combine this monotonicity with oscillation estimates to prove nondegeneracy, and uniqueness follows by continuation.
  Moreover, for every $1/2\le s<1,p>0$, both uniqueness and nondegeneracy hold for positive solutions. Our novelty is to use the properties of Green kernel of the mixed operator to derive the upper bound and lower bound on the maximum of each solution. This peak estimate allows us to prove uniqueness by direct comparison and to establish nondegeneracy.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence of two-dimensional deep capillary solitary water waves with constant vorticity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider two-dimensional capillary water waves with nonzero constant vorticity in infinite depth. We first derive the Babenko equation that describes the profile of the solitary wave. When the velocity $c$ is close to a critical velocity, the Babenko equation can be reduced to the stationary focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation plus perturbative error. This gives the existence of small-amplitude solitary wave solutions for the water wave system with constant vorticity whose profiles are close to solutions of the stationary focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global compactness results for fractional $p$-Laplace Hardy Sobolev operator on a bounded domain
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we establish a Struwe type global compactness result for a class of nonlinear critical Hardy-Sobolev exponent problems driven by the fractional $p$-Laplace Hardy-Sobolev operator.

Analysis of PDEs.title: BMO Vorticity Strong Ill-Posedness for the 2d Incompressible Euler Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For the two dimensional incompressible Euler equation, Yudovich, and independently Serfati, extended the classical existence and uniqueness class to include vorticity with mild singularity. This class is sometimes called the generalized Yudovich class. Then, Vishik extended the uniqueness class to include vorticity in BMO, allowing for stronger singularities than the generalized Yudovich class. In this work, we prove strong ill-posedness of vorticity in BMO.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Normalized solutions for Schrödinger-Maxwell equation with Sobolev critical and mass subcritical perturbation
An operator theoretical approach to weak solvability of a porous medium equation with Neumann boundary condition
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
This paper is concerned with the Neumann problem for the porous medium equation, \[
  u_t - Δa(u) = f \quad \mbox{in}\ Ω\times (0, T), \qquad
  \nabla a(u) \cdot ν=0
  \quad \mbox{on}\ \partial Ω\times (0, T),
  \qquad u(\cdot, 0) = u_0
  \quad \mbox{in}\ Ω\] in a smoothly bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^N$ $(N \in \mathbb{N})$, where $T \in (0,\infty)$, $ν$ is the outward unit normal vector to $\partial Ω$, and where $f$ and $u_0$ are given. A typical example in mind is $a(u)=|u|^{p-2}u$ with $p \in [2, \infty)$. The main interest is weak solvability of the problem in the case that $u_0 \in H^1(Ω)^*$, $f \in L^2(0,T; H^1(Ω)^*)$. Under the condition that the mean value of $f(t)$ vanishes for almost all $t \in (0,T)$, existence of weak solutions is established by an application of abstract results from operator theory, for instance, properties of Gâteaux derivative. The key of the proof lies in the approximate equation \[
  [(\varepsilon I - Δ)^{-1} u_\varepsilon]_t
  + a(u_\varepsilon) = (\varepsilon I - Δ)^{-1} f,
  \quad \varepsilon \in (0,1), \] where the map $\varepsilon I - Δ$ from $H^1(Ω)$ onto its dual space is regarded as the Riesz isomorphism of $H^1(Ω)$ equipped with an appropriate topology.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On evolution of mean curvature and minimal areas in general codimension for inverse problems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Many seemingly standard formulas for the evolution of the mean curvature vector in higher codimension assume only normal variations, which are ill-suited for analyzing the evolution of submanifolds- with-boundary whose boundaries may not be moving orthogonally at each time. Such situations arise when one considers inverse problems for minimal areas, for example, where such boundaries are confined to a larger ambient boundary. In this note, we provide coordinate-free identities for use in such problems, including higher order derivatives of mean curvature. We translate these identities to some of the existing inverse problem literature in codimension one. We also hope readers may find the computational framework helpful in other situations arising in geometric analysis.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the free-boundary incompressible porous media equations with surface tension
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the free-boundary incompressible porous media equations with surface tension in dimension $1+d$. For fixed positive surface tension, we establish local well-posedness for arbitrary initial interfaces in $H^{s+1}$ and density perturbations in $H^s$, with $s>(d+3)/2$. When $s>(d+5)/2$, we justify the local vanishing-surface-tension limit for stable interfaces and sufficiently small density perturbations. In a finite-depth strip over $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a flat bottom and fixed positive surface tension, we prove global well-posedness and uniform anisotropic energy bounds for small compatible perturbations of an equilibrium with strictly stable stratification, under a horizontal low-frequency condition.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Partition-of-Unity Gaussian Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Gaussian basis functions provide an efficient and flexible alternative to spline activations in Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs), but their performance is sensitive to the Gaussian scale parameter ε. We introduce the partition-of-unity Gaussian KAN (PU-GKAN), a kernel-based normalization framework that transfers the Shepard partition-of-unity principle to trainable KAN edge functions. Each Gaussian edge basis is normalized by its local sum over fixed centers, preserving the standard edge-based architecture and essentially the same trainable coefficient structure as GKAN. The resulting feature map reproduces constants exactly at the edge level and admits an explicit normalized finite-feature kernel interpretation. Numerical experiments show that PU-GKAN reduces sensitivity to ε, improves validation accuracy for most smooth and moderately non-smooth targets, and provides more stable training behavior. These benefits persist across variations in sample size and number of centers, higher-dimensional architectures, and Matern RBF bases. PU-GKAN also improves physics-informed neural networks for Helmholtz and wave equations, with validation-error reductions of up to 90%. These results establish partition-of-unity normalization as a mathematically grounded and broadly applicable framework for improving the reliability and accuracy of radial basis function KANs.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the sharp weak-type inequality for Riesz transforms
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that the weak-type $(1,1)$ norm of each classical Riesz transform $R_j$, $j=1,\dots,n$, on real-valued inputs on $\R^n$ and $\T^n$ is $\KD$. The constant $\KD=π^2/(8\Gcat)$, where $\Gcat$ is Catalan's constant, was obtained by Davis \cite{Davis1974} for the Hilbert transform on $\R$ and the conjugate-function operator on the circle $\T$. The Burkholder--Bellman function argument also applies to coordinate Riesz transforms of product generators. If $-L$ generates a symmetric sub-Markov semigroup on a nonzero standard $σ$-finite measure space $Y$, then $-\partial_x(-\partial_x^2+L)^{-1/2}$ has the same exact norm on both $\mathbb R\times Y$ and $\mathbb T\times Y$. The derivative acts in the ordinary line or circle factor, while $L$ governs the independent transverse variables. An explicit integral inequality strengthens the weak-type estimate and bounds the truncated second moment of the transform. The general theorem applies to Gaussian, Dunkl, Laguerre, Jacobi, Schrödinger, and Laplace--Beltrami transverse generators, finite reversible chains, and subordinated semigroups.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonexistence of cusp singularities for gravity waves of extreme form
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper we revisit the geometric approach developed by Vărvărucă and Weiss for the Stokes conjecture for gravity water waves near stagnation points, in both the irrotational and rotational settings. They introduced monotonicity formulas and frequency formulas to classify all possible singularities of solutions at stagnation points. Two questions were left open: 1. whether cusp singularities can be excluded in higher dimensions $n\geq 3$ [Acta Math. 206 (2011)]; 2. whether cusp singularities for rotational waves can be excluded under the Rayleigh-Taylor condition [Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré C Anal. Non Linéaire 29 (2012)]. We answer both questions in the affirmative. Our main results show that cusp singularities do not exist in higher dimensions and cannot occur for rotational waves even without assuming the Rayleigh-Taylor condition. Our argument combines a delicate analysis of the weighted volume arising from the corresponding free boundary problem with a weighted isoperimetric inequality.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Alt-Phillips Multiple Membrane Free Boundary Problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Motivated by diffusion--reaction processes in porous catalysts, we study an Alt--Phillips model for ordered membranes with weighted gap interactions. The model connects adhesive harmonic junctions \cite{DSS24} and forced multiple membranes \cite{SY19} through the exponent $0<γ<1$. For arbitrary positive weights, we prove optimal $C^{1,β-1}$ regularity, where $β=2/(2-γ)$, and obtain nontrivial $β$-homogeneous blowup limits through Weiss almost monotonicity. Under strict discrete concavity of the weights, we establish a gluing principle, minimality of flat single-gap cones, and $C^{1,α}$ free boundary regularity at points admitting such blowups. We also classify all one-dimensional vertically critical cones. For three membranes, we identify cone families that are non-minimizing for small $γ$ and minimizing near $γ=1$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the Stokes conjecture for compressible gravity waves of extreme form
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
In 1880, G. G. Stokes [Mathematical and Physical Papers, Vol.I] examined an extreme two-dimensional irrotational periodic traveling water wave under the influence of gravity and conjectured a symmetric corner of \(120^\circ\) at the crest. The conjecture was first proved rigorously by Amick, Fraenkel, and Toland [Acta Math. 148 (1982)] and, independently, by Plotnikov [Dinamika Sploshn. Sredy 57 (1982)] via the Nekrasov integral equation. In the early 2010s, Varvarua and Weiss [Acta Math. 206 (2011)] revisited the conjecture by introducing a novel geometric method, which provided an affirmative answer to the conjecture without requiring the structural assumptions used in earlier works, such as the isolation of the stagnation points and the symmetry and monotonicity of the free surface.
  The main purpose of this paper is to establish the validity of the Stokes conjecture in the context of compressible gravity water waves. More precisely, we prove that, at each stagnation point of a compressible gravity water wave, a sharp crest with an included angle of \(120^\circ\) forms, which gives the first rigorous confirmation of the compressible counterpart of the classical Stokes conjecture of 1880.
  The central aspect of our approach is the discovery of a new monotonicity formula and a modified version of it for quasilinear free boundary problems of Bernoulli type. Another key ingredient is a new nonlinear frequency formula, which we combine with the concentration-cancellation theory of Evans and Muller [J. Amer. Math. Soc. 7 (1994)]. These newly developed monotonicity formulas are valid for nonlinear problems and enable us to carry out a blow-up analysis at each stagnation point and to provide a complete classification of the blow-up limits near each stagnation point.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 95 Pages. This revision corrects typos and an erroneous estimate from the previous version. The results are strengthened

Analysis of PDEs.title: The topology of end-periodic smoothing operators
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We develop an algebra of smoothing operators adapted to the geometry of end-periodic manifolds. We extend the renormalized trace and trace defect formula of Mrowka-Ruberman-Saveliev to this algebra, and establish a Fredholm criterion and winding-number index formula for smoothing perturbations of the identity. Our main result computes the homotopy groups of the associated end-periodic smoothing group. This provides a foundation for future work on relative index theory for families of end-periodic differential operators.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Double exponential growth for the Euler equation on the whole plane
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the incompressible Euler equation on the whole plane $\R^2$, without boundary and without forcing, and we construct two smooth solutions whose vorticity gradient grows fast for all large times. The first solution has finite energy, integrable vorticity and initial data in every Sobolev space. Given any function $Γ(t)$ with $Γ(t)/t\to 0$, the logarithm of its vorticity gradient is not bounded by any multiple of $Γ(t)$, and, at every sufficiently large time $t$, it is larger than any multiple of $t/\log_*t$, where $\log_*$ is the iterated logarithm. The second solution has bounded vorticity, bounded vorticity derivatives on every finite time interval, and a velocity given by the absolutely convergent Biot--Savart integral which grows at most logarithmically in space. Its vorticity gradient grows double exponentially in time for all large times. Its initial vorticity is neither integrable nor square integrable, and its initial velocity and strain are unbounded. Both constructions place infinitely many localized amplification mechanisms far apart from each other in one initial datum. The first one is based on the hyperbolic stagnation point behind a smooth traveling dipole, controlled for long times by an energy--Casimir argument. The second one is based on the hyperbolic point of the Bahouri--Chemin cross on the torus, transported to the plane by spatial dilations and by the uniqueness theory of Serfati solutions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A weak maximum principle and solvability for two-dimensional elliptic equations with $L^2$-drifts and singular zero-order coefficients
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study homogeneous Dirichlet problems for second-order linear elliptic equations in divergence form on bounded open subsets $U$ of $\mathbb R^2$. The diffusion matrix is bounded, measurable, and uniformly elliptic, and the drift belongs to $L^2(U,\mathbb R^2)$. If the zero-order coefficient $c$ belongs to $L^1(U)$ and satisfies $c\ge0$, we prove a weak maximum principle and deduce uniqueness of $H^{1,p}$-weak solutions for every $p \in (2, \infty)$. No regularity of the boundary is required for this result. The proof uses a logarithmic test function and an estimate for circular means of Sobolev functions. If, in addition, $U$ is a bounded open set with Lipschitz boundary and $c\in L^s(U)$ for some $s>1$, then for every $q\in(2, \infty)$ there exists $\varepsilon\in(0,q-2)$ such that the Dirichlet problem admits a unique $H^{1,2+\varepsilon}$-weak solution for every right-hand side in $H^{-1,q}(U)$. For existence, we use estimates for the lower-order terms, the global $H^{1,p}$-estimate for the diffusion operator, and the method of continuity. Finally, on the unit disk $B_1\subset\mathbb R^2$, we construct $c\in L^1(B_1)$ with $c \geq 0$ and $f\in C_0^\infty(B_1)$ such that the Dirichlet problem for $-Δu+cu=f$ has a bounded weak solution in $H^{1,2}_0(B_1)$ but no weak solution in $H^{1,p}_0(B_1)$ for any $p\in(2,\infty)$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Trichotomy for Modified Scattering Across the Yukawa-Coulomb Transition
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the long-time asymptotics of the three-dimensional Hartree equation with Yukawa potential \[ V_μ(x)=\frac{e^{-μ|x|}}{|x|}, \qquad 0\leqμ\leq1. \] The Coulomb case corresponds to $μ=0$, while $μ>0$ introduces the screening length $μ^{-1}$. In the limit $μ\to0$ and $t\to\infty$, the asymptotic behavior depends on the comparison between the observation scale $t$ and the screening length $μ^{-1}$, equivalently on the parameter $μt$. This leads to three distinct asymptotic regimes, according as $μt\to0$, $μt\to L\in(0,\infty)$, or $μt\to\infty$, with different modified scattering phases in each case.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Corrected minor errors, simplified the notation and organization

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniform dispersive estimates for the semi-classical Hartree equation with long-range interaction
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we consider the Hartree equation with smooth but long-range interaction in the semi-classical regime, in three-dimensional space. We show that the density function of a small-data solution decays at the optimal rate. When the semi-classical parameter $\hbar \in (0,1]$ is fixed, our result is essentially covered by the recent work by Nguyen and You; however, the novelty of this paper is the uniformity with respect to $\hbar$. Namely, both the smallness condition for the initial data and the bounds for the solution are independent of $\hbar$. Our proof relies on three main ingredients. First, we prove the boundedness of finite-time wave operators modified by phase corrections. Second, we show an $L^1$--$L^\infty$ dispersive estimate for the modified propagator. Third, we give various kinds of commutator estimates for density operators. By combining them, we can apply the usual bootstrap argument to obtain the main result.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $ω_φ(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Non-uniqueness for the Complex Ginzburg-Landau Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We show that singularities of the three-dimensional cubic complex Ginzburg-Landau equation developing from smooth initial data can induce non-uniqueness of solutions after the time of blowup. The solutions we study start as backward self-similar solutions, and the source of the non-uniqueness is an unstable eigenvalue of the linearization around the forward self-similar profile generated by the singularity. We establish the existence of this eigenvalue, and hence the non-uniqueness, by a computer-assisted proof for specific values of the parameters in the equation. The work is in part motivated by similarities to conjectured behavior for the Navier-Stokes equation, with which the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation shares several important properties, such as an energy inequality and the scaling symmetry.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Asymptotic Stability of Moving Kinks with an Internal Mode
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We prove asymptotic stability of moving kinks for one-dimensional scalar field equations with one internal mode and no threshold resonance, under a transformed repulsivity condition introduced in Kowalczyk, Martel, Muñoz, and Van Den Bosch and a Fermi golden rule at the second harmonic. Near every fixed subluminal velocity, arbitrary sufficiently small perturbations in $H^1\times L^2$ converge locally in the energy space to a kink with a limiting velocity. The principal difficulty is the coupling between the damping of the internal mode and modulations: the internal oscillation enters the modulation equations quadratically, whereas the damping mechanism provides only quartic time integrability. Inspired by Martel, we derive a velocity normal form from conserved momentum and incorporate the corrected velocity into the virial functional, cancelling the quadratic modulation terms that obstruct the local energy estimates. Matrix Darboux transformations, virial identities at two spatial scales, and a localized Fermi golden rule then yield simultaneous spacetime control of the internal mode and radiation, together with convergence of the velocity.
  We apply our criterion to the double sine-Gordon equation and suitable perturbations of the $φ^4$ model. Through a perturbative analysis of threshold resonances, we determine the full-space discrete spectrum and establish the absence of threshold resonances. We further verify the repulsivity of the twice-transformed potential and the Fermi golden rule.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global regularity of axisymmetric Navier--Stokes equations under total slip and critical smallness
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the axisymmetric incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in a finite cylinder subject to the Navier--total--slip boundary condition, that is, the Navier slip condition with zero friction. We prove that the solution remains smooth for all time provided that the initial swirl $Γ_0 = r v_{θ,0}$ has zero mean and an explicit smallness condition on the initial data holds. The condition involves $Γ= rv_θ$ and the variables $V = v_θ/\sqrt{r}$ and $Ω= ω_θ/r$, and it is invariant under the natural scaling of the Navier--Stokes equations, hence critical. The total-slip condition produces a boundary term on the lateral wall that cannot be controlled by the dissipation alone; we overcome this with a sharp trace-type identity combined with a remainder controlled by $\|Γ\|_{L^2}$. In addition, the Robin-type boundary condition $\partial_r Γ= 2Γ$ destroys the maximum principle for $Γ$, and we replace it with a uniform $L^4$ bound. These estimates yield uniform $L^4$ bounds for the velocity, and regularity follows from the Ladyzhenskaya--Prodi--Serrin criterion together with boundary regularity results for the Navier slip condition.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Linear Asymptotic Stability of the Smooth 1-Solitons for the Degasperis-Procesi Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the asymptotic stability of smooth 1-solitons in the Degasperis-Procesi (DP) equation. Such solutions necessarily exist on a non-zero background, and their spectral and orbital stability has previously been verified by Li, Liu & Wu and by Lafortune & Pelinovsky. Using the complete integrability of the DP equation to establish the strong spectral stability of smooth solitary waves, namely that the origin is the only eigenvalue of the associated linearized operator acting on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and that, moreover, in appropriate exponentially weighted spaces the non-zero spectrum for the linearized operator admits a spectral gap away from the imaginary axis. This spectral gap result {is then} upgraded to an exponential decay estimate on the semigroup associated with the linearized operator, establishing a linear asymptotic stability result in exponentially weighted spaces. Finally, we outline analytical challenges with extending our result to the nonlinear level.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 44 pages, 2 figures. Correcting typos, adding additional exposition

Analysis of PDEs.title: The doubling property of the elliptic measure, for elliptic operators with drifts satisfying an average diverging condition
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We show doubling of the elliptic measure corresponding to the operator with an elliptic principal term and a drift that diverges, on average on Whitney cubes, like the inverse distance to the boundary, with a small constant. Essentially a small Carleson constant assumption on the drift, this generalizes earlier results with the hypothesis of pointwise smallness of such a drift. This relates to recent perturbative results of rough Dirichlet solvability in domains with drifts or potentials that satisfy a Carleson measure condition, which have also been considered earlier by Hofmann-Lewis and Kenig-Pipher. While we work in 1-sided chord arc domains, these results are new even for the half-space. In the process, we also prove Hardy inequalities in such domains with Alhfors-David regular boundary, using a stopping time argument.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Corrected a minor error with addition of Lemma 6

Analysis of PDEs.title: Microscopic derivation of the classical KMS condition for one-dimensional Bose gases
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) condition provides an intrinsic characterization of thermal equilibrium, both in quantum and classical statistical mechanics. In this work, we establish stability of the KMS condition through the quantum-to-classical limit for one-dimensional defocusing Bose gases. More precisely, we consider scaled quantum KMS states in the (mean-field) semiclassical regime and prove that every associated Wigner measure satisfies the classical KMS condition corresponding to the nonlinear Schrödinger Hamiltonian. This result extends to an infinite-dimensional setting an earlier derivation of the classical KMS condition for finite-dimensional Bose--Hubbard systems. It also provides a complementary perspective on the derivation of nonlinear Gibbs measures from many-body quantum statistical mechanics.

Functional Analysis.title: The Brown measure of a sum of two free nonselfadjoint random variables, one of which is R-diagonal
Functional Analysis.summary: Suppose that $X_1$ and $X_2$ are two $*$-free, possibly unbounded, random variables with Brown measures $μ_{X_1}$ and $μ_{X_2}$ respectively. Using properties of classic free additive convolution, we develop a method for calculating $μ_{X_1+X_2}$ when $X_2$ is $R$-diagonal. This method determines a density relative to Lebesgue measure on an open set whose closure equals the support of $μ_{X_{1}+X_{2}}$. We prove that $μ_{X_1+X_2}$ has no singular continuous part, that its density is strictly positive on this open set, and we determine the masses of its atoms. Explicit calculations are possible in several important cases. As an application, we combine our Fuglede--Kadison determinant formula with known subordination convergence results to calculate the limiting logarithmic potentials of free multiplicative random walks. We identify the limit with the Fuglede--Kadison determinant formula for free multiplicative Brownian motion previously proved by some PDE methods.

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp double logarithmic $L^\infty$ bounds for second-order Sobolev functions in dimension four
Functional Analysis.summary:
Although $W^{2,2}(\mathbb{R}^{4})$ does not embed into $L^\infty$, we prove that radial symmetry allows the $L^\infty$ norm to be controlled by the homogeneous Sobolev seminorm $\dot H^2$, at the cost of a logarithmic correction involving a stronger Hölder-type norm.
  Our main result is a sharp double-logarithmic inequality with optimal leading constant $1/(8π^2α)$. We also establish a single-logarithmic estimate and prove the sharpness of its threshold. The optimal lower bound is derived by analysing a biharmonic obstacle problem with Hölder-type obstacle. A tailored penalization argument yields existence, uniqueness, and regularity of the minimizer, while an explicit transcendental equation for the free-boundary radius determines the sharp constant through its asymptotic behavior.
  These results provide fourth-order, four-dimensional analogues of the two-dimensional first-order inequalities of Ibrahim--Majdoub--Masmoudi (\textit{Proc.\ Amer.\ Math.\ Soc.}, 2007), with potential applications to fourth-order semilinear evolution equations with exponential nonlinearities.
Functional Analysis.comment: The title has been revised, and the presentation has been further enhanced and improved

Functional Analysis.title: Extensions from Positive and Full Unit Spheres of $C^\infty([0,1])$ with a Compatible Fréchet Metric
Functional Analysis.summary:
We study isometric extensions from positive and full unit spheres of $C^\infty([0,1],\mathbb F)$, where $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. We equip these spaces with a translation-invariant metric that induces the usual Fréchet topology, is unbounded, has convex balls, and has strictly increasing distances from zero along nonzero rays.
  Every surjective isometry of the pointwise positive unit sphere extends uniquely to a complex-linear surjective isometry of the complex-valued space. Restriction gives the unique real-linear isometric extension on the real-valued space. On the full unit sphere, every surjective isometry extends uniquely to a real-linear surjective isometry. The positive-sphere maps are compositions with the identity or an admissible reflection. The full-sphere maps also allow constant unimodular factors and, over the complex field, conjugation. We also classify the surjective ambient isometries.
  A counterexample shows that these metric properties alone do not guarantee positive-sphere extension. Under an explicit anchor condition, we classify surjective isometries of finite-order jet-positive spheres for maximum-type anchored metrics and prove that they extend uniquely to complex-linear surjective isometries. The classification allows any permutation of the anchored coordinates, combined with the identity or reflection on the highest-derivative component. The condition holds for every anchor when $m=1$ or $m=2$.

Functional Analysis.title: Concave shifts and the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $\mathcal H$ be a reproducing kernel Hilbert space of holomorphic functions on the unit disc, and assume $\mathcal H$ is invariant under the forward and backward shifts. We show that if the forward shift on $\mathcal H$ is concave, then $\mathcal H$ is a complete Nevanlinna--Pick space. This gives an affirmative answer to the concavity part of Shimorin's question \cite{Sh02} and extends his theorem on the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property of Dirichlet-type spaces with superharmonic weights.

Functional Analysis.title: Algebraic properties of Truncated Toeplitz $+$ Truncated Hankel operators
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we study the algebraic properties of $\mathcal{S}_θ$ --- the class of truncated Toeplitz plus truncated Hankel operators --- on the model space $\mathcal{K}_θ$. We also give a complete characterization of the intersection class of truncated Toeplitz and truncated Hankel operators. As a by-product of our findings, we give a complete characterization for $S_θ$, where $θ$ is a finite Blaschke product and also obtained the commutant of $S_θ+ S_θ^{*}$ in that case.
Functional Analysis.comment: Pages 24. Revised. A new reference was added

Functional Analysis.title: Separable $\mathcal L_{\infty}$-spaces with Kalton's property $Q$
Functional Analysis.summary: We construct separable $\mathcal L_\infty$-spaces with Kalton's property $Q$, which, to the best of our knowledge, are the first known examples of this kind. Our technique employs the Bourgain--Pisier construction and a quantitative analysis of metric types in limits of finite-dimensional $η$-admissible embeddings. The argument rests on two complementary estimates: approximate radial centres yield asymptotic separation of tree increments, while an admissibility inequality yields asymptotic gain, leading to concentration on Kalton's interlacing graphs. This leads to an abstract criterion for property $Q$ in terms of asymptotic separation $AS_θ$ and asymptotic gain $AG_α$. We illustrate the limitations of this criterion with Johnson--Lindenstrauss spaces. Our examples exclude uniform embeddings of the unit ball of $c_0$, strengthening in a nonlinear direction the classical Bourgain--Delbaen phenomenon. As an application, every separable Banach space embeds isometrically into a separable $\mathcal L_\infty$-space whose unit ball is not a uniform retract of the unit ball of its bidual.

Functional Analysis.title: On Solvability of Irregular Infinite-Dimensional Differential-Algebraic Equations
Functional Analysis.summary: This paper investigates the solvability of infinite-dimensional differential-algebraic equations (DAEs) on Hilbert spaces. We focus on irregular systems for which the operator pencil is not surjective onto the full state space, but only onto a subspace determined by the algebraic constraints. We establish a Lumer-Phillips-type generation result for this class of systems, showing that dissipativity together with a partial surjectivity condition yields a contraction semigroup on the dynamic subspace. The resulting wellposedness conditions are compared with existing solvability results. We further extend the analysis to systems in which hidden algebraic constraints restrict the dynamics to a proper closed subspace of the dynamical subspace. Under an additional structural condition, we show that the resulting constrained system is $E$-radial on suitably chosen spaces. We also demonstrate that semigroup generation does not, in general, imply $E$-radiality on the original state spaces. This provides a Weierstraß-type decomposition useful for controller design. The framework is illustrated by some examples.

Functional Analysis.title: The vector-valued Stein inequality and dimension-free R-sectoriality
Functional Analysis.summary: For a complex Banach space \(X\), we characterise dimension-free \(R\)-sectoriality of the Walsh operator, the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator, the Laplacian, and the Poisson operator by the vector-valued Stein inequality. For each family, the dimension-free \(R\)-bound of the resolvents on the negative real axis equals the Stein constant. Consequently, the resolvent estimate on the negative real axis already implies uniform \(R\)-sectoriality at an angle strictly smaller than \(π/2\). We furthermore prove that the full and dyadic Stein properties are equivalent and that they are independent of the exponent \(1<p<\infty\) entering their definition.

Functional Analysis.title: Twisted convolution with conic support and the parabolic algebra
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that tempered distributions on \(\mathbb R^{2n}\) whose supports satisfy a common strict cone condition form a unital associative algebra without zero divisors under twisted convolution \(\star\). The supports may be noncompact, and the associated Weyl maps need not be bounded. As applications, we show that the parabolic algebra and the norm-closed algebra generated by positive translations and modulations have no zero divisors, confirming Levene's conjecture. We also obtain a zero-product theorem for Toeplitz operators on the one-dimensional Fock space with bounded symbols whose distributional Fourier transforms satisfy a common strict cone condition. The proof of the distribution theorem uses Schwartz smoothing between distributional Weyl maps to convert a hypothetical zero product of nonzero distributions into a smooth function \(h\not\equiv0\) satisfying the same cone condition and \(h\star h=0\). The cone bound implies the \(Q\)-support condition, meaning that some linear functional is bounded above on \(\operatorname{supp}h\) and has compact upper level sets there. Truncating \(h\) near the maximum of this functional and applying the support identity for compactly supported twisted squares rule out \(h\star h=0\). For the operator applications, uniformly bounded Weyl-conjugation averages identify twisted convolution with bounded operator composition under the common cone condition.

Functional Analysis.title: Gelfand and sampling numbers of weighted Wiener spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: The aim of this paper is to establish sharp asymptotic bounds on the Gelfand numbers of weighted Wiener spaces $\mathcal{A}^r_θ$ measured in $L_q$. This is done by using results for Gelfand numbers of sequence spaces and applying them to each layer of a hyperbolic cross to obtain results for Gelfand numbers between different (weighted) Wiener spaces. These can then be used to establish bounds in $L_q$ by combining them with known results and techniques for Besov spaces. This significantly narrows a gap in the current research, since the Gelfand numbers provide a lower bound on the (non-linear) sampling numbers, whereas upper bounds on this quantity have been studied in multiple papers via an upper bound given by the best m-term approximation.

Functional Analysis.title: Singularising quantum channels preserving kappa-additivity
Functional Analysis.summary:
We construct quantum channels by averaging unitary shift conjugations with respect to $κ$-additive probability measures on measurable abelian groups.
  The channels act on the duals of operator algebras generated by shifts and bounded measurable multiplication operators.
  They preserve $κ$-additivity of quantum states and admit a weak-$*$ integral representation on this class.
  If the averaging measure vanishes on singletons, every output state is singular.
  In the appendix, we also establish the corresponding Fubini's theorem for $κ$-additive measures.

Functional Analysis.title: Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties.

Functional Analysis.title: Fixed-occurrence cases of the shuffle-word-embedding conjecture
Functional Analysis.summary: For self-adjoint contractions in a finite tracial von Neumann algebra, binary shuffle traces with $m=1,2,4$ occurrences of the second variable admit simultaneous finite-dimensional approximation by commuting diagonal contractions. For every odd $m$, a commuting diagonal self-adjoint pair reproduces any prescribed finite set of shuffle traces exactly. When the first operator has finite spectrum and $m\geq3$ is odd, a weighted symmetric cycle reproduces all degrees simultaneously. We prove fourth-order trace-derivative positivity in finite tracial von Neumann algebras and obtain a positive measure representing the four-occurrence coefficients. For each even $m$, we characterize the contraction model property by positivity of an associated trace-derivative functional.

Functional Analysis.title: An almost sharp tomas-stein restriction theorem for a class of anisotropic operators
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $d\geq 2$. For each $j\in \{1,\dots,d\}$, let ${\ell}_{j}\geq 1$ and $m_{j}\geq 2$ be integers, and let $a_{j}$ be a nonzero real number. We prove that the oscillatory integral operator \begin{equation*} T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} e^{\dot{\imath} \left(a_{1}x^{{\ell}_{1}}_{1}y^{m_{1}}_{1}+\dots +a_{d}x^{{\ell}_{d}}_{d}y^{m_{d}}_{d} \right)}f(y)dy,\;\;\; x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation*} satisfies the restriction estimate \begin{equation*} \|T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{d})}, \end{equation*} for each $1\leq p\leq 2$, whenever $(\frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}-\frac{1}{m_{j}}+1)\frac{2}{p^{\prime}}\geq 1$, for every $j\in Γ$, and \begin{equation*} \mathcal{E}:=\min{\left\{\min_{1\leq j\leq d}{\frac{m_{j}}{{\ell}_{j}}},\,\min_{1\leq k\leq d}{\frac{d-1}{\sum_{j\neq k} \frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}+\frac{2}{m_{k}}}}\right\}}> \frac{2}{p^{\prime}}. \end{equation*} We also give counterexamples that show that the condition $\mathcal{E}\geq 2/p^{\prime}$ is necessary for this restriction inequality.

Functional Analysis.title: The symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric problem in the plane
Functional Analysis.summary: We resolve the symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric conjecture in the plane: every minimizer of Gaussian perimeter among centrally symmetric sets of prescribed Gaussian measure is a centered ball, a symmetric strip, or the complement of one of these sets. A quadrant-reflection argument reduces the problem to unconditional sets. The planar structural results of Barchiesi, Cagnetti and Julin then leave only a noncircular strictly convex stationary oval. We exclude this oval by an explicit volume-preserving and perimeter-decreasing linear deformation, which geometrically corresponds to an "unconditional squeezing". More generally, without requiring any symmetry assumptions, we show that any noncircular closed embedded $λ$-self-shrinker is always unstable via linear deformations. We also record a reduction to the unconditional case in dimension three, using an orthogonal equipartition theorem of Musin.

Functional Analysis.title: Vector metrics with values in pre-Riesz spaces I: transfer of order convergence along vector lattice covers
Functional Analysis.summary: Vector metric spaces in the sense of Çevik and Altun take values in a vector lattice, but their axioms use only the order of the value space. We develop the theory for vector metrics with values in an Archimedean pre-Riesz space $E$, i.e.\ an ordered vector space admitting a bipositive order dense embedding $i$ into a vector lattice $Y$. We ask when an $E$-valued vector metric $d$ and the vector-lattice-valued metric $i\circ d$ have the same convergent and Cauchy nets and sequences. Relatively uniform convergence transfers along every cover. For nets, $\mathrm{o}_3$-convergence transfers if and only if the cover has an intrinsic domination property. This property holds for pervasive covers, by a result of Kalauch and van Gaans, for uniformly dense covers and in finite dimensions; it fails for an example of Kalauch and van Gaans. Sequential convergence transfers under a countable domination property implied by uniform density, but not under pervasiveness. For uncountable $Γ$, the vector lattice $\mathbb{R}\mathbf 1\oplus c_{00}(Γ)$ is pervasive in its Dedekind completion $\ell^\infty(Γ)$ without the transfer, while for countable $Γ$ the transfer holds; the difference is explained by order separability. In finite dimensions, with a closed generating cone, all these convergences coincide with norm convergence in every cover. For $C^1[0,1]$-valued integral metrics, positivity of the kernel on the diagonal forces all order convergences to coincide with $L^1$-convergence. For the Volterra kernel $(t-s)_+$, by contrast, $L^1$-convergence, relatively uniform convergence and order convergence are pairwise different, and we describe each explicitly.

Functional Analysis.title: Completions of vector metric spaces and the diagonal property of order convergence
Functional Analysis.summary: A vector metric space carries a distance with values in an ordered vector space $E$; a sequence converges if its distances to the limit are dominated by a sequence decreasing to zero in $E$. We show that, for Archimedean $E$, every $E$-valued vector metric space has a completion if and only if order Cauchy sequences in $E$ converge and $E$ has the diagonal property of order convergence (SDP): for every double sequence $(a^k_n)$ with $a^k_n\downarrow_n0$ there are indices $n_k$ and $e_k\downarrow 0$ with $a^k_{n_k}\le e_k$. In vector lattices this is the classical diagonal property of Kantorovich, equivalently the strong Egoroff property. We show that its standard characterisations remain valid in Archimedean ordered vector spaces, and that it holds if and only if convergence in every $E$-valued vector metric space satisfies the iterated limit axiom. For an ordered Banach space with a closed normal cone, all completions exist if and only if the norm is $σ$-order continuous; if the cone has an interior point, all vector metrics are then scalar. By a theorem of Veksler and of Hager and van Mill, for compact Hausdorff $K$ either $K$ is an almost $P$-space and $C(K)$-valued vector metrics are scalar, or there are countable $C(K)$-valued vector metric spaces without completion. A product of ordered vector spaces with (SDP) and nonzero cones has (SDP) if and only if there are fewer than $\mathfrak b$ factors, extending a result of Hager and van Mill for $\mathbb{R}^A$. We also prove permanence results for direct summands and uniformly dense vector lattice covers of pre-Riesz spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: $L_p$-spaces, $1\leq p\ne 2<\infty$, associated with type III and semifinite von Neumann algebras are not isomorphic
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $M$ be a type III von Neumann algebra, and let $N$ be a semifinite von Neumann algebra. We prove that the Banach space $M_*$ does not embed isomorphically into the Banach space $N_*$. More generally, we prove that $L_p(M)$ is not isomorphic to a subspace of $L_p(N)$ for $1\le p<2$. In particular, the Banach isomorphism class of $L_p(M)$ distinguishes type III algebras from semifinite algebras for $1\le p<\infty$, $p\ne2$. This answers several long-standing open questions in the literature.

Functional Analysis.title: Finite dimensional approximations for Hilbert space operators and applications in Quantum Mechanics
Functional Analysis.summary: In this work, we develop a unified framework for quasidiagonal and Følner-type approximations of linear operators on Hilbert spaces. These approximations (originally formulated for bounded operators and operator algebras) involve sequences of non-zero finite rank orthogonal projections that asymptotically commute with the operator -- either in norm (quasidiagonal) or in mean (Følner). Such structures guarantee spectral approximation results in terms of their finite sections. We extend this theory to unbounded, densely defined closable operators, establishing a generalization of Halmos' classical result: every closable quasidiagonal operator is a compact perturbation of a closable block-diagonal operator on the same domain. Likewise, we introduce sparse Følner sequences and establish an interplay between quasidiagonal approximations and the existence of sparse Følner sequences. The theoretical developments are illustrated with explicit examples using different types of weighted shifts and applied to quantum mechanical models, including a detailed treatment of the Weyl algebra and its Schrödinger representation.
Functional Analysis.comment: New definition of sparse Foelner sequence and proof of Theorem 2.8; new Proposition 3.3; variation in the definition of Foelner sequences for unbounded operators; general improvement of the presentation and new references; 21 pages

Functional Analysis.title: Recurrent and rigid multipliers on commutative Banach algebras. The Fourier algebra
Functional Analysis.summary: We study recurrence, rigidity and uniform rigidity of multipliers on semisimple commutative Banach algebras. For a power-bounded multiplier $T$ on a Tauberian, self-adjoint algebra $\mathfrak{A}$, we show that $T$ satisfies each of these properties if and only if the multiplication operator on $C_0(Δ(\mathfrak{A}))$ induced by the Gelfand transform of $T$ does. One consequence of our analysis is that, if $Δ(\mathfrak{A})$ is $σ$-compact, then recurrence implies rigidity for such multipliers. We examine in detail the multipliers of the Fourier algebra $A(G)$. In particular, we show that recurrence of a multiplier of $A(G)$ is equivalent to recurrence of the corresponding multiplier on $C_0(G)$ when the connected components of $G$ are open. For multipliers that are not power bounded, a flexible construction based on chains of compact subgroups of a locally compact abelian group $G$ produces multipliers of $A(G)$ that are rigid but not uniformly rigid, and multipliers that are recurrent but not rigid, such that in each case the corresponding multiplier on $C_0(G)$ is uniformly rigid. Via the Fourier-Stieltjes transform, these results describe the recurrence and rigidity properties of convolution operators on $L^1(G)$.

Functional Analysis.title: On operators with many spectral components
