Functional Analysis.summary: For a complex Banach algebra $\mathscr A$ with unit and $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ be the set of all elements whose spectrum has at least $n$ connected components, and let $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\sup\{n;\;\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)\neq\varnothing\}$ be the spectral depth of $\mathscr A$. We characterize nonemptiness of $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ in terms of orthogonal idempotents, compute $d_σ(\mathscr A)$ for finite-dimensional algebras, and show that every class $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ is open. For operators on an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space $X$ these classes are dense in $\mathscr B(X)$, which implies that $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr B(X))$ is a dense $G_δ$-subset of $\mathscr B(X)$. By contrast, we exhibit a commutative Banach algebra whose spectral classes are all nonempty and none of which is dense. For self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space, we obtain sharper perturbation results, with positive semi-definite perturbations of prescribed rank producing spectra with exactly $n$ components. We show that a quasinilpotent weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $X$ admits a nilpotent rank-one operator $F$ such that the spectrum of $S_w+αF$ has infinitely many components for every nonzero $α$.

Functional Analysis.title: The Zaporozhets-Tarasov Conjecture on Mean Distances
Functional Analysis.summary: For a convex body $K \subset \mathbb R^d$ let $Δ(K)$ be the expected distance between two independent uniform points of $K$, and let $θ(K)$ be the corresponding expectation for normalized surface measure on $\partial K$. The Zaporozhets-Tarasov conjecture asserts $Δ(K) \le θ(K)$. We prove this conjecture in case $d=2$. In addition, we give a six-vertex convex polytope in $\mathbb R^3$ for which the reverse strict inequality holds, and obtain counterexamples in every dimension $d \ge 3$ by taking products with segments.
Functional Analysis.comment: Split off Section 5 from previous version to make it a separate manuscript

Functional Analysis.title: Whitney-Type Real-Analytic Approximation on Banach Spaces I: The $C^0$ and $C^1$ Cases
Functional Analysis.summary:
The classical Whitney theorem on real-analytic approximation is a fundamental result in finite-dimensional analysis and geometry. Extending this theory to general infinite-dimensional Banach spaces involves longstanding open problems. This paper is the first part of our study of Whitney-type real-analytic approximation on Banach spaces, focusing on the $C^0$ and $C^1$ cases.
  We prove that a real Banach space admits a separating polynomial if and only if it admits a polynomial topological embedding into a real Hilbert space. We also introduce classes of mappings that locally factor through polynomial maps into finite-dimensional spaces and develop methods of real-analytic approximation for these classes. Using these tools, we establish fine $C^0$ and $C^1$ real-analytic approximation theorems for broad classes of Banach spaces, including nonseparable ones.
  As applications, we resolve several open problems, including those concerning Whitney-type extensions with real analyticity off closed sets, real-analytic approximation preserving Lipschitz constants, and the real-analytic equivalence of diffeomorphic open subsets of Hilbert spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: Controllability with and without Dissipation - a Port-Hamiltonian Approach
Functional Analysis.summary: A port-Hamiltonian system with energy dissipation can be modelled by connecting a larger, non-dissipative system with a so-called closure relation. We study whether approximative controllability of the dissipative system is characterised by the same property of the larger system. The answer is negative in general, but positive for sufficiently well-structured systems - this is our main result. As a simple illustration, we show how approximate controllability of a wave equation implies approximate controllability of a heat equation.

Functional Analysis.title: On fractal minimizers and potentials of occupation measures
Functional Analysis.summary: We highlight two basic types of variational problems and prove the existence of fractal minimizers through the direct method in the calculus of variations. By design these minimizers are Hölder curves or Hölder parametrizations of surfaces whose images generally have a non-integer Hausdorff dimension. Their origin is deterministic, but their regularity properties are roughly similar to those of typical realizations of stochastic processes. As a key tool and our main technical result, we prove novel continuity and boundedness results for potentials of occupation measures of Gaussian random fields. These results complement well-known results for local times, but hold under much less restrictive assumptions. In an auxiliary section, we generalize earlier results on nonlinear compositions of fractional Sobolev functions with $BV$-functions to higher dimensions.

Functional Analysis.title: Forelli--Rudin Type Operators in Infinite Dimensions, I
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce Forelli-Rudin type operators on the open unit ball of $\ell^2$. The weighted $L^p$-$L^q$ boundedness of these operators are completely characterized for all $p,q\in[1,\infty]\times [1,\infty]$, and every Schatten class between the weighted $L^2$ spaces are also completely characterized. Meanwhile, we derive trace formulas for corresponding operators, which cannot be obtained from their finite-dimensional counterparts by formally replacing the dimension parameter with infinity. These results are not only infinite-dimensional extensions of those obtained by Cheng, Fang, Wang, and the second author (2017), Zhao and Zhou (2022), and Ding (2022). They also reveal new phenomena that are unique to infinite dimensions and arise from the geometric and measure theoretic differences between finite- and infinite-dimensional spaces. The key ingredient of our proofs is that we also establish the Forelli-Rudin type estimates in infinite dimensions, which may shew some night on the function theory in the infinite-dimensional unit ball.

Functional Analysis.title: Extreme amenability and failure of the Lévy property for the trace-class special unitary group
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that the trace-class special unitary group, equipped with the trace-norm topology, is extremely amenable but is not a Lévy group, answering questions posed by Pestov. The failure of the Lévy property follows from a uniform non-concentration estimate for every nontrivial compact subgroup. Extreme amenability is established through a transverse spectral-gap estimate and trace-norm duality, yielding asymptotic invariance of Lipschitz observables under each fixed finite-dimensional special unitary subgroup. A limiting argument then gives fixed points for continuous actions on arbitrary compact Hausdorff spaces. We also formulate an abstract criterion for extreme amenability based on asymptotic quadratic invariance along a dense chain of compact subgroups. Neither argument uses concentration results for other Schatten exponents.

Functional Analysis.title: A reverse entropy power inequality for i.i.d. log-concave random variables
Functional Analysis.summary: We show that $h_\infty(X+Y)\leq h_\infty(Z+W)$, where $X, Y$ are independent log-concave random variables, and $Z, W$ are exponential random variables having the same respective $\infty$-Rényi entropies. Analogs for integer-valued monotone log-concave random variables are also obtained. Our main tools are decreasing rearrangement, majorization, and the change of measure.

Functional Analysis.title: A Dimension-Free Bound on the Poincaré Constant of Isotropic Log-Concave Measures
Functional Analysis.summary: The Kannan--Lovász--Simonovits (KLS) conjecture asserts that isotropic log-concave probability measures have Poincaré constants bounded by a universal constant, independently of dimension. In this work, we provide a deterministic variational proof that the Poincaré constant $C_P(μ)\le25$, where $μ$ is any isotropic log-concave probability measure. The proof centers on mean-zero integration of compatible symmetric tensor fields. Starting from constant tensors, we obtain factorially normalized Appell polynomials by iterating this procedure. Using moment estimates and a quadratic variance inequality, we establish geometric bounds on these iterated primitives through a \emph{joint} variational argument over the measure and test function. At a maximizing pair, stationarity in the test function controls the weighted sum of the two highest-order cumulant terms arising from the measure variation. To extend these bounds to arbitrary compatible fields, we use a weighted Helmholtz--Hodge decomposition of weighted divergence, the formal adjoint of differentiation. Controlling the curl in the decomposition yields a curvature comparison for the integration operators, uniformly in tensor order. Combining this comparison with the Appell bounds gives a bound on the full integration operator and hence the stated Poincaré inequality. The estimate is independent of the auxiliary positive curvature, allowing approximation to general isotropic log-concave measures.

Functional Analysis.title: Two-mode stability for multi-marginal optimal transport maps
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish a two-mode stability theory for Monge solutions of the multi-marginal optimal transport problem with barycentric quadratic cost. The associated tuple of maps splits into an external barycentric mode and internal relative modes. A quadratic lower bound for the Kantorovich defect controls the internal modes and yields a square-root estimate without invoking any two-marginal map-stability theorem. The external mode is the optimal transport map from the fixed source to the Wasserstein barycenter. Combining the resulting two-mode estimate with Mérigot's sharp theorem gives a $\frac{1}{4}$-Hölder estimate for general perturbations, while barycenter-preserving perturbations satisfy a $\frac{1}{2}$-Hölder estimate. We prove that both exponents and the dependence on the weights are optimal. We also examine the scope of such decomposition beyond the barycentric cost: collective-coordinate perturbations and uniformly concave costs of the sum retain the two-mode estimate, whereas the analyses of graph interactions, hedonic costs, and translation-invariant costs identify the two possible obstructions -- loss of relative coercivity and lack of stability for the remaining external modes.

Functional Analysis.title: Fredholm weighted composition operators on the Lipschitz space of a tree
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the Lipschitz space of a tree. In this paper, we establish a complete characterization of the weighted composition operator $W_{ψ,\varphi}$ to be Fredholm on $\mathcal{L}$. Applying our characterization, we describe the connection between the Fredholmness of $W_{ψ,\varphi}$ and that of the composition operator $C_\varphi$.

Functional Analysis.title: A general framework for universal bounds on the analytic functional calculus
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish a general principle for bounding the matrix-valued analytic functional calculus $F\mapsto F(T)$ of a Hilbert space operator $T$, independently of the matrix size. It rests on two properties of an auxiliary Hilbert space of holomorphic functions: the accretivity of its moment map at $T$ and a uniform bound for its multipliers. The mechanism of OpenAI's direct proof of the complete Crouzeix conjecture is the instance in which these properties come from the positivity of the double-layer potential and from norm estimates for Faber series of a convex domain. The main advantage of our method is that the auxiliary space can be chosen freely, to fit the class of operators, and a well-chosen space can give sharp constants, also on domains that are not convex, simply connected or bounded. On every intersection of two disks of the Riemann sphere, for operators with both closed disks as spectral sets, we obtain the complete bound $2$, which is sharp for the quantum annulus and the strip. For operators, bounded or m-sectorial, with numerical range in a sector, our bounds improve on the complete Crouzeix inequality for every opening; they are optimal for the right angle, answering a question of Crouzeix, and nearly optimal for acute angles. On Jordan domains with regular real-analytic boundary, a space built from the exterior conformal map and the Faber polynomials of the domain gives complete bounds for operators whose double-layer potential is bounded below. They are optimal for the disk, recover the complete Crouzeix inequality on convex domains, and improve on earlier bounds, including bounds of Crouzeix and Greenbaum, also on nonconvex domains.

Functional Analysis.title: On fractal minimizers and potentials of occupation measures
Functional Analysis.summary: We highlight two basic types of variational problems and prove the existence of fractal minimizers through the direct method in the calculus of variations. By design these minimizers are Hölder curves or Hölder parametrizations of surfaces whose images generally have a non-integer Hausdorff dimension. Their origin is deterministic, but their regularity properties are roughly similar to those of typical realizations of stochastic processes. As a key tool and our main technical result, we prove novel continuity and boundedness results for potentials of occupation measures of Gaussian random fields. These results complement well-known results for local times, but hold under much less restrictive assumptions. In an auxiliary section, we generalize earlier results on nonlinear compositions of fractional Sobolev functions with $BV$-functions to higher dimensions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: SDEs with critical general distributional drifts: sharp solvability and blow-ups
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We develop weak solution theory of SDEs having general distributional drifts that can introduce local blow-up effects. Our assumption on the drift is closely related to the variational theory of the Kolmogorov backward equation in the standard Hilbert triple $W^{1,2} \hookrightarrow L^2 \hookrightarrow W^{-1,2}$. Under suitable smallness assumption on the drift, one has well-posedness of the Cauchy problem in this Hilbert triple. In turn, by a result of Mazya and Verbitsky, boundedness of the drift term from $W^{1,2}$ to $W^{-1,2}$ is equivalent to a decomposition of the drift in the sum of a form-bounded drift (including, for example, Morrey or Chang--Wilson--Wolff drifts) and a divergence-free distributional drift in the ${\rm BMO}^{-1}$ space of Koch and Tataru; such decomposition is our class of drifts.
  We apply our results to finite particle systems with strong attracting interactions immersed in a stationary turbulent flow. This includes particle systems of Keller-Segel type. Crucially, in dimensions $d \geq 3$, we cover almost the entire admissible range of attraction strengths, reaching nearly to the blow-up threshold. As a further application of our results for SDEs and of the theory of Bessel processes, we obtain an improved upper bound on the constant in the many-particle Hardy inequality of Hoffmann-Ostenhof, Hoffmann-Ostenhof, Laptev, and Tidblom.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Fixed a number of minor errors and typos

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local well-posedness for viscous heat-conducting fluids with discontinuous densities
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
In this paper, we consider the Navier-Stokes-Fourier system in space dimension $d\geq2$. We prove local well-posedness of solutions having density only in $L^p\cap L^\infty$, for suitable $p\in\,]1,+\infty[\,$, with no further regularity requirements. In particular, our result yields existence and uniqueness of solutions in the case of discontinuous densities presenting a jump across a smooth interface.
  The existence proof is based on the use of the Hoff effective viscous flux and on a combination of both maximal regularity and Chemin's striated regularity arguments. Uniqueness, under the assumption of slightly more regular initial velocity fields and temperatures, relies on a Lagrangian approach, supplemented with an original bootstrap argument which shows improved time integrability properties of the solution.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Submitted. No use of AI in any sense, at any level

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stabilization of an Euler--Bernoulli beam equation with distributed damping and interior time delay
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we investigate the effect of a fixed time delay on the internal stabilization of an Euler--Bernoulli beam clamped at one end with distributed damping. Under appropriate assumptions on the feedback weights, we first establish that the problem is well-posed using semigroup theory. Furthermore, using the multiplier method combined with a suitable Lyapunov functional, we prove the exponential stability of the system.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Exponential stabilization of an Euler--Bernoulli beam via internal feedback under distributed time delay
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we investigate the internal stabilization of a closed-loop system which consists of an Euler--Bernoulli beam subjected to a structural damping mechanism with a distributed delay into the domain. Under appropriate assumptions on the weights of the delay term and internal damping, we first prove the well-posedness of the system by a semigroup approach. Then, by constructing an appropriate Lyapunov functional and utilizing the multiplier method, we establish the exponential decay of the system energy.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Geometric Endpoints, Global Trajectories, and Teichmüller Projection for the Möbius-Invariant Willmore Flow
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study endpoints and conformal projection of the Möbius-invariant Willmore flow in the round three-sphere. Under uniform nonumbilicity or an integrable weighted condition, image-measure transport yields a unique finite-time integral-varifold limit. Reduced Hopf trajectories have unique anchored finite-time profile and marked conformal endpoints at arbitrary energy. Every smooth global reduced trajectory converges smoothly modulo reparametrization to an elastic profile, with quantitative rates and finite dissipation length. We compute the differential of the conformal-class projection along reduced trajectories and prove that its maximal rank persists at every finite time when it holds initially. Near the Clifford torus, Hopf tori with the same marked conformal type can have noncollinear projected velocities, ruling out a common autonomous Teichmüller equation even after positive time recalibrations.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness of Finite-Time Varifold Limits for the Möbius-Invariant Willmore Flow
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove uniqueness of finite-time geometric endpoints for the Möbius-invariant Willmore flow in $\mathbb{S}^3$ under uniform quantitative nonumbilicity. The multiplicity-counting varifolds converge, without reparametrization or Möbius renormalization, to a unique integral two-varifold. An intrinsic transport estimate gives quantitative total-variation convergence of the induced area measures on the fixed domain and bounded-Lipschitz Cauchy control of their pushforwards. Together with Allard compactness and rectifiability, this upgrades subsequential compactness to full-trajectory varifold convergence. The limit has generalized Euclidean mean curvature in $L^2$ with the natural endpoint lower-semicontinuity bound. For finite maximal trajectories with initial energy at most $8π$, Jakob's subsequential alternative becomes sequence independent: the limit is zero, or it has unit density and embedded Lipschitz support of genus zero or one. For Hopf-torus trajectories under the same energy bound, nonumbilicity is automatic and the anchored constant-speed profiles converge weakly in $W^{2,2}$ and strongly in $W^{1,2}$ and $C^{1,α}$ for every $α<\frac{1}{2}$. At infinite time, the same method yields a unique limit under an additional finite-dissipation-length condition.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Talenti-type rigidity theorem and P-function constraints for the Pompeiu--Schiffer problem in every dimension
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Schiffer's conjecture asserts that the ball is the only bounded domain, with boundary homeomorphic to a sphere, carrying a nonconstant Neumann eigenfunction of the Laplacian that is constant on the boundary; for such domains it is equivalent to the Pompeiu problem. In 2026 it was disproved in the plane and in many higher dimensions by computer-assisted and analytic constructions. We study what survives. Our main result is a Talenti-type theorem valid in every dimension $N\ge2$: if the eigenfunction $u$ stays strictly below its boundary value $c>0$, then $kR^*\ge j_{N/2,1}$, where $k^2$ is the eigenvalue, $R^*$ the radius of the ball of equal volume and $j_{N/2,1}$ the first positive zero of $J_{N/2}$; equality holds only for the ball. We compare this threshold with the unconditional bound $kR^*\ge 2^{1/N}j_{N/2-1,1}$ given by the Krahn--Szegő inequality. Using Payne's P-function $P=|\nabla u|^2+λu^2$ we prove that every Schiffer domain satisfies $\max|u|>\sqrt N\,|c|$, together with pointwise and distance bounds. We correct the shape-optimization approach of an earlier work by computing the optimality condition of the associated boundary functional with an adjoint state. Using the transcendence of the zeros of Bessel functions of integer and half-integer order, we prove the infinitesimal rigidity of the ball, in every dimension, both for the Schiffer problem and for the Berenstein problem. Finally, we reconstruct numerically the convex four-dimensional counterexample of Guo and check the above statements on it.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As consequences, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family, and each critical spherical catenoid admits a smooth family of free boundary constant mean curvature deformations in its supporting ball. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$. We also show that the energy index of every critical spherical catenoid in $\mathbb{H^3}$, that is, the index of the second variation of its energy, equals four; hence the inequality between the energy index and the spectral index conjectured by Medvedev for geodesic balls of $\mathbb{H^n}$ fails.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 18 pages. v3: added Theorem 2 and Section 9: the energy index of every critical spherical catenoid in $\mathbb{H^3}$ is four, disproving the inequality in Medvedev [10, Remark 7]

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Talenti-type result for the Pompeiu-Schiffer Conjecture
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Schiffer's conjecture asserts that the ball is the only bounded simply connected domain carrying a Neumann eigenfunction of the Laplacian that is constant on the boundary; it is equivalent to the Pompeiu problem. In August 2026 it was disproved in the plane by computer-assisted constructions. We revisit the shape-optimization approach of~\cite{Se24} in the light of these counterexamples. We first show that the vanishing of the material derivative on the boundary, assumed in~\cite{Se24}, never holds, and we compute the correct optimality condition, involving an adjoint state, for the associated functional $J_2$. We prove that every planar Schiffer domain satisfies $\max|u| > \sqrt{2}|c|.$ Our main result is a Talenti-type theorem: if $u < c$ in $Ω$ , then $kR^* \geq j_{1,1},$ where $R^*$ is the radius of the disc of equal area, and equality holds only for the disc. Finally, using Siegel's transcendence theorem, we prove the infinitesimal rigidity of the disc for the Berenstein problem.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Comparability for quadratic forms with space-dependent singular measures
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper investigates quadratic forms $\mathcal{E}^Γ$ generated by configurations $Γ$ and families of measures that are parametrized in the space variable and singular with respect to the Lebesgue measure. A first basic result is the construction of corresponding integro-differential operators in divergence form. These operators are obtained by symmetrizing the family of singular measures. The main result is the comparability of the quadratic form $\mathcal{E}^Γ$ with the quadratic form $\mathcal{E}^s$ which is associated with the fractional Laplacian $(-Δ)^s$. Comparability of $\mathcal{E}^Γ$ and $\mathcal{E}^s$ implies Hölder regularity and a weak Harnack inequality for solutions to integro-differential equations involving these operators.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Asymptotic Stability of Planar Viscous Contact Waves for the Three-Dimensional Full Compressible Navier--Stokes Equations in the Whole Space
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The asymptotic stability of planar viscous contact waves is established for the three-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations in the whole space. The exact evolving planar background is constructed in a companion one-dimensional paper and may arise from a large integrable perturbation. The three-dimensional remainder has small energy, prescribed second-derivative bounds for density and velocity, and a prescribed first-derivative bound for temperature. Its initial temperature lies in a fixed positive interval; its second derivatives need only be finite. A unique global positive strong solution and algebraic decay in the uniform norm are obtained. The wave-strength threshold depends on lower-order planar bounds, while the allowed remainder size may depend on the complete planar datum.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 105 pages. Companion paper to "Stability and Optimal Decay of Viscous Contact Waves under Large Perturbations"

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stability and Optimal Decay of Viscous Contact Waves under Large Perturbations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The stability of viscous contact waves is established for the one-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations under large integrable perturbations. A unique global positive solution is obtained, which converges uniformly to a fixed Eulerian contact profile at the optimal inverse square-root rate in time. The wave-strength threshold depends only on bounds for the initial density perturbation in the first-order Sobolev norm, the energy of the initial velocity perturbation, the thermal relative entropy and the total conserved excess, together with positive lower bounds for the initial density and temperature. It is independent of higher Sobolev norms and the common far-field velocity. No square-integrability condition is imposed on the initial anti-derivatives. Derivative and pressure decomposition estimates are also established for the evolving solution.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 122 pages. Companion paper to "Asymptotic Stability of Planar Viscous Contact Waves for the Three-Dimensional Full Compressible Navier-Stokes Equations in the Whole Space"

Analysis of PDEs.title: Qualitative properties of positive solutions to mixed local and nonlocal critical problems in $\mathbb{R}^n$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the following mixed local and non-local critical elliptic equation: \begin{equation*}\label{0.1} \left\{ \begin{array}{lll} -Δu+(-Δ)^su=λh u^{p}+u^{2^*-1}, &\text{in}\,\, \mathbb{R}^n, u>0, &\text {in} \,\, \mathbb{R}^n, \lim\limits_{|x|\to\infty} u(x) = 0, \end{array} \right. \end{equation*} where $n\geqslant4, \,\, p\in (0,2^*-1),\,\, 2^*:=\frac{2n}{n-2}$ and $h$ is a positive function. We first show the existence and regularity results of viscosity solutions to the above critical elliptic equation. More precisely, from \cite{Su-Xu} weak solutions are obtained and we prove they are indeed viscosity solutions and their regularity is: \( u \in C^α(\mathbb{R}^n) \) for $p\in(0,1);$ \( u \in C^{2,β}(\mathbb{R}^n) \) for $p\in [1, 2^*-1).$ Moreover, for $p\in [1, 2^*-1)$, these viscosity solutions are indeed classical ones and we then prove the existence of positive solutions with the qualitative properties such as the decay estimates and the radial symmetry.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundary Harnack principle for abstract supersolutions on uniform domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We develop an axiomatic approach to the boundary Harnack principle on diameter-uniform domains in proper doubling metric measure spaces. Under critical-density and upper-contraction assumptions, we establish a scale-invariant one-sided boundary comparison between nonnegative supersolutions and positive solutions as well as Hölder continuity of quotients of positive solutions. Our framework does not require linearity or rectifiable curves. Applications include classical elliptic equations with Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, spectral fractional Laplacians, harmonic functions on fractals, and Pucci operators.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems I: The Half-Plane
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, the first in a series devoted to finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in domains with boundaries, we investigate finite-time boundary collisions and interior collapse for three vortices in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}^+$. We first prove that finite-time boundary collisions are impossible for arbitrary nonzero vortex circulations, without any restrictions on their signs or algebraic relations. The result excludes both simultaneous boundary collapse and individual vortex approaches to the boundary, without requiring convergence of the vortex trajectories. In contrast, we establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse by treating the boundary-induced interactions as a perturbation of the classical self-similar Gröbli collapse in the full plane. Under suitable conditions on the vortex circulations and collapse profile, we prove the existence of a one-dimensional local strong stable manifold of the augmented rescaled system, which generates exact solutions in which three distinct vortices collapse simultaneously at any prescribed interior point $z^*\in\mathbb{H}^+$. Moreover, these solutions are asymptotically self-similar, with the characteristic square-root collapse rate $O(\sqrt{T-t})$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the $W^{2,p}$ solvability for mixed boundary value problems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish global $W^{2,p}$ solvability for the Poisson equation with mixed Dirichlet--Neumann boundary conditions in two classes of domains in all dimensions $n\geq 2$. For $C^{1,α}$ domains with a Reifenbeg flat interface, we obtain the optimal range $1<p<4/3$, provided that $α>1-1/p$. For Lipschitz polyhedra with facewise boundary decompositions, we obtain solvability for $p$ close to $1$. In both settings, we establish endpoint $W^{2,1}$ solvability for data in an adapted atomic Hardy space. Applications of the methods to Lamé systems are also discussed.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniform $L^{\infty}$-Boundedness and Upper Semicontinuity of Global Attractors for Reaction--Diffusion Equations with Neumann Boundary Conditions on Uniform Jones Domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider a family of semilinear parabolic equations with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions on a family of varying non-smooth domains $\{Ω_μ\}_{μ\in Λ} \subset \mathbb{R}^n $. Assuming only that the domains have uniformly bounded volumes, bounded away from zero, and satisfy a uniform Jones condition, together with the usual structural requirements on the linear and nonlinear terms, we establish the well-posedness of the problem in an appropriate scale of fractional Banach spaces and prove the existence of global attractors. The attractors themselves are shown to be uniformly bounded in $L^{\infty}(Ω_μ)$ by an elementary truncation argument, which uses no property of the domains beyond the weak formulation of the Neumann condition. A Moser--Alikakos bootstrap iteration, in conjunction with the uniform Gronwall lemma and the uniform properties of the Jones extension operator, then yields the stronger statement that bounded sets of $L^{q}(Ω_μ)$ are absorbed, in finite time and uniformly in $μ$, into a fixed ball of $L^{\infty}(Ω_μ)$; this iteration uses only first-order Sobolev embeddings, which is what makes it available on domains where the domain of the elliptic operator is not contained in $H^{2}$. Finally, assuming the volume convergence of the domains, $|Ω_μ\triangle Ω_0| \to 0$, we construct a framework of connecting maps, show that the uniform Jones condition upgrades this convergence in measure to Mosco convergence of the associated bilinear forms, and prove that the family of attractors is upper semicontinuous at $μ= 0$ in $L^2(Ω_μ)$ and hence, by interpolation, in $H^s(Ω_μ)$ for every $s<1$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Propagation failure in heterogeneous FitzHugh--Nagumo systems via coupled upper and lower solutions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Traveling waves are fundamental objects in reaction--diffusion systems; however, spatial heterogeneities can distort or inhibit their propagation. Determining whether a given heterogeneity results in propagation failure remains challenging, particularly in systems with coupled components. In this paper, we present explicit constructions of stationary coupled upper and lower solutions tailored to specific heterogeneities for a one-dimensional FitzHugh--Nagumo system. By leveraging the mixed quasimonotone structure of the system, these barriers yield sufficient conditions for the failure of propagation for families of trapped initial conditions. The stationary constructions establish directional signal blocking in FitzHugh--Nagumo neuron models with localized reaction heterogeneities, including light-gated ionic conductances, and with abrupt geometric variations; the resulting stationary barriers persist for sufficiently small recovery diffusion. Additionally, we introduce explicit almost stationary barriers, which provide conditional bounds on the expansion of componentwise threshold regions in homogeneous media.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 36 pages, 7 figures. The new version corrects some minor typos and adds a new optogenetics motivation

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp coercivity estimates and stability loss for the Ginzburg-Landau energy
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper we investigate how the coercivity of the Hessian of the Ginzburg-Landau energy at local minimizers $u$ depends on the Ginzburg-Landau parameter $κ$ in the regime of large $κ$. This question is motivated by its crucial role in the numerical approximation of energy minimizers. Accounting for the degeneracy that is induced by phase invariance and possible additional neutral directions, we establish a universal lower bound of order $κ^2$ for the inverse coercivity constant $ρ_u(κ)$ of local minimizers with uniformly bounded Hessian kernel dimension. For nonvanishing states that satisfy a quantitative subcriticality condition, we prove a matching upper bound, showing that the quadratic scaling is sharp. On a fixed annulus with a fixed smooth magnetic potential, we then construct nonvanishing local minimizers for which $ρ_u(κ)\simeqκ^4$. Moreover, we exhibit branches of strictly stable local minimizers along which the inverse coercivity constant diverges as stability is lost. Consequently, no locally bounded upper estimate depending only on $κ$ can hold uniformly over all phase-nondegenerate local minimizers, even for a fixed domain and magnetic potential.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Elliptic $L^p$ Carleman estimates near the boundary, quantitative unique continuation, and applications to controllability and stabilization
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This article deals with quantitative unique continuation results up to and from the boundary for second-order elliptic equations with variable coefficients via $L^p$ Carleman estimates. The coefficients in the leading part are assumed to be Lipschitz continuous, and the potentials in the lower order term are allowed to belong to almost scale-invariant $L^q$ spaces. As applications, following the method of Lebeau and Robbiano, we obtain a spectral estimate which yields the interior null controllability of the associated parabolic equation, with an explicit dependence of the control cost on the potential. We also prove the logarithmic decay of the energy for damped wave equations with unbounded dampings and potentials.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global Classification of the Flat Singular Escobar-Yamabe Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In every dimension $n\geq3$, we classify positive solutions of the flat Escobar--Yamabe equation on the Euclidean half-space with a possible isolated boundary singularity at the origin. Solutions with a removable singularity are boundary bubbles. Up to dilation, the nonremovable solutions are the cylindrical solution and a family of periodic Delaunay solutions uniquely parametrized by the necksize $ε\in (0,1)$, the minimum of the normalized boundary trace. In each fundamental period $T_ε$, the trace has exactly two critical points, a nondegenerate minimum and a nondegenerate maximum. The period and the solution centered at the trace minimum and rescaled to period one depend smoothly on $ε$. As $ε\to 0$, $T_ε= \frac{4}{n-2}\log(1/ε)+O(1)$. As $ε\to 1$, the solutions converge to the cylindrical solution and their periods tend to that of its linearized oscillation. We use uniqueness in the odd and even classes for linear Robin equations to obtain reflection symmetry and continuation in the necksize.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Generalized Sobolev-Orlicz spaces based on the Riesz fractional gradient as interpolation and potential spaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this work we establish that the recently introduced fractional Sobolev spaces based on the Riesz fractional gradient of Musielak-Orlicz functions by one of the authors, coincide with the space of Bessel potentials of functions on such generalized Orlicz setting. Moreover, we identify them as complex interpolation spaces, and exploiting the well known properties for interpolation of operators we obtain several structural properties for those spaces.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Quantitative Homogenization and Global Lipschitz Estimates for Elasticity with Periodic Rigid Inclusions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the pure traction problem for linear elasticity in a bounded domain containing an $\varepsilon$-periodic array of perfectly rigid inclusions. For compatible $L^2$ boundary tractions on a Lipschitz domain, we prove an $O(\varepsilon^{1/2})$ error estimate in $H^1$ for a smoothed first-order two-scale expansion. If the exterior and inclusion boundaries are $C^{2,β}$, we also obtain a global Lipschitz estimate, uniform in $\varepsilon$, for compatible $C^{0,σ}$ tractions, where $0<σ<β$. The displacement is normalized modulo rigid motions, and the estimate controls the full gradient in the matrix and the inclusions. The boundary argument uses a local Neumann comparison estimate whose constant is independent of the choice of inclusions retained in cells cut by an artificial localization boundary. We prove this estimate by combining cellwise rigidification, divergence-free stress extensions, and duality, and then apply a boundary Campanato iteration and local estimates at the microscopic scale.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonlinear Stability of Planar Shock Waves for the Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations in R^3
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we investigate the global nonlinear stability and large-time decay rates of small-amplitude planar viscous shock waves for the three-dimensional (3-D) full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier equations in the whole space $\R^3$. {We prove that if the initial perturbation is sufficiently small in $H^3(\R^3)\cap\Hm(\R^3)$, then the Cauchy problem admits a unique global strong solution that converges to the planar shock profile without any phase shift. In the moving shock frame, both the conservative and primitive perturbations decay at the rate $(1+t)^{-1/4}$ in $H^3(\R^3)$. Their time and transverse spatial derivatives decay at the rate $(1+t)^{-1/2}$, measured in $\Hm(\R^3)$ for the conservative perturbation and in $H^1(\R^3)$ for the primitive perturbation.} No zero-mass condition or spectral stability assumption is imposed. On the whole space $\R^3$, the main analytical difficulties stem from the continuous transverse low frequencies, the opposite signs of shock compression in $L^2(\R^3)$ and unweighted $\Hm(\R^3)$, and the absence of density dissipation in the continuity equation coupled with temperature variations. To overcome these difficulties, we introduce a density-weighted $\Hm(\R^3)$ multiplier built from the inverse entropy Hessian and a modified curl operator. Through entropy symmetrization and the curl projection, all second-order acoustic derivatives of the potential cancel out and the transverse acoustic modes are controlled, so that the normal Euler drift is governed by the compressive derivative of the characteristic speed. Combined with an effective momentum variable and a momentum--density cross estimate, this negative-order energy absorbs the unfavorable compression term in the $L^2$ energy and closes the $H^3(\R^3)$ a priori estimates without loss of derivatives.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness of Axisymmetric Vortices in the Magnetic Ginzburg-Landau Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study vortex solutions of the magnetic Ginzburg-Landau model (or the Abelian-Higgs model). We establish uniqueness of axisymmetric vortex solutions for every winding number $n\geq1$ and coupling constant $λ>0$. Our proof uses a lattice inequality and constrained minimization to construct a positive radial solution lying above any two given radial solutions. A comparison argument based on the virial identity then establishes uniqueness. We further prove that the unique radial solution depends real analytically on $λ$ and that both radial profiles are strictly increasing with respect to $λ$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Elliptic theory and dimension drop for operators with divergence-free form-bounded drifts in one-sided chord-arc domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We develop a boundary value and potential theory for elliptic operators \[ L=-\Div(A
abla)+\B\cdot
abla \] with form-bounded drift in one-sided chord-arc domains. Assuming that the positive part of $\Div\B$ has sufficiently small form bound, we establish local regularity estimates and solvability of the Dirichlet problem, and construct the associated harmonic measure. Under the additional assumption $\Div\B\le0$, we construct a Green's function and prove pointwise and gradient estimates. For the characteristic distributional identity with a Dirac mass at the pole to hold, we will additionally assume either $\Div\B=0$ or $\B\in L^{n,1}_{	extup{loc}}(Ω)$. Moreover, in the divergence-free case, we obtain a local lower bound for the Green's function, CFMS estimates, doubling of harmonic measure, a comparison principle for nonnegative solutions with zero trace, and a change of pole formula. Finally, we construct, in the upper half-space, an operator of the form $-Δ+\B\cdot
abla$ with $\B$ form-bounded and divergence-free, whose harmonic measure exhibits dimension drop.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Maximal regularity for a compressible fluid-structure interaction system with Navier-slip boundary conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate a fluid-structure interaction system in which the dynamics of the fluid is described by the compressible Navier-Stokes equations, while the elastic structure is modeled by a damped plate equation. The fluid evolves in a three-dimensional bounded domain, with the structure occupies a part of its boundary. Instead of standard no-slip boundary conditions, we consider the Navier-slip boundary conditions at the fluid-structure interface as well as at the fixed boundary. We establish the local-in-time existence and uniqueness of strong solutions within $L^{p}-L^{q}$ framework. The existence result is obtained for small time by decoupling the linearized system and employing a cascade strategy combined with the Second Schauder fixed point theorem, whereas the uniqueness is shown by deriving weak regularity properties for the associated linear coupled operator in a Hilbert space setting. It is the first result addressing strong solutions for a compressible fluid interacting with a damped plate under Navier-slip boundary conditions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Regularity and Asymptotic Radial Symmetry of Solutions to Mixed Local-Nonlocal Parabolic Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the regularity and the long-time asymptotics of the solution to the following mixed local-nonlocal parabolic problem
  \[
  \left\{
  \begin{alignedat}{2}
  \partial_t u - Δu + (-Δ)^s u &= f \qquad &&\text{in }Ω\times(0, T),
  u&=0 \qquad &&\text{in }\bigl(\mathbb{R}^{n}\setminusΩ\bigr)\times[0, T),
  u(\,\cdot\,,0)&=u_{0} \qquad &&\text{in }Ω,
  \end{alignedat}
  \right.
  \]
  where $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$ is a bounded domain, $s\in(0,1)$ and $(-Δ)^s$ denotes the fractional Laplacian.
  We first develop the well-posedness theory for the problem on finite time intervals ($0<T<+\infty$).
  Existence and uniqueness of weak solutions are established in the natural energy space, followed by interior $H^{2,1}$-regularity and global $L^\infty$-bounds.
  Then, under the restriction $s\in(0,1/2)$ and $0<α\le 1-2s$, we prove that weak solutions become classical ones, obtaining $C^{2+α,1+α/2}$-regularity up to the boundary via the method of continuity and a perturbation argument.
  The accompanying a priori estimate guarantees that these classical solutions can be extended globally in time, thereby allowing us to consider the parabolic problem on the whole half-line ($T=+\infty$).
  Finally, for the special case $Ω=B_1(0)$ and $f=0$, we employ the moving-plane method together with the previously established boundary regularity to show that every positive classical solution is attracted, as $t\to +\infty$, by a steady state that is radially symmetric and strictly decreasing.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 25 pages. This version was submitted for publication in March 2026. The revised version will appear soon

Analysis of PDEs.title: Critical radial Green potential heat flow: A tension-controlled residue and a two-bubble example
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We compare two heat flows for the same corotational map of a disk into a warped product of two spheres, with the same fixed boundary values. The ordinary harmonic map heat flow develops a singularity in finite time. When the domain metric is instead determined by the critically normalized Green potential of the current energy distribution, the solution exists for all time. Two harmonic spheres of energy $4π$ form at separated scales, in addition to a nonconstant harmonic root. The energy and the image diameter of the necks tend to zero without restriction to a sequence of times. The main estimate controls the difference between the inner source mass and its critical value by the weighted tension. This is necessary because that difference is integrated over a neck of unbounded logarithmic length. Along a sequence of times the Green metric on the middle neck is asymptotically cylindrical after a spatially constant normalization.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Three-Dimensional Stability of Weakly Asymmetric Burgers Vortices: A Circulation-Independent Asymmetry Threshold and Optimal Decay
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Burgers vortices are stationary solutions of the Navier--Stokes equations in a background straining flow and serve as a model for vortex tubes in three-dimensional turbulence. In this paper, we consider weakly asymmetric strains and establish the local nonlinear asymptotic stability of the corresponding Burgers vortices against small three-dimensional perturbations for arbitrary circulation. Our proof exploits the specific axial structure of the linearized operator, combining a two-dimensional resolvent analysis with decay estimates for axial derivatives to control the full three-dimensional evolution. A first-moment decomposition isolates the slow modes, and Gaussian resolvent bounds are transferred to polynomially weighted spaces. This yields nonlinear stability with the endpoint exponential decay rate $(1-λ)/2$, where $λ$ denotes the strain asymmetry, without any additional polynomial factor in time. An exact nonlinear first-moment law demonstrates that this rate is optimal over the full admissible perturbation class, including at zero circulation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The geometry of anisotropic propagation for multidimensional reaction-diffusion equations in shifting habitats: A zero-sum stopping game approach
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the propagation geometry of multidimensional reaction-diffusion equations in shifting habitats. Using geometric optics techniques and viscosity solution theory, we prove that the associated rate functions converge locally uniformly to the unique viscosity solution of a variational inequality with singular initial data. We identify this limit as the value of a zero-sum stopping game whose zero set determines the Wulff shape. This zero set coincides with that of the positive part of the value function of an unconstrained optimal control problem if and only if Freidlin's condition holds. When Freidlin's condition fails, we derive a pointwise characterization of the stopping-game zero set, yielding a convex hull representation. These results then yield explicit Wulff shapes and directional spreading speeds for all habitat speed. As the habitat speed increases, the Wulff shape evolves from a large ball to a truncated ball. It then develops conical, cylindrical, and paraboloidal boundary components attached to spherical parts, before eventually becoming a smaller ball. Some of these geometric transitions occur while both axial spreading speeds remain unchanged. Moreover, by characterizing the optimal trajectories, we distinguish two mechanisms of nonlocal speed selection and show that such selection can occur in oblique directions even when it is absent in both axial directions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Rayleigh's conjecture in dimensions four and five
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove Rayleigh's conjecture for the clamped plate in dimensions four and five. In fact, we obtain a sharp comparison with the first Dirichlet eigenvalue: on every open set of finite positive measure, the first plate eigenvalue is at least the square of the Dirichlet eigenvalue multiplied by the ratio attained on a ball. The proof uses a homogeneous transformation of a trial function and its gradient. Two divergence identities reduce the comparison to positivity of a quadratic form in the Hessian. We establish the required Bessel inequalities by rational estimates for entire profiles and their remainders. An exact defect identity accounts for regular nodal sets, so the argument allows trial functions of either sign and imposes no boundary regularity. The domains may be disconnected or unbounded. We characterize equality up to sets of zero Sobolev capacity. We also obtain quantitative stability with the optimal quadratic power of the Fraenkel asymmetry.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Continuity of solutions to nonlocal nonlinear diffusion equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish an explicit modulus of continuity for locally bounded weak solutions to nonlocal porous medium type equations with measurable kernels. The nonlocal tail is only assumed to be integrable in time. The result lays a solid foundation for the intrinsic Harnack estimates of these equations.

Analysis of PDEs.title: An elementary observation on the Robin problem for NLS
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We present an infinite set of explicit solutions of the integrable focusing NLS equation on the half-line that are rapidly decaying and satisfy a homogeneous Robin condition but have very different behaviors on the wall $x=0$. We then argue that a similar phenomenon exists for a small non-homogeneous perturbation of the Robin problem. This renders a potential application of the unified transform method to non-linearizable Robin problems impossible.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Support of stochastic porous medium equations on bounded domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the spatial support of stochastic porous medium equations on bounded domains. Under a local nondegeneracy condition, additive noise gives full distributional support at every fixed positive time. For the Dirichlet problem with nonlocal multiplicative noise, we prove that the solution is either identically zero or has full support; excluding the zero state requires a separate non-hitting assumption. For a Neumann model, nonzero initial mass excludes the zero state and yields full support. The proofs combine Galerkin approximation with terminal Malliavin estimates. Numerical results illustrate the propagation mechanisms.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Almost global existence for quadratic Schrödinger equations in two dimensions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the two-dimensional quadratic Schrödinger equation $(i\partial_t+Δ)u=λ_1u^2+λ_2\overline u^{\,2}$ with initial data of size $\varepsilon$ in a weighted $H^2$ space. We prove almost global existence, with a lifespan of at least $\exp(c/\varepsilon)$ and decay at the optimal linear dispersive rate $t^{-1}$. Our proof is based on the space--time resonance method introduced by Germain, Masmoudi, and Shatah. The main new ingredient is the construction of a Besov-type profile space $\mathcal Z$, together with one-sided weighted bilinear estimates and spatially localized nonstationary phase estimates. This framework allows us to close the bootstrap argument without controlling the global second spatial moment of the free profile.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local $Tb$ theorems with applications to the Neumann problem and caloric measure
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We prove a local $Tb$ theorem with testing conditions on metric balls, for possibly non-doubling measures of polynomial growth on geometrically doubling metric spaces. It resolves the maximal-truncation version of Hofmann's local $Tb$ problem for all $1<p,q\leq\infty$, without assuming antisymmetry of the Calderón-Zygmund kernel.
  Our theorem allows accretive systems of complex testing measures satisfying a quantitative small-set condition; these measures need not be absolutely continuous with respect to the underlying measure. Testing requires only a one-level $L^0$ bound for maximal truncations, with an alternative for balls on which the underlying measure concentrates in a set of small relative diameter. We also remove antisymmetry from the known buffered and unbuffered fixed-truncation criteria. The proof combines a mixed corona decomposition adapted to the two testing systems with two-measure $L^2$ estimates for suppressed operators. We obtain the following applications:
  - If $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, $n\geq 2$, is a bounded domain with Ahlfors regular boundary satisfying the interior corkscrew condition, and the Neumann problem for the Laplacian in $Ω$ is solvable with data in $L^p$ for some $1<p<\infty$, then $\partialΩ$ is uniformly rectifiable. The proof applies the matrix-valued version of the theorem to the Cauchy-Clifford operator.
  - In the parabolic space $\mathbb{P}^n$, local time-directed $A_\infty$-type conditions on caloric and adjoint caloric measure imply $L^2(σ)$-boundedness of the spatial gradient of the heat single layer potential for boundary measures $σ$ with upper parabolic $(n+1)$-growth. This gives a parabolic counterpart of the harmonic-measure theorem of Mourgoglou and Tolsa without Ahlfors regularity, corkscrew or Harnack chain assumptions.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 141 pages. v2: we added the application to the Neumann problem

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the sharpness of a Liouville exponent in a competitive elliptic Schrödinger system
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We identify $p_*(n)=(n-1)/(n-3)$, $n\geq 5$, as the sharp exponent for Liouville theorems concerning a two-component elliptic Schrödinger system with self-focusing interactions and repulsive intercomponent coupling. We consider the strictly copositive regime, in which the repulsion strength is smaller than the geometric mean of the two self-interaction strengths. Quittner and Souplet (Comm. Math. Phys. 2012: 1--19) established a Liouville-type nonexistence result in the range $1<p<p_*(n)$. For every $p_*(n)<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, we construct bounded, nontrivial, nonnegative entire solutions whenever the repulsion strength approaches the copositivity threshold from below. The construction combines a compact variational functional, a periodic spectral gap, and uniform exterior estimates that remove a truncation. Our result gives a negative answer to the open question posed by Quittner and Souplet (Comm. Math. Phys. 2012: 1--19) of whether strict copositivity implies nonexistence of nontrivial nonnegative entire solutions throughout the Sobolev subcritical range when $n\geq 5$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A second-order estimate linear in the gradient for complex Hessian equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We use the maximum principle to prove a second-order estimate with linear dependence on the gradient for the nondegenerate complex Hessian equation on a compact Kähler manifold. The proof combines $C^0$ compactness and a refined concavity inequality with the use of nearby smooth admissible functions. A standard interpolation argument then yields the known uniform gradient and complex Hessian bounds.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Dirichlet problem for complex Monge--Ampère equations with Hölder continuous right-hand sides
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Dirichlet problem for the complex Monge--Ampère equation on bounded strongly pseudoconvex domains with $C^3$ boundary and $C^3$ boundary values. For every $n\ge2$ and $0<α<1$, each continuous Bedford--Taylor solution with a strictly positive $C^α$ right-hand side satisfies a global $C^{2,α}$ estimate. There is a unique such solution, which is strictly plurisubharmonic up to the boundary. Combining new boundary estimates with weighted integral estimates for the trace of the complex Hessian along an auxiliary parabolic flow, we obtain global $C^{1,β}$ bounds for every fixed $0<β<1$ in every dimension. Green function estimates and comparison arguments near the boundary give the boundary Hessian bound. Solutions of auxiliary Dirichlet problems with locally constant right-hand sides have uniform $W^{2,2n^2}$ bounds. Rescaling and interpolation then reduce the global Hessian estimate to interior regularity.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Well-posedness and attractors for the sub-quintic weakly damped wave equation with low-regularity forcing on $\mathbb{R}^3$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the weakly damped semilinear wave equation on $\mathbb{R}^3$ with a sub-quintic nonlinearity $f(u)$ and a forcing term of low regularity, $g\in H^{-1}(\mathbb{R}^3)$. By absorbing the forcing term into a stationary solution $h$ and then expanding the solution around $h$, we reduce the problem to a wave equation with potentials. Relying on Strichartz estimates for this equation, obtained through the Besov spaces associated with the Schrödinger operator, we establish the global well-posedness of weak solutions by an iteration argument on the Besov scale. In particular, uniqueness holds unconditionally in the energy class for $3<p<5$. Combining a refined decomposition of the solution with uniform tail estimates for trajectories starting from bounded sets, we then prove that the associated solution semigroup is asymptotically compact and, consequently, possesses a compact global attractor in the energy space $H^1(\mathbb{R}^3)\times L^2(\mathbb{R}R^3)$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local exact boundary controllability for the full compressible magnetohydrodynamic equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we are concerned with the local exact boundary controllability for the full compressible magnetohydrodynamic equations in a bounded domain in two and three space dimensions. We establish the local exact controllability around a constant equilibrium state. Our proof relies on the observability and controllability analysis of a suitably reformulated linearized system, together with a fixed point argument in weighted Sobolev spaces. The main novelty of this paper is to overcome the structural difficulties arising from the divergence free constraint and the strong coupling between the fluid and magnetic variables. To accommodate the solenoidal constraint, we introduce a magnetic potential formulation and develop a mixed coordinate approach.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The non-uniqueness of Leray solutions of the forced MHD equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct two distinct Leray solutions of the three-dimensional forced viscous, resistive magnetohydrodynamic equations in the whole space, with zero initial data and identical forcing. Our construction begins with a periodic axisymmetric unstable MHD mode associated with a rotating column and a nonconstant axial magnetic field. The rotating profile is also centrifugally unstable at zero magnetic field; the construction uses an unstable MHD eigenvalue and does not require magnetic destabilization of a hydrodynamically stable flow. Our spectral construction tracks a prescribed unstable MHD eigenvalue under radial truncation, the addition of small positive viscosity, and toroidal closure. The first two steps use a decomposition into a skew-adjoint principal part and compact feedback at a fixed Fourier frequency. Keeping the viscosity fixed, we bend the column into a compactly supported toroidal profile and obtain a genuine whole-space unstable eigenvalue through convergence of localized Stokes resolvents. A small-dilation limit and an exact rescaling then yield an unstable background in similarity variables. A nonlinear trajectory along its unstable direction produces the second solution. Both solutions are smooth for positive times and satisfy the energy equality. The forcing acts in both the velocity and magnetic equations.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Large-Time Analysis of the Langevin Dynamics for Energies Fulfilling Polyak-Łojasiewicz Conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this work, we take a step towards understanding overdamped Langevin dynamics for the minimization of a general class of objective functions $\mathcal{L}$. We establish well-posedness and regularity of the law $ρ_t$ of the process through novel a priori estimates, and, very importantly, we characterize the large-time behavior of $ρ_t$ under truly minimal assumptions on $\mathcal{L}$. In the case of integrable Gibbs density, the law converges to the normalized Gibbs measure. In the non-integrable case, we prove that the law diffuses. The rate of convergence, in terms of relative Dirichlet energy with respect to the Gibbs measure, is $\mathcal O(1/(σt))$, where $σ$ is the diffusion parameter. Under a Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition on $\mathcal{L}$, we also derive sharp exponential contractivity results toward the set of global minimizers. Combining these results we provide the first systematic convergence analysis of Langevin dynamics under PL conditions in non-integrable Gibbs settings: a first phase of exponential in time contraction toward the set of minimizers and then a large-time exploration over it with rate $\mathcal O(1/(σt))$ in terms of the relative Dirichlet energy.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Blow-up solutions of parabolic $p$-Laplacian inequalities on locally finite graphs
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study blow up behavior of the semilinear parabolic inequality with $p$-Laplacian operator and nonlinear source $u_t - Δ_p u \geq σ(x, t)Φ(u)$ on a locally finite connected weighted graph $G = (V, E)$. We extend the comparison principle and thereby establish the relationship between the initial value and the existence of blow-up solutions to the problem under different growth rates of $Φ$. We prove that when the growth rate of $Φ$ exceeds linear growth, blow-up solutions exist under appropriate initial conditions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The sharp Fourier extension estimate for the sphere
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The full strong Fourier extension estimate for the unit sphere is established in every ambient dimension at least three. The finite Knapp boundary is obtained by combining a uniform diagonal estimate on rescaled spherical graphs with a transverse product bound. A Whitney decomposition and a dyadic dual pairing yield strong type at the exact scaling exponents. The critical local estimate and the strict mixed range come from the recent work on Euclidean local smoothing.

Functional Analysis.title: Eccentricity in mutual strong Birkhoff-James orthographs of C*-algebras
Functional Analysis.summary: We determine the eccentricity of every vertex in the orthograph of mutual strong Birkhoff-James orthogonality for arbitrary finite-dimensional C*-algebras and for the algebra K(H) of compact operators on an infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space. This gives a more detailed description of the orthograph introduced by Arambašić et al. (Banach J. Math. Anal. 14 (2020), 1751-1772). As an application, we characterize scalar multiples of unitary elements among invertible elements of finite-dimensional C*-algebras in terms of eccentricity alone. We also show that M_3(C) is the only finite-dimensional C*-algebra whose orthograph has a non-trivial connected component of radius 3.

Functional Analysis.title: Adjoint Kernel Sensitivity of the Rough Heston Characteristic Exponent
Functional Analysis.summary: Multi-factor approximations of rough volatility kernels affect the characteristic exponents used in Fourier-based derivative valuation. We derive an adjoint representation for the first-order sensitivity of the rough Heston characteristic exponent with respect to its memory kernel, with model parameters and the input variance curve held fixed. The Volterra--Riccati functional $\mathcal L_T(K,z)$ admits a local real-analytic extension, jointly in the kernel perturbation and the transform parameter. The Fréchet derivative of this extension with respect to the kernel in $L^1$ is represented by integration against a continuous sensitivity kernel $B_K(u,z)$, obtained from a backward linear Volterra equation and independent of the perturbation direction. This representation resolves the leading-order contributions of kernel perturbations across memory lags. On the structural kernel class, which contains the fractional kernel and its multi-factor approximations and has empty interior in $L^1$, the extension yields Hadamard directional differentiability and a first-order expansion with a quadratic $L^1$-remainder for all sufficiently close structural kernels, uniformly on compact subsets of the strip of transform parameters. The same sensitivity kernel yields multi-factor weight and decay-rate derivatives. Numerical experiments at multi-factor reference kernels assess the finite-resolution implementation and illustrate how the lag distribution of positive perturbations with equal $L^1$ mass affects the first-order response.

Functional Analysis.title: The Canonical Family of Reduced Row Pivot Echelon Forms and the Induced Lexicographic Canonical Algorithm for Linear Programming
Functional Analysis.summary: A complete canonical family of uniquely normalized, row-equivalent representatives of an $m\times n$ matrix is introduced and termed the family of Reduced Row Pivot Echelon Forms (RRPEFs). All RRPEFs represent the same row space, with the standard reduced row echelon form, renamed the Upper RREF (URREF), and the Lower RREF (LRREF) as its extreme members. A reformulation of Noether's Complementary Subspace Basis Theorem yields normalized bases of the row space that coincide with the nonzero rows of the corresponding RRPEFs. Constructively, each RRPEF is obtained by multi-index Gauss--Jordan reduction of a nonsingular transition submatrix. Factoring the admissible pivot-index sets by equality of their associated RRPEFs yields a quotient set in canonical bijection with the set of distinct RRPEFs. This bijection transfers the strict lexicographic order to the distinct RRPEFs and induces a finite chain from the URREF to the LRREF. The resulting structure gives rise to the Induced Lexicographic Canonical Algorithm (ILCA). Lexicographic confinement and singular-transition skipping restrict the candidate domain, whereas RRPEF reuse and scalar-equivalent transition bypassing avoid redundant Gauss--Jordan reductions while retaining the corresponding basic-solution tableaux. Strict lexicographic progression prevents cycling, while the traversal proceeds independently of objective improvement under degeneracy-induced stalling. ILCA terminates when a feasible tableau satisfies the standard optimality conditions and otherwise completes the finite traversal, including for Tucker- and Cunningham-type totally degenerate configurations.

Functional Analysis.title: A Pricing and Hedging Framework for Infinite-Dimensional Financial Markets
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we provide a comprehensive study of how the classical Black--Scholes-type market framework behaves in an infinite-dimensional setting. The asset prices are modeled by stochastic evolution equations in a separable Hilbert space. The evolution of the risk-free asset and the corresponding discounting operators are governed by a strongly continuous group of bounded linear operators. Accordingly, we consider contingent claims with Hilbert-space-valued payoffs, whose values are discounted through the corresponding operators. Within this framework, we investigate the pricing and hedging of contingent claims, deriving the corresponding Hilbert-space-valued Black--Scholes equations and establishing exact replication results for both strong and mild solutions. We also study the special case where the infinitesimal generator is given by $A=rI$, allowing for real-valued contingent claims. We further investigate no-arbitrage and market completeness, introducing a Hilbert lattice structure to formulate arbitrage and characterizing attainability through operator equations associated with martingale representations. We also establish asymptotic completeness through finite-dimensional noise truncations. We introduce geometric Brownian motions in Hilbert spaces and derive sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of an equivalent risk-neutral measure, together with explicit pricing formulas for some tractable examples. These results extend key aspects of the classical Black--Scholes framework to markets with infinite-dimensional asset-price dynamics. As a concrete application, the model can be interpreted as a segmented market consisting of a sequence of one-dimensional geometric Brownian motions.

Functional Analysis.title: On Słociński-type decomposition, BCL model and unitary extension of commuting Banach space Wold isometries
Functional Analysis.summary: The adjoint of an operator plays the central role in Hilbert space operator theory. In particular, dilations of Hilbert space contractions, extension of commuting Hilbert space isometries to Hilbert space unitaries, orthogonal decompositions of contractions and functional models for commuting isometries are heavily dependent on the presence of adjoint. In this paper, we develop a theory of Banach space Wold isometries with right-complemented ranges by showing explicit constructions of Berger-Coburn-Lebow model and unitary extension for such isometric tuple without the help of adjoint. We also show that a Słociński type decomposition is possible for such a commuting tuple of Banach space isometries. Each of our results generalizes the corresponding result in the Hilbert space theory.

Functional Analysis.title: Generalized Sobolev-Orlicz spaces based on the Riesz fractional gradient as interpolation and potential spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: In this work we establish that the recently introduced fractional Sobolev spaces based on the Riesz fractional gradient of Musielak-Orlicz functions by one of the authors, coincide with the space of Bessel potentials of functions on such generalized Orlicz setting. Moreover, we identify them as complex interpolation spaces, and exploiting the well known properties for interpolation of operators we obtain several structural properties for those spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: Rayleigh's conjecture in dimensions four and five
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove Rayleigh's conjecture for the clamped plate in dimensions four and five. In fact, we obtain a sharp comparison with the first Dirichlet eigenvalue: on every open set of finite positive measure, the first plate eigenvalue is at least the square of the Dirichlet eigenvalue multiplied by the ratio attained on a ball. The proof uses a homogeneous transformation of a trial function and its gradient. Two divergence identities reduce the comparison to positivity of a quadratic form in the Hessian. We establish the required Bessel inequalities by rational estimates for entire profiles and their remainders. An exact defect identity accounts for regular nodal sets, so the argument allows trial functions of either sign and imposes no boundary regularity. The domains may be disconnected or unbounded. We characterize equality up to sets of zero Sobolev capacity. We also obtain quantitative stability with the optimal quadratic power of the Fraenkel asymmetry.

Functional Analysis.title: Harmonic and Monogenic Representations of White Noise and its weighted harmonic Bergman estimates
Functional Analysis.summary: Continuing Feichtinger's generalized stochastic process theory, we analyze harmonic and monogenic representations of white noise in Euclidean spaces. We define its convolution with square-integrable functions. Using the weighted Sobolev regularity of the white noise, we establish a high-dimensional Sokhotski-Plemelj formula for the white noise density. Furthermore, we embed these representations into new weighted Bergman spaces, proving that the weighted Bergman norms of the harmonic representations are bounded by the white noise's weighted Sobolev norms.

Functional Analysis.title: Stable topology and stable compactness
Functional Analysis.summary: To solve a large class of noncompact problems ubiquitous in random functional analysis and its applications, most of compactness-based fundamental theorems established for normed spaces or locally convex spaces are required to be extended for random normed modules and random locally convex modules in an appropriate way of weakening compactness. To achieve this goal, in this paper we first develop stable set theory by introducing some new set-theoretic tools, then propose a class of topological spaces with a stable structure, called stable topological spaces, and in particular propose and systematically develop the theory of stably compact spaces, which is a natural generalization of that of compact spaces. The resulting theory is of independent interest from the perspective of general topology since its investigation requires an analysis of stratification structures coordinated with partitions of unity in a complete Boolean algebra. Finally, we show the power of the theory of stable compactness by establishing random Banach-Alaoglu, random James and random Banach-Bourbaki-Kakutani-Šmulian theorems.

Functional Analysis.title: Hausdorff operators and fractional Hausdorff operators in the Dunkl setting
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we investigate the boundedness properties of the Dunkl-type Hausdorff operator on generalized Dunkl-type Morrey spaces and generalized Dunkl-type Campanato spaces. Furthermore, we introduce the fractional Dunkl-type Hausdorff operator and study its boundedness from $L^p(\mathbb{R}, dμ_α)$ to $L^q(\mathbb{R}, dμ_α)$. We also establish the boundedness of the fractional Dunkl-type Hausdorff operator on generalized Dunkl-type Morrey spaces under suitable conditions. As a consequence of our main results, we derive several applications. Finally, we evaluate the exact norm of the Dunkl-type Hausdorff operator on Dunkl-type Morrey spaces and Dunkl-type Campanato spaces.
Functional Analysis.comment: NA. arXiv admin note: text overlap with arXiv:2504.17241

Functional Analysis.title: Spectral Limits of the Neumann-Poincaré Operator on Degenerating Tori
Functional Analysis.summary: We determine the limit of the spectrum of the Neumann-Poincaré operator on circular tori as the torus degenerates. As the central hole closes, the spectrum converges to $[-1/2,0]$ together with a set of positive points, which we characterize as eigenvalues of explicit limiting operators. As the cross-section shrinks, the spectrum converges to $[0,1/2]$.

Functional Analysis.title: Nonisomorphic separable Banach spaces at Lipschitz distance one
Functional Analysis.summary: We construct nonisomorphic separable real Banach spaces whose multiplicative Lipschitz distance is one. Building on OpenAI's graph-space construction, we arrange two sequences of graph spaces into countably many blocks and form two spaces that differ by a single additional block. This block distinguishes their linear structures: one space contains a complemented copy of $\ell_1(c_0(\ell_2))$, whereas the other does not. By mapping the additional block to increasingly late positions and rearranging the remaining blocks, we obtain homeomorphisms whose Lipschitz constants and those of their inverses tend to one, while both spaces and their norms remain unchanged.
Functional Analysis.comment: 66 pages. Added information on the Lean formalization, its public release, and the use of AI in its development. Mathematical results unchanged

Functional Analysis.title: The Douglas property for multiplier algebras of operators
Functional Analysis.summary: For a collection of reproducing kernels k which includes those for the Hardy space of the polydisk and ball and for the Bergman space, k is a complete Pick kernel if and only if the multiplier algebra of the Hilbert space H^2(k) associated to k has the Douglas property. Consequences for solving the operator equation AX=Y are examined.
Functional Analysis.comment: V2 (Nov 2011) to V3 (Nov 2026): A false finite-to-infinite assertion between Definition 1.8 and Theorem 1.9, which did not materially impact the stated results, has been removed and a counterexample added. See the discussion in the penultimate paragraph in the introduction and the appendix for other changes. We thank Daniel Alpay for questioning the validity of this finite-to-infinte claim

Functional Analysis.title: Differentiation, Taylor series, and all order spectral shift functions, for relatively bounded perturbations
