Functional Analysis.summary: Given $H$ self-adjoint, $V$ symmetric and relatively $H$-bounded, and $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{C}$ satisfying mild conditions, we show that the Gateaux derivative $$\frac{d^n}{dt^n}f(H+tV)|_{t=0}$$ exists in the operator norm topology, for every natural $n$, give a new explicit formula for this derivative in terms of multiple operator integrals, and establish useful perturbation formulas for multiple operator integrals under relatively bounded perturbations. Moreover, if the $H$-bound of $V$ is less than 1, we obtain sufficient conditions on $f$ which ensure that the Taylor expansion $$f(H+V)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty\frac{1}{n!}\frac{d^n}{dt^n} f(H+tV)\big|_{t=0}$$ exists and converges absolutely in operator norm. Finally, assuming that $V(H-i)^{-p}\in\mathcal{S}^{s/p}$ for $p=1,\ldots,s$ for some $s\in\mathbb{N}$ (for instance, when $H$ is an order 1 differential operator on an $s-1$ dimensional space), we show that the Krein--Koplienko spectral shift functions $η_{k,H,V}$, satisfying $${Tr}\left(f(H+V)-\sum_{m=0}^{k-1}\frac{1}{m!}\frac{d^m}{dt^m} f(H+tV)\big|_{t=0}\right)=\int_{\mathbb{R}} f^{(k)}(x)η_{k,H,V}(x)dx,$$ exist for every $k=1,2,3,\ldots$, independently of $s$. The latter result (which is significantly stronger than \cite{vNS22}) is completely new also in the case that $V$ is bounded. The proof is based on \cite{PSS}, combined with a generalisation of the multiple operator integral compatible with \cite{HMvN}. We discuss applications of our results to quantum physics and noncommutative geometry.

Functional Analysis.title: Cesàro means of firmly nonexpansive iterates need not converge strongly
Functional Analysis.summary:
Firmly nonexpansive operators arise naturally as resolvents of monotone operators and as generalizations of projections and proximal mappings in convex optimization and fixed point theory. While their iterates are known to converge weakly to a fixed point, strong convergence is not guaranteed (Genel and Lindenstrauss, 1975). Strong convergence of Cesàro means of iterates is also known to fail for general nonlinear nonexpansive mappings (Krengel and Lin, 1987).
  In this paper, we show that this failure persists in the much smaller class of firmly nonexpansive mappings. Using suitable meshes, we construct a new explicit family of counterexamples in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces with the origin as the unique fixed point. In the harmonic case, the Cesàro means of the iterates remain bounded away from the origin. Another variant yields Cesàro means that converge strongly to the origin. A third variant presents Cesàro means whose norms oscillate in the sense that their liminf is zero while their limsup is positive. Thus the strong convergence conclusion in von Neumann's linear mean ergodic theorem does not extend to Baillon's nonlinear mean ergodic theorem, even for firmly nonexpansive mappings.

Functional Analysis.title: Spectral comparison of compound cocycles generated by delay equations in Hilbert spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We study linear cocycles generated by nonautonomous delay equations in a suitable Hilbert space and their extensions, called compound cocycles, to exterior powers. Using a recent version of the frequency theorem, we develop analytical techniques for comparing spectral properties, such as uniform exponential dichotomies, between such cocycles and semigroups generated by stationary equations. Most of this work is devoted to the theoretical foundations related to regularity and structure in PDEs associated with delay equations. We briefly discuss some specific applications, especially those related to the global stability problem, which are described in detail in our adjacent works.

Functional Analysis.title: On the Bendixson criterion for attractors of dynamical systems in metric spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We revisit the Bendixson criterion for attractors, originally proposed by R.A. Smith for the finite-dimensional case and subsequently extended by M.Y. Li and J.S. Muldowney to Banach spaces. First, we give a concise proof of the criterion for general dynamical systems (semiflows, mappings, cocycles) in metric spaces using Čech cohomology. This approach allows for a significant weakening of previously known conditions while simultaneously resolving existing misunderstandings. Second, for compact invariant sets of semiflows that are topologically one-dimensional and possess zero first cohomology (e.g., attracting a superset with zero first cohomology), we prove that any chain recurrent point within the invariant set must be an equilibrium. In the proof, we construct a global strict Lyapunov function using Whitney-Bebutov sections. Third, we generalize and refine R.A. Smith's theorem concerning the finiteness of the set of fixed points for analytic mappings, as well as M.L. Cartwright's theorems on to almost periodic flows.

Functional Analysis.title: Schwartz-Class Gabor Windows and the Balian-Low Classification
Functional Analysis.summary: A lattice Gabor frame consists of a window function and its time-frequency shifts along a lattice. We classify the lattices that admit Schwartz-class and, equivalently, Feichtinger frame windows. Except for symplectically irrational lattices of critical covolume 1, we determine the lattice-dependent achievable window smoothness and decay using the scale of modulation spaces. For symplectically rational lattices, including the rational lattices typically used in digital applications, the classification is governed by an integer lattice parameter introduced herein, the symplectic index gap. Our results extend the classical and amalgam Balian-Low theorems. The companion paper "Tilings, Packings, and Smooth and Compactly Supported Gabor Windows" develops the associated tiling-packing theorem and compact-support constructions.

Functional Analysis.title: Eaton Triples, Polar Representations, and Lie Triple Systems
Functional Analysis.summary: An Eaton triple consists of a finite dimensional real inner product space, a closed subgroup of its orthogonal group, and a closed convex cone that meets every orbit and satisfies an extremal inner product inequality. In the literature on group majorization and invariant norms it is a standing hypothesis that the triple admits a reduced triple, obtained by restriction to the span of the cone. We prove that this is always the case: the axioms force the span of the cone to be a section of a polar representation, and Gichev's orbit intersection theorem applies. The reduced group is a finite reflection group, crystallographic when the group is connected; Eaton cones are its closed chambers, unique up to the group action; and a compact linear group admits an Eaton cone if and only if its representation is polar with a finite reflection group as Weyl group. For connected groups we construct a Lie triple system on the space, determined by the inner product and the orbits alone, for which the cone is a Weyl chamber; unlike Dadok's orbit equivalence with a symmetric space, it involves no choices.

Functional Analysis.title: Controlled Riemannian rigidity
Functional Analysis.summary: Given a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on a compact connected manifold, we prove that the space of invariant Riemannian metrics whose symmetry group is precisely the group in question is open dense in that of all invariant metrics provided the orbit space is sufficiently large. This strengthens the author's prior results and recovers Ebin's to the effect that trivial-symmetry Riemannian metrics constitute an open dense set. In the process, the discussion also addresses a number of apparent gaps in said sources, pertaining to the rigidity results in question.

Functional Analysis.title: Schauder exponential basis which is not Riesz
Functional Analysis.summary: We show that there exists a Schauder basis $\{e^{i λ_n t}\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with real frequencies in $L^2(-π,π)$ which is not a Riesz basis.

Functional Analysis.title: On the lower bound for the $L^1$ norm of Liouville exponential sums. II
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $λ$ denote the Liouville function, and put \[ I_λ(X)=\int_0^1\left|\sum_{n\le X}λ(n)e^{2πi nα}\right|\,dα. \] In this paper, we prove that \[ \limsup_{X \to \infty} \frac{\log I_λ(X)}{\log X} \ge \frac{1}{3}. \]

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp Constants and First-Order Asymptotics in a Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu Formula for Riesz Potentials
Functional Analysis.summary: We investigate sharp constants and asymptotic properties of a pointwise inequality of Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu type in dimension \(n\geq2\), involving Riesz potentials and Spector's nonlinear fractional differential operator \(\mathcal D^α\) of order \(0<α<1\). For every \(n\geq3\) and \(0<α<1\), we determine the optimal constant without symmetry restrictions and prove that it is attained by smooth radially monotone functions centered at the evaluation point. The proof combines geodesic-flow invariance, kernel monotonicity, and circular rearrangement. In dimension two, we establish the leading-order asymptotic behavior of the optimal constant and derive an explicit formula in the radial class. We further refine the pointwise limit established by A. Claros and C. Pérez [Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu formula for Riesz potentials, Adv. Math. 503 (2026), Art. 111226] by obtaining an explicit first-order correction with a quadratic remainder uniform in the spatial variable. Finally, we strengthen their convergence-in-measure result on compact subsets for functions in \(W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^n)\) by establishing almost-everywhere convergence as \(α\to1^-\), without passing to a subsequence.

Functional Analysis.title: Higher-order derivatives and their applications to diffeomorphism groups
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we apply higher-order tangent bundles and higher-order derivative maps to study countable subgroups of the diffeomorphism group ${\rm Diff}(M)$ of a closed smooth manifold $M$. Using this framework, we introduce the concept of higher-order $μ$-discreteness for subgroups $Γ< {\rm Diff}(M)$, and show that both the strong Novikov conjecture and the coarse Baum--Connes conjecture hold for countable groups with higher-order $μ$-discreteness. Finally, we give examples showing that higher-order $μ$-discreteness encompasses a strictly larger class of subgroups of $\operatorname{Diff}(M)$ than its lower-order counterpart.

Functional Analysis.title: Analytic criteria for criticality of subordinated Schrödinger operators
Functional Analysis.summary: For a subordinated Schrödinger operator, we introduce a quantity that plays a role analogous to the bottom of the spectrum of a Schrödinger operator, and establish analytic criteria for subcriticality, criticality and supercriticality of a subordinated Schrödinger operator.

Functional Analysis.title: Nearly invariant subspaces in the real Hardy space
Functional Analysis.summary: The objective of this article is to study nearly invariant subspaces of the backward shift operator on the real Hardy space. We also investigate nearly invariant subspaces with finite defect, and as a consequence, provide a characterization for almost invariant subspaces of the backward shift operator.

Functional Analysis.title: A New Approach to Universal Measurability
Functional Analysis.summary:
V. Fedorchuk, A. Chigogidze and T. Banakh in 2003 and V. Bogachev in 2024 posed the following questions: (i) is it true that $P_τ(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $P_σ(X)$; (ii) is it true that $P_R(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $P_R(βX)$ if and only if $X$ is pseudocompact, where $P_σ$, $P_τ$ and $P_R$ are the functors of probability measures on the space $X$ that are, respectively, $σ$-additive on the Baire $σ$-algebra, $τ$-additive, and Radon? The answers to these questions are negative. In this paper the questions are put into a general framework: for spaces of measures $Q_p(X)\subset Q_q(X)$ of various types we study when $Q_p(X)$ is $C$-embedded ($C^*$-embedded) in $Q_q(X)$. It is proved that for spaces of alternating measures $M_p(X)\subset M_q(X)$ the $C$-embeddedness, the $C^*$-embeddedness and the $G_δ$-density of $M_p(X)$ in $M_q(X)$ are equivalent, and a criterion in terms of sequences of continuous functions is given. The question of $C$-embedding of measure spaces is an extension of the question of coincidence of measure spaces, which is a development of the classical concepts of universally measurable and universal measure zero sets.
  Note (corrected version): incorrect statements of the previous versions are marked or removed; see the last section of the paper.

Functional Analysis.title: Basis selection, universal sampling discretization, and sampling recovery
Functional Analysis.summary: For every real $N$-dimensional subspace of $L_2$, we construct one orthonormal basis such that, for every $1\le v\le N$, at most $Cv\log(eN/v)$ positively weighted samples discretize the squared $L_2$ norm of all $v$-term combinations. Random rotations also give simultaneous weighted $L_p$ estimates and a sharp $C\log(eN)$ bound for the squared $L_2$ norm of the pointwise maximum. For prescribed coefficient classes, a change of measure yields sampling recovery estimates from $Cv\log^3(2v)$ samples under a lower Riesz inequality and a common square-integrable pointwise bound.

Functional Analysis.title: Weighted Logarithm Laws in non-commutative Probability
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove analogues of weighted laws of iterated logarithm and laws of logarithm for non-commutative martingales and independent random variables respectively. First we obtain a weighted LIL for non-commutative martingales, extending the sharp unweighted result of arXiv:2509.22037v2 to the case for polynomial weights, then by approximation to a broader class of functions. Then we proved a weighted law of logarithm for triangular array of weights and replacing the coefficient in the denominator by regularly varying functions with index $α$. We show that the normalised sums converge to 0 for $α> 1/2$ and for the case $α=1/2$, we obtain the sharp upper bound with constant $\sqrt{2}$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Gradient Estimates for Singular-Degenerate Elliptic Equations with Solution-Dependent Coefficients
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a conormal boundary value problem for a class of singular-degenerate quasilinear elliptic equations in divergence form in bounded domains. The leading terms are measurable in the spatial variable and depend nonlinearly on both the solution and its gradient. The singularity or degeneracy is governed by a power of the distance to the domain boundary, with exponent greater than negative one. In particular, the corresponding weights need not belong to the Muckenhoupt $A_2$ class. Assuming that the weighted mean oscillations of the leading terms in the spatial variable are sufficiently small on small balls and that the domains have Lipschitz boundaries with sufficiently small Lipschitz constants, we establish global weighted $W^{1,p}$-estimates for weak solutions with bounded weighted mean oscillation. Our results extend recent estimates for equations whose leading terms are independent of the solution itself.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp Quantitative Convergence of Compactly Supported Aggregation-Diffusion
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish the quantitative convergence of nonlinear aggregation-diffusion equations in dimension one, with sublinear attraction kernel and degenerate diffusion higher than quadratic. In these models, steady state is known to be the unique, compactly supported, and radial decreasing probability distribution. In this paper, we work with compactly supported densities in dimension one, we prove these solutions converge to the steady state exponentially fast.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Dynamic linear equations in the presence of small perturbations of an interface
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider solutions to the initial boundary value problems for both heat and wave equations in two dimensions. In this paper, we aim to advance the development of high-order terms in the asymptotic expansions of current boundary perturbations caused by small perturbations of the shape of a $C^2$-boundary inhomogeneity. Our derivations are rigorously derived by the field expansion (FE) method (formal derivation) and proved by layer potential techniques. It extends those already derived for small-volume inhomogeneities to develop efficient algorithms for determining certain properties of the shape of an inhomogeneity based on boundary measurements.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Allard Regularity for Abelian Yang--Mills--Higgs Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove an Allard regularity theorem for critical points of the Abelian Yang-Mills-Higgs energy at critical coupling in every ambient dimension. A new cylindrical monotonicity formula for the full excess, based on an improved Modica inequality, converts the tilt-excess decay of De Philippis-Halavati-Pigati into rigidity of nontrivial entire critical points with almost unit density. This resolves their Gibbons conjecture without a local minimising assumption. Adapting the local vortex expansion and projected linear theory of Badran-del Pino, we obtain quantitative vortex approximation and uniform interior $C^{2,α}$ estimates for the nodal sets. To pass to nonzero complex levels, we use a Hodge decomposition of the difference between the actual and approximate connections: curvature comparison controls the co-closed part, while the Coulomb condition gives estimates for the exact part and hence for the phase. In the Coulomb gauge with vanishing normal component on the outer boundary, this yields graphical $C^{2,α}$ bounds for all levels $\{u_\varepsilon=t\}$, uniformly for $|t|\leq1-b$, in an interior tubular neighbourhood of the nodal set.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: This is a substantial update to the previous paper - we remove the dimension restriction and extend the regularity from the nodal set to all level sets

Analysis of PDEs.title: Non-local phase transition models for partial singularities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study $Γ$-convergence, under appropriate scalings, of the energy functionals \[ F_\varepsilon(u) := [u]_{H^s(Q)}^2 + \int_{Q} W_\varepsilon(u)\,dx, \] where $s \in (0,1)$, $[\cdot]_{H^s(Q)}$ denotes the $H^s$-seminorm in $Q\subset \mathbb{R}^{n}$, and $W_\varepsilon$ is a multi-well potential featuring infinitely many equally spaced wells together with additional intermediate wells whose height vanishes at a prescribed rate. Depending on this rate, different limiting behaviors emerge, ranging from classical models to new intermediate regimes.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Bayesian inverse problems and epidemic-threshold uncertainty for a heterogeneous SIS reaction-diffusion model
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study Bayesian inference of persistence from early observations of a heterogeneous susceptible--infected--susceptible (SIS) reaction--diffusion model with standard incidence. We show that the leading prevalence dynamics depend on the unknown coefficients only through the difference between the transmission and recovery rates and the infected diffusivity. The same pair determines the principal eigenvalue whose sign governs persistence, so early prevalence can inform the threshold even when the individual rates remain uncertain. We prove global weak well-posedness and quantitative parameter stability for the SIS system and use the resulting observation-map estimates to establish Bayesian well-posedness. For an initial infection of size $\varepsilon$, we derive a uniform second-order expansion that describes how the separate rates enter prevalence. Incidence depends explicitly on transmission at leading order. When the noise standard deviation is proportional to $\varepsilon$, we prove $O(\varepsilon)$ convergence in Hellinger distance of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits for both prevalence alone and joint prevalence and incidence data. We bound the principal eigenvalue using the growth rate of the infected $L^2$ norm between two times. This rate gives a lower bound for the full nonlinear system, and the upper bound separates spatial transients from nonlinear saturation. Uniform spectral estimates and bounds on infection size and measurement error give sufficient conditions for persistence and extinction. We also bound the error in posterior persistence probabilities under forward and eigenvalue approximation, accounting for posterior mass near the threshold. Numerical examples illustrate threshold inference and the predicted \(O(\varepsilon)\) convergence of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits in Hellinger distance.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Regularity of minimisers for the $p$-distance functional
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider regularity of minimisers of the $p$-distance functional $\mathcal{F}[u]=\int_Ω\mathrm{dist}(Du,K)^p \mathrm{d}x$ where $K \subset \mathbb{R}^{N \times n}$ is a compact set. We distinguish the scalar and vectorial cases, and consider geometric conditions on $K$ where regularity can be improved.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp regularity results for variational integrals asymptotic to the $p$-Dirichlet integral
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the regularity for minimisers of $\int_ΩF(Du) \mathrm{d}x$ where $F(z) \approx |z|^p$ in suitable senses at infinity. Depending on the strength of this asymptotic condition, we discuss various regularity results, and by means of counterexamples we show they are sharp. An effort is made to obtain results without assuming unnecessary regularity of $F$ while covering the full range $1<p<\infty$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Regularity of $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic functions with applications to stable minimal hypersurfaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We show that the derivative of a $Q$-valued $C^1$ function on an $n$-dimensional domain that is locally harmonic on its regular set is locally Dirichlet minimising, and that its branch set coincides with that of its derivative. As a consequence, we get that a $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic function is $C^{1,α}$ and that its branch set is countably $(n-2)$-rectifiable when $n\geq 3$ and discrete when $n=2$.
  Our methods are directly applicable to the regularity theory of stable minimal hypersurfaces. We show that a multi-valued Lipschitz function whose graph is a two-sided, properly immersed, stable minimal $n$-dimensional hypersurface with locally $\mathcal{H}^{n-2}$-finite singular set, and whose Lipschitz constant is sufficiently small is in fact multi-valued $C^{1,α}$. As a consequence, we obtain optimal regularity conclusions for a branched sheeting theorem of Bellettini for singular immersions.
  When $n=2$, we obtain stronger conclusions and show that locally about a branch point, a $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic function is the real part of a Dirichlet minimiser which is itself obtained from a finite number of holomorphic functions via classical branching, thus giving a full series expansion for the function near the branch point. Furthermore, we prove that the class of branched, two-sided, properly immersed, stable minimal surfaces with isolated singularities is compact under varifold convergence.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Scattering thresholds for the NLS equation with polynomially decaying damping
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a linear damping of strength $a(1+t)^{-θ}$, where $a>0$ and $θ\ge0$, in the whole energy-subcritical range. For $θ>0$, the time-averaged damping vanishes, so that the scattering theory developed in our previous work does not apply. We show that the long-time dynamics is governed by the time integrability of an effective coupling, which decays faster than any power when $θ<1$, polynomially when $θ=1$, and not at all when $θ>1$. In the mass-subcritical case, all solutions are global. They scatter when $θ<1$ and, for $θ=1$, above an explicit exponent depending on $a$. On the other hand, no non-trivial solution is asymptotically free below a second explicit exponent when $θ=1$, and below the short-range exponent $1+2/N$ when $θ>1$. In the mass-critical case, solutions are global below the ground state. Moreover, for $θ\le1$, every solution which survives until its decaying mass becomes subcritical is global and scatters. In the intercritical case, we prove small data scattering and, for $θ\le1$, a dichotomy between scattering and grow-up of the gradient. Finally, in the scale-invariant case $θ=1$, we analyze the range between the two thresholds. We reduce the equation exactly to a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a decaying repulsive harmonic potential, and we construct approximate solitary waves with an integrable error. This leads to a conjecture, supported by numerical simulations, on the sharpness of the scattering threshold.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Phragmén-Lindelöf theorems for parabolic equations of p-laplacian-type
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider rigidity properties of ancient solutions to parabolic equations of $p$-Laplacian-type. We start with the degenerate range $p>2$. First, a solution which is bounded above in an intrinsic backward paraboloid is either bounded in an entire half-space, or grows in space at least like a power with a sharp, explicit exponent. This relies on the expansion of positivity and on the Comparison Principle. Then, we turn to the growth in time. Positivity in the paraboloid alone yields no upper rate: we present explicit self-similar solutions, positive in the paraboloid, with $u(0,-T)\simeq T^β$ for every $β\le0$ and every $β\ge1$. For solutions bounded below in the paraboloid, we prove a dichotomy for the infimum of $u(\cdot,-T)$ on a ball whose radius is a fixed fraction of that of the paraboloid at time $-T$: either it is of order $T$ along a sequence of times, or it grows sublinearly, like $T^ζ$ with $ζ<1$ explicit. In the second case, a Harnack-type argument shows that the supremum on the same ball grows at most linearly. Then, we carry out the same program in the singular, supercritical range $\frac{2N}{N+1}<p<2$, where the picture is similar but several roles are reversed. In space, the iteration via the Comparison Principle can only be started from a point lying above an explicit slope, and explicit solutions show that nothing better than a cone bound can be expected below it. The self-similar profiles are unique but only local, and positivity in the paraboloid is compatible with every exponent $β\le1$ and with no exponent in $(1,\frac1{2-p})$. In time, the dichotomy is replaced by an a priori linear bound for the infimum. Similarities and differences between the two ranges are collected at the end of the work.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Pseudoconformal characterizations of scattering in weighted Sobolev spaces for non-scaling-invariant mass-subcritical NLS
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider mass-subcritical nonlinear Schrödinger equations with finitely many power-type nonlinearities and initial data in weighted Sobolev spaces. In the short-range regime, we prove a pseudoconformal characterization of scattering in the weighted energy space $Σ$. We also establish a fractional counterpart in $Σ^s$, $s\in(0,1)$, formulated in terms of the boundedness of the order-$s$ pseudoconformal operator. Our results include equations with combined nonlinearities, for which no distinguished scaling symmetry is available. As an application of the fractional theory, we prove small-data scattering in $Σ^s$, $s\in(0,1]$. The arguments rely on the lens transformation, harmonic-oscillator Strichartz estimates, and fractional harmonic Sobolev estimates.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Scattering of the defocusing Calogero--Moser derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the long time behavior of solutions to the defocusing Calogero--Moser derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation (CM-DNLS). Using the Gérard-type explicit formula, we prove the scattering result of solutions to this equation with initial data in $L_{+}^2(\mathbb{R}):=\left\{f \in L^2(\mathbb{R}): \operatorname{supp}(\widehat{f}) \subset[0,+\infty)\right\}$. We also characterize the scattering term using the distorted Fourier transform associated with the Lax operator. This is one of the first works that apply the Gérard-type explicit formula to study the long-time behavior of an integrable equation for a broad class of initial data, beyond the previously studied rational cases.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Introduction revised (compared to v6). This is the version submitted to a journal in August 2026

Analysis of PDEs.title: From Distribution of Extremes With Degradation to the Stress Redundancy Principle
Analysis of PDEs.summary: How a degradation source affects the statistics of the first among many identical independent stochastic particles to successfully reach a narrow target remains unclear. Here, we investigate the impact of degradation on the distributions of first-passage times and exit locations by exploiting the time-dependent fluxes associated with the corresponding Fokker-Planck equation. We also compute the escape probability by solving a mixed boundary value problem. In the large initial population $N_0$ limit, we derive an asymptotic formula for the mean first passage time associated with the fastest particle, revealing how the killing field modifies the classical $1/\log(N_0)$ scaling. However, when considering the population size at the time of the first exit, we obtain a specific dependency with respect to degradation, a phenomenon that we call the stress redundancy principle. For a degradation field restricted to a narrow subregion, we use an optimal control approach to derive the optimal trajectory where the fastest escape particles will be concentrated: interestingly, we report here that the optimal trajectories avoid the degradation area depending on killing intensity. Finally, we obtain analytical expressions for the distribution of first exit points along a narrow absorbing arc in two-dimensional regular domains. In addition, for a killing subregion tangent to the target boundary, our computations reveal how geometrical parameters influence the exit distribution. In summary, a killing source can significantly affect the statistics of the fastest diffusing particles, relevant for defining cellular and molecular time scales.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Construction of Cauchy Data for Trapped Surface Formation in the Massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon System
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct a class of smooth, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat Cauchy data for the massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon system that are initially untrapped but give rise to trapped surface formation in their maximal Cauchy developments. These data coincide with contracting Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) data on an interior ball and with Schwarzschild data outside a larger ball. The data can also be made to have arbitrarily small compactness: the ratio $2m/r$, where $m$ is the Hawking mass and $r$ is the area radius, can be made arbitrarily small throughout the initial Cauchy hypersurface.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the optimal mass threshold for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel system coupled to the Navier-Stokes equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the mass threshold for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel system coupled with the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. In the absence of fluid interaction, the classical Keller-Segel system admits a well-known $4π$-critical-mass dichotomy: for every suitably regular initial datum of total mass $m<4π$, the associated no-flux initial-boundary value problem admits a global bounded classical solution, whereas for $m>4π$, there exist smooth initial configurations of mass $m$ such that the associated solution blows up in finite or infinite time. For the fluid-coupled system, Winkler ({SIAM J. Math. Anal.}, 52:2041-2080, 2020) first established global generalized solvability under the condition $m<2π$ and posed an open question whether the fluid action may lower the critical blow-up mass to some value lying between $2π$ and $4π$. Based on numerical evidence, Bonilla and Gutiérrez-Santacreu ({J. Numer. Math.}, 32:175-212, 2024) later conjectured that the critical value is still $4π$. In the present work, we resolve this open problem and provide a rigorous mathematical proof to the conjecture, which indicates that the presence of the fluid does not alter the critical mass threshold, and the entire classical subcritical regime remains intact---every admissible initial datum with total mass $m<4π$ generates a unique global classical solution that is uniformly bounded in time. Our proof relies on the construction of a new quasi-energy inequality. The key underlying observation is that combining relative isoperimetric estimates with rearrangement techniques yields a Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality on bounded planar domains with an explicit leading constant.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Saturation on compact manifolds via Stone-Weierstrass type theorem, and forced nonlinear PDEs
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider polynomial nonlinear PDEs on compact manifolds with finite-dimensional forcing terms. We provide necessary and sufficient conditions under which the forcing, through the nonlinear dynamics, attains a dense subspace on manifolds with and without boundary. Our key argument is Nachbin's theorem, which is an analogue of the well-known Stone-Weierstrass theorem in spaces of differentiable functions. As applications, we prove small-time approximate controllability by additive finite-dimensional controls, topological irreducibility, and almost sure unboundedness of Sobolev norms.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Geodesically Semiconvex Approximations in the Wasserstein Space and Applications to Flow Interchange
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the approximation of functionals by geodesically semiconvex functionals in the Wasserstein space, with applications to dissipation estimates along the Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) scheme.
  For the potential and interaction energies, the approximation problem reduces to approximate the underlying potentials in Euclidean space. For the internal energies, we construct approximations by decomposing truncated functionals into differences of geodesically convex functionals and applying Moreau-Yosida regularization to the second component. Under suitable assumptions, we establish strong quantitative convergence of the gradient of the first variation in weighted \(L^2\) space. These approximations may enable us to obtain dissipation estimates along the JKO scheme for functionals that are not geodesically semiconvex. We illustrate this approach by deriving an \(L^{m+1}\) bound for the JKO scheme of fast diffusion equation, and by establishing internal energy dissipation for the JKO scheme of Fokker-Planck equation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Regularity via subequations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Is there a unified theory of a priori estimates for purely second-order constant coefficient elliptic PDE? A strong indication that such a theory exists is provided by the foundational a priori estimates of Caffarelli--Nirenberg--Spruck (1984) and Trudinger (1995) that treated many equations, yet left out many others. This article develops such a unified theory based on Harvey--Lawson's theory of subequations, the aforementioned a priori estimates, and some new ingredients. Serendipitously, this also solves a problem posed by Nirenberg (2007). In addition to unifying all previously known such estimates, we find a vast number of new a priori estimates (e.g., spanning real, complex, quaternionic, $G_2$, among other natural equations, and even differential inclusions that generalize PDEs).

Analysis of PDEs.title: Reverse inequality for the Riesz transforms on Riemannian manifolds
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let M be a complete Riemannian manifold satisfying the doubling volume condition for geodesic balls and L^q scaled Poincar{é} inequalities on suitable remote balls for some q<2. We prove the inequality $||Δ^{1/2}f||\_p\lesssim ||\nabla f||\_p$ for all p $\in$ (q, 2], which generalizes previous results due to Auscher and Coulhon. Our conclusion applies, in particular, when M has a finite number of Euclidean ends. The proof strongly relies on Hardy inequalities, which are also new in this context and of independent interest.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Generic singularity formation in two-dimensional Keller-Segel systems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: On bounded domains, the mass-conserving parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system admits smooth equilibria at every mass. Nevertheless, we prove that on a disk, an open dense set of positive initial densities leads to finite-time blow-up or infinite-time grow-up whenever the effective mass is at least the critical value $4π$. This threshold is sharp: below $4π$, every solution exists globally, remains uniformly bounded, and converges to a smooth equilibrium. At the critical mass, all solutions are global, while infinite-time grow-up accompanied by boundary concentration is generic. We extend the result to other bounded planar domains and closed surfaces, obtaining sharp mass thresholds for the round sphere and the flat square torus.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Two-scale estimates for limit-periodic Schrödinger operators
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove strong ballistic transport for one-dimensional continuum Schrödinger operators by comparing the spectral geometry at two consecutive periods. Enlarging a period decomposes each fiber into the eigenspaces of translation by the smaller cell. Away from the larger-period symmetry momenta, a simple ordered band remains in one translation sector and agrees with one translated smaller-period band. This permits us to combine large-period ordering and non-overlap with a smaller-period derivative bound. We obtain lower bounds for folded band widths and confine all near-collisions to a common neighborhood of the symmetry momenta, with the exponential cost at the smaller period. For nested periods $p_n$ with $p_{n+1}/p_n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p_{n+1}\ge2p_n$, approximation errors $o(p_{n+1}^{-2}e^{-ηp_n})$, where $η>7\sqrt{2R}$ and $\|V\|_\infty\le R$, give a nonzero strong asymptotic velocity on a weighted $H^2$ class containing the Schwartz space. Every position moment of order $0<r\le4$ has two-sided ballistic growth. A period-uniform form estimate, ordered-gap summation, and a linear dynamical comparison complete the argument. No upper bound on successive period ratios is assumed, and the sufficient approximation exponents are not claimed to be optimal.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global existence and sharp decay rates of weak solutions for the 2D inviscid Oldroyd-B model with fractional stress tensor diffusion
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper is devoted to the global existence and optimal decay rates of weak solutions to a two-dimensional inviscid Oldroyd-B model with fractional stress diffusion. For $\frac{1}{2}<β<1$, by virtue of energy estimates and compactness arguments, we establish the existence of global weak solutions with $(u,τ)\in H^{1}\times (H^{1}\cap L^{\infty})$. Moreover, based on the Littlewood-Paley decomposition theory and the improved Fourier splitting method, we derive the optimal decay rates. In particular, by constructing a suitable low-frequency energy functional and exploiting the dissipation mechanism of the coupled system, we obtain the optimal $L^\infty$ decay rate for the stress tensor.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Scattering of water waves in presence of a partially immersed obstacle
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study linear water waves in two dimensions in a fluid of infinite depth containing a fixed, partially immersed obstacle. Under natural geometric assumptions on the wetted boundary, we construct the harmonic lifting and prove that the associated Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator is an unbounded, self-adjoint and non-negative operator on a $L^2$ space. This yields global well-posedness and conservation of energy. We establish the absence of trapped modes and, by a compact perturbation argument, a limiting absorption principle at every positive spectral parameter. Consequently, for all finite energy initial data, the physical local energy tends to zero as $|t|\to\infty$, including in neighborhoods of the obstacle and the contact points. Quantitative resolvent estimates and fractional regularity in the spectral parameter yield algebraic local energy decay for Sobolev initial data in weighted $L^2$ spaces.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Timelike curves: homotopies and domain of determinacy
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper studies domains of determination of linear strictly hyperbolic second order operators $P$. For an open set $\mathcal O$, a set $Z$ is a domain of determination when the values of solutions of the differential equation $Pu=0$ are determined on $Z$ by their values in $\mathcal O$. Fritz John's global Hölmgren theorem implies that points that can be reached by deformations of noncharacteristic hypersufaces with initial surface and boundaries in $\mathcal O$ belong to a domain of determination provided that local uniqueness holds at noncharacteristic surfaces. Using spacelike hypersurfaces yields sharp finite speed results whose domains of determination are described in terms of influence curves that never exceed the local speed of propagation. This paper studies deformations of noncharacteristic nonspacelike hypersurfaces. We prove that points reachable by (repeated) deformations by noncharacteristic nonspacelike hypersurfaces coincide exactly with the set of points reachable by (repeated) homotopies of timelike arcs whose initial curves and endpoints belong to $\mathcal O$. When the set $\mathcal O$ is a small neighborhood of a forward timelike arc connecting $a$ to $b$, a natural candidate for $Z$ is the intesection of the future of $a$ with the past of $b$. This candidate is exact for D'Alembert's equation. We prove that it is also exact when $a,b$ are points close together on a fixed timelike arc. The timelike homotopy criterion fuels the construction of surprising examples for which the domain of determination is strictly larger (resp. strictly smaller) than the future-intersect-past candidate.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A stochastic chemical system in contact with reservoirs
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper we analyse the behaviour of a non-reversible stochastic chemical system obtained as an approximation of a stochastic chemical system in which the concentration of some chemicals is higher than the concentration of the other chemicals. The master equation associated with this approximated system is characterised by a discrete part, modelling the reactions among chemicals that have low concentration, by a transport term and a diffusion term. The transport-diffusion terms describe the fluctuations in the concentration of abundant chemicals. The model contains a second order term is of order ε, that describes the fluctuation in the concentrations of the abundand substances. We prove that the master equation has a spectral gap that is independent on $ε$ and we analyse in detail the asymptotics of the solution to the master equation as $ε\to 0$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness of global weak solutions for the defocusing energy-critical NLS
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the defocusing energy-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation and establish global uniqueness for weak solutions. The key idea comes from the weak uniqueness in the uniform-in-time high-frequency threshold (UTHT) class introduced in [12,14]. We derive a new energy defect threshold (EDT) criterion from the UTHT criterion. Along the strong solution flow, energy conservation propagates the EDT condition for weak solutions and, combined with the global well-posedness theory for strong solutions, yields global weak uniqueness. As an application, we prove unconditional uniqueness for the quintic defocusing energy-critical Gross-Pitaevskii hierarchy.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Critical Well-Posedness of a Euler-Chemotaxis System in 2D
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
This article is about well-posedness results for a 2D Euler-Chemotaxis-Consumption system with initial data in scale critical spaces, namely existence, uniqueness and critical initial data to solution continuity. This problem is related to the well-known family of Keller-Segel equations, although it bears major differences which will be crucial for our study.
  In most recent results, solutions to such Chemotaxis-Consumption systems have used a free-energy balance law to obtain well-posedness. This has the disadvantage of requiring initial data to be positive almost everywhere. Our main goal, in addition to sharp well-posedness, is to show that this positivity condition is not needed for existence and uniqueness. In fact, we will never use the concept of free-energy in our proof.
  Our argument revolves around an understanding of the scaling of the different parts of the equation, and especially the subcritical interaction terms. This will allow us to upgrade basic low regularity estimates (e.g. mass conservation) into critical bounds. In the process, we find out that closing $L^2$ estimates leads to the Besov space $\dot B^0_{\infty, 2}$ as the most natural choice of regularity for the initial chemo-attractant concentration. Extensive use of real interpolation also plays a key role for deriving Chemin-Lerner bounds for the solutions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A new notion of Dirichlet boundary condition for elliptic equation of divergence form
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
In this paper, we consider Dirichlet boundary conditions for elliptic equations in divergence form on rough domains by introducing a truncation-based weak solution framework that circumvents global Sobolev trace obstacles. We establish well-posedness on bounded admissible domains for continuous boundary data and $L^2$
  sources, deriving boundary Hölder regularities that require only uniform ellipticity and an exterior measure-density condition. This approach eliminates the uniform domain regularity and coefficient continuity imnposed in Guam, Wang and Zhou(2026). Furthermore, on sufficiently flat Reifenberg domains, we obtain boundary $C^α$ regularity for any $α\in (0,1) $ using natural energy estimates, thereby bypassing
  $L^p$($p>\frac {n}{2}$) restrictions found in Lian and Zhang(2026). Crucially, we obtain global $H^1$
  regularity for Hölder boundary data ($α>\frac 12$) a posteriori, without requiring small-BMO coefficient assumptions on the coefficients.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Mesoscopic derivation of predator-prey dynamics via diffusive fast-reaction asymptotics: cross-diffusion and fear effects
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We propose a kinetic derivation of a spatial predator-prey model with cross-diffusion interactions and a Beddington-DeAngelis functional response. At the mesoscopic level, we divide the two populations into distinct behavioral states: prey can be active or hidden in a refuge, while predators can be either searching or handling. The microscopic state of each subpopulation is described in terms of group size and a continuous directional velocity variable, with state transitions governed by suitable Boltzmann-type interaction operators. By combining a diffusive scaling with a slow-fast formulation of the kinetic reaction operators, we formally derive a macroscopic reaction-cross-diffusion system for the total population densities of prey and predators. The limiting model consistently recovers the Beddington-DeAngelis functional response along with its associated nonlinear diffusion terms. Crucially, the kinetic upscaling yields a predator-dependent prey growth term taking a logistic form with an effective carrying capacity. This carrying capacity depends non-monotonically on predator density because prey redistribute between active and refuge states. Since density-dependent competition acts separately within these behavioral states, intermediate predator levels reduce aggregate crowding and thereby increase the effective carrying capacity of the total prey population. Overall, our derivation provides a mechanistic link connecting predator-induced behavioral shifts, refuge use, and macroscopic cross-diffusion.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp asymptotic stability of the incompressible porous medium equation on the whole plane
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the asymptotic stability of the steady state $e_s(x)=-x_2$ of the incompressible porous media equation in $\mathbb R^2$. For every $s>2$, we prove that sufficiently small initial perturbations $θ_0\in H^s(\mathbb R^2)$ of $e_s$ generate unique global solutions $ρ=e_s+θ$, where $θ$ remains uniformly bounded in $H^s$ and converges strongly to zero in $H^s$ as $t\to\infty$. The main innovations of this work are threefold. First, exploiting the structure of the equation, we construct a weighted energy that eliminates the need to control $\|\nabla u^2\|_{L^1_tL^\infty_x}$. Second, rather than estimating the anisotropic commutators directly, we study the integral terms containing these commutators and establish suitable bounds through refined computations in frequency space. Third, we establish convergence in the highest-order $H^s$ norm under uniform energy bounds involving only an $L^\infty_tH^s_x$ bound on $θ$ and an $L^2_tH^s_x$ bound on $\mathcal R_1θ$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Logarithmic gradient estimate and Universal bounds for semilinear elliptic equations revisited
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We derive the complete and optimal Cheng--Yau gradient estimates and universal bounds for subcritical semilinear elliptic equations on Riemannian manifolds with (Bakry-Émery) Ricci curvature bounded below. This answers a fundamental question that has existed for a long time. As a corollary, this provides a new proof of the Gidas-Spruck classical Liouville theorem. The Harnack inequality is also obtained.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Accepted final version, to appear in International Mathematics Research Notices

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Kato-Type Criterion for Vanishing Viscosity and Magnetic Diffusivity Limits for Compressible Magnetohydrodynamics
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we investigate the vanishing viscosity and magnetic diffusivity limits for the compressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) equations on a smooth bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Under the assumptions of interior regularity and uniform local boundedness near the boundary, we establish a Kato-type criterion under which finite energy weak solutions to the dissipative MHD system converge to weak solutions to the ideal MHD system as the viscosity and magnetic resistivity coefficients decrease to zero. In particular, under such criterion, the anomalous energy dissipation in the vanishing viscosity and diffusivity limits for MHD is precluded.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Silverman-Meadows-type criterion for the null controllability of time-dependent coupled heat equations with non-diagonalizable diffusion matrices
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper is devoted to a uniform spectral Silverman-Meadows rank condition for the nullcontrollability of coupled systems of heat equations with time-dependent diffusion, coupling and control matrices. The proof relies on an adaptation of the Lebeau-Robbiano strategy combined with uniform finite-dimensional observability estimates associated with each Laplace eigenmode.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Energy Dissipation Along Trajectories and Wasserstein Gradient Flow of Aggregation-Diffusion Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this work, we established the Wasserstein gradient flow structure of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations on bounded domains involving both nonlinear diffusion and nonlocal interaction effects. Our approach is based on stochastic analysis. More precisely, we investigated the associated stochastic differential equation (SDE) with normal reflection at the boundary from a trajectorial perspective and derived a semimartingale decomposition of the corresponding energy process. This decomposition leads to a trajectorial energy dissipation identity, which, together with the characterization of the metric derivative, allows us to establish the Wasserstein gradient flow structure of the aggregation-diffusion equation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Landau equation in a domain
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This work deals with the Landau equation in a bounded domain with the Maxwell reflection condition on the boundary for any (possibly smoothly position dependent) accommodation coefficient and for the full range of interaction potentials, including the Coulomb case. We establish the global existence and a constructive asymptotic decay of solutions in a close-to-equilibrium regime. This is the first existence result for a Maxwell reflection condition on the boundary and that generalizes the similar results established for the Landau equation for other geometries in \cite{GuoLandau1,GS1,GS2,MR3625186,MR4076068}. We also answer to Villani's program \cite{MR2116276,MR2407976} about constructive accurate rate of convergence to the equilibrium {(quantitative H-Theorem)} for solutions to collisional kinetic equations satisfying a priori uniform bounds. The proofs rely on the study of a suitably linear problem for which we prove that the associated operator is hypocoercive, the associated semigroup is ultracontractive, and finally that it is asymptotically stable in many weighted $L^\infty$ spaces.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: v2: We corrected a few minor errors; main results and proofs remain unchanged. The trace result was revised to remove an overly optimistic estimate and now matches the statement used elsewhere. In the ultracontractivity proof, an auxiliary weight function was slightly modified to ensure validity for all values of $γ$. This technical detail does not require modifying the rest of the proof

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global weak solutions to nonlinear kinetic Fokker--Planck equations in bounded domains under physical initial data
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish the global existence of weak solutions to a nonlinear kinetic Fokker--Planck equation with degenerate diffusion, under either inflow or partial absorption-reflection boundary conditions. The novelty of our approach lies in constructing solutions under solely the physical assumptions on the initial and boundary data, namely finite mass, kinetic energy, and entropy, with no additional regularity imposed. To overcome the lack of uniform ellipticity, we develop a compactness principle based on weighted Fisher information, which yields strong $L^1$ convergence of approximate solutions. This framework provides a robust existence theory under only the physically relevant conditions, and applies uniformly to both inflow and partial absorption-reflection boundary settings.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Clarified some parts of the manuscript and added references. This version has been accepted in Communications in Partial Differential Equations

Analysis of PDEs.title: On Monotonicity in Mean Field Games Induced by Discount Factor Transformations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper is devoted to the well-posedness of a class of infinite horizon discounted Mean Field Games (MFGs) problems, where both an exponential discount and a so-called cheap control factors are present simultaneously, and scale in a possibly different way. We introduce a new class of transformations of variables, at the level of both the MFG PDE and the corresponding FBSDE systems. We then show how these transformations reveal a new mechanism that generates semiconvexity estimates for the value function and ensures the existence of mean field equilibria, as long as the parameters land in a suitable regime, that we quantitatively describe. This new mechanism demonstrates furthermore how discount factors lead to a source of strong displacement monotonicity for the Lagrangian, without any initial monotonicity assumptions on the running costs. Consequently, in such regimes of parameters uniqueness of solutions manifests. Our approach uses a Lagrangian point of view, which lets us treat general non-separable Lagrangians and both deterministic and idiosyncratic noise driven models in a transparent, unified way. For a specific class of quadratic Lagrangians, using turnpike-type methods, we further obtain an exponential contractivity estimate for the mean field equilibria.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Phase transitions and sharp localisation in anomalous localised resonance
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study how detuning and absorption determine the strength and spatial extent of anomalous localised resonance in a two-dimensional quasistatic coated structure with shell permittivity $-1+c\ell^p+i\ell$, where $\ell>0$ is the loss and $c\ne0$, $p>0$ are fixed. Detuning can carry the material path through narrow resonances, producing intermittent rather than sustained power growth. For an explicit family of noncircular shells and a smooth exterior dipole source, both fixed, we classify the dissipated power under a quantitative smallness condition on the deformation. Depending on the detuning exponent and conformal source distance, the power diverges along the entire path, exhibits divergent peaks with vanishing gaps, or decays, including the threshold cases. We also identify the sharp conformal boundary beyond which the field, normalized by the square root of the dissipated power, converges locally to zero along every divergent-power sequence. For resonant sources, tangential reference crossings yield an explicit nonzero limit for the exterior gradient energy divided by the dissipated power at the critical radius.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Pólya's conjecture for hyperbolic balls and Berezin--Li--Yau type inequalities
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We prove the strict shifted Dirichlet Pólya inequality \[ λ_k(B_R)>\frac{(d-1)^2κ^2}{4}+4π^2\left(\frac{k}{ω_d\operatorname{Vol}_κ(B_R)}\right)^{2/d},\qquad k\ge1, \] for every geodesic ball $B_R$ in hyperbolic space of constant sectional curvature $-κ^2$, in every dimension $d\ge2$. As a consequence, we obtain the shifted Berezin--Li--Yau type inequality for hyperbolic balls, thereby providing a concrete family of domains satisfying both conjectures proposed by Laptev in 2023.
  For arbitrary nonempty open subsets $Ω\subset\mathbb{H}^d_κ$ of finite volume, we establish the weak Berezin--Li--Yau type inequality \[ \sum_{j=1}^{m}λ_j(Ω)\ge a_{d,κ}m+\frac{d}{d+2}\,4π^2\left(\frac{m}{ω_d\operatorname{Vol}_κ(Ω)}\right)^{2/d}m,\qquad m\ge1, \] with the optimal leading coefficient, where $a_{2,κ}=κ^2/4$ and $a_{d,κ}=d(d-1)κ^2/6$ for $d\ge3$. We also establish the global two-sided estimate for the renormalized eigenvalue sum on hyperbolic space, originally proposed by Strichartz in 1996 and valid for $d\ge3$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Connectivity and the equilibration of Boltzmann-type equations on dense graphs
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the equilibration of solutions to a homogeneous Boltzmann-type equation whose collision kernel is given by a graphon encoding the connectivity structure of interacting agents. For a broad class of Lipschitz-continuous binary interaction rules, we show that, under suitable conditions relating the interaction parameters to the connectivity properties of the graphon, solutions converge exponentially fast towards those of the classical homogeneous Boltzmann-type equation without preferential connections, and hence towards its equilibrium distributions. We then consider in detail compromise-diffusion interaction rules and establish a quasi-invariant limit leading to a Fokker-Planck-type equation parametrised by the graphon connectivity. This limiting equation allows us to characterise explicitly both connectivity-independent and connectivity-dependent equilibrium distributions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Well-posedness of the weakly singular Burton-Miller equation for Helmholtz transmission problems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Although various boundary integral formulations are available for the Helmholtz transmission problem, the weakly singular Burton--Miller equation is promising because it possesses favorable properties for numerical computation. This paper rigorously shows that the weakly singular Burton--Miller equation is well-posed. We establish bounded invertibility on $C(Γ)\times C(Γ)$ for $C^2$ boundaries by proving injectivity and applying the Fredholm alternative. For the prescribed analytic incident field, the integral equation further yields $u\in C^{1,β}(Γ)$ and $q\in C^{0,β}(Γ)$, for $0<β<1$. We also provide a proof that its fictitious eigenvalues are associated with an exterior Dirichlet problem and an interior impedance problem.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence and Splitting of Dirac Points in Honeycomb Gyromagnetic Photonic Crystals
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish the existence of Dirac cones and magnetically induced local band gaps for the transverse magnetic Maxwell system in a two-dimensional honeycomb array of circular yttrium iron garnet (YIG) cylinders. For fixed positive material parameters with nonzero permeability contrast, we prove that sufficiently small cylinders support a Dirac point in the nonmagnetic case $κ_g=0$: two Bloch dispersion surfaces meet at a double eigenfrequency and form a nondegenerate cone. For each fixed sufficiently small nonzero gyrotropic bias $κ_g$, we show that this degeneracy splits and a local band gap opens near the original Dirac point. Our approach combines a quasi-periodic layer-potential formulation with honeycomb symmetry and rigorously controlled finite-dimensional reductions. The central contribution is a unified derivation of the conical crossing and magnetic gap opening directly from the full Maxwell transmission problem, without assuming an effective discrete model. This establishes the transition from Dirac dispersion to a locally gapped spectrum in a small-inclusion regime with fixed material contrast.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global existence for a Fritz John equation in expanding FLRW spacetimes
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the family of semilinear wave equations $\square_{\mathbf{g}_p}φ=(\partial_tφ)^2$, on fixed expanding FLRW spacetimes, having $\mathbb{R}^3$ spatial slices and undergoing a power law expansion, with scale factor $a(t)=t^p$, $0< p \le 1$. This is a natural generalization to a non-stationary background of a famous Fritz John ''blow-up'' equation in $\mathbb{R}^{1+3}$ (corresponding to $p=0$, i.e. the case in which $\mathbf{g}_0$ is the Minkowski metric). While, in Minkowski spacetime ($p=0$), non-trivial solutions to this equation are known to diverge in finite time, here we prove that, on the referred FLRW backgrounds ($0<p\leq 1$), sufficiently small, smooth, and compactly supported initial data yield global-in-time solutions to the future. Previous work, co-authored by the first two authors, considered accelerated expanding spacetimes ($p>1$) and relied on the integrability of the inverse of the scale factor to establish future global well-posedness. In the current work, where such an integrability condition is lacking, we rely on a vector field method that captures and combines dispersive estimates with the spacetime expansion to control the solution and suppress the nonlinear blow-up mechanism. To achieve this, we commute the Laplace-Beltrami operator with a boosts-free subset of the Poincaré algebra and employ Klainerman-Sideris types of inequalities. Our strategy is general and is developed to handle the non-stationary nature of FLRW spacetimes. While we focus solely on this Fritz John type of equation, which serves as a prototype to study blow-up of non-linear waves, our approach provides a rigorous proof of the regularizing effects of spacetime expansion and can be exploited for a wider range of applications and nonlinearities.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 23 pages, extended abstract in the paper; v3: typos fixed, and a few references and comments were added; v2: references updated

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundedness of radial solutions to the parabolic-parabolic Keller--Segel system on the plane with subcritical mass
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish uniform-in-time boundedness of radially symmetric global solutions to the two-dimensional parabolic-parabolic Keller--Segel system on the whole space with mass below $8π$. While global existence is known throughout this subcritical mass range, uniform-in-time boundedness has remained open. On bounded domains, the free energy method of Nagai, Senba and Yoshida (1997) yields both global existence and boundedness under the optimal mass condition. On the whole space, however, the corresponding estimates are not uniform in time due to the behavior of solutions at spatial infinity. Indeed, the free energy of self-similar solutions diverges to $-\infty$ as $t\to\infty$, preventing a direct application of this approach to establish boundedness. The key ingredients are new interior estimates controlling the localized free energy in terms of its dissipation, together with uniform-in-time exterior estimates exploiting radial symmetry.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A remark on Liouville-type theorems for the stationary Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$ under pointwise conditions on the head pressure
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the stationary Navier--Stokes equations in the three-dimensional whole space and the Liouville-type problem under the condition of finite Dirichlet integral. We give a remark on the recent result by Chae [7, Theorem 1.2], in which an upper bound of the gradient of the head pressure and a lower bound of the head pressure with certain rates were assumed to prove triviality of solutions. In this paper, we extend the range of admissible rates by two different arguments. One relies on the pointwise decay of head pressure and the classical argument of Galdi [11]. The other is similar to the argument of Chae [4, 6] and is based on the maximum principle for the head pressure, the integral identity between the vorticity and the gradient of the head pressure on the upper level set of the head pressure, and the coarea formula. This also gives a more refined proof for [7, Theorem 1.2].
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Dedicated to Professor Yoshikazu Giga on the award of the Kodaira Kunihiko Prize

Analysis of PDEs.title: The anisotropic De Giorgi conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^4$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish the anisotropic De Giorgi conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^4$ under the limiting assumption. More precisely, every entire solution of the anisotropic Allen-Cahn equation satisfying $u_{x_4}>0$ and $u(x,x_4)\to\pm1$ as $x_4\to\pm\infty$ for each $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$ is one-dimensional. We show that every nontrivial generalized subgraph globally minimizing the anisotropic perimeter in $\mathbb{R}^4$ is a halfspace. Combining an anisotropic tilt-excess decay estimate with a Liouville argument, we then deduce one-dimensional symmetry.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Non-existence of solutions to a system of quadratic derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the Cauchy problem for a system of quadratic derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equations introduced by M. Colin and T. Colin (2004) as a model of laser-plasma interaction. Under a coefficient condition, we prove that there are initial data admitting no solution in Sobolev spaces, both on the torus and on the Euclidean space.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness and nondegeneracy of ground states for the pure-power Born-Infeld equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
For \(N\ge3\) and \(p>2N/(N-2)\), we study the Born--Infeld equation \[
  -\diver\!\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1-|\nabla u|^2}}\right)
  =|u|^{p-2}u \qquad\text{in }\R^N . \] We prove that the positive ground state \(Q\) is unique up to translation. We also prove that the kernel of the linearized operator at \(Q\) is spanned by \(\partial_{x_1}Q,\ldots,\partial_{x_N}Q\), and determine all nonzero optimizers of the sharp Born--Infeld Sobolev inequality. To prove nondegeneracy, we first rule out nonzero radial kernel functions using the Morse index and a Wronskian identity. We then treat the angular modes by spherical harmonics. To prove uniqueness, we compare radial solutions for large \(p\), and extend the result to all \(p>2N/(N-2)\) by compactness and continuation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local well-posedness, wave breaking and ill-posedness for the unidirectional non-local wave model
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we first establish local well-posedness (existence, uniqueness and continuous dependence) for the Cauchy problem associated with the unidirectional non-local wave model in the Besov spaces $B^s_{p,r}$ with $s>1+\frac{1}{p}$ and $1\leq p,r\leq\infty$, as well as in the critical Besov spaces $B^{1+\frac{1}{p}}_{p,1}$ with $1\leq p<\infty$. Next, by exploiting the fine structure of the equation and performing a delicate analysis of the commutator terms, we establish a new sufficient condition for wave breaking without using any conservation law. Finally, we prove that the model is ill-posed in $B^{1+\frac{1}{p}}_{p,r}$ for $1\leq p\leq\infty$ and $1<r\leq\infty$. Our analysis further clarifies the well-posedness theory and wave-breaking behavior of the unidirectional non-local wave model arising from the motion of a cold plasma in a magnetic field, which refines and improves previously known related results.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Mean Curvature Flow with Thermal Fluctuations in Dimensions Two and Higher
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
Surface tension drives interfaces towards smaller area, while thermal motion produces shape fluctuations whose strength is linked to the interfacial mobility through the fluctuation--dissipation relation. These mechanisms lead to mean-curvature flow with thermal noise, whose graph formulation is known as the Kawasaki--Ohta equation. We establish global-in-time existence of energy martingale solutions to the spatially regularized Kawasaki--Ohta equation for periodic graphs in every dimension $d\geq2$, with initial data in $H^1(\mathbb T^d)$. No restriction on the noise intensity is needed for $d=2$, while a smallness condition is required for $d\geq3$. The key new challenges arise from the thermal noise, which has a $(1+|
abla u|^2)^{1/4}$-type coefficient. This coefficient gives rise to an irregular Stratonovich-to-Itô correction term of the form $
abla u\cdot D^2u
abla u/(1+|
abla u|^2)^{3/2}$. Our main innovation is a compactness argument tailored to the structure of the correction. By combining a factorization of this term with $H^1(\mathbb T^d)$ and area estimates, we establish strong convergence of the normalized gradients and reconstruct the weighted Hessian, which allows us to define the correction at energy regularity and identify its approximation limit.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness and Nondegeneracy of Ground States for Critical-Hardy Fractional Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study ground states of nonlinear fractional Schrödinger equations with the critical Hardy potential in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $d\geq3$. We prove the existence and qualitative properties of ground states, based on which we analyze the uniqueness and nondegeneracy of ground states. As a byproduct, we also investigate the optimizers of the critical Hardy--Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality, from which a sharp Keller--Hardy--Lieb--Thirring inequality is analytically derived.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global existence and blow-up for a fractional wave equation with logarithmic nonlinearity and strong damping
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper studies a fractional strongly damped wave equation with logarithmic nonlinearity. Based on local well-posedness of weak solutions via the Galerkin approximation, we employ the potential well theory to derive the existence of global solutions under subcritical and critical initial energy conditions. Moreover, infinite time blow-up phenomena are obtained under subcritical, critical, and arbitrarily high supercritical initial energy conditions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Spectral inequalities for weighted $p$-Laplacians via Talenti symmetrization
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the weighted $p$-Laplacian associated with a measure $μ$ having a continuous positive density with respect to the Lebesgue measure on an open convex subset $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$. We prove that Talenti's weighted Pólya--Szegő inequality---originally established for Lipschitz functions on $X$---extends to the weighted Sobolev space of functions vanishing on the relative boundary of an open set $Ω\subset X$, defined as the closure of Lipschitz functions supported away from it. This yields Faber--Krahn-type inequalities for the first $(p,q)$-eigenvalue of the weighted Dirichlet $p$-Laplacian. We present several examples fitting this abstract framework, in which the isoperimetric sets are balls, half-spaces, or complements of balls.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Classical solvability of the Cauchy problem for multi-order time-fractional systems with full matrices of differential operators
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This article investigates the Cauchy problem in the whole space for a system of linear time-fractional partial differential equations with an arbitrary fixed number of components and a full matrix of constant-coefficient spatial differential operators. Each component is governed by its own Caputo derivative, and no rational relation between the fractional orders is required. We assume that the diagonal spatial symbols are homogeneous, positive and elliptic, while the off-diagonal entries have strictly lower order than the diagonal operator in the corresponding column. Using spatial Fourier and temporal Laplace transforms, we construct solution operators through convergent series of time convolutions involving scalar Mittag--Leffler kernels. These series account for all coupling paths, including repeated interactions between components. A fractional Duhamel representation incorporates nonhomogeneous source terms. We establish uniform convergence on bounded frequency regions and weighted multiplier estimates by separating low and high spatial frequencies. Under suitable Sobolev regularity assumptions on the initial data and continuously differentiable source terms, we prove existence and uniqueness of a classical solution, together with continuity and regularity properties in the appropriate Sobolev spaces. The general result includes two-component systems and is illustrated by fully coupled examples.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sonic-supersonic jet flows from a straight two-dimensional nozzle with van der Waals equation of state
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This article concerns sonic-supersonic jet flows issuing from a two-dimensional straight nozzle described by the steady compressible Euler system under the van der Waals equation of state. The flow state is prescribed at the nozzle exit, while the surrounding medium is assumed to be either a vacuum or a static atmosphere with lower pressure. When the flow reaches the sonic state at the nozzle exit, the governing equations become degenerate hyperbolic and the resulting jet flow problem can be formulated as a degenerate free boundary problem. The analysis is further complicated by singular behavior near the endpoints of the nozzle exit. By employing characteristic decompositions and suitable a priori estimates, we establish the global existence of locally Lipschitz continuous sonic-supersonic jet flows expanding into a vacuum. Moreover, in the presence of a static atmosphere with pressure lower than that at the nozzle exit, we prove the local existence of sonic-supersonic jet flows near the nozzle exit.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence and uniqueness of asymptotic traveling waves in a time-fractional bistable reaction-diffusion equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study asymptotic traveling waves for a reaction-diffusion equation with a Caputo time derivative. For general $C^1$ bistable imbalanced nonlinearities, we prove the existence of an asymptotic traveling wave connecting the two stable states. The asymptotic wave speed is unique, and the asymptotic profile is strictly increasing and unique up to translation. The proof uses continuation from a stationary front and the sliding method. For a cubic nonlinearity, we also derive an asymptotic formula for the speed near the balanced case, with an explicit leading coefficient. Finally, we perform numerical simulations to compare the speed predicted by the asymptotic formula with the front propagation speed in the original equation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Interaction between nonlinear diffusion and mean curvature of a surface with initial discontinuities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the Cauchy problems for a class of nonlinear diffusion equations where each initial data is given by a characteristic function of an open set $Ω$ in the whole Euclidean space. If the boundary $\partialΩ$ is of class $C^2$ in a neighborhood of a point $x$ on it, then we extract the mean curvature of $\partialΩ$ at $x$ from the initial diffusion at $x$. This corresponds to the author's previous result for the two-phase linear diffusion equation. Applications to some overdetermined problems for nonlinear diffusion equations are given.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 22 pages; added comments on Theorem 1.1 in the case of the heat equation in section 1

Analysis of PDEs.title: Gradient regularity without gap conditions for parabolic double phase systems with coefficients depending only on time
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study degenerate parabolic double phase systems with growth exponents $p<q$ whose modulating coefficient depends only on time. In this case, the operator on each time slice has Orlicz growth with structural constants independent of the coefficient, and the system is invariant under spatial translations. Using these features, we prove second order estimates and local bounds for the gradient when the coefficient is merely bounded and measurable, and $C^{1,α}$ regularity when it is Hölder continuous in time. For weak solutions with gradients in $L^q$, these results hold without any gap condition between $p$ and $q$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Perturbations of a minimal surface with triple junctions in $\mathbb{R}^2 \times \mathbb{S}^1$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct stationary perturbations of a specific minimal surface with a circle of triple junctions in $\mathbb{R}^2 \times \mathbb{S}^1$, that satisfy given boundary data.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Add 1 figure, include Remark 1.2 and 1.3 right after Theorem 1.1. To appear in CAG

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the two-component $b$-family system modeling shallow-water waves of medium amplitude
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We formally derive a two-component $b$-family system from the full governing equations for two-dimensional water waves in the medium-amplitude regime. The system contains higher-order nonlinearities and includes a two-component Camassa-Holm type system for equatorial shallow-water waves with the Coriolis effect as a special case. We establish the local well-posedness of the Cauchy problem in $B^{s-1}_{p,r}\times B^s_{p,r}$ with $s>\max\{1+\frac1p,\frac32\}$. Using Littlewood-Paley theory and Osgood's lemma, we also prove local well-posedness in the critical Besov space $B^{\frac12}_{2,1}\times B^{\frac32}_{2,1}$. Furthermore, we derive a blow-up criterion for strong solutions.
