We then adapt the argument to the corresponding Neumann problem in a smooth bounded planar domain and obtain infinite-time blow-up solutions for any mass $M>4π$. At the critical mass $M=8π$, we show that the solutions are globally bounded on spheres equipped with the canonical spherical metric, and we construct a solution blowing up in infinite time on the Riemann sphere equipped with a special metric.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Spectral gaps and uniqueness in the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $p<-n$. We prove that a smooth strictly convex solution $K$ is the unit ball if the second non-zero eigenvalue of the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator satisfies $λ_2(-L_K)\ge\frac{-p-1}{n-1}$. We also derive a lower bound for $λ_2(-L_K)$ in terms of concentric inner and outer ellipsoids and give improved bounds for origin-centred and origin-symmetric bodies. Combined with a weighted centroid identity for the polar body, these estimates yield an explicit $\varepsilon_n>0$ for which the unit ball is the only solution when $-n-\varepsilon_n\le p<-n$.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Updated version. 21 pages. All comments are welcome

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundary value problems for 0-elliptic operators
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $X$ be a manifold with boundary, and let $L$ be a 0-elliptic operator on X which is semi-Fredholm essentially surjective with infinite-dimensional kernel. Examples include Hodge Laplacians and Dirac operators on conformally compact manifolds. We construct left and right parametrices for L when supplemented with appropriate elliptic boundary conditions. The construction relies on a new calculus of pseudodifferential operators on functions over both $X$ and $\partial X$, which we call the "symbolic 0-calculus". This new calculus supplements the ordinary 0-calculus of Mazzeo--Melrose, enabling it to handle boundary value problems. In the original 0-calculus, operators are characterized as polyhomogeneous right densities on a blow-up of $X^2$. By contrast, operators in the symbolic 0-calculus are characterized (locally near each point of the boundary of the diagonal) as quantizations of polyhomogeneous symbols on appropriate blown-up model spaces.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 153 pages, 8 figures. Version published by Ars Inveniendi Analytica. Major changes from v1: 1. Addition of a "guiding example" (§2.6, §3.5, §6.5 §7.3) illustrating the theory. 2. Addition of a section (§7) with a new regularity theorem for solutions of 0-elliptic equations

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Spacetime-Diffeomorphic Approach to Magnetohydrodynamics around Black Holes: Dilation Covariance, Linearization,and the No-Hair Limit
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The ideal magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) system that governs a conducting plasma---the Maxwell equations together with the conservation laws of mass, momentum and energy---is the same local balance structure that describes hot accretion flows around black holes. We introduce a uniform four-dimensional spacetime dilation \[ Φ_L:\;(t',x',y',z')\mapsto (t,x,y,z)=(Lt',Lx',Ly',Lz'),\qquad L>1, \] and show that it is a smooth, orientation-preserving $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of flat spacetime. Pulling the MHD conservation laws back through $Φ_L$, we prove that the closed ideal-MHD system is form-invariant (covariant), with the current density rescaling as $\bm j=\bm j'/L$, the magnetic diffusivity as $η'=η/L$, and external sources rescaled by $L$. The transformation realises three physically distinct effects on the perturbed flow: a \emph{linearization} to the tangent-space (linearised MHD) system, a \emph{movie slow-motion} dilation of dissipative and dynamical timescales, and an \emph{electron-microscope} magnification of small-scale structure. Taking the formal limit $L\to\infty$ localises the dynamics on a neighbourhood of a horizon: resistivity vanishes, the asymptotic time derivative freezes, and all transient multipolar structure of the infalling plasma redshifts away. The remaining stationary, axisymmetric, asymptotically flat electrovacuum is uniquely the Kerr--Newman geometry, so that the exterior of the compact object is characterised only by its mass $M$, angular momentum $J$ and charge $Q$. The result provides a local, conservation-law-based perspective on the black hole no-hair theorem that is complementary to the classical Israel--Carter-- Robinson theorems and to contemporary gravitational-wave and Event Horizon Telescope tests.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sufficient conditions for multiplicity and uniqueness of positive solutions of the Hénon equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish explicit sufficient conditions for multiplicity of positive solutions of the Hénon equation in the unit ball and for uniqueness in one dimension. In the Sobolev-subcritical range, a spherical harmonic function argument shows that the radial solution has Morse index greater than one and therefore differs from a ground state. In even dimensions, a degree-four perturbation in a symmetry and monotonicity cone yields a sufficient condition for nonradiality in the supercritical range. The one-dimensional uniqueness criterion follows from a comparison of weighted Dirichlet eigenvalues and a concavity estimate.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Energy gaps for critical Dirac equations on spheres
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the critical Dirac equation \[
  Dψ=H(x)|ψ|^{\frac{2}{m-1}}ψ\] on the round sphere $\mbs^m$, $m\ge2$, where $D$ is the Dirac operator. For $H\equiv1$, the ground-state energy $E_m=\frac{m^{m-1}}{2^{m+1}}\vol(\mbs^m)$ depends only on the dimension $m$. In dimension two, the nonzero solution energies are exactly $π,3π,4π,\ldots$. For $m\ge3$, we prove a gap $(E_m,(1+\Ga_m)E_m)$ above the ground-state energy and give bounds for its optimal relative size $\Ga_m$. For positive $H$, let $τ_H=E_m/(\max H)^{m-1}$ be the first bubble energy. If $m\ge3$, every $H$ in a residual subset of the positive $C^1$ functions admits solutions with infinitely many distinct weighted energies in $(τ_H,\min\{2,1+\Ga_m\}τ_H)$ tending to $τ_H$. Along a subsequence these solutions form a single ground-state bubble at a global maximum of $H$. For each $k\ge1$, smooth positive coefficients admitting at least $k$ distinct energies in this interval are dense among positive functions in $C^1$ and $W^{2,s}$, $m/2<s<\infty$. In the $C^2$ topology, however, an open set of positive coefficients admits only the trivial solution. We approximate a smooth $H_*$ in this set by smooth positive $H_j$ in every $C^{1,\al}$ and $W^{2,s}$ with $0<\al<1$ and $1\le s<\infty$. Solutions for $H_j$ form a single bubble at the unique maximum of $H_*$ as their weighted energies tend to $τ_{H_*}$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp low-dimensional Constants in the second-order hydrogen Heisenberg uncertainty principle via Jacobi chains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish the sharp constants $\mathcal H_N$ of the second-order Hydrogen Heisenberg uncertainty principle for $N=2,3$. Starting from the first angular mode reduction, we rewrite the fourth-order radial quotient as two coupled radial Coulomb channels. Then we turn the compatibility constraint into an explicit Jacobi chain by expanding the $B$-channel in generalized Laguerre polynomials and passing to parity-tail variables. Its tail energies satisfy scalar Riccati recursions, equivalently continued fractions. Furthermore, we characterize $2\mathcal H_2$ and $2\mathcal H_3$ as the unique roots of two explicit scalar equations, and we show that free-tail and Dirichlet finite sections provide monotone lower and upper approximations converging to the sharp constants. This yields rigorous bounds and the values $$\mathcal H_2\approx0.84478056,\quad \mathcal H_3\approx1.82348779.$$ We also obtain uniqueness of the first-mode radial extremizer up to amplitude, rotation, and dilation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global-in-time dynamics of the pressureless Euler/incompressible non-Newtonian equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper addresses a two-phase fluid system on the periodic domain $\mathbb{T}^3$, consisting of the pressureless Euler equations and the incompressible non-Newtonian equations coupled through a drag force. We prove the global-in-time existence of strong solutions to this system for a certain class of stress tensors in the non-Newtonian fluid. Our proof combines a priori large-time behavior estimates for classical solutions with a bootstrapping argument on the $L^2$-Sobolev norms, which effectively handles the difficulties caused by the lack of dissipation in the density of the Euler equation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global existence, blow-up behavior and numerical simulations for a class of chemotaxis-driven fish-mussel systems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this work, we investigate a chemotaxis-driven fish--mussel ecosystem model described by a coupled system of partial differential equations subject to homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. Under suitable assumptions on the system parameters and initial data, we establish the global existence of classical solutions by employing semigroup methods together with a priori estimates. We also examine the possible blow-up behavior of solutions in a three-dimensional domain. To support the theoretical analysis, a finite element method is developed for the numerical approximation of the system, and convergence studies based on mesh refinement are carried out to verify the accuracy and stability of the proposed numerical scheme. Furthermore, numerical simulations illustrating the blow-up behavior of solutions in the computational domain are presented.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Dissipative solutions for 2D Onsager's conjecture
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In 1949, L. Onsager conjectured that weak solutions of the Euler equations in $C_{t,x}^γ$ are energy conservative when $γ>\frac{1}{3}$, whereas nonconservative solutions exist when $γ<\frac{1}{3}$. Constantin, E and Titi [13] proved the conservation part, while Isett [26] constructed nontrivial $C^γ_{t,x}$ weak solutions with compact support in time in three dimensions for each $0<γ<\frac{1}{3}$. Building on this breakthrough work, Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi Jr. and Vicol [7] obtained strictly dissipative solutions below the Onsager threshold. In two dimensions, Giri and Radu [23] first constructed a nontrivial weak solution in $C^{\frac{1}{3}-}(\mathbb T^2\times[0,T])$ and left an open problem whether it would be possible to construct dissipative solutions (controllable energy) below $\frac{1}{3}$ threshold. In this paper, we reslove this question and thereby obtain infinitely many strictly dissipative weak solutions in $C^γ(\mathbb T^2\times[0,T])$ for every $0<γ<\frac{1}{3}$. Moreover, we prove that the associated wild initial data are dense in the divergence-free subspace of $C^{γ'}(\mathbb{T}^2)$ for any $0<γ' <\frac{1}{3}$. The key new ingredient is a family of staircase traveling waves, which we combine with a Picard iteration coupled to the Newton--Nash scheme to control both the Reynolds stress and the kinetic energy. The construction also applies in every dimension $d\geq2$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonlocal elliptic equations involving logarithmic Laplacian: Existence, non-existence and uniqueness results
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this work, we study the existence, non-existence, and uniqueness results for nonlocal elliptic equations involving logarithmic Laplacian, and subcritical, critical, and supercritical logarithmic nonlinearities. The Poho\u zaev's identity and Díaz-Saa type inequality are proved, which are of independent interest and can be applied to a larger class of problems. Depending upon the growth of nonlinearities and regularity of the weight function, we study the small-order asymptotic of nonlocal weighted elliptic equations involving the fractional Laplacian of order $2s.$ We show that the least energy solutions of a weighted nonlocal problem with superlinear or sublinear growth converge to a nontrivial nonnegative least-energy solution of Brézis-Nirenberg type and logistic-type limiting problem respectively involving the logarithmic Laplacian.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Due to a mistake in the proof of Pohozeav identity the paper is withdrawn. A new draft is prepared with extended existence results for a large class of nonlinearity in arXiv:2504.18907.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stable solutions to $p$-Laplacian type equations with variable coefficients
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study stable regular solutions of the equation $-\operatorname{div} igg(\Big(A(x)
abla u \cdot 
abla u\Big)^{p/2-1}A(x)
abla u igg) = f(u)$ in $B_1 \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, where $p > 1$, $f \in C^1(\mathbb{R})$ is nonnegative, and $A$ is a locally Lipschitz, symmetric, uniformly elliptic matrix field. We prove that stable regular solutions satisfy an interior Hölder estimate for $n < p + 4p/(p - 1)$ when $p \ge 2$, and for $n < 5p$ when $1 < p < 2$. This extends the result of Cabré, Miraglio, and Sanchón [7] for the $p$-Laplace equation.
  Note that the constant in our Hölder estimate depends on the local $C^1$ norm of $A$, but not on its $C^2$ norm. Our approach is motivated by the interior regularity estimates of Cabré, Miraglio, and Sanchón [7] for the $p$-Laplace equation and by Erneta's [14] treatment of variable coefficients in semilinear elliptic equations.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Long-time action stability for perturbed KdV near finite-gap tori
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove action and spectral stability near finite-gap tori of the periodic Korteweg--de Vries equation under autonomous analytic Hamiltonian perturbations of size $\varepsilon$. The estimates are uniform over prescribed compact families, without small-amplitude or nonresonance assumptions, and allow nearby initial data with infinitely many open gaps. Assuming a strong solution and a uniform higher Sobolev bound on $[0,T_0/\varepsilon]$, we permit one-derivative loss in the perturbing Hamiltonian's normal gradient. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ and initial normal Birkhoff size $r_0$, the tangential action variations and weighted sum of normal actions are bounded by $C_δ(r_0^2+\varepsilon^{2δ})$, while the spectral-gap variation in $\ell^2$ is bounded by $C_δ(r_0+\varepsilon^δ)$, for every $0<δ<1/4$. A key ingredient is coercivity of the negative Hessian of the nonlinear KdV Hamiltonian on the full $\ell^2$ action space at every finite-gap action. We combine this with resonance analysis and corrected action observables evaluated along the solution. The hypotheses are verified for several local and nonlocal Hamiltonian perturbations.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Maximum Principles and Principal Eigenvalue for Coupled Local/Nonlocal Models
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we analyze the validity of the maximum principle and the existence of a principal eigenvalue for a problem involving two regions, in one of them the main operator is the classical Laplacian (a local operator) while in the other region the operator is a nonlocal one (these regions are coupled via a transmission term that is also nonlocal). The main difficulty here comes from the lack of compactness of the nonlocal part that occurs since we are considering non-singular kernels.

Functional Analysis.title: Structured coordinate systems in $L^p(\mathbb{R})$
Functional Analysis.summary: We construct Schauder bases of $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ with significant structural constraints on their elements. For every $1 \leq p< \infty$, we obtain bases of non-negative functions with basis constants arbitrarily close to one, as well as bases with positive biorthogonal functionals. For every $2 \leq p < \infty$, we construct Schauder bases consisting of translates of a single function, which can be chosen to extend to an entire function. When $p>2$, the translation parameters can be chosen from any prescribed unbounded subset of $\mathbb{R}$, a conclusion that fails for $p=2$. Finally, for $p>2$, the entire function generating the basis of translates can also be chosen non-negative.

Functional Analysis.title: Frame constructions associated with operator orbits
Functional Analysis.summary: This paper studies frames in Hilbert spaces generated by the orbits of finitely many vectors under a single operator, presenting new results on normal operators and multiplication operators as well as on operators composed of Jordan blocks. These results generalize existing results of Cabrelli, Molter, Paternostro and Philipp by means of techniques which deal with weighted interpolation, weighted composition operators, and Beurling--Lax theory related to shifts of finite multiplicity. Likewise, we discuss Carleson frames and construct counterexamples to a recent conjecture of Aldroubi, Cabrelli, Krishtal and Molter, showing that the relevant necessary condition is of density type rather than the Müntz--Szász condition. Moreover, by using the theory of weighted composition operators, we answer a question of Cheshmavar on frames produced by iterative multiplication. Finally, for orbits of infinitely many vectors the underlying model is a shift of infinite multiplicity which, by a theorem of Rota, is a universal operator; consequently, a complete description of such frames along these lines would encompass the Invariant Subspace Problem.
Functional Analysis.comment: 26 pages, paper totally rewritten with several new results (see the abstract)

Functional Analysis.title: Hardy Spaces and Toeplitz operators on the Hexablock
Functional Analysis.summary:
The hexablock is a domain in $\mathbb{C}^4$ given by
  \[
  \mathbb{H}=\left\{(a,x_1,x_2,x_3)\in \mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{E}:
  \sup_{z_1,z_2\in\mathbb{D}}
  \left|
  \frac{a\sqrt{(1-|z_1|^2)(1-|z_2|^2)}}
  {1-x_1z_1-x_2z_2+x_3z_1z_2}
  \right|<1
  \right\},
  \] where $\mathbb{E}=\left\{(x_1,x_2,x_3)\in\mathbb{C}^{3}: 1-x_1z_1-x_2z_2+x_3z_1z_2\neq 0
  \ \text{for all}\ z_1,z_2\in\overline{\mathbb D}\right\}$ is the tetrablock. We introduce a Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb H)$ associated with a canonical measure $μ_{\mathbb H}$ on the distinguished boundary $b\mathbb H$ of the hexablock. We identify $H^2(\mathbb H)$ with a closed subspace of $L^2(b\mathbb H,μ_{\mathbb H})$ and show that it is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We prove that $\mathbb H$ is the interior of the polynomial convex hull of $Ψ_{\mathbb H}(\overline{\mathbb D}^4)$, where \[
  Ψ_{\mathbb H}(ξ_1, ξ_2,λ_1,λ_2)
  =
  \left(\frac{λ_1(ξ_1-1)}{2},
  \frac{ξ_2(ξ_1+1)}{2}, \
  \frac{λ_1λ_2(ξ_1+1)}{2}, \
  ξ_1 ξ_2λ_1λ_2
  \right). \] We obtain a Brown-Halmos type characterization of Toeplitz operators on $H^2(\mathbb H)$ and a commutant lifting theorem for $\mathbb H$-isometries. We characterize $\mathbb H$-unitaries as the images of commuting quadruples of unitaries under $Ψ_{\mathbb H}$ and present a class of $\mathbb H$-contractions from commuting quadruples having $\overline{\mathbb D}^4$ as a spectral set. We prove an analogous characterization of $\mathbb E$-unitaries and present a class of $\mathbb E$-contractions arising from commuting triples of contractions having $\overline{\mathbb D}^3$ as a spectral set. En route, we also study a weighted Hardy space on the hexablock.
Functional Analysis.comment: This is a preliminary draft. It shall be revised soon

Functional Analysis.title: Augmented Dynamical Sampling under unmodeled Forcing
Functional Analysis.summary: We study recovery of an initial state from dynamical samples of a trajectory driven by unknown additive forcing. Measurements against both the original sensors and their images under the adjoint nominal evolution yield one-step residuals that cancel the initial state exactly. These residuals separate forcing estimation from initial-state reconstruction. For a centered Gaussian forcing model with fixed covariance parameters, we combine Gaussian conditioning with canonical dual-frame reconstruction and derive an exact unconditional second-moment identity, including the correlation between the forcing-estimation error and the measurement noise. We also obtain high-probability bounds and identify the irreducible forcing uncertainty through a conditional covariance in the geometry induced by the prior. A hierarchy of augmented sensor systems separates the role of sampling depth in forcing visibility from that of the observation horizon in nominal observability. An image-transport experiment and finite-dimensional and periodic-convolution experiments illustrate the residual correction and the separate roles of sampling depth and observation horizon.

Functional Analysis.title: Musielak-Orlicz-Sobolev embeddings: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper we study the necessary and sufficient conditions on domain for Musielak-Orlicz-Sobolev embedding of the space $W^{1,Φ(\cdot,\cdot)}(Ω)$ where $Φ(x,t):=t^{p(x)}{(\log(e+t))}^{q(x)}.$

Functional Analysis.title: Quantitative characterization of Gaussian small ball probabilities
Functional Analysis.summary: The quantitative study of the Gaussian measure of symmetric convex sets is a central theme at the interface of probability theory and convex geometry. From a probabilistic perspective, it amounts to analyzing the tail behavior of suprema of Gaussian processes. The typical magnitude and upper tail of Gaussian processes are well-understood, thanks to Talagrand's celebrated Majorizing Measures theorem and to Gaussian concentration. In contrast, despite fundamental connections with metric entropy established by Kuelbs and Li, no general sharp characterization of the lower tail is available. In this work, we close this gap by establishing a sharp two-sided characterization of Gaussian small ball probabilities, involving both metric entropy and local widths of the underlying convex body. This yields an explicit chaining-type description of lower quantiles of Gaussian processes in terms of the metric structure of the convexified index set, as well as a general comparison inequality for convex sets. We further obtain analogous quantitative characterizations of two important geometric quantities associated with symmetric convex sets, namely intrinsic volumes (quermassintegrals) and the radii of random sections beyond the classical Dvoretzky range. A unifying theme of these results is the central role of convexity in the quantitative understanding of small ball probabilities.

Functional Analysis.title: Translation Continuity and the Structure of Infinite-Dimensional Lebesgue Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: For Baker's Borel-rectangle measure $μ$ and $1\le p<\infty$, we classify the continuous vectors of each one-parameter translation group on $L^p(μ)$. For each $v\in\mathbb{R}^\mathbb{N}$, the continuous vectors form a projection band, which coincides with the whole space when $v$ has finite support, is trivial when $v\notin\ell^1$, and is nonzero and proper otherwise. We also establish in ZFC the isometric classification considered in [Isometric classification of the $L^{p}$-spaces of infinite dimensional Lebesgue measure, Banach J. Math. Anal. 20 (2026), no. 1, Paper No. 7], showing that both $L^p(μ)$ and the kernel of restriction to integer cubes are lattice isometric to $\ell^p(\mathfrak{c},L^p[0,1])$. When $v\in\ell^1\setminus c_{00}$, the continuous band and its disjoint complement have the same lattice-isometric structure, with the latter contained in the cube-restriction kernel.

Functional Analysis.title: The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
Functional Analysis.summary:
We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture.
  The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity.
  We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar.
  In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.
Functional Analysis.comment: This is an expository version with navigational aids, not intended for publication

Functional Analysis.title: The Bishop--Phelps--Bollobás Property for Extremally Disconnected Ranges
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $\mathbb F$ be either $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let $L$ be a nonempty extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space. We show that $(X,C(L,\mathbb F))$ has the Bishop--Phelps--Bollobás property with $η(\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^2/2$ for every Banach space $X$ over $\mathbb F$. For each fixed $L$ and either scalar field, this bound is optimal uniformly over $X$.
Functional Analysis.comment: 2nd version; the separability assumption on the domain is removed. The title is changed accordingly

Functional Analysis.title: Kac lemma on noncommutative probability spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove non-commutative Kac's formula for actions of countable groups. We replace the return time functions by suitable projections in von Neumann algebras. Moreover, we prove a generalised Kac's formula in the non-commutative setting which extends the allocation construction of Meyerovitch and Weiss and is motivated by the random Kac inequality of Aaronson.
Functional Analysis.comment: 19 pages; preliminary version. Comments are welcome

Functional Analysis.title: The linear scale in metric cotype for Alexandrov spaces of nonnegative curvature
Functional Analysis.summary: We answer a question of Eskenazis, Mendel, and Naor by proving that the optimal universal scaling parameter in metric cotype $2$ for complete Alexandrov spaces of nonnegative curvature has order $n$. The upper bound follows from a dyadic application of the Lang--Schroeder inequality, and the lower bound follows from snowflake universality of $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^3)$.

Functional Analysis.title: Crossed-Heinz Inequalities
Functional Analysis.summary: For positive matrices $A,B$ and $p,q>0$, the second author (2009) asked whether the inequality \[ \|A^pB^q+B^pA^q\|\leq \|A^{p+q}+B^{p+q}\| \] holds for every unitarily invariant norm. Despite a series of papers addressing this question, as well as recent intensive computational and AI-assisted investigations by Matthew Colbrook (2026, \cite{Col}), the problem remains open. It is a striking example of how an elementary scalar statement can become extremely difficult to handle in the noncommutative setting. Some partial positive results are known. In this note, we provide one more: the crossed-Heinz inequality holds for two-by-two matrices. This result also leads to a new and elegant characterization of the singular values of two-by-two matrices. In arbitrary dimension, we turn to the special case $p=q=1$, obtaining a series of eigenvalue estimates for the anticommutator $AB+BA$.
Functional Analysis.comment: This paper has been accepted for publication in the Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society

Functional Analysis.title: Three Lipschitz functions on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces with no common point of Fréchet differentiability
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that on every infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space \(H\), there exist three real-valued Lipschitz functions with no common point of Fréchet differentiability. This gives a negative answer to a longstanding question of Lindenstrauss, Preiss, and Tišer. The proof is constructive and relies on elementary calculus and finite-dimensional linear algebra. Since every Lipschitz map from a Hilbert space into $\mathbb R^2$ has a point of Fréchet differentiability, the target dimension three is optimal.

Functional Analysis.title: Invariant subspaces for integration and differentiation on convex domains
Functional Analysis.summary: For a conformal map $g$ of the unit disc $U$ onto any bounded convex domain $Ω$ we determine the invariant subspaces for the integration operator $T_gf = \int_0^zfg'$ on the Hardy space $H^p$, by means of a Fock space model. Under some additional regularity assumptions on $\partialΩ$ we also treat integration from a boundary point of $U$, and we determine the residual subspaces (those invariant subspaces on which the operator has empty spectrum) for the left inverse $D_gf = f'/g'$ of $T_g$ on the smooth disc algebra $A^\infty$. The latter result is new even for $Ω= U$.

Functional Analysis.title: Bilinear embedding for divergence-form operators with first-order terms and negative potentials
Functional Analysis.summary: This article establishes a bilinear embedding for second-order divergence-form operators with complex coefficients, characterized by the simultaneous presence of first-order terms and negative potentials. This work provides a further development of the theory initiated by Carbonaro and Dragičević for the homogeneous case, and recently extended by the second author in two papers where first-order terms and negative potentials were treated separately. We work in the general setting of arbitrary open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ under Dirichlet, Neumann, or mixed boundary conditions. Our main contribution is the introduction of a unified notion of generalized $p$-ellipticity that extends all its predecessors and serves as the natural condition for the bilinear inequality. Methodologically, we overcome the rigidity of the Bellman-heat method on arbitrary open subsets by introducing a novel sequence-based approach that unifies and simplifies the previous techniques. As fundamental applications, we prove the boundedness of the $H^\infty$-calculus on $L^p$ and establish $L^p$-maximal regularity. Moreover, we show that this generalized $p$-ellipticity provides a sufficient condition for the $L^p$-contractivity and $L^p$-analyticity of the generated semigroup. Finally, we apply our theory to magnetic Schrödinger operators, characterizing the range of exponents $p$ for which the associated coefficient tuple satisfies the generalized $p$-ellipticity condition introduced here.
Functional Analysis.comment: In v2 we have slightly modified the presentation of our results and added the example of magnetic Schrödinger operators; 65 pages

Functional Analysis.title: The Gleason--Kahane--Zelazko theorem: a gentle introduction
Functional Analysis.summary: After some personal recollections of Jean-Pierre Kahane, this paper gives a gentle introduction to the Gleason-Kahane-Zelazko theorem. The theorem states that a normalised complex-linear functional on a unital complex Banach algebra is multiplicative whenever it does not vanish on invertible elements. Neither continuity of the functional nor commutativity of the algebra is assumed. We give a detailed account of three proofs: the original argument of Gleason and, independently, Kahane and Zelazko; the polynomial proof of Roitman and Sternfeld; and a proof by the author. We explain the complex analysis behind each: a special case of Hadamard's factorisation theorem, a polynomial argument using the fundamental theorem of algebra, and the Polya-Saxer theorem on zero-free entire functions and their derivatives. The elementary entire-function lemma needed for the first proof is proved in full; the Polya-Saxer theorem is used without proof. We give full details of the algebraic argument common to the three proofs, which deduces multiplicativity from the preservation of squares, including the non-commutative case. We then discuss applications and counterexamples, and present an extension to Ransford's generalised spectra using the Roitman--Sternfeld argument. We conclude with a brief guide to the more recent literature.
Functional Analysis.comment: 31 pages. Paper submitted to a volume in memory of Jean-Pierre Kahane

Functional Analysis.title: Invariance Preserving Conjugation and Linear Operators on the Hardy Space
Functional Analysis.summary: We study linear and anti-linear operators on the Hardy space $H^2$ in connection with the Beurling lattice. First, in contrast to Sarason's result \cite{S1}, we show that no non-zero anti-linear operator leaves every shift-invariant subspace invariant. Then we completely characterize the class of conjugations, isometries, and invertible linear operators preserving the shift-invariant subspace structure in terms of weighted composition operators induced by disk automorphisms--combined with the canonical conjugation, isometric multiplication, and invertible Toeplitz operators, respectively. We also establish the existence and non-existence of conjugations that map shift-invariant subspaces to coinvariant subspaces. Finally, we construct a counterexample that rules out an analogous factorization for bounded linear operators preserving shift-invariance of closed images.

Functional Analysis.title: Fast approximation and learning of binary classification tasks in o-minimal structures using ReLU neural networks
Functional Analysis.summary: We study binary classification tasks whose decision sets are given by definable sets in o-minimal expansions of the real field. Motivated by the cell decomposition theory of definable sets, we introduce traceable sets that isolate the analytical properties of definable sets used for fast approximation by ReLU neural networks. Under uniform bounds on the number of cells and a suitable extension assumption for the boundary functions, we prove that classifiers can be approximated in $L^p$ up to accuracy $\varepsilon>0$ by ReLU neural networks of size $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-p(n-1)/m})$, with depth independent of $\varepsilon$ and polynomially bounded weights. This establishes quantitative approximation rates for suitable definable collections in o-minimal structures using ReLU neural networks. Furthermore, the stated approximation rates are also derived for definable maps under similar geometric assumptions on their smoothness domains. We then obtain statistical learning rates for empirical risk minimization with hinge loss over the approximating ReLU neural network classes. For $N$ uniformly distributed samples, the predicted classifiers achieve expected misclassification error of order $N^{-m/(m+n-1)}$ up to an arbitrarily small polynomial loss.

Functional Analysis.title: Improvement of a Hardy-Littlewood inequality and applications to the boundedness of analytic paraproducts on mixed norm spaces
Functional Analysis.summary:
Let $\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$ denote the space of analytic functions in the unit disc $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$. For $0<p<\infty$ and $f\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$, let $M_p^p(r,f)=\int_0^{2π}|f(re^{iθ})|^p \frac{dθ}{2π}$ and $M_\infty(r,f) = \sup_{|z|=r}|f(z)|$.
  For $0<p<q\leq \infty$, Hardy and Littlewood proved the prevalent inequality $$M_q(r,f)\le C(p,q)\frac{M_p(ρ,f)}{(ρ-r)^{\frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{q}}}$$ for $0\leq r<ρ\leq 1$ and $f\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$.
  In this paper, we obtain an improvement of this well-known inequality which is employed to characterize the symbols $g\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$ such that the analytic paraproducts $T_gf(z)=\int_0^z f(ζ)g'(ζ)\,dζ$, $S_gf(z)=\int_0^z f'(ζ)g(ζ)\,dζ$ and $M_gf(z)=f(z)g(z)$, are bounded between two different mixed-norm spaces $A^{p,q}_ω=\{ g\in \mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D}): \int_0^1 M_p^q(r,g) ω(r)\,dr<\infty\}$ induced by a radial doubling weight $ω$. En route to the proof of these characterizations, we consider an open Carleson measure problem posed by Luecking and we solve it in a meaningful particular case.

Functional Analysis.title: Analogs of crystalline measures in tube sets
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $μ$ be a pure point complex measure on a tube set $R^d+i F$, where $F$ is a compact convex subset in $R^d$, such that this tube set is the minimal closed convex tube set containing support of $μ$. Furthermore, assume that the Fourier transform $\hatμ$ (in the sense of distributions) is a measure. We determine conditions on the measure $μ$ under which the variation of the measure $\hatμ$ grows at least as $\exp\{2πH_F(t)\}$, as well as conditions under which this variation grows at most as $\exp\{2πH_F(t)\}$; here $H_F(t)$ is the support function of $F$.

Functional Analysis.title: Banach-Valued Carré du Champ Operators and Functional Gaussian Approximation
Functional Analysis.summary: We develop a projective-tensor-valued carré du champ for Malliavin-differentiable Banach-valued random elements and establish an associated integration-by-parts formula. The resulting dimension-free comparison principle bounds Gaussian approximation against twice Fréchet-differentiable test functions by the expected projective norm of a random covariance discrepancy. For processes on Skorokhod space equipped with the uniform norm, a smoothing argument converts this comparison into a quantitative bound in the bounded-Lipschitz metric, subject to explicit regularization errors. On Banach-valued Wiener chaos we express the carré du champ through contractions and obtain quantitative estimates in terms of contracted kernels. As a concrete application, we establish a quantitative functional Breuer--Major bound for the canonical polygonally interpolated partial-sum process, together with a corollary for the original Skorokhod step process. The estimate applies to the entire path in the uniform topology under explicit covariance conditions. We also record the trace-class specialization of the contraction bounds in Hilbert spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: The Strong Naor--Schechtman Convolution Inequality on the Product of Cyclic Groups
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we resolve the convolution inequality problem posed by Naor and Schechtman in \cite[Question 6.1]{N-S2016} (see also \cite{Na2016}). More precisely, we establish the following strong convolution inequality on products of finite cyclic groups: For each $1\leq p<\infty$ there exists $c_{p}>0$ such that for every $n$, $m\in \mathbb{N}$ the following holds \[ \begin{split} &\sum_{\varepsilon\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}\sum_{x\in \Z}\left|E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}}f(x+\varepsilon)-E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}}f(x-\varepsilon)\right|^{p}\\ \leq& c^{p}_{p}\sum_{\varepsilon\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}\sum_{x\in \Z}\left|\varepsilon_{j}\left[E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}\setminus\{j\}}f(x+e_{j})-E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}\setminus\{j\}}f(x-e_{j})\right]\right|^{p}, \end{split} \] $E_{A}f(x)=\frac{1}{2^{n}}\sum_{δ\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}f\left(x+\sum_{j\in A}δ_{j}e_{j}\right)$ for every $A\subseteq \{1,\cdots,n\}$. The growth order we obtain here $c_{p}=O(p)$ as $p\to \infty$. For the endpoint $p=\infty$, we show by a counterexample that the strong convolution inequality fails for the $L_{\infty}$, and we prove that the appropriate endpoint for $p=\infty$ is the martingale $BMO$ space.

Functional Analysis.title: Weighted STSAFT-Modulation Spaces and Approximation by Phase-Adapted Neural Networks
Functional Analysis.summary: We develop a transform-adapted approximation framework for shallow neural networks based on the short-time special affine Fourier transform (STSAFT). Replacing the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) in the definition of classical modulation spaces, we work with weighted STSAFT-modulation spaces, building on the existing SAFT-associated modulation-space framework, and use their chirp correspondence with classical weighted modulation spaces through the chirp factorization of the SAFT kernel. We construct an associated neural dictionary and establish an $N$-term Sobolev approximation bound of order $N^{-1/2}$ on bounded one-dimensional domains. A global approximation theorem is also obtained when the spatial translation parameter ranges over the whole real line; a compact-support argument explains why an unrestricted global conclusion cannot in general be inferred from a bounded translation range. For a fixed-scale chirp family $f_κ(x)=e^{iπκx^2}u(x)$, we combine the global estimate with a phase analysis to obtain the stronger phase-dependent upper-bound factor $\langleλ\rangle^n\langleκ-λ\rangle^{n+3/2-1/r}.$ For each fixed nonzero Schwartz envelope, matching the dictionary phase reduces the growth of this specified upper bound from order $|κ|^{n+3/2-1/r}$ to order $|κ|^n$, while preserving the $N^{-1/2}$ rate. The associated mismatch scale is stated as a comparison of upper bounds, not as a threshold for the optimal approximation error. Four numerical experiments examine model comparison, error decay with dictionary size, phase mismatch, and the obstruction caused by restricted translations. We discuss the effective number of fitted output coefficients, including the rank loss of the sine branch at zero phase, and distinguish the numerical diagnostics from the theoretical best-approximation estimates.

Functional Analysis.title: Convolution on quantum tori I: Sharp Young inequalities and endpoint Sobolev embeddings
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce a convolution of noncommutative tori. The construction is the preadjoint of a trace-preserving cocycle-addition homomorphism. Its zero-parameter case is the function--operator semi-convolution. We prove both mixed $L_{1}$--$L_\infty$ inequalities and various Young inequalities with the optimal constant one, including their limiting cases. The endpoint bounds also yield submajorization and convolution estimates in fully symmetric spaces. As applications, we establish, for every integer $k\geq1$ and $1\leq p\leq\infty$, $W_{p}^{k}(\mathbb{T}_θ^{d})\hookrightarrow B_{\infty,\infty}^{k-\frac{d}{p}}(\mathbb{T}_θ^{d})$, and prove the critical embedding $W_{1}^{d}(\mathbb{T}_θ^{d})\hookrightarrow L_\infty(\mathbb{T}_θ^{d})$. These results settle the two questions posed in Remark~6.8 of Xiong, Xu and Yin \cite{XiongXuYin}.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Evolution of Internal Waves on Surfaces of Revolution with Flat Ends
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We generalize the 2D linear internal wave equation to non-compact surfaces of revolution with flat ends. We show that the leading profile of this equation with oscillatory forcing is the unique incoming solution to the corresponding stationary equation. This is done by proving a limiting absorption principle via propagation of semiclassical defect measure.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Bounds for spectral projectors on the three-dimensional torus
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study $L^2$ to $L^p$ operator norms of spectral projectors for the Euclidean Laplacian on the torus in the case where the spectral window is narrow. With a window of constant size this is a classical result of Sogge; in the small-window limit we are left with $L^p$ norms of eigenfunctions of the Laplacian, as considered for instance by Bourgain. For the three-dimensional torus we prove new cases of a previous conjecture of the first two authors concerning the size of these norms; we also refine certain prior results to remove $ε$-losses in all dimensions. We use methods from number theory: the geometry of numbers, the circle method and exponential sum bounds due to Guo. We complement these techniques with height splitting and a bilinear argument to prove sharp results.
  We exposit on the various techniques used and their limitations.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Final version, published by Ars Inveniendi Analytica

Analysis of PDEs.title: Logarithmic derivatives of variational and singular stochastic partial differential equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For a stochastic partial differential equation posed on a Gelfand triple and satisfying the fully local monotone conditions of Röckner, Shang and Zhang, we compute the logarithmic derivative of the law of the solution at a fixed time along a prescribed direction of the state space. The formula is intrinsic, expressed through the Hilbert-Schmidt Malliavin derivative $Φ_r = \mathcal{D}_r X(t)$ and the covariance $γ_t = \int_0^t Φ_r Φ_r^{*}\,\mathrm{d}r$ alone, so that neither the inversion of the first variation nor uniform Malliavin-Sobolev bounds on the Tikhonov family are needed. It follows from an integration-by-parts identity on a Hilbert space, a Moore-Penrose covering field on Wiener space and a trace formula for the Tikhonov limit, brought to the equation by the representation $Φ_r = Y(t,r)\mathcal{B}(r,X(r))$. The linearised theory is carried by $Φ$ and by its own Malliavin derivative $\mathcal{W} = \mathcal{D}Φ$, whose regularity is measured in the time-integrated quadratic energy that the dissipative structure of the linearisation produces, so that no operator norm of the first variation between the spaces of the triple occurs. The stochastic $p$-Laplacian and the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equation are treated in detail; for the latter the dissipative, forcing and exponential-moment hypotheses are established together under trace-class additive noise and a smallness threshold on the noise covariance. A scalar reduction carries the identity beyond the variational class, to the law of a pairing $\langle u(t), \varphi\rangle$ for the singular equations of Bruned, Chandra, Chevyrev and Hairer, on the same Hölder triangle of moment exponents.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Small-data $L^2$ theory for the intermediate NLS and the Calogero--Moser derivative NLS
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study a class of nonlinear Schrödinger equations (NLS) in a unified way. This class includes two important examples: the intermediate NLS (INLS) and the Calogero--Moser derivative NLS (CM-DNLS). Our main results are twofold. First, we prove small-data global well-posedness in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ for a broad class of equations. This includes both focusing and defocusing CM-DNLS and the INLS for arbitrary choices of its parameters. Second, we prove small-data scattering in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ under an additional assumption. This result covers both focusing and defocusing CM-DNLS and the INLS for specific choices of its parameters. Both the formulation of the problem, including the notion of solution, and the proofs rely crucially on a linear theory for Schrödinger equations with rough time-dependent potentials. This theory is also of independent interest, since we allow potentials so rough that the standard Duhamel formulation may not make sense. Our approach is perturbative and is built on the bilinear Strichartz estimate proved by Ozawa and Tsutsumi in 1998. In particular, our argument does not rely on integrability.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Remarks on some quasi-linear fourth order parabolic equations arising in mathematical physics
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This note proves existence and uniqueness of strong solutions to a broad class of fourth-order quasi-linear parabolic equations in the class of Wiener spaces. It improves upon previous results in the literature, devoted to some special cases falling within the general framework developed here, in which uniqueness held true in a smaller class than the space where existence was proven. Gain of analyticity, as well as generalisations to higher-order equations and to propagation of higher regularities, are also discussed.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Blow-up rate for 1-d semilinear wave equations without scaling invariance at characteristic points
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the blow-up behavior of solutions to the semilinear wave equation $$ \partial_t^2 u - \partial_x^2 u = |u|^{p-1}u \ln^a(u^2+2), \quad (x,t)\in \mathbb{R} \times [0,T), $$ with $p > 1$ and $a<0$. While the blow-up rate at non-characteristic points was determined for all $a \in \mathbb{R}$ in previous work, the analysis at characteristic points has remained an open problem. The main obstruction is that known constructions of a Lyapunov functional in similarity variables require several steps and rely on a covering argument, which is not available at characteristic points. Focusing on the regime $a < 0$, we construct a Lyapunov functional directly, without any covering argument. This yields uniform bounds on the solution in similarity variables, and hence the blow-up rate at every point, including characteristic ones. To our knowledge, this is the first work to determine the blow-up rate at characteristic points for an equation without scaling invariance.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The anisotropic Weyl law and Grassmannian equidistribution
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish a Weyl law for the codimension-one anisotropic volume spectrum on compact Riemannian manifolds. We then use this law to obtain equidistribution in the full Grassmannian bundle while keeping the ambient metric fixed. More precisely, on every closed connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension three through six, we construct smooth, embedded hypersurfaces stationary for anisotropies smoothly converging to area. The cumulative sum of their area measures, when lifted to the Grassmannian bundle, converges to the uniform measure.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Strong and weak mean value sets for elliptic operators: uniqueness and counterexamples
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
Classical theorems of Epstein--Schiffer and Kuran characterize balls by the mean value identity for integrable harmonic functions. In the Fermi Lectures, Caffarelli described an obstacle problem construction of analogous averaging sets for symmetric uniformly elliptic divergence-form operators. Working in dimension $n \ge 2$ throughout the paper, we prove that for symmetric uniformly elliptic operators with bounded measurable coefficients, every bounded open set satisfying the mean value inequality for all integrable subsolutions defined on that set (what we call ``strong mean value sets'') agrees almost everywhere with the canonical set from Caffarelli's construction which has the same center and volume. The proof uses weak modified Schwarz potentials and an energy comparison.
  Additionally, we construct smooth symmetric uniformly elliptic operators for which the unit ball satisfies the mean value identity for all integrable solutions but fails the subsolution inequality, showing that there can be two distinct notions for what one can consider to be a ``mean value set.'' The canonical mean value set with the same center and volume as this weak mean value ball has a hole of positive measure.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Electromagnetic scattering by Minkowski-type bianisotropic media
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the time-harmonic scattering of electromagnetic waves by a bounded stationary inclusion whose effective constitutive law is of Minkowski type. The constant vector $V$ is regarded as a constitutive moving parameter. Such a law arises as an effective description of synthetic moving media and of suitable traveling-wave space--time modulations. Starting from the implicit Minkowski relations, we derive a Maxwell transmission system and its Lippmann--Schwinger volume-integral formulation. The dimensionless parameter $β=|V|/c_Ω$ governs the pointwise constitutive inversion, namely the matrix is invertible precisely for $β\neq1$, while on the subcritical branch $0\leqβ<1$ its inverse admits an explicit convergent expansion. Using the algebraic structure of the cross-product operator, we obtain a spectral characterization of solvability and a quantitative sufficient condition separating the static material contrast from the $V$-dependent contribution which allows to justify the convergence of the corresponding Born series. As an application, we prove that full-aperture electric far-field data at a fixed frequency uniquely determine the support of the inclusion within this perturbative regime without assuming that $V$ is known.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Gaussian fluctuations and moderate deviations for two-dimensional stochastic nematic liquid crystal flows
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the small-noise behaviour of a two-dimensional stochastic nematic liquid crystal model, where the Navier--Stokes equations with multiplicative noise are coupled with a Ginzburg--Landau equation for the director field driven by geometric Stratonovich noise. While large deviations for stochastic nematic liquid crystal models have been studied earlier, the central limit and moderate deviation regimes have not been considered. We first prove a central limit theorem in the natural energy space and show that the rescaled fluctuations converge, in every $L^p$-norm and with rate $\sqrt{\eps}$, to the solution of a linear stochastic system. The limiting process is centred Gaussian. We then establish a moderate deviation principle with a quadratic rate function determined by the corresponding linearised skeleton equation, which coincides with the Cameron--Martin form of the Gaussian limit. We also show that the moderate deviation principle holds uniformly over bounded sets of initial data. The main arguments use a cancellation between the coupling terms, a one-sided estimate for the polynomial potential, and energy estimates with deterministic Gronwall coefficients, thereby avoiding exponential moment estimates.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Non-local SDEs, critical drifts and local blow-ups
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The paper is concerned with $α$-stable SDEs with singular time-inhomogeneous general drift. Our drifts satisfy e.g.\,a close to minimal possible critical Morrey class condition that covers local blow-ups of the type arising in some particle systems with strong attracting interactions. We develop detailed Sobolev regularity theory for the forward and backward equations, construct Feller propagator and prove weak existence and conditional uniqueness for the $α$-stable SDE.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Fixed a few minor errors and typos

Analysis of PDEs.title: Point symmetries and Lie reductions of Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We compute the point symmetry pseudogroup of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation using both the direct and the algebraic methods. We also revisit the classical Lie symmetry analysis of this model in detail, concentrating on hidden infinitesimal and hidden point symmetries. Additionally, we re-examine the symmetry properties of each codimension-one reduced model and determine their point symmetry pseudogroups.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A PINNs approach for the computation of eigenvalues in elliptic problems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we propose a method for computing eigenvalues of elliptic problems using Deep Learning techniques. A key feature of our approach is that it is independent of the space dimension and can compute arbitrary eigenvalues without requiring the prior computation of lower ones. Moreover, the method can be easily adapted to handle nonlinear eigenvalue problems.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Emulating the Darcy Solution Operator by Heat-Semigroup Functional Calculus and Pointwise Products
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We approximate the Darcy solution operator $(a,f)\mapsto u$, where $-\operatorname{div}(a
abla u)=f$, by operator networks built only from heat-semigroup evaluations $e^{-tL_0}$ of a single fixed reference operator and pointwise products. The key obstacle is the variable-coefficient coupling $
abla a\cdot
abla u$. We show that it is produced by the heat product defect $[P_t(bu)-P_tb\,P_tu]/(2t)$, which converges quantitatively to $
abla b\cdot
abla u$. Inserted into a Laplacian-preconditioned Richardson iteration, this yields an explicit scheme of depth $O(\log(1/\varepsilon)/\log(1/q))$ whose $\dot H^1$ error is at most $\varepsilon$, uniformly over the coefficient class and $L^2$ data, with all parameters explicit. Each block is controlled in continuum operator norm, without Galerkin truncation. On the torus, band-limited inputs admit an exact pseudo-spectral realization on a grid of $O(1/(\varepsilon a_{\min}))$ points per direction, up to logarithmic and class-dependent factors. The argument extends by carre du champ calculus to strongly local Dirichlet spaces with a spectral gap and a Bakry--Emery bound $\mathrm{BE}(-K,\infty)$, with dimension-independent constants after spectral-gap normalization. On the torus we also obtain a $C^2$-type coefficient class and a refinement to Wiener classes of regularity $1+θ$, with product-defect rate $t^{θ/2}$. The factor $1/(2t)$ makes the proved scheme ill-conditioned at small $\varepsilon$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Linearize or Discretize First? Error Estimates under Mesh-Uniform Regularity and Exponential Stability for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation, and its spatial semidiscretization by a weighted cubic Hermite Galerkin method. A small nonlinear wave can be approximated by a linear discrete simulation in two orders: linearize first and then discretize, or discretize first and then linearize. Both orders lead to the same total error. They divide this error differently between linearization and discretization. The difference of the two divisions is what we call the ordering error. We show that it is quadratic in the size of the initial datum and carries a positive power of the mesh size, for all time. It can be used to assess the effect of a coarse-mesh correction for nonlinear problems.
  For the continuous problem, the solution map is analytic, and the semigroup of the linearized equation has Crandall-Pazy regularity with the exact index 3/2. For the weighted scheme, the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit exponential stability, Kato smoothing and Crandall-Pazy regularity, with bounds uniform in the mesh size. The nonlinear solution maps are analytic, also uniformly in the mesh size.
  These properties give error estimates in which the error and the datum are measured in the same norm: in the energy norm, in $H_0^1$ and in $H^2$. On every interval $[t_0,\infty)$, $t_0>0$, same-norm convergence holds uniformly on balls at algebraic rates. The ordering error is of order $h^{1/6}$ times the square of the energy norm of the datum, uniformly for all $t\ge0$.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 36 pages. Ancillary files: the Lean 4 development for Theorems 4.1-4.4. Companion paper: arXiv:2611.12585

Analysis of PDEs.title: Dynamic Prandtl-Reuss Thermoplasticity with Degenerating Yield Constraints
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a three-dimensional dynamic thermoplastic system with a temperature-dependent convex yield set whose deviatoric section may collapse completely at a finite temperature. The underlying constitutive model is rate-independent Prandtl-Reuss perfect plasticity, without Kelvin-Voigt viscosity, hardening, or a safe-load condition. We construct global approximation-generated relaxed entropy-energy states by a one-parameter Temam-Norton-Hoff-Galerkin scheme with an undiscretized heat equation and untruncated plastic heat production. The logarithmic temperature is strongly compact in $L^2(0,T;L^q(Ω))$ for every $q<6$ and in $L^p((0,T)\timesΩ)$ for every $p<8/3$. An entropy-weighted work estimate yields convergence of the overstress at rate $O(\sqrt{\log n/n})$ in every fixed finite Lebesgue space and identifies stress admissibility. The constitutive limit comprises a distributional plastic balance, finite support-weighted measures, and compact-fibre lifts carrying exact normality and maximum plastic work. A locally finite lift on the positive-radius fibres unifies the level-restricted limits at every continuity level. At the macroscopic level, however, the available compactness does not identify a canonical stress-plastic-flow pairing. Moreover, an explicit smooth state satisfying the intrinsic relaxed balance conditions shows that these conditions do not imply macroscopic Prandtl-Reuss normality. In the fully collapsed regime, an energy-entropy rigidity argument determines the evolution and yields approximation-generated examples in which the plastic flow need not be a finite measure or the displacement need not retain its full boundary trace. Thermal concentration and plastic entropy production remain explicit throughout.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Energy rigidity and weak--strong uniqueness for the anisotropic Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^2_+$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the two-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with only horizontal dissipation in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{R}^2_+$. The combination of the missing directional regularity and the influence of the boundary presents an essential difficulty for the pressure estimates. We circumvent this difficulty by establishing an extension theorem for the weak formulation, based on the divergence-free condition and the homogeneous impermeability boundary condition. A key feature of this extension principle is that no boundary condition is required for the tangential velocity component. Consequently, every weak solution in the natural energy class on $\mathbb{R}^2_+$ admits a reflection extension that is a weak solution of the corresponding whole-space problem on $\mathbb{R}^2$. This extension allows us to transfer the energy rigidity and weak--strong uniqueness properties established by Demmel and Wiedemann \cite{E-W} to the half-plane setting. In particular, we prove the energy equality for weak solutions in the natural energy class and establish weak--strong uniqueness under the corresponding additional regularity assumptions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Newton's Method and Policy Iterations for Viscous Hamilton--Jacobi Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study Newton's method for the Cauchy problem for viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equations with Hamiltonians that need not be convex. Each Newton step solves a linear parabolic equation obtained by linearizing the equation at the current iterate. We prove that the iterates converge geometrically in \(L^\infty\) from any initial guess satisfying the initial condition, and quadratically in the parabolic Hölder space \(C^{2+α,1+α/2}\) from initial guesses close to the solution. When the Hamiltonian admits a control representation, the Newton iterates coincide with those of classical policy iteration, which therefore inherits both convergence rates. We extend the local quadratic convergence to uniformly parabolic fully nonlinear equations. For small viscosity, we introduce a Nash--Moser variant that smooths the iterate and the residual in space, and we give a convergence criterion with constants independent of the viscosity. Finally, we show how computable residuals certify the error of inexact Newton corrections computed with physics-informed neural networks.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Asymptotic behaviors of solutions to the critical fractional $p$-Laplace equations with Hardy potential
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper we consider positive weak solutions $u\in\mathcal{D}^{s,p}(\mathbb{R}^{N})$ to the critical fractional $p$-Laplace equation with Hardy potential $(-Δ_p)^s u-μ\frac{u^{p-1}}{|x|^{ps}}=u^{p_s^{*}-1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{N}$, where $N\geqslant 2$, $s\in(0,1)$, $p\in(1,\infty)$ satisfying $ps<N$, $p_s^{*}=\frac{Np}{N-ps}$ and $μ\in(0,\mathcal{C}_{N,s,p})$, $\mathcal{C}_{N,s,p}$ denotes the sharp constant of the fractional Hardy inequality. By means of a suitable comparison principle for weak subsolutions and supersolutions of the equations $(-Δ_p)^sf=\big(\fracμ{|x|^{ps}}+a(x)\big)f^{p-1}$ on general open set $Ω$, with nonzero exterior data and $a\in L^{\frac{N}{ps}}(\mathbb{R}^{N})$, combined with careful constructions of the weak subsolutions and supersolutions, we prove that every positive weak solution $u$ of the above problem satisfies $C^{-1}\leqslant|x|^{μ_1}(1+|x|)^{μ_2-μ_1}u(x)\leqslant C$ for a.e. $x\in\mathbb{R}^{N}$, where $μ_1<μ_2$ are the two roots of the indicial equation associated with the Hardy operator and $C\in[1,\infty)$ depends on $u$. Also, we show that the constant $C$ cannot be chosen to depend only on $N$, $s$, $p$ and $μ$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Calderón-Zygmund estimates and their failure for PDE with linear growth
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate when Calderón-Zygmund estimates hold for PDEs of the type \[ \operatorname{div}(A(\nabla u)) = \operatorname{div}(F) \] where $A: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ is a continuous map with linear growth. We show that, under natural assumptions, $L^p$-Calderón-Zygmund estimates hold for all $p \in (1,\infty)$ if and only if $v \mapsto \lim_{t \to \infty} A(tv)/t$ is linear and non-degenerate.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Time asymptotics, time regularity and separation rates for Navier-Stokes flows in supercritical solution classes
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper extends the weak solution theory for the 3D Navier-Stokes equations of Barker, Seregin and Sverak from a critical setting to a supercritical setting making sure to include a useful a priori energy bound as well as a statement about stability under weak-star convergence. Two applications of the a priori bound are then explored. The first provides a spatially local, short-time asymptotic expansion in the time variable starting at $t=0$ which, as a corollary, provides an upper bound on how fast hypothetical non-unique solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations can separate locally. The second establishes higher-order time regularity at a singular time and at spatial points positioned away from the singularity. This quantifies the degree to which the non-local nature of the pressure allows a far flung singularity to disrupt the time regularity at a regular point.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 45 pages. Fixed an error and addressed a gap

Analysis of PDEs.title: Determination of a Bi-periodic Refractive Index for the Helmholtz Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate an inverse problem for the Helmholtz equation in a three-dimensional half-space with a biperiodic medium above a sound-soft plane. We establish the uniqueness of a real-valued, bounded, biperiodic refractive index that depends only on the horizontal variables using spectral techniques. %The frequency and quasiperiodicity parameter are fixed. An orthogonality identity is first derived from near-field measurements. By constructing suitable separated solutions, this identity is reduced to relations involving eigenfunctions of two-dimensional quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators. To recover Fourier information from these relations, we project horizontal plane waves onto suitable high-energy spectral subspaces, obtaining finite combinations of eigenfunctions that approximate the plane waves with a quantified error. Combining these approximations with the orthogonality identity, we show that all Fourier coefficients of the difference of two refractive indices vanish, thereby establishing the desired uniqueness.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence result for a 2 x 2 system of conservation laws with discontinuous flux and applications
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Cauchy problem for a one-dimensional 2x2 non-symmetric Keyfitz-Kranzer system of conservation laws with a flux f= f(x,U) that is discontinuous with respect to the spatial variable x. No monotonicity assumption is imposed on the mapping x \to f(x,U). We introduce a Kruzhkov-type entropy condition and establish global existence and uniqueness of entropy solutions for initial data with arbitrarily large total variation. The proof relies on a wave-front tracking approximation. The main technical novelty consists in the introduction of adapted Riemann invariant coordinates, specifically designed to account for the discontinuities of the flux, which yield a uniform-in-time bound on the total variation of the approximate solutions U^n(t). As an application, we discuss the second-order ARZ model for vehicular traffic on inhomogeneous roads with abrupt collective changes in the speed law or road capacity.

Analysis of PDEs.title: An almost sharp $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$-$L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})$ restriction theorem for a class of anisotropic operators
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $d\geq 2$. For each $j\in \{1,\dots,d\}$, let ${\ell}_{j}\geq 1$ and $m_{j}\geq 2$ be integers, and let $a_{j}$ be a nonzero real number. We prove that the oscillatory integral operator \begin{equation*} T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} e^{\dot{\imath} \left(a_{1}x^{{\ell}_{1}}_{1}y^{m_{1}}_{1}+\dots +a_{d}x^{{\ell}_{d}}_{d}y^{m_{d}}_{d} \right)}f(y)dy,\;\;\; x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation*} satisfies the restriction estimate \begin{equation*} \|T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}} f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d})}, \end{equation*} whenever \begin{equation*} \mathcal{U}:= \min{\left\{ \min_{1\leq j\leq d}{\frac{m_{j}}{{\ell}_{j}}},\,\min_{1\leq k\leq d}{\frac{d-1}{\sum_{j\neq k} \frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}+\frac{2}{m_{k}}}}\right\}}>1, \end{equation*} and we necessarily have $\mathcal{U}\geq 1$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Gamma-Convergence of Weak-Type Nonlocal Functionals
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $p\in[1,\infty)$, and let $Ω\subset\mathbb R^N$ be a bounded open interval when $N=1$ or a bounded Lipschitz domain when $N\ge2$. For $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ and $λ\in(0,\infty)$, consider the weak-type nonlocal functional \begin{align*} F_{λ,p,γ}(u;Ω):=λ^p \underset{\scriptscriptstyle |u(x)-u(y)|>λ|x-y|^{1+γ/p}} {\int_Ω\int_Ω}|x-y|^{γ-N}\,dy\,dx \end{align*} with $u:Ω\to\mathbb{R}$ measurable. We prove that, as $λ\to\infty$ for $γ\in(0,\infty)$ or as $λ\to0^+$ for $γ\in(-\infty,-1]$, $F_{λ,p,γ}(\cdot;Ω)$ converges, in the sense of $Γ$-convergence in $L^p(Ω)$, to \begin{align*} Ψ_{p,γ}^Ω(u) :=\begin{cases} C_{N,p,γ}^{\rm cell}\displaystyle\int_Ω|\nabla u|^p\,dx, &p\in(1,\infty)\ \hbox{and}\ u\in W^{1,p}(Ω),\\ C_{N,1,γ}^{\rm cell}|Du|(Ω), &p=1\ \hbox{and}\ u\in BV(Ω),\\ \infty,&\hbox{otherwise}, \end{cases} \end{align*} where the positive constants $C_{N,p,γ}^{\mathrm{cell}}$ are independent of $Ω$. We also establish the $Γ$-convergence of $F_{λ,p,γ}(\cdot;\mathbb R^N)$ in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^N)$ for all $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, with the limit functional having an additional term when $(N,p,γ)=(1,1,-1)$. These results affirmatively answer [Open Problem~9.3, Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 2023] of Brezis and also the other problem by Brezis et al. in [Section~7C, Anal. PDE 2024].
Analysis of PDEs.comment: This version is a combination of the articles arXiv:2608.18414 and arXiv:2610.07001

Analysis of PDEs.title: Duality for the Adversarial Total Variation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Adversarial training of binary classifiers can be reformulated as regularized risk minimization involving a nonlocal total variation. Building on this perspective, we establish a characterization of the subdifferential of this total variation using duality techniques. To achieve this, we derive a dual representation of the nonlocal total variation and a related integration-by-parts formula, involving a nonlocal gradient and divergence. We provide such duality statements both in the space of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on proper metric spaces and for the space of essentially bounded functions on separable metric spaces. Furthermore, under some additional conditions we provide characterizations of the subdifferential in these settings.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The periodic Short-Pulse equation by the Riemann-Hilbert problem approach
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we formulate a Riemann--Hilbert problem framework -- based on the Unified Transform Method (Fokas method) -- for the Short Pulse equation posed on a periodic domain. Under the stated spectral and reconstruction regularity assumptions, we show that a local solution of the periodic initial-value problem can be reconstructed from the solution of a suitably defined Riemann--Hilbert problem, whose jump data are explicitly characterized by spectral functions associated with the initial condition.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $ω_φ(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Semigroups with periodic complex-time boundedness and holomorphy regions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the periodicity of complex-time boundedness and holomorphy domains of operator semigroups. We show that an imaginary-time covariance identity involving an isometry yields periodicity of these domains. The method is applied to the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator and the hypoelliptic Laplacian on the circle, providing a spectral explanation of periodicity independent of the explicit geometry of their boundedness regions. We also discuss the distinction between boundedness and contractivity, using the classical heat semigroup as an example.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A sharp lower bound for torsional rigidity of convex domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For every bounded convex domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, we establish the following sharp inequality for torsional rigidity $$\frac{2(d+1)}{d}\int\limits_Ω\operatorname{dist}(x,\partialΩ)^2{\,\mathrm d} x\le T(Ω),$$ where $T(Ω)=4\int\limits_Ωu{\,\mathrm d} x$ and $-Δu=1$ in $Ω$, $u\in H_0^1(Ω)$. Moreover, equality holds if and only if $Ω$ is a ball.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 7 pages. Revised version. It is also proved that equality holds if and only if domain is a ball

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonlinear selection in vanishing discount problems for Hamilton--Jacobi equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the vanishing discount problem $G(x,Du_λ,λu_λ)=c_0$, where $G$ is convex and superlinear in the momentum and strictly increasing in its last variable. Assuming a leading-order expansion of the Lagrangian of order $q>0$, we prove uniform convergence and characterize the selected solution by nonlinear inequalities against Mather measures. In particular, our results cover discount terms whose first derivative at the origin vanishes, such as the cubic discount, beyond existing convergence results based on first-order nondegeneracy. Our proof uses truncated calibrated curves and time averages, without the exponentially weighted measures used by Davini--Fathi--Iturriaga--Zavidovique. In the linear case, it gives a short alternative proof of their convergence and selection theorem. An example shows that linear and cubic discounts may select critical solutions that do not differ by an additive constant.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Circular Cantor Construction Without Dimension Drop for Harmonic Measure
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For every $0<s<1$ we construct a compact $s$-Ahlfors regular set $K\subset\mathbb C$ for which harmonic measure of $\mathbb C\setminus K$ with pole at infinity is comparable to $\mathcal H^s|_K$. In particular, there is no dimension drop for harmonic measure in the domain $\mathbb C\setminus K$. The construction is $N$-adic and based on configurations close to the $N$-th roots of unity. Our construction with corrections to the first order gives the range $0<s<2/3$, while corrections of arbitrary finite order yield the full range $0<s<1$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence of minimizing $n$-harmonic maps in homotopy classes by critical exponents
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We investigate the existence of energy minimizing $n$-harmonic maps from an $n$-dimensional sphere to a compact manifold inside a prescribed homotopy class. Our results are of two kinds.
  First, inspired by the work by T. Rivière (1998) on minimizing 3-harmonic maps from $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{2}$ with given Hopf degree and by the work of R. Hardt and T. Rivière (2008) on critical and optimal Sobolev exponents for rational homotopy classes, we exhibit a general principle that guarantees the existence of infinitely many homotopy classes with a minimizing map inside. We apply this principle, each time proving the optimality of the relevant Sobolev exponents, to mappings from $\mathbb{S}^{4n-1}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{2n}$, where the relevant homotopical quantity is the Hopf invariant, and to mappings from $\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}$ to $\mathbb{CP}^{n}$, where homotopy classes are generated by the circle bundle on the projective space. These results hold for first-order as well as for fractional Sobolev mappings.
  Second, elaborating on the recent preprint of Wang G. and Zhang M. (2026), we derive sharp lower energy bounds for mappings with given Hopf invariant. We apply these bounds to deduce a sufficient energetic condition for the existence of minimizing maps in a given homotopy class. Finally, we exploit this condition, by explicit construction of mappings satisfying it, to prove the existence of energy minimizers from $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{2}$ of Hopf degree $d \in \{\pm2,\pm3,\dotsc,\pm6\}$ and from $\mathbb{S}^{7}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{4}$ of Hopf degree $\pm1$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Weak null singularities for the Einstein--Vlasov system
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the formation and stability of weak null singularities for solutions to the massive and massless Einstein--Vlasov systems without symmetry assumptions. Extending previous results of Luk in the vacuum setting, we establish the existence of spacetimes arising from characteristic initial data that develop a singular null boundary while remaining extendible with a continuous metric. For both massive and massless particles, the energy-momentum tensor and Ricci curvature remain bounded and extend continuously to the singular boundary.
