For genuinely singular initial data, the Christoffel symbols in the original double-null coordinates fail to be locally square integrable near the boundary. We introduce new commutator vector fields that avoid both derivative loss and the most singular curvature component. Under additional curvature assumptions, we also prove Lipschitz inextendibility across the singular null boundary.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp Defect Thresholds and Concentration for Radial Elliptic Equations and Systems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we consider positive radial entire solutions of nonlinear elliptic equations with bounded positive coefficients and optimize the negative logarithmic derivative of the coefficient. For the scalar equation, we determine the exact, unattained defect threshold and establish quantitative gaps when the coefficient ratio is fixed. Near the threshold, we prove a sharp stability estimate and describe the loss of compactness through a profile decomposition in logarithmic radius, including a characterization of the possible diffuse energy and conditions that exclude it. We also show that the resulting profile configurations can be realized by suitable monotone coefficients. For unequal weighted elliptic systems, we obtain the corresponding sharp defect threshold and fixed-ratio gap, and analyze near-threshold sequences through local homogeneous limits and logarithmic spreading. A BV relaxation and smoothing argument further relates the relaxed and smooth optimization problems.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Cumulants of Operator Semigroups for Hierarchies of Many-Particle Evolution Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
The paper presents a brief overview of recent advances in the mathematical theory of evolution equations for quantum many-particle systems.
  The structure of expansions representing non-perturbative solutions to the Cauchy problem for hierarchies of fundamental evolution equations for many quantum particles is outlined. It has been shown that the concept of cumulants of operator semigroups forms the basis for non-perturbative representation of solutions to hierarchies of evolution equations that describe the state and observables.
  It is proven that the constructed dynamics of correlations underlie the description of the evolution of the state, both for finitely and infinitely many particles, governed by the BBGKY hierarchy for reduced density operators or by the hierarchy of nonlinear evolution equations for reduced correlation operators. In fact, it is demonstrated that the behavior of particle correlations governs the dynamics of states in quantum systems with an infinite number of particles.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the well-posedness of two-dimensional Hele-Shaw flow with an elastic interface
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate a two-dimensional Hele-Shaw free-boundary problem with a nonlinear elastic interface, for both one-phase and two-phase scenarios. Using the paradifferential formulation, we demonstrate that the problem is locally well-posed in $H^s$ for $s\geq 2$ for arbitrary initial data. Furthermore, for the one-phase case and the stable two-phase case $(ρ^+ \leq ρ^-)$, we establish global well-posedness for small initial data in $H^s$ when $s> \frac{3}{2}$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp Liouville theorems for the Hardy-Hénon p-Laplace equation and classification of positive solutions for the critical Hardy p-Laplace equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove subcritical nonexistence for $-Δ_pu=|x|^au^q$ in $R^N$, with $1<p<N$ and $a>-p$, in the positive locally bounded weak class. Continuous Steiner symmetrization of a nonlinear auxiliary potential yields a directional pressure inequality; a localized Pohozaev identity and scaling give the Liouville theorem. At criticality, for $N\ge3$ and $-p<a<0$, we classify all positive entire weak solutions in $W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(R^N)$, without assuming local boundedness, symmetry, stability, finite energy, or decay at infinity.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundary-layer detachment and infinite-Reynolds limit of two-dimensional wall-bounded flows
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Understanding boundary-layer detachment and its consequences for the infinite-Reynolds-number limit remains a major challenge in fluid mechanics. Here, direct numerical simulations of incompressible flow in a two-dimensional periodic channel with no-slip walls are used to investigate this problem. Reynolds-number-dependent initial conditions are constructed with a boundary layer of Prandtl thickness that converge in the energy norm to an analytic, stationary Euler flow, while the associated Prandtl system develops a finite-time singularity. Highly resolved simulations show boundary-layer detachment and departures from Prandtl scaling, yet provide numerical evidence that the Navier--Stokes solutions continue to converge to the Euler flow over the simulated time interval. In particular, the squared energy norm of the velocity difference and the time-averaged energy dissipation both scale approximately as $Re^{-1/2}$, consistently with established convergence criteria. Although the detached vortices become more numerous and intense as the Reynolds number increases, their characteristic size and occupied area appear to decrease. These observations suggest how boundary-layer detachment and the breakdown of the Prandtl description can coexist with convergence to a smooth Euler flow.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Finite-Time Singularities of Lagrangian Mean Curvature Flow with Quantitatively Precise Dynamics
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
For each integer $K\geq2$ when $n\geq4$, and for $K=2,3,4$ when $n=3$, we construct an almost-calibrated Lagrangian mean curvature flow $L_K(t)$ in $\mathbb{C}^{n}$, starting from initial data arbitrarily close to being special Lagrangian, which develops a finite-time Type II singularity at time $T$ with the explicit curvature blow up rate \[
  \sup_{L_{K}(t)} |\mathbf{A}_{L_{K}(t)}| \sim (T-t)^{-K/2}
  \qquad \text{as } t\nearrow T . \] The tangent flow at the singularity is a transverse pair of cohomogeneity-one special Lagrangian cones, while the Type II blow-up limit is a smooth cohomogeneity-one special Lagrangian desingularization.
  This gives a quantitative construction of Type II blow-up for a fully nonlinear parabolic PDE arising from cohomogeneity-one Lagrangian mean curvature flow. Our construction is based on a modulation analysis around a shrinking family of cohomogeneity-one special Lagrangian desingularizations, using the perturbative spectral theory developed in the companion paper.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 114 pages, 1 figure. Comments welcome. Corrected minor errors and added Appendix B

Analysis of PDEs.title: Polychromatic Localized Waves with Complex Frequencies in Nonlinear Maxwell Equations with Material Dispersion
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the existence of polychromatic solutions of cubically nonlinear Maxwell equations in the whole space and with dispersive media, i.e., with a time delayed polarization. Due to the complex nature of the dielectric function, the frequencies are complex, resulting in a decay in time. The geometry is that of a waveguide in $x$ with the propagation direction being $y$ and the solutions are localized in $x$ and have a transverse magnetic polarization. These are often referred to as breathers. They are given as a Fourier series in $y$ and $t$ with the leading frequency $ω$ being an eigenvalue of a corresponding operator pencil on $\mathbb{R}$ (in the $x$ variable). Each term in the series corresponds to a different temporal decay rate or a different frequency. The series is constructed iteratively via a sequence of linear ordinary differential equations. Our general result provides the existence under some assumptions on the spectrum and on estimates of the resolvent of the corresponding linear operator. We also produce an example of a waveguide given by the interface of two spatially homogeneous physically relevant media for which these assumptions are satisfied. For such an interface setting the constructed solutions correspond to nonlinear polychromatic surface plasmons.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 41 pages, 6 figures; proof of Lemma 5.4 corrected (its statement has been slightly simplified); new assumption (B5) introduced; proofs of Lemma 5.3 and Lemma 5.5 improved slightly

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Calderón Problem with Randomly Distributed Resonant Droplets
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the recovery of an acoustic coefficient from boundary measurements made after the injection of a collection of small, highly contrasting droplets. This enters into the framework of quantitative ultrasound imaging using contrast agents. The centers are randomly distributed according to a prescribed strictly positive density $ρ\in C^1(\overlineΩ)$. We choose real incident frequencies near an active Newtonian resonance and prove a point-interaction approximation, followed by a comparison with the effective model $(-Δ+P^2ρ-ω^2n^2)u=0$. The constants are uniform as the amplitude $P^2$ increases, provided it is coupled to the size and distribution discrepancy of the droplets. A random rounding and displacement construction verifies the distribution assumption for each such given density. The effective Neumann-to-Dirichlet map is then linearized with a remainder of order $P^{-4}$. We derive reconstruction identities using complex geometrical optics solutions of the known reference operator $-Δ+P^2ρ$. We also estimate the amplification of the boundary-map error in these identities and give a boundary integral correction for reconstruction from the full (and not the linearized) measured map.

Functional Analysis.title: The Wasserstein cost of the Girsanov Theorem
Functional Analysis.summary:
This is an expository note on the asymptotics of the Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure of infinite-dimensional random paths and their common distribution. We present the classical proof for these asymptotics in the case of the Wiener measure, unifying quantization arguments from Dereich and coauthors or Boissard and Le Gouic, and we adapt it for Itô diffusions sampled through the Girsanov theorem.
  More precisely, let $\mathbb{Q}$ be the law of the solution of a stochastic differential equation with a bounded Lipschitz drift. Let $W_1,\ldots,W_n$ be independent Brownian paths, and let $Z_i$ be their Girsanov weights for $\mathbb{Q}$. The reweighted empirical measure $$\widehatμ_n=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n Z_iδ_{W_i}}{\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i}$$ approximates $\mathbb{Q}$ when $n$ is large. We prove that the Wasserstein cost $W_p^p(\widehatμ_n,\mathbb{Q})$ is of order $(\log n)^{-p/2}$, in expectation and almost surely, for every fixed $p\geqslant1$.
  In the Brownian case where $Z_i=1$ these results show that $\sqrt{\log n}W_p(\widehatμ_n,\mathbb{Q})$ is asymptotically sandwiched between $\sqrt{2λ_d}$ and $4\sqrt{2λ_d}$, where $λ_d$ is the first eigenvalue of the Laplacian operator in the unit ball. We provide numerical experiments to estimate the (conjectured) limiting constant in dimension $d=1$.
Functional Analysis.comment: 16 pages. Full Lean formalization publicly available at gitlab.com/SimonCoste/wasserstein

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp constants and martingale proofs for two-weight Hardy inequalities with general measures
Functional Analysis.summary: We study the least constant $C_*$ in the two-weight Hardy inequality from $L^p(σ)$ to $L^q(ω)$ for the operator $H_σg(x)=\int_{(0,x]}g\,dσ$, where $σ$ is a Borel measure on the half-line that is finite on each interval $(0,x]$ and $ω$ is a $σ$-finite Borel measure there, atoms allowed. Let $\mathcal A$ be the Maz'ya--Rozin functional and let $1<p<\infty$. For $0<q<p$ we find the best factor $κ_{p,q}$ in $C_*\leκ_{p,q}\mathcal A$. For $1\le q<p$ we prove $C_*\ge\mathcal B\ge\mathcal A$, where $\mathcal B$ is a Lebesgue--Stieltjes form of $\mathcal A$. The factor $1$ is best possible. For $0<q<1$ we give a lower factor valid for all such measures and an upper bound for the best lower factor. This bound comes from atoms of $ω$. It is smaller than the lower factor proved by Sinnamon (1991) for weights. A two-atom example shows that the bound is not always sharp. The proofs use a reverse martingale with Doob's inequality, a special function of Osękowski (2015), a quantile coupling and a splitting of atoms. The same tools recover the theorem of Li and Mao (2020) for $1<p\le q$, in the closed-interval form of Klaassen and Wellner (2021). They also recover the two-sided estimate of Sinnamon and Stepanov (1996) for $0<q<p$, which goes back to Maz'ya (1979) for $q\ge1$ and to Sinnamon (1991) for $q<1$. We also treat the case $p=1$ and a discrete criterion.
Functional Analysis.comment: 39 pages, 2 tables. Ancillary file: exact rational recheck of the numerical steps in the proof of Theorem 2.7(3)

Functional Analysis.title: Path Components of Almost Doubly Commuting Fredholm Tuples
Functional Analysis.summary: In this article, we prove that the Fredholm index classifies the norm-path components of almost doubly commuting Fredholm n-tuples on a separable infinite dimensional Hilbert space. Using Kasparov's technical theorem, we join each tuple to an essentially normal one by a straight-line Fredholm path and applying the Douglas-Curto theorem.

Functional Analysis.title: The norm formula in a Banach space and in its complete theory
Functional Analysis.summary: We study how stability and the independence property of the norm formula $\varphi(x,y)=\lVert x+y\rVert$ on a real Banach space relate to the same properties in its complete theory. We construct separable Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$ and a separable elementary extension $W$ of $X$. The norm formula is stable on $X$ and has the independence property on $W$, and therefore in $\operatorname{Th}(X)$. It is unstable on $Y$ and has no independence property in any model of $\operatorname{Th}(Y)$. Together with $\ell_2$ and $X\oplus_2Y$, these spaces realize all five possible combinations of stability, instability without the independence property, and the independence property on a space with the presence or absence of the independence property in its complete theory. All five spaces are uniformly convex and $\sqrt3$-isomorphic to Hilbert space. Their norms satisfy the common midpoint estimate $\lVert x\rVert,\lVert y\rVert\leq1 \Longrightarrow \lVert(x+y)/2\rVert^2\leq1-(1/12)\lVert x-y\rVert^2$, and $W$ contains no isomorphic copy of $c_0$. The proof for $Y$ uses coordinate truncation and a polynomial bound on threshold patterns for vectors of bounded support. These bounds give finite fat-shattering dimension at each positive scale, from which the complete-theory conclusion follows.

Functional Analysis.title: Non-local SDEs, critical drifts and local blow-ups
Functional Analysis.summary: The paper is concerned with $α$-stable SDEs with singular time-inhomogeneous general drift. Our drifts satisfy e.g.\,a close to minimal possible critical Morrey class condition that covers local blow-ups of the type arising in some particle systems with strong attracting interactions. We develop detailed Sobolev regularity theory for the forward and backward equations, construct Feller propagator and prove weak existence and conditional uniqueness for the $α$-stable SDE.
Functional Analysis.comment: Fixed a few minor errors and typos

Functional Analysis.title: Logarithmic double phase embeddings with variable exponents: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we study the necessary and sufficient conditions in the domain for Sobolev-type embedding of the space $W^{1,Φ(\cdot,\cdot)}(Ω)$ where $Φ(x,t):=t^{p(x)}+ a(x) t^{q(x)}\log^{r(x)}(e+t)$ with $1\leq p(x)\leq q(x).$ We have established subcritical embedding in bounded John domains under some regularity assumptions on exponents $p,$ $q,$ $r$, and $a$. Conversely, we have proved that if the embedding holds in any domain $Ω$ in $\mathbb{R}^n,$ then $Ω$ must satisfy the log-measure density condition.

Functional Analysis.title: Nagata dimension, separation modulus and stochastic embeddings into trees
Functional Analysis.summary: The separation modulus of a metric space, introduced by Bartal in 1996, is related to different notions of dimensionality. Most generally, Naor and Silberman gave in 2011 an upper bound on the separation modulus in terms of Nagata dimension. We prove that this bound cannot be reversed; that is, there are metric spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension and stochastically embeddable into trees with uniform distortion, which therefore have uniformly bounded separation modulus. Similarly, we construct spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension whose spaces of probability measures endowed with the Earth Mover's Distance (equivalently, their Lipschitz-free spaces) are embeddable into $L_1$ with uniformly bounded distortion. By gluing these spaces together, we obtain infinite Nagata dimensional metric spaces whose separation modulus is finite and whose Lipschitz-free space is isomorphic to $\ell_1$, respectively. Finally, we provide relations between separation modulus and stochastic embeddability into trees, also known as random approximability by tree metrics, in particular for the case of snowflake metrics.

Functional Analysis.title: A Stone-Weierstrass Theorem for Polish Spaces, Given by Logic
Functional Analysis.summary: The Stone-Weierstrass theorem obtains every continuous function on a compact space as a uniform limit of functions built from a separating family by finitely many operations. We extend the theorem to every separable metric space, and in particular to every Polish space, by admitting countable suprema and infima according to weights computed from the construction. For a countable, uniformly bounded separating family whose supremum metric makes the space separable, the functions so built are exactly the bounded Lipschitz functions, and their uniform limits are exactly the bounded uniformly continuous functions. The theorem was discovered, and first proved, in infinitary real-valued logic, where the weights are the a priori bounds of formulas and the uniform approximation is equivalent to an approximate form of Beth's definability theorem, which carries Reggio's correspondence from compact spaces to separable metric spaces. The same bounds draw an exact line between the two forms of definability when the values of the coordinates in the models of the implicit definition form a set separable for the supremum metric: an implicitly defined predicate has an explicit definition precisely when the defining function is Lipschitz, and admits uniform approximation by sentences precisely when that function is uniformly continuous. We also give a purely topological-analytic proof of the theorem.

Functional Analysis.title: Quasicentral modulus for almost normal operators
Functional Analysis.summary: In 1984, Voiculescu conjectured that the Hilbert--Schmidt quasicentral modulus vanishes for every almost normal operator. We prove this conjecture.

Functional Analysis.title: Strongly reducible operators in factors
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $\mathcal M$ be a factor acting on a separable complex Hilbert space. For every operator $T$ in $\mathcal M$ with dense generalized kernel and $T^2\ne 0$, we characterize the strong reducibility of $T$ relative to $\mathcal M$ based on a $3\times 3$ asymmetric matrix representation of $T$. As applications, we obtain criteria for the strong reducibility of algebraic operators in finite factors and type $\mathrm{III}$ factors. We also prove that every Hilbert space operator with an infinite-dimensional multicyclic direct summand is similar to an irreducible operator.

Functional Analysis.title: Sampled resolvents of $C_0$-semigroups: aliasing and sharp rates on the Crandall-Pazy scale
Functional Analysis.summary: For a $C_0$-semigroup $(S_t)$ with generator $B$, sampling the Laplace integral $(λ-B)^{-1}=\int_0^\infty e^{-λt}S_t\,dt$ on the grid $T\mathbb{N}$ gives $Q_T=T(I-e^{-λT}S_T)^{-1}$, the impulse-invariant discretization of the resolvent. The motivation is a dyadic series of Castillo, Costin and Costin for the resolvent of a self-adjoint operator: its partial sums are exactly $Q_{2^{-N}}$, so the series is a telescoped rectangle rule. By Poisson summation, on $D(B)$ the error of $Q_T$ is the scalar $T/2$ plus the symmetric limit of the resolvents at the alias points $λ-2πin/T$, $n\ne0$, and the dyadic levels remove these aliases according to the $2$-adic valuation of $n$. Our main result is a sharp scale of rates for the trapezoid correction $Q_T-\frac T2I$. If $(S_t)$ belongs to the Crandall--Pazy class with parameter $α\in(0,1]$, that is $\|BS_t\|=O(t^{-1/α})$ as $t\to0$, the error is $O(T^α)$ in operator norm, $O(T^{α+θ})$ on the interpolation space of order $θ$ between $X$ and $D(B)$, and $O(T^{1+α})$ on $D(B)$, the last requiring only resolvent decay of order $α$ along the line $\mathrm{Re}\, z=\mathrm{Re}\,λ$. This interpolates between unitary groups with unbounded generator ($α=0$, no convergence in norm) and analytic semigroups ($α=1$), and every exponent is attained. For smooth data an Euler--Maclaurin expansion justifies Romberg extrapolation. For self-adjoint generators we give closed forms for the contribution of each dyadic level to Stone's formula, and we translate the results into an explicit error bound and step-size rule for Green functions computed from sampled autocorrelations. Experiments, including a structurally damped string whose semigroup is of Gevrey class, confirm the rates.

Functional Analysis.title: Hypercyclic Algebras for Weighted Double Shifts
Functional Analysis.summary: Building on the approach of Bayart, Costa Júnior and Papathanasiou, we establish a Baire criterion for possibly noncommuting operator pairs to support hypercyclic algebras, with hypercyclicity defined through all finite compositions.We then study weighted double backward shifts under different multiplications and topologies.We characterize the existence of hypercyclic algebras for coordinatewise multiplication on sequence algebras admitting a continuous norm and, separately, on $ω^2=\mathbb C^{\mathbb N_0^2}$ with the product topology.For the noncommutative triangular product induced by upper triangular matrix multiplication, we obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of dense hypercyclic algebras on $ω^2$.In this setting, their existence is equivalent to that of one freely generated by countably infinitely many elements.Finally, we exhibit a pair on a fixed Fréchet space that supports a dense hypercyclic algebra for coordinatewise multiplication and a nonzero hypercyclic algebra, but no dense one, for the triangular product.

Functional Analysis.title: An almost sharp $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$-$L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})$ restriction theorem for a class of anisotropic operators
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $d\geq 2$. For each $j\in \{1,\dots,d\}$, let ${\ell}_{j}\geq 1$ and $m_{j}\geq 2$ be integers, and let $a_{j}$ be a nonzero real number. We prove that the oscillatory integral operator \begin{equation*} T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} e^{\dot{\imath} \left(a_{1}x^{{\ell}_{1}}_{1}y^{m_{1}}_{1}+\dots +a_{d}x^{{\ell}_{d}}_{d}y^{m_{d}}_{d} \right)}f(y)dy,\;\;\; x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation*} satisfies the restriction estimate \begin{equation*} \|T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}} f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d})}, \end{equation*} whenever \begin{equation*} \mathcal{U}:= \min{\left\{ \min_{1\leq j\leq d}{\frac{m_{j}}{{\ell}_{j}}},\,\min_{1\leq k\leq d}{\frac{d-1}{\sum_{j\neq k} \frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}+\frac{2}{m_{k}}}}\right\}}>1, \end{equation*} and we necessarily have $\mathcal{U}\geq 1$.

Functional Analysis.title: Duality for the Adversarial Total Variation
Functional Analysis.summary: Adversarial training of binary classifiers can be reformulated as regularized risk minimization involving a nonlocal total variation. Building on this perspective, we establish a characterization of the subdifferential of this total variation using duality techniques. To achieve this, we derive a dual representation of the nonlocal total variation and a related integration-by-parts formula, involving a nonlocal gradient and divergence. We provide such duality statements both in the space of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on proper metric spaces and for the space of essentially bounded functions on separable metric spaces. Furthermore, under some additional conditions we provide characterizations of the subdifferential in these settings.

Functional Analysis.title: A Rigorous Fredholm Framework and Stabilized Equal-Order Finite Element Methods for the Time-Harmonic Biot Model
Functional Analysis.summary: We investigate the well-posedness and finite element approximation of a three-field formulation of the time-harmonic Biot model, motivated by frequency-domain magnetic resonance elastography. The underlying complex-valued mixed variational problem is noncoercive because of the inertial elasticity term and the coupled three-field structure. Continuous well-posedness is established under a non-resonance condition by decomposing the variational operator into an invertible principal part and a compact perturbation and applying the Fredholm alternative. We then develop stabilized equal-order finite element methods based on momentum-residual stabilization and local projection stabilization of the pore pressure. For the discrete problem, we establish mesh-uniform stability and well-posedness on sufficiently fine meshes via an a priori stability estimate and a Schatz-type compactness argument, without invoking discrete $T$-coercivity. Optimal-order a priori error estimates are derived in the natural energy norm. We also develop systematic selection principles for the stabilization parameters. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates and demonstrate stable approximations for heterogeneous low-permeability media and anatomically realistic brain geometries relevant to magnetic resonance elastography.

Functional Analysis.title: Noncommutative Maximal Ergodic Theorems for Modulated $(C,α)$-Averages with Operator-Valued Weights
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we study modulated $(C,α)$-ergodic averages with operator-valued weights and their subsequential versions in the setting of semifinite von Neumann algebras. Our framework combines $(C,α)$-type modulation with operator-valued weights and extends both scalar-weighted and operator-valued weighted ergodic theories. We establish mean ergodic theorems and maximal inequalities for these averages on noncommutative $L_p$-spaces. We then study bilateral almost uniform and almost uniform convergence in noncommutative Orlicz spaces, including convergence along subsequences of density one when $α\geq 1$. A key ingredient in our approach is the introduction of the $p$-convexity condition on the underlying Orlicz function. This condition allows us to transfer appropriate maximal estimates from noncommutative $L_p$-spaces to establish bilateral uniform equicontinuity in measure at zero on the corresponding noncommutative $p$-convex Orlicz spaces. Together with the noncommutative Banach principle, this yields the desired pointwise convergence results. As an additional consequence of our $p$-convexity argument, we extend Rota theorem to a larger class of noncommutative Orlicz spaces associated with the $p$-convex Orlicz functions considered in this article.

Functional Analysis.title: Flows on uniform Roe algebras
Functional Analysis.summary:
For a uniformly locally finite metric space $(X, d)$, we investigate \emph{coarse} flows on its uniform Roe algebra $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$, defined as one-parameter groups of automorphisms whose differentiable elements include all partial isometries arising from partial translations on $X$. We first show that any flow $σ$ on $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$ corresponds to a (possibly unbounded) self-adjoint operator $h$ on $\ell_2(X)$ such that $σ_t(a) = e^{ith} a e^{-ith}$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$, allowing us to focus on operators $h$ that generate flows on $ \mathrm{C}^*_u (X)$.
  Assuming Yu's property A, we prove that a self-adjoint operator $h$ on $\ell_2(X)$ induces a coarse flow on $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$ if and only if $h$ can be expressed as $h = a + d$, where $a \in \mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$ and $d$ is a diagonal operator with entries forming a coarse function on $X$. We further study cocycle equivalence and cocycle perturbations of coarse flows, showing that, under property A, any coarse flow is a cocycle perturbation of a diagonal flow. Finally, for self-adjoint operators $h$ and $k$ that induce coarse flows on $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$, we characterize conditions under which the associated flows are either cocycle perturbations of each other or cocycle conjugate. In particular, if $h - k$ is bounded, then the flow induced by $h$ is a cocycle perturbation of the flow induced by $k$.

Functional Analysis.title: Semigroups with periodic complex-time boundedness and holomorphy regions
Functional Analysis.summary: We study the periodicity of complex-time boundedness and holomorphy domains of operator semigroups. We show that an imaginary-time covariance identity involving an isometry yields periodicity of these domains. The method is applied to the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator and the hypoelliptic Laplacian on the circle, providing a spectral explanation of periodicity independent of the explicit geometry of their boundedness regions. We also discuss the distinction between boundedness and contractivity, using the classical heat semigroup as an example.

Functional Analysis.title: Optimal approximation results for non-standard growth functionals in the super-dimensional case
Functional Analysis.summary: In the super-dimensional case $p>n$ we show that $W^{1,p}$-functions can be uniformly approximated by Hölder continuous functions with improved exponent $\frac {p-n}{p-1}$. We use this to show density of smooth functions and absence of Lavrentiev's phenomenon for $(p, q)$-growth with optimal conditions. The special cases of double phase and Musielak--Orlicz growth are also included. Finally, we improve the conditions for maximal regularity of the double phase minimizers. In each case the optimality of our range of exponents is shown by known examples.

Functional Analysis.title: On the Equivalence of Linear and $C^*$ Extremality for Unital Completely Positive Maps on Commutative Real $C^*$-algebras
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $\mathcal A$ be a unital commutative real $C^*$-algebra and $\mathcal H$ be a finite dimensional real Hilbert space. In this article, an easily verifiable necessary and sufficient condition for a linear extreme unital completely positive (UCP) map $Φ:\mathcal A \rightarrow B(\mathcal H)$ to be C*-extreme, is obtained. As an application, the $C^*$-algebras $\mathcal A$ on which linear extreme UCP maps coincide with the $C^*$-extreme ones, are classified.

Functional Analysis.title: Characters on star algebras
Functional Analysis.summary: We study conditions under which a unital linear functional on a complex star algebra is multiplicative. We introduce a class of star algebras, called AC*-algebras, which captures certain algebraic properties of unital C*-algebras. Our main result characterizes positive characters on unital AC*-algebras through a nonvanishing condition on a distinguished subset of the algebra. This provides an algebraic counterpart to the Gleason-Kahane-Zelazko theorem and addresses questions concerning the characterization of characters by nonvanishing conditions. We apply the result to unital C*-algebras and self-adjoint function algebras whose real parts are sublattices. We further obtain a Banach-Stone-type theorem for realcompact spaces, characterizing homeomorphisms in terms of bijective invertibility-preserving linear maps between their algebras of continuous complex-valued functions.

Functional Analysis.title: Isomorphic embeddings of $L_q(0,1)$ into Lorentz--Schatten ideals
Analysis of non-linear fractal functions on PCF self-similar sets
Functional Analysis.summary:
This article addresses three problems: (1) the construction of a general nonlinear fractal interpolation function on post-critically finite (PCF) self-similar sets; (2) the study of the energy and normal derivatives of uniform nonlinear fractal functions; and (3) the estimation of the box-counting dimensions of the proposed fractal functions on the Sierpiński gasket and the von Koch curve.
  We present a general framework for constructing attractors and fractal functions on PCF self-similar sets using Edelstein contractions. Further, we derive upper and lower bounds for the box-counting dimensions of the graphs of nonlinear interpolants. Finally, we provide several graphical and numerical examples to illustrate the construction and estimate the dimensions for different data sets.

Functional Analysis.title: Diffusion phenomena for evolution equations
Functional Analysis.summary:
We study the diffusion phenomenon for the abstract damped wave equation $u''+Bu'+Au=0$ on a Banach space and its possibly degenerate parabolic counterpart $Bv'+Av=0$. We assume that $B$ is bounded and the wave equation is well-posed, without requiring symmetry, injectivity, or commutativity of $A$ and $B$. Our aim is to identify initial data for which the parabolic solution is a genuine diffusive profile: $\|u(t)-v(t)\|=o(\|v(t)\|)$ as $t\to\infty$.
  Using Fourier analysis of resolvent expressions for the associated quadratic and linear operator pencils, we establish decay estimates for the difference of hyperbolic and parabolic solutions and their time derivatives. In particular, we characterize broad classes of initial data yielding the classical upper bounds of orders $t^{-1}$ and $t^{-2}$. We also prove lower bounds for both solutions, of the form $\|u(t)\|,\|v(t)\|\gtrsim r(t)$, for large sets of initial data and arbitrary prescribed functions $r(t)\to0$ that decay sufficiently slowly. Combining these results with high- and low-frequency resolvent estimates and a condition on the ranges of $A$ and $B$, we obtain genuine diffusive profiles. The analysis uses spectral properties of a sectorially holomorphic parabolic solution semigroup, which need not be strongly continuous.
  We apply the theory to damped wave equations on $L^2(Ω)$ with the Dirichlet Laplacian and bounded nonnegative damping that may vanish on large sets. We establish criteria for the required resolvent and range conditions, treat the whole space and exterior domains, and construct diffusive initial data using Weyl sequences.
